1.當年發售時CA的宣發策略。當年CA讓主播先玩了一個月完整版，而非測試版，才將遊戲上市。這與遊戲本身無關。

2.後續DLC價格飆漲，內容卻沒增加，這點和遊戲本身有關。

3.Bug修復緩慢，每次更新都有新Bug，這點也與遊戲本身相關。

4.CA近期商業策略上的失敗，投注重金的鬣狗和法老一個終止，一個市場表現差勁。另外還有之前停止開發三國的問題。這與遊戲本身無關。

5.關於CA辦公室的傳聞，特別是政治正確的部分，這與遊戲本身無關。

綜合以上，其實只有兩點與遊戲本身有關連。不過幾條合起來，玩家很容易產生一種"CA整天都在忙其他沒有的事"被忽視的情緒，至於這個情緒至不至於(或應不應該)上升到否定整個遊戲，這點就見仁見智。至少我個人認為不必。

TWWH3 has sure had a rocky history straight from the launch, which was a little unusual even when being familiar with CA's past blunders considering the outstanding base Warhammer 2 should have provided and simply be expanded and improved on. Sure enough, it has been expanded and improved on in many ways, but the technical issues and DLC fiascos set it back significantly. Realms of Chaos campaign is just plain unfun for most factions and I didn't even play it for the first time at its worst. Immortal Empires however, is good.
As mentioned, the already huge world and faction variety have been further expanded and certain systems refined, but it's more balanced than WH2 which makes it overall a little less entertaining on grand campaign map. The added base game demon factions are not as interesting as WH1 and WH2 core races either imho, and different Kislev / Cathay lords playthroughs are too similar due to geographical vicinity. Still, I genuinely enjoyed playing both of those Order factions. Sadly, I can't say the same for any of the chaos demons which are all very one dimensional.
In conclusion, Immortal Empires experience now is alright. Regardless of all issues and CA's practices, this is still the most impressive and ambitious strategy game to date and I hope it will be reinvigorated and achieve it's full potential in the upcoming years.

In advance, I loved Total War Warhammer II and has at least 1000 hours in that game. Even though they at that time made me have to buy even Warhammer I to play the entire game, I still think it was worth the price when on sale. 

My review is pretty much for those who've played Warhammer II and not those who're new to the game. If you've never played ant Total War Warhammer at all, I'd recommend trying it out when on sale. 

Warhammer III feels like it's more just a Warhammer II DLC where you have to buy massive amounts of other DLCs to make it a fully new game. The races one can choose from are pretty much already in Warhammer II and the new content is very little new.  Even though it's pretty much just a DLC in itself, it's probably playable for around a 100 hours or so, so even 35 USD might be a fair price even though you'd probably get the same amount of playtime with a 25$ game or DLC on sale.

I feel the biggest issue is that for all of this to be a full game, one should have had at least more new races to choose from and more different quest scenarios. In this there are more or less just three races to choose from in the new Chaos campaign which are Russia, China and Chaos, where I think most of the Chaos factions are already in Warhammer II. They all have pretty much the same story where you're supposed to fight a chaos-lord partly in the chaos realm to save/claim Ursoc the Bear-god. 
If you want to play any of the other new races like the Chaos Dwarfs and Ogre Kingdoms who seem to be way more interesting, then you must pay up about the same for each DLC as you'd do for an entire new game that's on sale and you'd end up paying almost 100 USD in total.

Yet, there are some features that even though they should have fixed it already in Warcraft II, they've fixed it now. There is a proper tutorial, they've added some new features that makes the game more enjoyable to play and immersive, and a lot of other annoying things have been adjusted.
Warhammer III also has a bigger map, but that's really not that big of a deal if there's not that much more to do than one has already done in Warhammer II.

One other positive thing I noticed is that Warhammer III seems to run better on my old 2016 computer than Warhammer II did, so I guess they've optimized it better. 

Still, if you have played enough of Warhammer II and pretty much done all there is to do in it, then there's really not that much more to do in Warhammer III than you'd get in any other DLC which should rather cost 20-25 USD on sale.

It might sound a bit unfair to not recommend this just because it's more a DLC and the price should be 10 USD less on sale, but the game in general was a bit of a letdown where I had to wonder if this really was all that was new. It's also a bit annoying to think of that the developers could've done all the new adjustments in Warhammer II already a long time ago, instead of only doing it only in Warhammer III.

As rough as that intro sounds, it is very very replayable with integrated and easy to use mod support, and all of your prior DLCs owned from the last two games do still serve a function in this one unlike most other games where your old DLC is useless. Immortal Empires has gotten a good bit of work done to optimising it to chug less and run better, and the battles run very consistently without many drops in frames. There's a multitude of different factions, cultures, races, and playstyles to choose from with plenty of unique mechanics to each of them to make a strong majority of the roster play their own way (especially if you like Chaos and Skaven). Take buying DLC slowly and pick up what you actually want to play first and let the others come to you over time as you become more involved in playing new factions or wait for sales, definitely worth it to have everything at some point, but it's absolutely not required to enjoy the game or to play the most fun factions. 1. DLC价格高而且质量不符合售价。一款129RMB售价的DLC，只是多了三个派系和大约12个新兵种（不算精英部队）。如果卖80还好，129实在太贵！
2.游戏BUG多。我是MOD玩家，下载了大约350个MOD。（不是所有都用）。我玩个别派系譬如恶魔亲王时经常闪退，我尝试排除过MOD问题，但是其他派系游玩时候基本没有这个状况。这类BUG以及差劲的优化非常影响游戏体验。而且CA每次更新都会带来其他不同的BUG，知名的譬如秋名山大金牙和他的两个搞毛二哥神选孬布拉。这些BUG应该全部都要消除，否则我很难想象未来锤3经历4年的发售（还有很多内容可以出）这个游戏的体验会有多糟糕。
3.CA取消了中文社区的服务。这很一言难尽。有时候看到玩家对于CA发泄时的谩骂觉得很多的评论不一定客观但是也反映了玩家对于CA的不信任。毕竟这个游戏从一代到三代那么多DLC价格加起来不便宜，花那么多钱购买游戏质量不行，BUG多，会让玩家觉得累计花得钱不值得！同时我觉得CA对待一些问题有些过于回避了。
总结，我目前对于锤3非常失望，这本应该是一款非常出色的游戏。锤2时期的DLC譬如马鲁斯和斯尼克，不论从宣传动画还是游戏体验都很棒。但是从最新的变化之影DLC俨然找不到这种感觉了。我喜欢全面战争战锤3,和CA做的其他的历史性全面战争游戏，譬如罗马2。我是很期待CA出历史性全战的续作譬如阿提拉2或者罗马3。以后的DLC和新游戏我还会买，但是希望CA多用心做游戏，重视理性玩家的反馈和有价值且真诚的建议！我不希望这个IP以后消失！差评是目前阶段的，希望2024年我对战锤3的印象会有180°的转变！

虽然3代烂已经不是一个少数派意见，但是我来讲讲为什么3代本身为什么是烂作。战锤3最大的问题在3代的派系（比如我玩过的震旦和恐虐）几乎没有任何战术上的可变性和前中后期的区别。二代的四个初始派系的前中后期还是比较明显的，像高精前期用弓箭+盾过度，然后后期高精通过攻防一体的阿瓦隆或者龙，加上强大的魔法收尾。蜥蜴人前期依靠散兵，过渡到巨蜥，最后事务官侏罗纪公园收尾。其他两个派系也有自己的变化。但我玩过的无论是恐虐还是震旦，前中后期都是一个思路，震旦就是抗线加远程射射射，恐虐就更离谱直接F2A。前中后期的唯一区别就是你用更高级的兵种去重复同样一件事情，所以这些派系很快就会玩腻，而一旦脱离了每个派系的固定战术，其他兵种的性价比简直低得令人发指，起不了任何波澜。
然后说说在大战役玩2代的派系，你就会发现这个大战役现在也是粗制滥造。首先如果你是以长期战役胜利作为目标，那这个游戏的所谓后期基本上是不存在的，就算到了后期，游戏也快结束了。所以战役大部分时间就是你带着一堆垃圾兵去欺负别人的垃圾兵，然后由于维持费现在对暴兵更加友好，玩家的雪球一下子就滚起来了。这样一来还有什么必要去准备后期吗？所谓的终末危机无非就是逼着你去用垃圾兵去对抗顶级兵种，问题是这有什么乐趣可言吗？如果你想赢，那只要在终末来之前打完70+的目标就完事了，如果要打终末，要么打到一半然后龟起来等到天荒地老，要么就是把终末调前然后带垃圾兵去硬怼天灾，无论哪种反正我都不喜欢。
希望CA可以通过未来一些派系重做来加强一下派系的可玩性，战役上面可以加强一下人物和建筑的派系叠加效果，来提高后期的可玩性。

DLC pricing controversy's and some big slip ups with support aside, I do find this a worthy conclusion to the series.

The Immortal Empires campaign map is probably the largest map in TW history, and with the insane number of factions and lords, each with their own special mechanics, it makes for a hectic campaign experience as you go up against different factions with different abilities leaving you with a lot to consider tactically. Between the Vampire Counts spreading death and decay into your lands, the Skaven building undercities, the Lizardmen suddenly summoning a giant army of dinosaurs, etc, the campaign map is often just a lively as the battlemap.

Not only is there a lot of different races to play as, but often individual factions have wildly different playstyles even compared to other factions in the same race, so replay-ability is insane here. 

However a lot of the content is paywalled behind DLC. With some factions such as Skaven feeling very much like they are lacking in their roster without some of the DLC content. All the new races feel very bare bones due to them having gotten limited DLC expansions. Personally despite that I have found Khorne and Kislev fun to play, as well as the Ogre Kingdoms who got all their content in one DLC.  But as someone who has almost all the DLCs, when I look at Lizardmen's giant roster and then I go play as game a Kislev I am feeling the limitations there. Doesn't help that the new factions generally don't feel as easy to play as say, Lizardmen, Beastmen, and the High Elves. 

If picking up more DLC isn't an issue, this is probably going to remain the peak Total War experience for a while. That said, all the DLC together is still a giant amount of money to spend.

For me, Warhammer 3 is probably one of the best 3 strategy games out there - and the best when it comes to Warhammer.

Warhammer 3 is the perfect application of the Total War series game principle (in terms of administration, diplomacy & combat) with the addition of Warhammer lore. Anyone who likes to get information about their units (i.e. apart from numbers), the characters in the game, the races, etc. will find many texts describing their backgrounds in the Warhammer fantasy world. On the world map, which has been designed with great attention to (Warhammer) detail, there are also plenty of points of interest to see and read. And I think I've even seen Felix and Gotrek as an "army" on the map ...

The base game has included the (almost) complete Warhammer Fantasy map and races for some time now. However, you can only play a few of them after buying the basic game. You then have to buy expansions (or the two older games) to be able to play more races. But all the races are in the game, and they are then controlled by the AI.

The technical side also fits. The graphic/art style, the music and the voice acting create a dense Warhammer atmosphere. And the game also runs stable for me.

The low rating of the game seems to me to come mainly from players for whom the prices of the DLCs are too high. And I have to say: it's true, they are expensive. But I'd rather get new DLCs for a few more years than have the game cancelled just to make it cheap. Anyone who plays Warhammer as a table-top knows the price issue. In terms of content, however, I also found the last DLC too shallow for the price I paid.

Regardless of such (fan) discussions: it's a great strategy game that can really be fun for a very long time.

At the heart of Total War: WARHAMMER III are its magnificent battle sequences, where the spectacle of war is matched by the depth of tactical gameplay. The visual and auditory richness of each battle captures the essence of the Warhammer world, while the strategic complexity demands careful planning and swift decision-making. The introduction of the Realm of Chaos adds a new layer of strategic intrigue, offering players surreal battlefields and new challenges. The countless hours spent mastering these battles and strategies have not only been immensely satisfying but also a testament to the game's replayability and depth. Total War: WARHAMMER III is a strategic masterpiece, inviting players to lose themselves in a world where fantasy and strategy converge in epic proportions.

剣と魔法のファンタジー世界が舞台のSLG+RTS。
今回使えるのはロシアがモデルの氷の国キスレフ、
中国・モンゴルがモデルの竜の国キャセイ、
世界を滅ぼそうとする混沌の四神それぞれの軍勢、
混沌四柱勢力に属さない悪魔軍団デーモンオブケイオス。

○良い点
・剣や槍で打ち合い、矢や魔法が飛び交う合戦シーン。
　大軍勢によるファンタジーバトルは迫力満点。
　ドラゴンなどの大型モンスターを含む勢力もいる。

・簡潔にまとめられた都市づくり。
　何を建てるかを指示するだけでいいので簡単。
　しかし、都市設備が軍団の編成や支配度、
　その他の要素にも関係するので、疎かにできない。

・難易度変更が出来る。
　SLG、RTSそれぞれで難易度を細かく変更できるほか、
　ターン経過で起こる終焉イベントも調整可能。
　終焉イベントを起こさない設定まで可能となっている。
　絶望的な状況から始まる勢力でも安心して遊べる。

・色々と個性豊かすぎる各種族・勢力。
　ユニットの見た目も性能も種族によって全く違い、
　得意とする戦術が全く異なってくる。
　種族ごとに独自ギミックがある場合もある。
　同じ種族でも勢力によって補正や環境が違ったり、
　独自ギミック持ちの勢力もあるため、
　勢力ごとのプレイ感もなかなか異なる。

・都市防衛戦が防御側に有利になった。
　マップが複雑に入り組んだ地形になったほか、
　防衛兵器を設置できるため、防衛側が有利になった。
　一方、攻撃側も複数軍団で攻め込めば
　敵を分散させられるので、勝てないわけではない。

・前作からの細かい改修点。
　装備品の交換に1ターンかからなくなったり、
　外交の交渉材料に領地交換が追加されたり、
　クエストがバトルだけになったり、
　騎乗物にスキルポイントを取られなくなったり、
　宿営や待ち伏せ状態で進軍できるようになったり、
　ロードが快適になったりと、嬉しい改修が施された。

・長めのチュートリアルがある。
　1つの独立したモードとしてチュートリアルが存在。
　説明が丁寧かつ自分で考えて操作するパートもあり、
　チュートリアルとしての完成度は高いと感じた。
　独自のストーリーもあり、とあるキスレフの公子が辿る
　とんでもない旅路を追体験するというもの。
　ラストバトルを除き、戦闘の難易度は低くなっている。

・統合マップモード「インモータルエンパイア」。
　前作のモータルエンパイアモード(以下ME)の進化系で、
　1と2、そのDLCを本作と統合させた広大なマップで遊べる。
　その勢力数はモブ合わせ280ほどと非常に多い。
　全勢力が一斉に登場するが、自勢力として使うには
　勢力が含まれる1か2の本体・DLCを導入する必要がある。
　前作MEで1勢力のサブ指導者に甘んじていた一部指導者が
　遂に独自の勢力を得て別の場所に移ったり、
　初期配備戦力が整えられて個性的になっていたり、
　クリア条件が分かりやすく変更されていたり、
　首都が変更されている勢力があったりと、
　非常に嬉しい変更が多数行われている。
　前作MEは1を買わないと遊べなかったはずだが、
　こちらは1や2を持っていなくても遊べるようだ。

・日本語化MODが超高品質。
　公式では日本語サポートなしだが、
　有志の方が作成して下さった日本語化modがある。
　非常に高品質なうえに導入も超簡単だ。
　詳しくはワークショップで"Japanese"で検索。

○アレな点
・3の勢力だけのキャンペーンが辛すぎる。
　一定期間ごとに空間の亀裂が出現するので
　そこから指導者の軍団を別マップへ転移させ、
　最深部のクエストバトルでの勝利を目指す。
　このクエストバトルが異常に長丁場なうえに
　地形が入り組んでいたりしてかなり戦いにくく、
　イージーに設定していても容赦してもらえない。
　しかも、長丁場というだけで面倒くさいのに、
　それを4回もやらなければならないのも辛い。
　おまけに指導者が別マップに行っている間にも
　マップ上の亀裂から敵が出現し続けるため、
　それに対処し続けなければならない。
　自分の領土にある裂け目は閉じられるほか
　建物を建てれば出現すること自体を防げるが、
　他の国にある裂け目には手を出しにくく、
　しかもそこから湧く敵軍団はこちらにも来る。
　筆者はこちらのクリアを諦めている。

・DLCが過去作のものより高額。
　現状、多くのユーザーに非難されている点。
　内容量が前のDLCと大して変わらないor少なく、
　かつ価格が上がっていることが不評を招いている。
　DLCを買わないなら無関係。
　今後改善するらしいので期待して待とう。

・やはり開始状況が辛い勢力が少しある。
　ドワーフ「カラク＝カドリン」など、
　初期州の都市が少ない勢力は収入が伸びず、
　苦しい展開になりがちになってしまう。
　…が、決してクリアできないわけではない。

・2024年現在、種族にニッポンがない。
　各方面から結構怒られそうな名前が多いものの、
　やはり日本人としてはニッポンの登場に期待したい。
　神の力で動き出す守護石像「テンプルドッグ(狛犬)」、
　東洋の寺院で「オレンジのシムカ」なる神を信仰し
　「ヴィムト」なる格闘技を習得している僧侶、
　魔剣トヨタを手に戦うサムライ「サンヨー・カワサキ」、
　彼の腹心「ニッサン」に同盟相手の「ホンダ・スズキ」…
　ネタ抜きにしても、彼らがこの世界で戦う所を見たい。
　なお、公式から名指しで出さないと言われた模様。

[h1]《全面战争：战锤3》：数字数到3，战锤也迎来自己的集大成[/h1]
　　《全面战争：战锤》系列可能是市面上最好的即时策略游戏，那么战锤系列应该从那部入手？对于CREATIVE ASSEMBLY（后文简称CA）的全面战争来说，这个问题基本永远只有一个答案：买最新的。诚然CA在每部作品里都会丢掉一些内容再新增一些内容，不过对系列作品来说，永远是正在热卖的那部才称得上「集大成」。

[h2]中古战锤的前世今生[/h2]
　　首先还是得跟各位聊聊「战锤」这个IP，毕竟还有着“战锤40K”这个容易被混淆的存在。尽管大家都有着游戏车间Games Workshop这同一个爸爸，但是分属不同的游戏系列，甚至有着截然不同的故事背景。简单来说，[b]「战锤40K」是科幻系作品，而我们接触到的《全面战争：战锤》，则是名为「中古战锤」的奇幻背景故事。[/b]

　　作为CA旗下第一款非历史系作品，足以见到「中古战锤」这个IP的号召力。尽管如此，《全面战争：战锤》俨然已经成为CA旗下最卖座的系列，二、三代在销量上都要超越有国内市场加成的《全面战争：三国》，就不要说系列总销量了。

[h2]最好的全面战争[/h2]
　　坦白说我不算是《全面战争》的老玩家，对于系列的了解仅仅从《三国》开始，不过也因此接触了《全面战争》这个大坑，借着三国的东风关注到很多全战UP主，而他们也的确是尽心尽力地上传许多非常有新意的视频，让我对这个系列大开眼界。可以说三国除了题材占据优势以外，玩法上是最不全战的一作，尽管它吸收了过往作品中的很多优点。至于《战锤》系列，无疑是CA的当家IP，也是《全面战争》系列里拥趸最多的作品，[b]一方面得益于中古战锤这个IP本身的号召力，另一方面也是基于游戏自身的优秀素质。[/b]

　　《战锤3》是我接触的第一款战锤作品，尽管本人对三国还算精通，不过毕竟是全新的系列，在一些细节的操作上还是有所不同，[b]不过《战锤3》通过一个序章完美解决了系列上手难度高的问题：[/b]哪怕你是全战系列萌新，在把序章完成以后对游戏内容也就有了一个大体了解，后续的精细化操作则需要自己不断在实战中摸索以及跟着B站大佬的视频进行学习思考。

　　而整体的玩法还是CA惯用的大战略模式+即时战斗，大战略模式各位应该比较熟悉：玩家选择派系，建设城池、攻占领地，合纵连横、外交八方，最后让自己的旗帜布满整个大地。但是[b]不同于P社、文明这些4X战略游戏，《全面战争》的精华永远在于后面两个字：战争[/b]。作为即时战斗的扛把子，军队间的激烈交锋一直是CA作品中的重头戏，《战锤》自然也不例外。而[b]《战锤》系列在CA的作品梯队里有一个众人难以望其项背的长板：丰富的兵种。[/b]作为即时战斗游戏，战斗乐趣是最重要的一环。而海量的兵种和独特的派系体验，恰恰在游戏性上戳中了玩家的G点，而《战锤3》除了在兵种阵容上占据绝对优势以外，对于战斗中的细节也进行了不少优化，比如本代中的攻城战玩起来会更加心神荡漾，让系列在即时战斗中的这块绝对长板更为突出。

[h2]关于DLC的一切[/h2]
　　对于这类大战略游戏来说，DLC一直是个不可避免的话题，像P社这种节操比较低的也许会给你来个本体免费然后疯狂诱氪后续资料片。总的来说，CA在这方面吃相不算太难看，以我个人接触的《全战三国》为例，拢共也就寥寥几部资料片（当然你也可以说是底层代码太难改以至于CA挑骡子跑路了，也因为这一举措遭至了不少批评）。而这部《战锤3》截止目前的资料片足足有十几部之多！

　　 [b]不过就算没有像P社那样完全丢掉了节操，对于大战略游戏DLC太过氪命的诟病终究是不绝如缕。[/b]从目前的反馈来看，玩家对于《战锤3》的定价策略以及发行政策不太满意，一方面CA在锤三发布时弄了点骚操作，另一方面游戏庞大的DLC阵容以及高昂的价格的确有些让人望而却步。但是 ，作为粉丝而言，《战锤》系列永远要体会到最新版本和全DLC才更加能感受到派系间纵横交错的魅力，虽然这个代价有些过于“昂贵”。

[h2]总结[/h2]
　　简而言之，《全面战争：战锤3》可以说是CA目前为止在游戏质量上最出色的一作，目前的差评也仅仅是针对发行和定价策略而非游戏本身。如果你壕无极限，那么直接上战锤大包就对了。基本上每个DLC都有游玩的价值，只有把派系和兵种拉上去，才更加能领略到这个奇幻世界的迷人色彩。

Yes, corporate entities made very arrogant, tone-deaf statements that ultimately place the responsibility of success and game support on the customers rather than on their own shoulders where such responsibility belongs. However, this is about the game, and may be taken to apply to the trilogy albeit in a general sense.

TL;DR for those who hate long-winded rambling - This game (and the trilogy) are not worth investing in for newcomers to Total War games. I'm admittedly a big 4X + RTS fanboy, or at least that's what I tell myself looking in the mirror through rose-tinted glasses. That being said, between the extreme price tag to get the most out of the Total War: WARHAMMER experience, the reduction in substance of added content, and the rising prices for mediocre and/or over-tuned DLC... I would not recommend this game to the uninitiated.
The latest DLCs add content roughly on par with the Tomb Kings DLC released for TWW2, but at a 50% price increase. The game is nearing its second year and there has been zero Free DLC in the store as was available in previous titles. DLC faction identity and balance is becoming a shambles.


TWW3's main campaign gimmick sees you (mostly) racing against other playable factions to defeat assorted Chaos lords and save/kill/eat/enslave/whatever the bear god Ursin. Some DLC factions don't care about it though, similar to how the Tomb Kings of TWW2 had their own agenda.
There is also an Immortal Empires campaign that plays like the original game (TWW1) but with the combined content and maps of all three titles, modified and condensed for a more cohesive and streamlined conquest experience while still managing to be large enough where you have to make a very conscious effort to bring your warmongering to other continents. Not sure if you still need all three games to play it.


A short look at the factions:
- Cathay is China with magic and dragons and a need for harmony approaching fanaticism. They have a beginner-friendly unit roster neatly divided between ranged and melee options. They are also easy to build a stable economy with.
- Kislev is Russia, and it feels like every unit in their roster uses a gun, or has a gun-axe. Or is a bear. They're decently straightforward and forgiving in combat, having nearly all ranged units being also decent melee combatants. They are subject to a lot of infighting, especially between the two immediately-available playable Lords.
- There are five flavors of Chaos: One for each god, and one to represent the corruption of mortals and the neutral-but-directable nature of Chaos.
Khorne gets you Skarbrand, a big, red, angry exiled demon with big axes, big rage, and big stats. His entire roster is about blood and fire and demons and frenzy and the rejection of magic as a means of combat (unless it's fire breath I guess?). Every fight boils down to a moshpit, unless you go out of your way to be a meme but even then you end up in moshtown eventually. There's a lot of red.
Nurgle brings Ku'gath Plaguefather. If you like infectious materials, bulbous forms, and weaponized farts, he's your guy. Everything poisons the enemy, and the roster is severely lacking in missile-based (ranged) options, but you get wizard-type hero units that can actually throw hands. Surprise, everything's green but nothing's fresh.
Tzeentch rolls in with Kairos Fateweaver, a magic two-headed birdman. Of the rosters dedicated to one god, the Tzeentchian units have the most ranged offerings, and support a more skirmisher style of combat, having half of all units' maximum health converted to an energy barrier that regenerates much more infinitely than what's normally present. You can also just... take settlements. If you feel blue, be careful you don't da-ba-dee-da-ba-die. 
Finally, Slaanesh has N'Kari, a tall, pinky-purple, grotesque amalgamation of all things attractive but distorted in depraved and monstrous ways. This faction will have you feeling things, but also uncertain what you're feeling. War wasn't hot enough so now we have whips and leather and uncomfortably lithe forms. There's also only one unit in the entire roster that doesn't necessarily want to get up-close and personal. Purple and pink are lovely this time of year.
- Daemons of Chaos lets you play a rousing game of tactical Choose Your Own Body, bringing the only legendary lord that you can name yourself, as well as modify with unlockable body parts, and freedom to align with whichever Chaos gods you might prefer, whether for tactical reasons or not. I'd call it the vanilla demon faction, but it's more like Neapolitan. You can get any of the offerings from the other four Chaos rosters at the expense of maybe not being able to get the best of ALL the rosters.

And now for the overpriced or under-delivered DLC offerings.

Ogre Kingdoms gives you the race option of the same name. You can either play a meat-starved maniac with cleavers for hands and a cauldron of meat-and-blood hooked to his own body, or a vile, gaudy, greedy fellow with extra cellulose over other Ogres, and a habit of some Tokyo drifting. They were honestly hard to really get into, and their unique mechanics felt underwhelming and very restrictive. The roster is basically 51 flavors of fatness, some with a side-order of oversized gun. Probably more fun in skirmish gameplay than on the campaign, but priced almost appropriately as it doesn't bring as much or feel as clean as previous "whole entire race" DLCs did.

Champions of Chaos brings a little bit more Order to your usual marauding hordes. The changes it brings apply to the older Warriors of Chaos DLC from the first title, but given that they effectively entirely reuse already-existing rosters, the price is far too steep. You're paying for four legendary lords and a shake-up to how plain-old Chaos used to play, with the ability to establish fortresses and have an economy that isn't feast-of-famine with an income deficit reaching into five-digit territory.
There are some new mechanics that are slightly influenced or added to depending on the faction you choose, but ultimately the amount of added content is small enough that it should have been priced the same as the Ogres, or perhaps even the "The X and The Y" DLC duos of TWW2. There's not much new, it's just old stuff remixed to be more modern.

Forge of the Chaos Dwarfs lets you finally play as a race people have been asking for since TWW1's Hellcannon unit came along. They have their own agenda, without much of a race element to it, and play a lot like Discount Greenskins early on. Past that are fun warmachines and artillery. But it's 50% more expensive than similar DLC types from previous titles (Tomb Kings, Vampire Coast) without providing 50% more value.

Shadows of Change adds three factions to existing races, at least one of which is seriously too strong for Campaign, but the content added is similar in scope to DLCs from previous titles that were a third of the price, or even free. This is honestly just a sad cash grab, and the only DLC I would have actually refunded if it didn't take so long to find out if a faction is worth it or not.

All in all, TWW3 gets anywhere from a 4/10 to an 8/10, depending on the context. Content is getting significantly more expensive, and fun little FreeLC has all but disappeared. Corporate suits are suffocating the game and saying the quiet part out loud. I can't in good conscience recommend it outright. But the game... is fun? All in all, this is a solid game and it's fun. Total War has always been more challenging to me than Civilization or Age of Wonders, but it focuses on the real time combat. As campaigns continue, I find myself losing interest because the focus is on armies and defending your turf. But there's just so much randomness, revolts, and uncontrollable events that occur. If you enjoy epic fantasy battles and aren't necessarily in it to build a global all encompassing empire then I recommend this game - it's a 10/10 in this regard. However, if you want that experience of building a global empire then look elsewhere - it's only a 6/10  in this regard.

Pricing and PR aside, I recognize all the work that went into the game. It's just not very fun. The game has this weird collection of mechanics and designs that all point you towards playing the game as little as possible. 

I want to phrase my disappointments in this game carefully. There are difficulties, but I wouldn’t call the game challenging in the way I hoped it would be. Winning in this game on mid or higher difficulties feels like you do so because you recognize the repetition of AIs, not because you identified weaknesses and mistakes and how to exploit them. There’s not enough strategy in this strategy game. AI will become so very set in their tactics that there’s very little dynamics to fight. Hammer and anvil, checkerboard, oops all heroes, or some doom stack become essentially all the tactics you’ll need. Could you use more diverse and/or lower tier armies? Of course, but it will just make battles longer and tedious but not more engaging. Micromanaging large armies and heroes isn’t fun, it’s laborious. 

I’m sure you’re wondering why I rated this game negatively if I have so many hours in it. I’ve even bought dlc for it and the past two main games to get access to more factions. I regret it. Every purchase I hoped that it would add the depth I was looking for. More doesn’t make the game better, and in some cases the more should have been the minimum given how they balance races and factions. I’ve played every race I have access to and found the game wanting. Many factions' unique mechanics are just an iteration of other factions. Sure the lore and flavor is different, but they don’t change any faction meaningfully when it comes to fun. 

This game takes a special kind of person to find it fun. I admit that I’ve had fun at points, but it’s like watching a series with an interesting first episode that only gets worse as it goes on. I don’t lose wars, I lose interest. The game doesn’t really have an endgame. Sure there are victory conditions, but they’re not meaningful and the late game feels very tacked on. The end game for an immortal empire campaign is either an end game crisis where they just spawn 20+armies in one place that just kind of run amok or you can pursue a domination victory which is winning 270+ locations. Both feeling boring and wastes of time. Sure there’s the story campaign, but people at best play it once and never return to it. I’m in the same boat. 
I don’t think there’s any campaign I’ve played where I want to play the same race and faction again. They don’t bring me any joy. It sure is nice to see my firing line or cavalry charge do well, but I didn’t have to do much to make it effective. That’s the heart of the problem and I’m not sure Creative Assembly cares too much about solving it. They’re more focused on how to stylize the next update to sell more DLC.

Ok, onto the updated review for Warhammer Total War 3. 
- Giant map with a ton of choices for races and starting locations
- Some legendary lords are far better than others. Granted, most of their quest storylines are: “This ‘git stole my weapon while I was sleeping…”
- Building choices are boring. Usually, you will have the same layout in each province across the map. This area makes troops, this area makes money, and this area makes sorta money and sorta troops. 
- Diplomacy has less options than Master of Orion 2 in 1996. Options are goto war, trade (only if they REALLLLLLY like you otherwise Chaos can eat their soul before they trade for an extra $50 a turn), peace and Alliances. 
	- Want to negotiate to walk in their territory for 5-10 turns like in other Total War games? Nope. You get an agreement or just trespass. Trespassing is basically like drunken fratboys gone wild. You can have entire populations of folks roaming your lands and no way to tell them to leave unless you declare war on them. Other Total Wars would automatically have war declared should you dare cross that border. 
	- Want to negotiate for land? Sure, for 10 million wheelbarrows of money!!
                - Want to negotiate for someone to stop attacking your ally or friend? Nope, just go kill them.
                - Stop asking me every turn to goto War with someone on the other side of the world. I don’t care. 
-	Why don’t we have Mercenaries? Other Total War games you could hire anything or anyone if you had cash. Romans and need troops? Can hire some naked barbarians for cannon fodder. You mean to tell me I can’t recruit some crazy Orks, Dwarves or Elves into my army if I have the cash? It would make the armies a lot less vanilla across the board. 
-	End Times events. This is literally great! You can have all sorts of nonsense appear in the game at a set turn. Suddenly the world goes crazy, and everyone fights again. Granted, Chaos was removed from this? Chaos was the big bad for 1 and 2 but aren’t even an option here! The whole point of End Time books was Chaos killing the world???? Also, some parts of the map have 0 invasion forces from End Times. So, the rest of the world will get eaten and you will be chilling not even effected. 
-	Chaos Warbands get the ability to upgrade troops from naked dudes with axes all the way to Aspiring Champions. No other faction gets this. It would be awesome to see this across the board. Take your Peasant Spears to become awesome veteran spearmen. Otherwise you just disband them and make new expensive troops. What is the point of Veteran Tier 1 troops? 
-	Chaos Dwarves and the Anime Characters can do caravans. This is a great mechanic, why can’t everyone do this? It is a fun mini-game! 
-	Where is the Navy? I am sure the Vampire Counts would be fun to play if they had a navy chasing people around. Note: They aren’t fun to play.  
Basically, the game is a mismatch of other Total War games, watered down portions of better games, and some patchwork trying to make this work in some semblance of cohesion. I wish they’d make 3 Kingdoms 4 Players, as that game is far better than this one.

I can't recommend this. TLDR; if you haven't bought this game already, don't. Just stick with TWW2. It works better, and the new factions aren't worth it. 

With over 2 thousand hours in the second game, and a little over two hundred in the first, as well as every DLC CA has put out for them, this game makes me done with the Total War: Warhammer games. I've played the Ice Queen, the Chaos Dwarves, the Northern Provinces, and the shockingly obese, and before I got the game on steam I played on game pass where I finished off a Prince of Chaos and Skarbrand campaign, so I've touched on all the new factions. 

The new order factions are meh, and the new Chaos factions are really fun. But the main issue is the AI. The AI was almost a deal-breaker in TWW2. They make really terrible decisions, don't know how to correctly build settlements, or defend their territory, and still prioritize the player, which would be fine if they could take other threats into account. I had Grimgor declare war on me while having his capitol threatened by Kholek Suneater. I was able to ambush one army, take out the other by leaving someone to defend my settlement, and after I took five of his settlements, Kohlek came in and wiped him out. Why is the AI bad enough to let this happen?

The battle AI hasn't been fixed either. Units sometimes refuse to stay in formation, they sometimes will not go where you tell them to (if any units are in contact they tend to ignore most of your orders to fight the unit they're in contact with which is terrible news for cavalry), the ranged AI got much worse as they sometimes just won't fire even with clear line of sight and within range (at one point I had an artillery unit stop firing at a target that hadn't moved, when I tried to make it fire at that target again, they decided they needed to rush it), and other times they will just be standing idle after you gave them and order to attack a unit that is not fleeing or broken, just moving away. The enemy AI for sieges was never fixed and is still extremely easy, and I've broken the enemy AI a few times like when I was fighting zombies, and they didn't know how to line up, so they just kept moving back and forth on their line while I peppered them with artillery shots. It went on like that till I was out of aty ammo then rushed in and they barely fought back. 

It's still not worth it to make any allies until you've cleaned out most of the potential enemies around you. The benefit of being able to build their units is kinda cool, but the downside of being at war with everyone they are at war with outweighs it by a good bit. They did add the ability to trade land, so that's an awesome change, you no longer have to sit with one useless settlement in a region, and can now gift that settlement to a faction for a relations boost. Nice. they won't use it to improve themselves in any way, because again, the AI can't build settlements,but it was still a great addition.

So yeah, it doesn't improve anything, and the new factions aren't worth it. I would say wait for a fix, but I've been waiting two years, and I'm done waiting. 

Edit- For some reason I'm still surprised at the terrible AI in this game. Decided to try out the LL from Nuln, and the mechanics are really cool. Superpowered rocket artillery that drops miniature black holes when they explode is quite possibly one of the coolest things I've heard in my entire life. But holy hell, the AI is still God awful. I have been catching war declarations from literally anyone that shares a border with me for the past 50 turns (it's turn 66). This game is like an abusive lover that I keep going back to because I convince myself it'll get better.

This game has changed drastically since day one, when I definitely would not have recommended it. However, as you can probably tell from my hours, I kept getting dragged back in with every major update. As the game grew, so did my opinion of it, my perception of what it was trying to do, and my understanding of how it was meant to be played.

Unlike most other Total War games, this one is... chaotic. And I mean that thematically as much as mechanically.

You aren't standing on the brink of chaos. The world is already completely overrun by it. And I don't mean the Chaos faction specifically, but the overall state of the world. Even when playing as one of the major civilizations, you begin as a fledgling power and usually spend your opening turns eliminating some local rebel or minor faction just to establish yourself.

Then everything starts collapsing.

Within the first 10 turns, you can easily watch dozens of the 200+ factions on the Immortal Empires map disappear. In my opinion, though, the best part of the campaign doesn't really begin until after turn 100.

That's usually when the age of empires begins.

By then, one or two nations have often taken control of entire regions or continents, and the surviving powers are usually the strongest civilizations in the world. At that point, the game starts settling into the ancient rivalries you'd expect from Warhammer: Dwarfs versus Greenskins, Empire versus Vampires, High Elves versus Dark Elves, and so on.

Of course, the game constantly throws variations into that formula, usually at the most inconvenient possible time and occasionally with what feels like a personal vendetta against the player. Random Greenskin Waaaghs!, Skaven armies, Beastmen hordes, Chaos invasions, and various other disasters make sure the world never feels stable.

One of the most irritating late-game mechanics is having to kill the same legendary lord every five turns because they keep respawning with an absurdly powerful army. Until their faction is completely destroyed, they can keep coming back, retaining their level and buffs every time. It can be maddening.

But in a strange way, it also keeps that feeling of chaos alive throughout the campaign.

Then you eventually reach the final stage: the endgame crisis.

How dramatic this becomes depends entirely on your settings, and you can turn it off altogether if you want. Personally, I recommend setting it somewhere around turn 200. Even then, I've rarely faced the full strength of an endgame invasion because another civilization usually sits between me and the crisis and absorbs half the attack before it reaches my borders.

You can also enable multiple endgame scenarios at once if you really hate yourself.

I could go on for days about campaign progression, but eventually you just have to experience it for yourself. Some people will absolutely find the constant chaos irritating. I completely understand that. For me, though, it has become part of what makes the game interesting.

Warhammer III feels like it was designed to push Total War about as far as the formula can currently go: enormous world size, huge numbers of armies, hundreds of factions, wildly different campaign mechanics, increasingly elaborate graphics, and an absurd number of playable races and legendary lords. It brings everything from the previous Warhammer games together into one gigantic sandbox.

There are absolutely design decisions that, in retrospect, probably should have been scaled back. But the units, lore, heroes, monsters, faction mechanics, and sheer variety are incredible.

I also think they nailed magic.

Magic feels powerful without making every battle trivial. Once you understand when and how to use particular spells, it becomes incredibly satisfying, and the Winds of Magic reserve system generally feels fair. I rarely feel like magic is either completely useless or absurdly overpowered.

And the spectacle of the game is hard to beat.

You'll lose entire days discovering new factions, exploring the map, learning campaign mechanics, and building ridiculous armies. You can lead dragons, giants, sphinxes, dinosaurs, mammoths, and gyrocopters into battle.

You can kill a T-Rex with a mammoth.

You can sacrifice thousands of souls to fuel dark rituals.

You can unleash an army of rats from underneath someone's capital.

This game is fun.

My biggest criticism is sieges.

They're horrible.

Even after all the changes CA has made, sieges still don't feel good. To be fair, siege battles have been a problem in a lot of Total War games. Attila did some things well. Shogun 2 had its moments. Empire existed, unfortunately.

Warhammer III's siege maps are graphically impressive and technically functional, but they lack the grandeur that I want from a Total War game, never mind a Warhammer game.

The resource system is particularly strange. You accumulate supplies during the battle and can somehow construct barricades and defensive towers while thousands of soldiers are actively fighting around you. Sometimes you start building a tower and lose the position before the tower is even finished.

It feels less like defending a fortress and more like playing tower defense inside a Total War battle.

And considering the setting, I expected much more impressive defensive structures. Altdorf should feel like you're attacking fantasy Constantinople. Major Dwarf holds should feel almost impossible to breach. Ancient Elven cities should feel enormous.

Instead, many major settlements feel surprisingly ordinary.

Some of the dedicated forts and defensive maps are better and create more interesting battles, but even those rarely feel as monumental as they should.

Despite that criticism, I've gone from someone who absolutely would not have recommended this game at launch to someone who has spent an embarrassing number of hours playing it.

It is messy. It is occasionally infuriating. Some mechanics still feel unfinished or poorly thought out.

But there is nothing else quite like it.

Hopefully this gives you a slightly different perspective if you're unsure about buying it, rather than another review that is just a rant about how terrible Creative Assembly is.

Although, to be clear, I'm not necessarily disagreeing with those people either.

Now that I've 100% the game and can only derive enjoyment from Legendary (Campaign Difficulty) /Very Hard (Battle Difficulty) anymore I think I can finally leave a well rounded review.

This is definitely one of those games that I wish steam had a "Neutral" review option for. To give you an idea of where my thoughts are coming from, I have over a thousand hours across the Total War Series and started over a decade ago in middle school with Medieval II.

This is easily the most diverse of the franchise by far with the variety of races and the rosters for each one, and it has an incredibly good modding scene. The battles are as cinematic as it gets, and the game is beautiful on max settings. This entry in the franchise also has the most robust multiplayer campaign with the player slots going up to 10 (Medieval III multiplayer campaigns please.) The variety of lords, heroes, schools of magic, and tech trees for all the races allows for a variety of playstyles as well. However, it's really more of an illusion of choice, because when it comes down to it each Legendary Lord has their bread and butter to the point that with all the stat buffs you get between perks and research you'll steamroll armies that are composed of units that ARE SUPPOSED TO COUNTER YOU. Agents (Heroes) will 99% of the time be incorporated in your armies and be objectively better as a battlefield unit than for their campaign map purposes (I've beaten multiple legendary campaigns without utilizing an agent on the campaign map even once, which I feel shows their lack of impact if they're just a side option instead of being absolutely essential for well rounded play.) Sieges (and settlement battles) honestly feel like a downgrade from previous titles. Medieval II did it perfectly with multi-layered citadels, dedicated military settlements being entirely different than cities, etc. In this game there's multiple scenarios where you attack with a lord that just gets a free "destroy castle wall" button right at the beginning of the battle. You should have an inherent STRONG advantage as a defender in a siege situation, and this game just doesn't facilitate that at all.

The largest issue this games suffers from (which plagues essentially every game of the 4x/RTS genre by the way, I just need to point it out here), is difficulty scaling. The AI is DUMB. Want to make the game harder? Give them every cheat known to man stats wise. The only thing AI really know how to do is attack move their entire army at you. Even on Legendary they will regularly send full stacks to their death by initiating battles against you they don't even have any chance of winning (And I don't just mean in battle by the way, I mean the autoresolve will be an 80/20 split in your favor and the AI still attack for some reason).

The game is fun, I'll continue to experiment with mods and play with friends when they ask, but when it comes down to it once you crack the formula there's really no situation where you haven't really won the campaign by turn 50-60 and would just continue it for the sake of reaching the tedious win conditions of a Long Victory. (Which vary WILDLY, Wood Elves and Norsca were beyond annoying to complete whereas Chaos Dwarves I beat a Legendary campaign as Zhatan the Black in 2 hours.)

The core gameplay loop sees you essentially solve the first 10 turn puzzle for each Legendary Lords start, and once you're able to do that consistently, that illusion of depth for the game shatters and you're left with a quick 30 minutes of conquering and then an end turn simulator as you sweep through the map.

I DO recommend this game, the Warhammer lore is one of my favorite universes, and is done extreme justice here. The game is definitely enjoyable up until the point that you've mastered it, and you'll get your money's worth for that time. However after that even with such a diverse cast it's just boring due to the lack of actual challenge. Hitting start campaign feels meaningless (in my opinion), if you know there's no chance of actually losing.

My biggest issues with the game are the following:

The AI is extremely bi-polar and greedy. The AI wants you to go war with their enemies or they break an alliance with you. However, if you go to war or get war declared on you, there is a 90% chance that your AI ally will decline your request with aid even if you have great relations with them. It's broken and needs to be fixed asap. It would make total sense for Skaven, Vampire Coast or Vampire Count factions to betray since that's very lore accurate but to have every faction do that is nonsense. Oh, and the fact that a faction that I forced into becoming my vassal should never be allowed to say no at anytime. 

Outside the Chaos Dwarf DLC (which has hefty price tag so buy it during a Steam Sale), the DLC for Warhammer 3 is VERY underwhelming. The Ogre Kingdoms, which was a faction that I've been wanting to play since WH2, got boring way too fast. Why can't Goldtooth bribe other Ogre factions into joining him like how Slaanesh heroes can seduce units and factions? The Champion of Chaos DLC makes no sense to me. Why add more heroes to the Warriors of Chaos faction when the mono-chaos god factions each need a new hero? The Shadows of Change DLC not only has a hefty price tag too but has two heroes no one asked for. Fans of this series have been craving overhauls for Dwarf, Empire and Norsca for years now. Instead, we get a DLC that has an overpowered hero for Cathay (a faction that most players lost interest in) and a witch character that is relocated on the other side of the world near the Dark Elves for some reason. The Changeling seems cool but his main target is the Empire and not in the East. The Chaos Dwarf DLC is extremely fun and I've done numerous campaigns with the grumpy dorks but it's not worth the full price. 

Oh and of course, siege battles still suck. Unless you are Chaos Dwarfs but even then, it gets tedious.

Despite my complaints, I did put 900+ hours so this game as of this review. In many ways, it's both a step down from Warhammer 2 in terms of quality content but a step up in terms of replay value.

Total war: warhammer 3 é uma das coisas mais únicas já feitas no mercado de jogos. É surreal o que a creative assembly conseguiu fazer com o immortal empires, em que disponibilizam todo o continente do universo de warhammer fantasy para o jogador dominar, para os amantes de jogos de estratégia, com certeza não existe nenhum outro jogo capaz de te proporcionar horas e horas de gameplay com diferentes facções, e toda campanha jogada sempre traz algo de diferente, o que faz com que o jogo demore bastante para enjoar... No entanto, trago uma ressalva muito importante, especialmente para a comunidade brasileira... O investimento necessário para desfrutar ao máximo desse jogo é fora do comum... O jogo base possui uma campanha pequena e com poucas facções, o brilho do jogo, de fato, reside na outra campanha: immortal empires, onde é possível jogar num mapa gigante, no entanto, para o jogador poder ter acesso a todas as facções jogáveis, é necessário um investimento de mais de mil reais para adquirir todas as DLCs e todos os jogos anteriores, pois possuir os jogos anteriores conta para desbloquear as facções bases dos outros jogos, high elves no warhammer 2 e dwarfs no warhammer 1, por exemplo... e se tratando do mercado brasileiro, esse tipo de preço cria uma barreira de entrada enorme para qualquer um que queira desfrutar do jogo... O jogo é bom e divertido, mods também ajudam a manter o hype para jogar novas campanhas, mas saibam que se quiserem ter todas as facções jogáveis o investimento será grande, portanto, não recomendo o jogo simplesmente pelo preço fora do ordinário, mas caso a Creative assembly removesse algumas barreiras, como ter que comprar os 2 jogos anteriores para liberar boa parte das facções, já seria um enorme avanço e com certeza eu mudaria a minha avaliação...

If you're looking for epic battles in a fantasy setting, your best option is probably one of the games from the Total War: Warhammer series. Unless you prioritize graphics above everything else, I would recommend TWW 2 instead. Much of the critique applies to both games, but in general TWW 2 does things a bit better.

What made me keep playing were the battles which are very enjoyable. The graphics are good and it feels epic.

I just wish the campaign was better implemented. You may think that your strategic decisions regarding economy and expansion of your empire will lead you to victory, but it's just an illusion. In fact, there is barely enough depth to even be able to define different strategies.

Early game there are two structures that has some relevance (income + growth), so you build those. There are also some other available structures (increase control + reduce corruption) which will have close to zero effect in the majority of campaigns (regardless of difficulty), so they can be fully ignored. Just build whatever units you think look cool. As long as you don't go too heavy on ranged units, army composition has little impact (more so on auto resolve).

Many of the races' unique campaign mechanics have such a small impact that you don't even have to take them into account, the difference between races feels mostly cosmetic. Maybe the developers were too cautious about creating imbalance.

The single most important factor that determines the success of your campaign is simply the placement of your lords. If you leave the capital undefended at the wrong time, it could put an end to your campaign. Or if you misjudge the distance and venture a tiny bit too far, which puts you just in range of two enemy lords that can attack you together. Your choices about buildings and technologies has surprisingly little impact. I bet you could even ignore the whole tech tree and you still wouldn't notice much difference.

With that said, it can still be fun to play TWW 3 and it's hard to get the same epic fantasy experience somewhere else.

What happened? i thought this would be half ready by now; its was all looking so promising at the end of game 2..

PROS
------
Bigger immortal empires map (includes Cathay and Chaos wastes) and a new campaign.
Multiplayer campaign now supports up to 8 players with extra mp scenario.

New races to try.
Some game mechanics improvements (supply lines, dmg resists, trade settlements, allied recruitment, lightning strike, diplomacy etc).

More varied maps.
Map Artwork, Unit Models, Voice acting and sound design are great.
Its still Warhammer Total War and the modding community looks active.
 
CONS
-------
BUGS (HIGH) - Pathing just...wow (especially sieges), formation, forgetting orders, LOS attack, reinforcement, Textures and LOD, UI, gameplay mechanics, recruitment, quests and AI.

Campaign AI - same issues as TW2 but somehow this is worse even without the bugs. It just runs away now unless it has a huge advantage so the amount of the campaign you just auto-resolve now is almost all of it, you get a couple of actual battles per campaign. 

Battle AI - worse than 2, confused by: walls, siege maps, map edges, pathing, reinforcements, being attacked, moving, attacking, unit cohesion, having more than one target, being an allied reinforcement. 

BALANCE - its all over the place.. half baked factions, lords, campaign mechanics, units, rosters, unit limits, items, abilities, auto-resolves and despite this apparent available variety it all ends up a 3 click ability melted in 3 min samey blob regardless.

OPTIONS - the newer factions especially chaos feel like half the buildings, agents and units are missing.

PREFERENCE
--------------
Battles - over too fast for my taste, units increasingly feel flimsy more so than 2. Not the epic army magic clashes i was hoping for and more a second rate classic rts with overtuned spike damage. As a longtime fan of both the Total War series and the Warhammer universe, I can confidently say that this installment has exceeded all expectations. From the breathtaking visuals to the intricate mechanics, every aspect of the game is a testament to the dedication and passion of the developers at Creative Assembly.

One of the most impressive aspects of Warhammer 3 is the sheer scope of its content. With four distinct factions vying for control of the Mortal Realms, players are treated to an unprecedented level of variety and replayability. Each faction feels distinct, with its own unique units, abilities, and playstyle, ensuring that no two campaigns ever play out the same way.

The addition of the Realm of Chaos mechanic adds an exciting new layer of depth to the gameplay. As players navigate the shifting tides of magic and corruption, they must carefully balance their actions to avoid being consumed by the forces of chaos. It's a thrilling risk-reward system that keeps you on the edge of your seat with every decision.

Furthermore, the integration of the Grand Cathay faction is a masterstroke. This enigmatic empire brings a fresh perspective to the Warhammer universe, with its rich lore and diverse roster of units. Whether you're leading the noble armies of Cathay into battle or harnessing the dark powers of the Daemons of Chaos, there's something here for every type of player.

Above all, Total War: Warhammer 3 feels like the culmination of years of experience and innovation. It's clear that Creative Assembly has poured their hearts and souls into this game, and the result is nothing short of spectacular. Whether you're a seasoned veteran of the series or a newcomer to the world of Warhammer, this is a must-play experience that will keep you coming back for more.

In conclusion, Total War: Warhammer 3 is a triumph of strategy gaming. With its stunning visuals, deep mechanics, and rich lore, it sets a new standard for the genre. Creative Assembly has truly outdone themselves with this installment, combining everything they have learned over many years into a game that is nothing short of extraordinary.

There are three parts to this review: about the game, about Total War games, and about Creative Assembly.

Disclaimer: I am a historic fan. I started with Rome. Meaning: I prefer the historic titles. I was quite disappointed when I learned about the Warhammer franchise coming to TW, which I deemed to be subpar fantasy. But I gave the game a try, and it grew on me. First with TWW2, which I didn't like. I played with the Dark Elves, which I found to be insufferably cringeworthy (now my fav race). Then, one more time with TWW3. I quit the franchise after Thrones of Britannia and got into the game thanks to a Youtuber: LoTW.

Now that this is out of the park. Let's get to the meat on that bone.

First, pricing.
As I said to a friend who wanted to purchase the game, be mindful that, on top of the game, you need to invest, in my opinion, at least 30 USD or EUR in DLC in order to have fun. It is not a negative thing per se, but something to keep in mind for new players. 
Please note that this isn't me complaining about the pricing. I see this game as CA's (Creative Assembly's) live service, and as such, I would prefer this game to keep receiving love from the devs. The DLCs are all relatively reasonably priced too, so kudos to CA for that.
The game is fun and quite rich. You will sink many hours into it.
But.
Units are unresponsive and have terrible pathfinding; missile units are extremely finicky and will not shoot if there is a boulder in front of them or rugged terrain. 
Cavalry is bad; it will get stuck in enemy lines, and if one rider gets trapped in fighting, it will pull the entire retreating unit back into fray.
Small, single entities with high armor and shields will soak up ammo since they cannot get hit. There are so many ways to cheese the AI.
Maps are getting smaller and smaller. 
Siege battles, I mean; no comment.
Strong anti-player bias from the AI (try playing around Belakor with different factions and tell me it doesn't exist). 
Bugs, bugs, bugs.
All units can climb the walls, making said walls useless.
Units on walls are often spacing out.
Charging enemies will push them away but won't damage them if they don't get pushed down a slope.
The AI will run away from you on the campaign maps and try to sack you instead of fighting to absurd levels. I am getting mad listing this.

The Total War formula.
I've had enough, and this game will get it for all of the others.
As I said earlier, I stopped with Saga: Thrones of Britannia. I couldn't do it anymore. After Fall of the Samurai, I thought CA was at its peak and couldn't miss even with their odd game design choices. What a pitiful creature I was. 
The difficulty parameter in Total War games is dated; it is obscenely obsolete. A thing of the past. It is the manifestation of CA's most cardinal sin, laziness. To get a harder experience, CA is juicing the AI's unit stats and hammering yours. It was okay in Medieval II, perhaps, but come on, guys. It isn't 2005 anymore! By doing so, you render a ton of units useless since they will rout at the first contact. Why do you put money and time into coding units that won't get used by a sizeable portion of the playerbase due to your design? Why?! Make the AI smarter and viciouser, give it more money, and more. But the stat thing—get rid of it altogether.
Anti-player bias, a staple of Total War games. We can also have fun if the guy at the other end of the world doesn't hate us you know? I have unresolved trauma from the Date attacking me, the Shimazu in Shogun 2 cause I guess they can't stomach my japanese bosom.
Diplomacy gets shallower with each release. We want more depth on the campain map too. That goes for building and unit trees too.

About CA.
I commend you for improving the multiplayer campaign. I appreciate you listening to feedback from the playerbase regarding pricing. ToD DLCs were amazing. Love the communication and FLCs.
I do not like your philosophy of nerfing fun. Like nerfing hero traits or lords. Overnerfing units. Let us have fun, this is not a “competitive” game. Most of us play solo.

It also has nice little touches added here and there, such as when the developers added a building in-game that was a nod to the Ubersreik Five in Vermintide. It's the little touches and details that tell you a lot about the developers.

Despite problems here and there, they do not detract from what is a highly entertaining game.

"Total War: Warhammer 3" s'impose comme un titan dans le genre des jeux de stratégie, combinant avec brio la gestion complexe d'un empire et des batailles épiques en temps réel. Ce troisième opus enrichit l'univers déjà vaste de Warhammer avec de nouvelles factions fascinantes, des terrains de jeu gigantesques et une diversité de stratégies inégalée, offrant une profondeur de gameplay et une rejouabilité exceptionnelles.

L'une des forces majeures de ce jeu réside dans sa capacité à marier le lore riche de Warhammer avec les mécaniques stratégiques sophistiquées de la série Total War. Chaque faction est unique, avec ses propres unités, héros, et mécaniques de jeu, ce qui pousse les joueurs à adapter constamment leurs stratégies et à plonger dans les subtilités de chaque culture. Les campagnes narratives sont immersives, guidant les joueurs à travers des récits épiques qui reflètent les mythes et légendes de l'univers Warhammer.

Les batailles, cœur palpitant du jeu, sont spectaculaires, mettant en scène des milliers de troupes sur des champs de bataille où chaque décision tactique peut renverser le cours de l'affrontement. La variété des unités, des monstres gigantesques aux troupes d'élite, offre une richesse tactique et visuelle, capturant parfaitement l'essence dramatique et fantastique de Warhammer.

Graphiquement, "Total War: Warhammer 3" est un régal pour les yeux, avec des environnements variés et détaillés, des effets visuels impressionnants, et des animations fluides qui donnent vie aux batailles. La conception artistique est fidèle à l'esthétique de Warhammer, retranscrivant avec succès l'atmosphère sombre et mystérieuse de cet univers.

Le multijoueur ajoute une dimension supplémentaire au jeu, permettant des affrontements épiques entre joueurs, où la stratégie et la connaissance des différentes factions sont clés pour la victoire. Cette composante compétitive assure au jeu une longévité remarquable.

En conclusion, "Total War: Warhammer 3" est une réussite éclatante, un must-have pour les fans de stratégie et de l'univers Warhammer. Il offre une expérience de jeu riche, complexe, et incroyablement satisfaisante, qui pousse les limites de ce que l'on peut attendre d'un jeu de stratégie.

Its no secret this game has had a very bumpy ride. It didn't release in the best state. It took a better part of year for it to get the immortal empires addition to the game that unlocked the factions from previous entries, and it hasn't been well supported with many bugs remaining in the game for MONTHS before getting patched. 

On the other hand this is by far the most ambitious game Creative assembly has ever made. It is a BEAUTIFUL game with many unique factions each with its own play style and flair. The game has nearly unlimited replay value and is a good value for your money (just understand its a modern strategy game so be prepared for ALOT of DLC but it would be remiss to judge this game poorly for that when its basically just a industry standard at this point). The third iteration of this game adds unique siege mechanics (that are... questionable but much better than they use to be), an ally system that lets you recurit units from other factions (by far my favorite update) and a new campaign, and an overhaul to the diplomacy system. Overall Warhammer 3 really is an improvement on warhammer 2.

On the cons side though there are some issues... There are many many bugs in this game (few are game breaking and alot of them you wont realize even exist because they go on in the background or exist under the hood so to speak) but the fact that they exist for so damn long without getting patched out is a definite mark against the game. Furthermore the AI is more A than I. This has been a problem with total war games going back for YEARS and to be fair its probably hard to program a competent AI with so many units but still its a mark against a strategy game that you'll mostly be playing against the computer that its so easy to take advantage of and defeat. 

Now the elephant in the room. the recent behavior of creative assembly. to make a long story short they tried to charge 3 times as much for their most recent DLC for half the product. This did NOT sit well with the community. the backlash was extreme but you know what? They did something I haven't seen a company do in YEARS (sense no man's sky honestly). They didn't blame the fans and call people names, they didn't ignore the backlash, they didn't laugh and take people's money. the appalogized, they offered a refund, and they got to work making it better. So I'm writing this as a personal thank you to CA. You make my favorite games I've LOVED them sense i was a kid. Warhammer one unironically got me through my divorse and helped keep me going as stupid as that might sound. Keep up the good work. Keep working to make the best product you can.

你为什么要玩这款游戏：
1.如果你想体验类似于魔戒的感觉，你可以来尝试一下这款作品，我相信你能得到一定的游玩体验。有哪个男人不喜欢指挥军队碾压敌人呢？就像游戏宣传所说，你可以选择游玩许多派系，每个派系都有自己的特色，不论是裸男北佬还是全副武装的混沌勇士，亦或是选择指挥一只蜥蜴人大军，绝对能满足你对于统治世界的快感。当军队互相冲击，那肯定能带给你不一样的快感。
2.游戏目前还在更新，更有超级丰富的创意工坊内容，大修模组这里推荐SFO，radious，金花，当然了，如果你想体验桌面上的战锤，那你可以选择阿查的全面战争，也有非常多的美化（色孽）模组，让游戏的体验更加完好
3.可以联机，当然了，他需要朋友。联机可以选择对抗也可以选择合作，你将能看到鼠人和高精同流合污，或者是帝国和吸血鬼狼狈为奸，或者是混沌勇士和矮子一起灭世，谁不喜欢戏剧性的一幕呢？

1.原版就是一坨，讲真，平衡做的非常的烂，完全不符合定位，所以我只玩大修模组，如果没有创意工坊的加持，想必这游戏的热度可能连一半都没有，

Before I played this game I played it's predecessor (Total War Warhammer 2)  and loved it. Personally I love this game too, I love it even more than 2. However just because I love it does not mean everyone one will. Not to mention the game did not launch in a great state, and up until recently has been stuck in controversy over DLC prices not matching content offered The game is far from perfect and you may need to be ready to expect another bump in the road before it is truly done. But that is for the future, what I am here to write about is the now. I will now list my personal list of upsides and downsides to Warhammer 3 to help paint a picture of what the game is like and what I feel are it's stronger traits. 

Upsides: 
+ In this game there are 3 campaign styles you can play, a prologue to introduce you to the game mechanics and set up the main story of the 2nd campaign, a main campaign with all of the new things Warhammer 3 introduced, and finally the Immortal empires campaign which combines the EVERYTHING from Warhammer total war 1 2 and 3! 
+ Unlike in Warhammer 2 where you needed to own warhammer 1 in order to play the campaign that mixed both games 1 and 2, in 3 you just need to own 3 in order to play the worldwide experience. If you own just Warhammer 3 and nothing else, you can still play Immortal Empires.
+ There are an insane amount of quality of life changes for Warhammer 3 compared to 2.
+ Diplomacy is dramatically improved compared to 2. Alliances serve real purpose and can lead to HYBRID FACTION ARMIES. 
+ All of the New playable Races introduced in 3 (Including DLC) are fun in my opinion. While some may definitely be more fleshed out than others, all of them are viable choices for the player to enjoy. 
+ If you own Warhammer total Wars 1, 2, or any of their DLC, you can still use them in 3 within the Immortal empires campaign. This means that if you spent 60 to 100 dollars on any warhammer game (plus DLC), you can still make the most of your money in 3. 
+ There are more game play options than just the campaigns. You can play against other people in online battles. You can challenge yourself with the in game challenge missions and quest battles, and heck you can even just skirmish with the AI to test strategies or just to get into a quick fight when bored. 
+ Multiplayer is better than ever here. Back in game 2 the most number of people of you could have in a multiplayer campaign was 4. In 3 that number has been raised to 8 and multiplayer overall has been overhauled significantly. It's a really cool experience. 
+ Overall the game is full of little details that add to the experience. Whenever magical corruption gets high in a given province, the entire area begins to morph and change to reflect the corruption itself. Like if there is a huge amount of Vampire corruption in a given area, then the grass and trees turn from vibrant green to dull and muted grey. Ghosts and flickering souls can be seen in the air and floating through the forests, and occasionally a horrifying night monster can be seen in the trees or flying in the air in those areas. These details serve no purpose other than to visually show how messed up the land is becoming due to the corruption and I love it. 
+ Regardless of the faction you pick, or the race you choose to play, the game is overall a fun tactical experience that is deep enough to be super fun with room to master, while also not being impossible for new players to pick up. I may still not be the best player even after all this time playing, but at least I understand the game. 
+ PERFECT VOICE ACTING. I have not heard a single bad voice line in the entire game. All of the VA's put real effort into this and it shows. (Some of my favorite Voice performances are Karl Franz, Villitch the Curseling, Settra the Imperishable, and Malekieth the Witch King. All Stellar work). 
+ Amazing artwork is used for the game in many aspects. From loading screens to event notifications, every race has their own unique set of artwork that is absolutely stunning.  Even if you do not buy the game I recommend taking a look at the artwork at least once. 

I likely love more things about the game than I can list here. Some I just cannot think of off the top of my head for this review, and others are too minuscule or opinionated to bring up. Regardless I love this game. However I will not deny that it has some issues. 

- Game can get VERY pricey when trying to get the various DLC for the other games. So far all 3 Warhammer 3 DLC has priced in at about 20-25 USD and show no sign of dropping in price anytime soon.  
- Occasionally the game can have some bugs. It was a buggy mess at launch, and while things have improved dramatically (I very rarely if ever encounter bugs now), some still plague the game. From the minuscule visual bugs to the crashing, you are likely going to experience a few if you play for an extended period of time (for many days). 
- Some of the factions and playable lords are a bit unbalanced. Characters like any of the Warriors of Chaos factions are super powerful and can be used to sweep the world. The Changeling from the newest DLC is essentially an un-loseable campaign no matter where you play him. Meanwhile you have the Lizardmen and Dark Elves from Warhammer 2 who have still not been given an overhaul (as of writing this). 
- This game is LONG. Even when trying to complete the "shot campaign victories" in Immortal Empires, you can still be at this game for hours and make slow progress. 
- The AI does not like to play fair. The AI will constantly make armies larger than their economy can afford, and in most cases will favor fighting the player over other AI.
- The Realms of Chaos campaign for the base game is not the best. It's a sure improvement over 2's base main campaign, but that is not saying much. If you play through realms of chaos as a non-dlc faction be prepared for a potentially very annoying experience that is VERY easy to lose even when on the easiest difficulty. (SPOILERS FOR THAT CAMPAIGN: You need to compete with about 6 AI factions in a race to defeat 4 main bosses before fighting the big bad.  If you fall too far behind then you can easily lose the game just by being too far behind in the race to recover). 
- The game is technically not fully done yet. Every DLC also acts like something of an update to all the factions involved (and then some). So until the devs stop making DLC, the game will remain in a constant state of being updated and not being "done". It feels like a finished product to play, but there are some things missing that future DLC will try to address. 

With all of this in mind, here are some closing thoughts: Total War Warhammer 2 was one of my number 1 favorite games ever. It was my first real experience with grand strategy outside of Paradox games, and it was amazing. I fell in love with the world, the story, the characters, the entire setting as a whole. When 3 was announced I was immediately ready to fall in love with it too. The game launched and had a rocky start. Things did not go well for it and I struggled to keep playing despite all the good. However Immortal empires came out and pulled me right back. I was in love with the game again and was ready to truly enjoy it like never before. This game has been a trip to play but also an experience I would never wish to give up. This game truly feels grand and incredible to play, and I have yet to see another game even approach the level this one does. Flaws be damned, I love Total War Warhammer 3 and I hope you try it out.

The game is phenomenal. The most fun TW game I have played (I haven't played some of the other newer ones like Troy or Three Kingdoms). I have hundreds of hours across all three TW: Warhammer games. If you have not played TW games before I don't think I can really describe the experience or genre (such that it is) in the context of this review. 

Reading the other reviews does make me consider a few things. It is true that to get the maximum enjoyment from the game, you need the two other previous titles and a ton of DLC, some of which has been reasonably priced and obviously some of which has been offensively priced (more recently). When you think about it, to own it all is a massive investment for a single game. I can't say I support some of the business practices. However I did pick up a lot of the DLC on sale, like I do for most games I buy on Steam. However when I (rarely) review, I base my reviews on the game itself and I don't "review bomb" or whatever. If the company has disrespectful pricing practices or what have you, I leave it to the unwashed masses to protest in their desired fashion.

The quality and raw enjoyment factor of the game (particularly as a Warhammer fan), assuming you own a substantial amount of the above, is very high. It is comparatively very polished, although there are dated and seemingly unfixable elements of "the engine" that are noticeable (much like Bethesda games). People complain about this online, as well as the difficulty being too low (if you have never played these games, or you have real life commitments or engage in other games/hobbies, you're unlikely to have that problem). 

The current overall "mixed" review score is not representative of the fun factor, but probably is generous when one considers the cost to own factor.
