if you're checking to see whether this game is worth the price: the game is fun and has plenty of replayability, but the base game alone entitles you to a small fraction of the content in the game, so you'll need to sink a lot of money into overpriced DLC. always buy at a discount, and be aware that around a quarter of this game's factions can only be unlocked by buying the other games in the trilogy, even if you buy all the DLC for this game.

if you're a strategy gamer wondering whether this is a good buy: yes, but not at the normal price, and don't expect the game to play like a historical Total War game. this is a Total War game in a darwinian high fantasy setting, and the gameplay has adapted well. this game is set in the world of Warhammer Fantasy, an old tabletop game that mostly exists nowadays as a collection of licensed video games, but you won't need to have read the sourcebooks because what little story there is is explained in-game and much of it was written for this game. in short, this game takes place in a temporally-fluid pastiche of our world somewhere between the industrial revolution and several centuries BC, but with magic, polytheism, a looming invasion by demons, demon cultists & ratmen, and stereotypical fantasy species pasted over any race that isn't european or chinese. warhammer's analogue of america is populated by a race of backstabbing slavers who became psychopaths, turned on their majestic brethren overseas and now get off on torturing people. take that as you will.

returning players from historical Total War might find that the gameplay feels off, and i agree - i personally find that the less realistic design philosophy does cause me to visualize battles as two sets of stat blocks crashing into each other in arbitrary configurations rather than a test of wits between two forces whose units behave intuitively according to appearance. on the other hand, intuition inherently goes out the window to a degree when the game balance was determined by tabletop game designers rather than a collection of centuries-old military records - there's a good reason the human mind is disinclined to believe that a loosely arranged mob of naked people with whips can hope to defeat an equal quantity of heavy infantry with zweihänders. if you're a fan of naval battles, you should know that this game has no naval gameplay, despite having playable pirates (vampire coast), vikings (norsca) and british people (high elves). the only ships in the game are the transport fleets that all armies store in their asses at all times next to their siege ladders, and if two opposing armies meet at sea, they will agree to park at a nearby island and disembark to fight on land. the closest thing to a navy in this game is the dark elves' black arks, mobile settlements that provide ground troops and shore bombardment to friendly armies.

the game's only campaign at launch (tutorial excepted) was Realm of Chaos, a narratively-driven race against the other major factions to invade the titular realm and reach the wounded god Ursun, taking place along the northern latitudes of the world. the main attraction of total war: warhammer III, however, is Immortal Empires, a more traditional Total War campaign that combines the three campaign maps from the total war: warhammer trilogy into one large map spanning almost the entire Warhammer Fantasy world. this campaign contains over 200 factions (though the majority are minor NPC factions that exist to be trampled by or absorbed into playable factions), and the world's races are as diverse to fight as or against as they look.

there are plenty of playable factions with radically different playstyles and campaign mechanics. every race has a different core strategy in battle, a different approach to empire-building on the strategic map, and emphasize different mechanics. within each race, most factions have a distinct gimmick intended to encourage different uses of the same unit roster or change the player's diplomatic priorities. i'd feel comfortable saying that every faction in this game feels more unique to play than Rome does in Rome 2, and it is almost always better to do realpolitik and set war goals instead of just dividing the world into enemies and future enemies.

however, expect to drop several hundred dollars on DLC for this game, and the integrated content from the previous games in the trilogy, if you're interested in playing anyone other than Cathay (fantasy imperial china), Kislev (fantasy imperial russia) or the daemons of chaos (fantasy florida). if you got into Total War through the pre-Empire games like I did, I would recommend picking up the first game in the trilogy (yes, the base game), which will unlock some of the more accessible races in Immortal Empires if you own both games. Reikland or Couronne will ease you in with gameplay familiar to players of historical total war, and the Vampire Counts will force you to adapt. also consider buying the second game to unlock the Knights of Caledor, which is objectively the best faction. owning all three games, without buying any DLC, will unlock around two thirds of Immortal Empires' playable races. some factions within those races will remain paywalled, but this is more than enough content to get a feel for the game.

i would advise you to keep a firm grip on your wallet around this trilogy. more than one DLC has been controversial among consumers for high prices & thin content, and the developers have made a grand number of PR blunders, although they have recently been working to reverse their reputation by releasing new content for the Shadows of Change DLC. if, however, you can build up your DLC library and adapt to each faction's gimmick, there are easily 10,000 hours of gameplay before you've seen everything.

though they shouldn't factor into your purchase decision, i feel the need to mention mods, given how critical they are to the experience of playing this game. here's a brief primer, so you're not quite as lost if you choose to get into the modding scene: the steam workshop has a rich selection of mods to add new playable factions with unique mechanics, or revamp minor factions to have unique leaders and gimmicks. the community does its best to ensure cross-compatibility between mods (mostly by having every mod author bother one particular person to edit startpos.esf on their behalf), and i enjoy seeing how many mods i can stuff the game with without breaking it. be aware that the owners of the Warhammer IP do not allow workshop content referencing IPs outside of Warhammer Fantasy, so most mods add either original content or canon content that does not appear in vanilla. Mixu's Unlocker, Victory Conditions Overhaul, Heroes of Legend and the suite of faction mods from Team OvN are essential, even if you're not looking for a heavily modded experience. if you are, mods can more than double this game's playtime - just don't expect mods to carry the game if you're not sold on vanilla, and don't install SFO: Grimhammer unless you fancy begging for a compatibility patch whenever you want to use any other mod. consider downloading the fan-made Warhammer 3 Mod Manager if you intend to play with more than a handful of mods; it makes it a hell of a lot easier to figure out which mod is crashing your game or causing conflicts.

in summary: it's a good game that will last you a long time, but has a very different design philosophy from the historical games. faction variety is unparalleled. there's a deep pool of mods to choose from, and you can pack a lot of content into one playthrough, as long as you know what you're doing. you will need to make a lot of purchases to get the full experience, however - 20 DLC packs and counting, plus both of the previous games in the trilogy - so be prepared to wait for sales or look for discounted steam keys on third-party sites.

- la variété permis par l'univers de warhammer qui bouleverse les stratégies. On est plus dans le classique lance > cavalier > archer > épée > lance puisqu'il y a désormais toute une rimbambelle de monstres divers et variées qui bouleversent les équilibres et obligent à repenser la stratégie selon son peuple et le peuple en face.
- toujours la variété sur la façon dont les villes sont construites qui donne une bonne rejouabilité puisque la façon de jouer n'est pas la même
- les objectifs de victoire réellement différents selon les factions puisqu'au delà des factions qui doivent conquérir des territoires précis, pour les bretonniens il faut gagner de l'honneur, pour une race de mort vivant il faut retrouver un grand livre, pour les pirates il faut avant tout piller sans étendre forcément son empire, etc.

i bought this game more out of a love for the warhammer franchise than for the total war series but this game single handedly got me more into the grand stategy genre of total war.

my first complement to the game is its visuals in and out of game, all of the factions are beautifully designed and even low level armies manage to create an incredible visual film. every battle feels like a film and every unit even infantry look awesome.

my next point is the game play, the battle system has an enormous skill ceiling and is very rewarding to learn, outside of battle the civilisation system is so much fun as each faction adds huge changes to how your civilisation functions, to chaos factions spreading plagues to rats that build nukes under other peoples homes to dwarves never forgiving people. this variety leads nicely into my third point

my third point on why warhammer total war is so amazing is the repeatability, even after several play throughs of the game i still feel as though i have more game play to enjoy, each faction having a unique play-style and units causes each new run to feel so fresh.

my final point is the DLC value, i haven't bought all the DLCs but the ones that i have add so much to the game, my personal favourite is the chaos dwarves because their artillery looks sick as well as the elite units being terrifying, the steampunk engineer vibe of the dwarves faction mixed with the blood lust rage of chaos makes the chaos dwarves look stunning.

Steam should create an award for the game devs that hate their customers the most, then CA would have a title that wins at least one award every year.

But just so this is somewhat of an actual review:

The game is fun. It's three games that have been built up on each other with apparently little long-term planning so its mechanics can be convoluted and poorly adapted to later additions (look up Wulfhart in IE), but despite that the years have allowed for many interesting changes and improvements to various faction mechanics. I have a ton of fun with this game most of the time because its scale, variety, and fantastic mod community make up for a lot of its shortcomings.

With that being said... CA HATES its fans. Or rather, they seem utterly indifferent to the needs of its customers once they've been parted from their money. 
They'll acknowledge a persistent and somewhat significant glitch, say they're working on it, then not mention it for 3+ months while spitting out another DLC instead of fixing it. Luckily someone discovered that you fan fix it by buying the Blood God DLC because why not spend money on something you don't want to have a product work as advertised. 
There's the fact that new DLC factions have smaller and smaller rosters while the DLC prices keep going up. 
There's the whole "the right to discuss is a privilege" thing. 
And today they removed version 4.1.4, the most recent version compatible with most mods, from the Steam rollback options so you have to play vanilla with their most recent patch, which was so well-made at launch that it needed two hotfixes in 3 weeks (and probably needs more).

So, while the game is a lot of fun I don't recommend it unless you
1) Want to be furious every 2-6 weeks because CA is doing their thing again, and
2) Want to play a game with an entertainment value that is dependent on how many hundreds of dollars you'd like to spend getting past the DLC paywalls

But if those things don't bother you, you'll probably really enjoy it.

Une review rapide pour dire que, tout comme les deux précédents, celui-ci est tout aussi bon, si ce n'est meilleur encore, grâce à une chose, la campagne Immortal Empires, regroupant dans une carte absolument gigantesque, les 3 maps des 3 opus. (ok légèrement échancrées, mais ça reste monstrueux). 

Plus de 20 factions, chacune avec au minimum 2 généraux, si ce n'est plus, des centaines d'unités, des lieux iconiques, et la possibilité de faire tout ça avec vos potes en coop, font que Total War Warhammer 3 est une absolue dinguerie. Le fruit d'un travail acharné d'une équipe de devs passionnés, qui ont mis plus de 10 ans, avant de réaliser ce rêve de gosse, mettre dans 1 seul grand jeu de stratégie, d'une des plus grandes franchises du genre de tous les temps, l'intégralité (ou presque) de l'univers de Games Workshop Warhammer. 
Tout vous mettra dans l'ambiance, la musique, les personnages, les petits dialogues. Vous deviendrez vite accro.
La politique de DLC peut faire rire jaune, mais souvent en solde, et petit à petit, vous verrez que cela n'est pas si difficile de vous construire cette collection. 
Qui plus est, les développeurs se sont excusés récemment des augmentations de leurs tarifs, malheureusement nécessaire pour la survie du studio, et de futures mises à jours devraient apporter encore d'avantage de contenu. 

Alors si vous aimez Total War, si vous aimez Warhammer, n'hésitez plus, ce jeu est le jeu ultime pour tout fan de la franchise.

Scummy DLC prices aside, this game's "Immortal Empires" mode is the best thing that ever happened to strategy games.

So I finally bit the bullet and got this despite the repeated frustrations of random ganking by allies in most total war games.

First off I have to say that the review bombing for the game not having Immortal Empires on release is pretty stupid. Nothing releases perfectly these days and a degree of patience is expected. Also, let's face it, IE is only a pat on the head for everyone that just got stuck to playing certain of the old factions so it's just "more of the same".
Secondly, it's easy to ignore the fact that there have been massive quality of life improvements with wh3. Going back and playing 2 again is an absolute snore fest by comparison not to mention that it is vastly inferior graphically. The prologue tutorial is fun and vastly superior to having to mess around with individual tutorials with an advisor blathering on about the most remedial rubbish from previous tw games. If you've ever played a single tw game of any kind you can either set advice to low or turn it off altogether.

For those worried about the crazy amount of dlc when you include those from 2 you needn't because they are ALL optional and not needed in any way shape or form outside of multiplayer. 
If you are on a budget then do yourself a favour and just get the base game and install Radious mods which add more to the game for free than any dlc.

Outside of the cool prologue what you have here is a more interesting new main campaign, more and far more delineated and interesting factions. Cathay is clearly the jewel in this new crown and they are great fun to play, Khorne are massively changed from the old beastmen, Demon Prince is powerful and fun and continues directly from the prologue and Chaos Dwarves, which have a completely different campaign to the others, works like a total conversion mod if you decide to get that particular dlc.

Throw in the fact that for those who actually WANT "more of the same" being able to use everything they bought previously through  Mortal Empires and you have a VAST overall improvement from 2.

Me gustaría dejar por aquí esta reseña positiva sobre este juego. Vengo hace tiempo jugando a las dos primeras partes y ahora por fin, he conseguido esta tercera. Sé que la política de DLC que es tan criticada no gusta a mucha gente, pero no entiendo cómo se asalta a críticas negativas por ese sentido. Cada creador es libre de establecer el precio de su trabajo, cada cliente es libre de comprar o no el producto. El mercado, es sencillo. Yo compro este juego y me encantan los Total War. No voy a entrar a valorar sus precios, eso es cosa de los creadores y de los trabajadores que han hecho posible esta obra. Si puedo compro y si no, pues no compro, vuelve a ser sencillo. Por eso, más allá de esta polémica hablaré del juego.

Total War es una franquicia que consigue situarte en un posición de gestión y control de una facción en un escenario. Estos escenarios se han hecho con los años de lo más variado posibles. Con especial mimo por la historia y cada vez más, ganando detalle. Las batallas son muy divertidas y emocionantes, con los años creo que van mejorando. Yo soy historiador y era reacio a pasar a este género de fantasía, pues me llama bastante la atención el cuidado que le da a este juego al trato por la inmersión histórica. Pero lo vuelven a conseguir, este juego es un espectáculo visual y una forma de liberar estrés y relajarse muy agradable. Para mi el juego es un 10 y aunque me surgen ideas magníficas sobre mejoras de la diplomacia y gestiones más profundas de personajes concretos, supongo que es muy fácil juzgar cuando te lo dan todo hecho.

Espero que disfruten de este juego y todas sus variantes. Además de que la compañía se esmera en perfeccionar incluso lo que ya está hecho. Mi única sugerencia es que sigan haciendo tan magnífico trabajo y yo pueda verlo y jugarlo. Los profesionales detrás de estas genialidades sabrán innovar y perfeccionar con el tiempo, insertando más períodos históricos y, porque no, también otras variantes como el mundo fantástico.

While the third game did have a failed launch, while it did stumble and fumble some features and changes it's overall the ultimate adaptation of the tabletop into a PC game possible. The game has all the issues that a CA TW game has but it's streamlined, fun to play and the detached nature from historical scenarios means it can introduce challenges, events and gameplay that couldn't be done in a historical title.

Cathay and Kislev are excellent additions, Cathay in particular is an amazing addition and has one of the best army rosters and gameplay of the entire trilogy. The Immortal empires map is spectacularly large (and with the expanded mod map even larger). The one issue is that the map has massive portions inaccessible in the middle of the map. The entire Indian subcontinent (or at least what is supposed to be it's analouge) is inaccessible along with what looks like japan, korea and one massive peninsula directly south of cathay. This is not a huge issue as it would be areas without unique factions but the featureless and inaccessible nature of these parts makes the map look blatantly unfinished. (aforementioned mod opens up these areas and populates them but without it looks very strange).

The modding scene is vibrant and custom factions, rosters and gameplay changes/additions can be found and the relatively decent mod support of the game makes it always feel like you can find something fresh and interesting to try out.

The overpriced DLC is very icky but like previous TW warhammer titles there's no need buy factions you don't wanna play since all DLC factions still show up as NPC factions with their full roster and lords etc.

The artstyle is imo a clear improvement over previous titles. The gloomy atmosphere of the first game was decent but felt overly serious for such a goofy setting, the second games jarring clash of old assets with a newer (better looking) style was kinda bad. The Third games map is a beautiful and vaguely cartoony style that fits *perfectly* with the tabletop and the miniatures the game is based on. They really in my opinion found the perfect fit in the third game for the visual tone of warhammer fantasy in general. 

Summary, decent strategy game and "map painter" game that is elevated by it's setting, art style and simplicity to something really quite great.

By buying the base game, you only get a fraction of the content, and then you'll need to purchase tons of overpriced DLCs, not to mention the previous Total War: Warhammer games, to unlock the majority of the factions. It's like buying a car, but the engine is extra.

I can't recommend the game in this condition. If you're really interested in the game, I'd recommend checking Allkeyshop and finding the lowest price for the trilogy package - this way, you'll get the most bang for your buck.

После 950 часов, могу однозначно порекомендовать игру.

Начну с минусов, которые игнорировать нельзя.

В РФ не купить. Я не из России, но это пидорское решение.

Стоимость ДЛЦ и самой игры выходит суммарно больше 200 долларов (и это я из Казахстана, где цены сильно ниже долларовых). Да, это контент за 9 лет существования игры, но немалое число этих дополнений не добавляют чего-то интересного или стоящего вашего времени, а значит и денег. Рекомендую покупать лишь то, что вам кажется интересным. Для остального есть бесплатный анлокер, ибо много какие ДЛЦ добавляют контент, который устарел морально и просто проигрывает по силе новым дополнениям.

Баланс игры – большой минус. Немало кампаний, механик и персонажей сильно хуже или сильно лучше своих аналогов внутри расы. Некоторые расы, как Цари Гробниц в целом сосут, так что проблема не некоторых неудачных или устаревших кампаний, она шире и глубже. И дело даже не в том, что кому-то больше нравится тот или иной опыт игры, или что разные механики вынуждают адаптироваться под особенности кампании. Дело в том, что какие-то лорды как Гром Пузо, Малакай Макайсон и Ракарт интереснее и веселее Скарсника, Белегара и Маллюса, потому что вам не нужно пол игры мучаться с дебафом или ограничивать себя в выборе юнитов, а Юан Боу имеет больше интерактивных механик, чем Мао Йинг и Жао Минг, у которых просто дженерик баффы к цифрам тут и там. От такого трогать даже палкой некоторые кампании не интересно, просто потому, что лучшую версию их контента уже успеваешь пощупать со всех сторон за другого персонажа. И, естественно, когда выходит какой-то новый лорд или фракция, они жутко пересилены, которых в последствии нерфят.

Немаленький кусок карты просто закрыт, потому что туда ещё не завезли контента, так что вам придётся с грустью оплывать эти земли, мечтая о том, что там могло бы быть.

Игра не очень стабильно работает до сих пор. Даже до того, как я погрузился в моды, периодически игра просто крашилась без ясной причины. Это проблема не только у меня, но и у ютуберов, так что советую почаще сохраняться. Просадки ФПС и мелкие подвисания тут встречаются часто.

Баги и поведение компьютера – последний крупный минус. Одна из причин, почему многие не любят играть карты осад – проблемы с навигацией юнитов по карте. Ваши войска будут то и дело застревать в дурацких местах, оказываться проходить через открытые ворота, вместо этого забираясь по лестницам на стену, от чего получают дебафф усталости. Иногда ваши войска могут отказаться стрелять, если вы им несколько раз не отдадите приказ, иногда одна моделька юнита может застрять в группе вражеских юнитов, и тогда вы не сможете увести юнит или нормально отдавать ему команды, иногда юниты в полёте зависают в воздухе и начинают лететь очень медленно на конкретном участке карты. Иногда юниты просто ломаются, как было с супер сквигами, которые взрывались, но почти не наносили урона. Это может не раз сыграть вам злую шутку, так что имейте это в виду.

Теперь к положительным чертам, которых много.

В игре очень много контента под любой вкус и хотелки. Хотите превратить мир в фабрику, притворяться эко-террористом, бегать и бездумно со всеми драться, погрузить мир в хаос, отомстить всем на свете, погрузить мир в хаос или показать всему миру силу человеческого духа? Всё это сделать можно и всё это делать по-своему весело.

Игра красивая. Это субъективщина, но мне нравится смотреть на разные происходящие на ней мелочи, на то, как выглядят многие города (пускай некоторые из них и не дотягивают до своего лорного статуса). Можно было бы придраться к отсутствию смены сезонов, но я не буду, потому что игра и так весит 100 гигабайт.

У игры потрясающее сообщество мододелов, и сама игра работает с мастерской Стима, так что вам не придётся париться с их установкой от слова совсем. Даже несколько крупных модов, переворачивающих игру с ног на голову, ставятся в 1 клик и активируются через лаунчер игры, потому что они постарались и сделали вкладку с модами, где вы можете увидеть, что обновлено до последней версии игры, что у вас включено и в каком порядке загрузки стоят моды.

Геймплейный цикл можно ближе всего подвести к Факторио. Тут ещё немного, и вы улучшите все постройки в провинции, там ещё немного, и вы добьёте противника, ещё чуть дальше, и вы сможете установить аванпост, откуда будете вторгаться в другие регионы или даже на материки. Потом вы заканчиваете ход, и это желание сделать ещё одну мелочь напоследок легко засосёт вас ещё на полчаса, потому что вы продвинулись тут, и там, оставлять на пол пути что-то интересное не охота. 

В завершение обзора скажу, что советую всем кампании Икита Клешни и Дражоата Пепельного, когда разберётесь в механиках игры. За Икита кампания очень весёлая, а за Дражоата просто лучший скейлинг в лейте в сравнении с другими лордами чорфов, за которых кампании одни из самых разнообразных и сложных в плане ресурс менеджмента. Ну а если вы хотите просто всем поднасрать, берите Чейнжлинка и пакостите всему миру, совершая перекаты.

I'm a casual Gamer and although I previously owned some Warhammer 40k (when I was younger) my lore of the world isn't the greatest. 

CAMPAIGNS - That being said I have learned alot about the different races through the campaigns and prologues as the story telling is amazing. There is the ability to chose what kind of game you want at the start with the different campaign choices. The campaigns do limit you to certain races but that's to fit in with the story. 
Realms of Chaos - I find the realms of chaos campaign fun with the chaos it creates but going to the chaos realms is not to my liking. The idea is great fun but I find it to be a massive drain on time to move slightly towards a gate knowing you have to go towards a battle... waiting... and have a battle then next turn get to the gate... then wait... go through the gate wait... battle... and so on. Personally that takes the fun out of it for me as it feel less fluid with the pace of the rest of the game. I love the fact that in one of the realms you have the choice to gain great rewards but it stops you from closing the realm off. Perfect love it.  
The Lost God - I played this so long ago that my memory of it isn't the greatest. The fact it is to help newer players gain a taste of how the mechanics work is an amazing introduction. I remember the story but I'll leave that to you to explore for your own.
Immortal Empires - This is where I live. A sandbox campaign allowing you to choose a wide range or factions... even more if you buy one of the many... many DLCs. The different ways that each race is set up and plays makes this game highly replayable with the ability to change tactics. For instance you can play as the orcs and dominate lands by multiplying insanely quickly for a certain duration. Whereas a tactic I'm exploring in my current play through is as the vampires and going for a more diplomatic domination. Creating trades, giving gifts, setting up alliances, whilst destroying smaller factions that take issue with the alliances I make.

BATTLES - There are historical battles and skirmishes which you can do without starting a campaign. If you don't feel like playing for a long period you can jump start into the action. I'm less about this mode as I prefer to build up towns, my economy and army so the battles have more meaning to the outcome. But it's a great feature to have.

GAMEPLAY - I love the units and fighting tactics for this game. There is nothing more satisfying then zooming in to watch your hero destroy and fling your enemies around the battlefield. Trolls pick up soldiers and eat them. It's amazing! After playing for 300+ hours You do get a hold of how the AI works with armies coming at you but this doesn't make me want to play the game any less as I see this more as I'm a veteran commander who has studied his foes. 

Personal Overall View- I love playing this game I could write more about the campaign movement and buildings etc. but I thought with this review I'd give you a basic low down of what there is to do  and a little on gameplay. If you are thinking of if you should get this game I would say HELL YES. 
Still unsure? I would suggest reading other reviews on here and watch youtube walkthroughs to see if it is for you.

After 1k+ hours in WH2 I can say I enjoy this game with only 200+ now. There are some frustrations but also some highlights. For clarity, I play only Immortal Empires - to me that is *THE* TW:WH experience. The map is absolutely gigantic. I came close to a total takeover a single time as Tirion, but got swamped with work and ended up taking too long before the next major patch cycle came. That alone was 70+ hours of gameplay and I still had 1/4 of the map to take over, granted I could have went crazier with raising more armies to sprawl quicker. That said, the magic is fulfilling, the thrill from all total wars of watching your archer volley crash into unarmored flanks still sings and of course.... IRONDRAKESSSSS! The multiplayer being 8 players now is wonderful even with the lag because we just want to play the game together.

As a single player game, you can spend hundreds of hours but once you find *that faction* you only ever want to play them and for me it's the dwarves. They feel just as powerful and Thorek being in the Thunderdome this go around makes it hilarious to get into the battle. The Dawi remain supreme - but making Grombrindal's campaign a slog along the northern shelf is upsetting after fighting the green tide in 2. Nice to get to duke it out with the Dark Elves after the Betrayal, but still liked that being a quest battle more than trudging through the ice. Thorgrim gets lots of love and has many options which fits the High King, and once your economy explodes you simply cannot be stopped as the forges hiss with fresh engines of war and we bring the fire to the fields. The updated Oathgold shop also has way more options and it's always nice to know I can full deck all my newer officers once I've reached a certain point - something I sorely miss when playing the other goodly races.

All in all, I do like the game, I wish the multiplayer servers had less lag especially as of late I've tried 15 different campaigns and all of them are laggy on the campaign map and battle maps. Despite that, I continue to love and play this game. 

Just make DLC's more reasonably priced and give us some more dwarven factions please.

The Realms of Chaos campaign is nothing to write home about. It's an okay campaign but the time pressure - and the pressure to keep your settlement count small - is very different from most Total War campaigns. I respect them for trying something different though.

The Immortal Empires campaign, however, is the culmination of almost a decade of work by Creative Assembly to build a version of this world that everyone loved so much on tabletop and in roleplaying games. It is a gigantic, sprawling campaign map where you could very easily replay every faction - even those from previous games - and get a different experience given the new Crisis system and the new areas of the map making the defensible indefensible.  You could very easily play twenty campaigns with each their own twenty hours of play and still not yet be done.

They stumbled with Shadows of Change, initially overcharging for the DLC. But they course-corrected very quickly and you have to hand the response to them. I very much look forward to Thrones of Decay and the next hopefully two to three years of content that CA has for us for Total War Warhammer 3.

'토탈워 : 워해머' 라는 하나의 장르이자 주제이며, 여러 종족들이나 기존 설정집이 존재하는 게임이라는 한계를 벗어나지 못하는 'DLC와 본편 게임의 가격' 과 '반복적인 전투, 효율적인 로스터, DLC도 창작마당에서 유저들이 올린 것보다 못한 퀄리티'를 보이기 시작하면서 이 게임은 추천할 수 없는 게임이 되었다.

2024년 4월 말에 나올것으로 추정되는 '부패의 왕좌' 새로운 DLC이자 현재 워해머 세계관의 마지막 부활의 신호탄이라고 불리는 이 DLC의 문제점은 '유저가 창작해내는 모드의 퀄리티와 유사하다.'라는 부분이다.

무료인 '창작마당의 모드'와 유료인 'DLC'의 구현하는 정도가 비슷하다면 굳이 돈을 내고 구매할 이유가 있는가?
무수히 많은 모드들이 나오면서 없던 종족도 만들어내고 있던 종족은 상향시키고 새로운 병종, 시스템, 플레이 방향까지 '창작마당'이 해결하는 마당에 아직도 정신나간 가격이 될 'DLC'와 '타 종족에 있는 유닛 색칠놀이' 를 유저들에게 제공하는 정당한 '개발사의 제공거리'라기엔 그 값을 바탕으로 구매를 할 이유가 없다.

이번에 새롭게 제공될 DLC의 메인 팩션이 '제국, 드워프, 너글'로 방향성이 정해진 건 확실한데 DLC의 매력은 '새로운 유닛 병종의 추가'와 '전설적인 군주의 등장'이라기엔 시스템 전체를 갈아엎고 새로운 메타나 플레이 방식에 영향을 끼칠 정도의 DLC가 아니라면 워해머 토탈워는 절대로 살아날 수 없다.

10만원 이상 주고 토탈워 시리즈의 특유의 전략 전술과 부대 단위의 전쟁을 지휘하고 싶다는 이유가 아니라면, 절대적으로 추천할 수 없는 게임이다.

The biggest downside of Total War: WARHAMMER III has always been Creative Assembly itself.

CA still deserves plenty of criticism for its management, communication, and the way it has handled this game over the years. A few recent improvements cannot simply erase years of poor decisions and wasted potential.

That said, I have felt a genuine change since Hyenas was cancelled and SEGA stepped in. CA’s handling of Total War has gradually become more focused, more responsive, and more willing to listen to its players.

Now, with the End Times Update approaching, it finally feels as though that change may be leading somewhere meaningful.

For all its flaws, Total War remains almost impossible to replace. No other series offers quite the same combination of grand strategy, massive real-time battles, and the sheer scale of the Warhammer world.

So yes, I will continue to criticize CA when it deserves it. But criticism does not mean that I want it to fail. I want CA to learn from its mistakes, I want WARHAMMER III to finish strong, and I hope the End Times Update proves that CA can still do right by both this game and the players who have kept supporting it.

This game is incredible. A definitive addition for the armchair general's library. TWWIII is a great game to play single player or multiplayer. For those looking to go hard on the EXTERMINATE side of 4x, this is a great entry into Grand Strategy. 
Whether you're a fan of Warhammer Fantasy (WF) or classical fantasy like LOTR, you'll find a faction here that tickles your fancy. Even 40k fans will enjoy pointing out all the similarities between 40k factions and their WF counterparts. My personal favourites are Norsca (Fantasy Vikings/Space Wolves), Khorne, Nurgle, Chaos Dwarves (Evil Dwarfs/Dark Mechanicum/Iron Warriors), Dwarfs ("YOU KNOW WHO I AM"), Wild Elves (Lothlórien Elves/ Wood Elves/ Ents), Vampire Pirates (Pirate Zombies with canons). 

With the recent turn with CA, things seem to be improving as far as DLC pricing goes. With that in mind, be prepared to treat this like a Paradox game. I hope that they'll chop up Shadows of Change as they will be doing with Thrones of Decay. I'm excited to see what else CA has planned for the game.

Oh, did I mention mods? Oh hell yeah! Where CA currently is working to hone in on major changes to the game, the mod community is absolutely incredible and filling gaps with minor changes and overhauls. Doing things like completing the Immortal Empires Map (which is already impressively enormous) with the Immortal Empires Expanded Mod. But also for adding entirely new and fantastic factions like the Fimir and Jade Sea Pirates. Many mods change the game entirely too, maybe you've heard of the Grimhammer mods that add greater asynchronous balance between factions? Or, maybe you're a Radious Mod fan that adds more sameness between factions and lets you sit back and handle more macro than the tactical map's micro turning the game into more of something similar to Dominions. If those two mods establish the range of what's possible with mods, I can't wait to see what else is coming in the future.

I used to be tentative in the recommendation because of the DLC pricing model but it's hard to fault a game this good for what is really just the Devs wanting to continue to be able to fund the project. Can't fault them for wanting compensation for their incredible work.

First off, let me say that everyone has a right to their opinion. I am not here to say whether or not this game is right for anyone else as we are all in different life situations. It is, after all, a thing to do in our free time. Something to get our mind off of life for a while. So below is just "my" opinion on how I see this game. Hopefully it helps those who read it (along with any other reviews listed here) to come to their own conclusion. With all that being said, here are my thoughts..

I have been a fan of Games workshop(GW) since the 80's. If you are familiar with the company, then you know they're not cheap. But their commitment to quality models has been stead fast, and my "pile of shame" grows ever larger. This statement shows that I am vested in this hobby and the lore. I don't believe every video game they have released has been great, far from it in fact. BUT Total War: Warhammer I, II, III is truly an amazing game! I have also been a big fan of the total war series since the original Shogun. I bought just about every game in the series and have spent hundreds hours playing them. So when I heard these two companies were coming together, it was a sure thing for me! Below are the hours I have spent on each game and to be honest I'm surprised they are as low as they are.

TWW I - 751 hours*
TWW II - 3016 hours*
TWW III - 1044 hours*

*at time of this posting

This is a MASSIVE game that includes a least 24 races(not counting rogue armies or mods) with hopefully more to come. Within those races there are multiple factions, each with their own unique play style and goals. I'm pretty sure Creative Assembly(CA) & GW plan on reaching 100 faction leaders! This itself creates an incredible amount of replay ability. Now not all of them you may like, but with such variety, there's something in here for everyone's taste and play style. CA has done an epic job bringing all this together in one massive "immortal empires map". They game can be played as a giant sandbox but GW has so much rich lore that there is a story to follow as well. DLCs were also released with certain factions leaders squaring off with each other which helps with the immersion. The environments in this world are rich and ever expanding with the possibility of Ind, Kuresh, & Nippon opening up in the future. And if that wasn't enough, the AMAZING modding community has such mods as "Dynamic World" to enrich it more.

As far as game play, as mentioned above, I was very familiar with Total War game mechanics. So it was very easy to jump right in. For those of you that haven't played any of the series before(whats wrong with you?? jk jk), it may take a little getting use to, but in "my opinion" it is very intuitive on how it works. There are so many reviews on this page that I wont get into everything here but if you are interested I'm sure you can find another review that goes into it in more detail.

Now, to address the elephant in the room: the cost.. By now I have said enough about myself that you can tell price isn't a wall for me if I love the product. I can spend WAY more going out these days for this many hours of entertainment (listed above) then what this game has costed me. 

$237.00* / 4811 series hours played = $0.05 per hr

*Price of all available TWW I, II & III content, 10% off (not including Thrones of Decay)

I'm sure my math may be off a little but even if it was 10x that amount its worth every cent. And the more I play, the more value I get from it. My suggestion is to wait for a sale and start small. A large part of the player base plays Empire but do your research to see which race sounds most interesting to you. You will need to buy one of the base games to start with and with "Thrones of Decay"(ToD) release right around the corner, all of the base and DLCs will be on sale (good time to jump in!) I've seen the base game I & II up to 50% off in the past. But don't feel pressured to buy all the content at once. For those of you still on the fence, remember steam has that return window policy if you don't like it within the first few days.

If I have any complaint about the game, its the series has been so good that I have had trouble playing any of the old Total War historic games since due to the lack of variety in the factions/game play. I remember this being a worry from the Total War historic community before its release and now I see why. Yes, there are some bugs in the game but none of them are game breaking. Most of the time I didnt even notice them until I read the hot fixes. We need to remember few games have ever been this massive before and with all the new content these things can take time. You tube content creators, such as Great Book of Grudges, and the player base are always sure the devs are made aware of these so they are fixed. Maybe not as fast as they would like but again I barely notice them. 

I will make this part quick.. You may have heard the recent drama over the "Shadows of Change"(SoC) DLC and all the negativity along with it. I will say the player base stood up for what they felt was right, and I "believe" CA finally got the message. The extra content added to SoC DLC and the previews for ToD are looking like a move in the right direction to make the game community supportive again. But only time will tell.

So in conclusion I want to again say this is only "my opinion". I am not saying anyone complaining this game is to expensive for them is wrong. What I am saying is that I am willing to pay developers that will bring high level of entertainment and will continue to support them so it keeps coming out. Yes, we should make sure we are keeping the developers honest and the quality of product they are releasing is held at a high standard. But in a respectful and productive way. Thanks for reading and I hope to see you in game! =)

A very solid game in its current state, and the upcoming DLC looks promising.

Even though you need to buy the previous games and DLCs for the full(er) experience, even with just buying Total War: Warhammer III you can enjoy the game for the value you paid. Although you cannot play as the previous games' and DLCs' factions without purchasing those, you can still interact and fight against them with the starting races (Kislev, Cathay, Nurgle, Slaanesh, Khorne and Tzeentch + Be'lakor (Warriors of Chaos) in Immortal Empires).

It is very important to highlight, the Immortal Empires campaign combining the content of all three games is playable for owners of only Warhammer III as well.

The game is receiving FLC content and reworks with time, alongside the DLCs, so you are still receiving some new content if you are paying for the new DLCs or not.

Although the Warscape battle engine is always somewhat struggling in some way or form, it is rather polished, functional and enjoyable for the scope included in the Total War: Warhammer series.

The campaigns are quite enjoyable, with some exceptions, notably the late game feels rather dull and limiting in comparison to the earlier stages of campaigns because of the climate system and lack of a meaningful challenge. Scripted hostile armies spawning in completely secured territory through end game scenarios is not an enjoyable late game challenge.

With all this said, especially if you also buy the other games or DLCs you are interested in, you will have a blast in the first 100 or so turns of most of your campaigns.

From the campaigns I've played, I especially recommend playing as Katrin (Kislev) and Wulfrik the Wanderer (Norsca - paid DLC from the first game) in the Immortal Empires campaign, and I'm looking forward to a Karl Franz (Empire) campaign in the upcoming 5.0 version of the game. The Realms of Chaos campaign is not bad by any means, but the Immortal Empires campaign offers a more clean and varied fun experience.

As a conclusion, I recommend this game and I hope it will continue to receive support and new content in the years to come.

Total War: Warhammer III is (mostly) a fulfilment of a dream fantasy/strategy RTS.

I have no complaints whatsoever with the gameplay of Warhammer III. The immortal empires game mode is incredibly impressive, and though some of the older factions have archaic or seemingly unnecessary mechanics, on the whole the game offers a multitude of enjoyable ways to play. The graphics are similarly excellent, with my only complaint being the slightly, (if thematically), drab areas where chaos reigns. 

The campaign is decent. It serves as an okay tutorial to the mechanics, but really, I think most of your time will be spent in Immortal Empires. This does however bring me to my major complaint, which is the cost of all the DLCs. If you are a returning player, great! All your old factions will work in immortal empires. If not, you will need to buy several dlc packs or full games to experience anything beyond the few base-game empires. The developers have done a fair bit to make up for recent pricing mistakes, and I do commend them for this, but know that getting into Warhammer III can be an expensive endeavor, even on sale.

Overall, an enjoyable game worth playing, but be aware that large swathes of the game's 80 factions will require dlcs to play.

TWWAR3 Isn't a bad game over-all and it's worth the buy.  But I personally don't think it's as good as TWWAR2.  As I found 2 just way more fun than 3.  In CA's attempt to "re-balance" all the old races and older game mechanics, the game to me has become annoying at times to play.

Sieges as an attacker are a MAJOR headache & are frustrating now - path finding still bad, the supply system sucks and the computer AI in defense is mega annoying.  
   CA's response was to just eliminate siege battles from minor cities, rather than work to fix the issue.

Now although I do like the climate system for cities for each race, I don't really like how it's done.  Other than the chaos wastes, magic forests, and ocean climates which should always be unique, the other climates I feel each race can spend gold or build something to adapt the climate to a green suitable climate.  I feel every race should be able to go anywhere they want on the map to colonize/conquer.  With the system now, for a race to settle in a "red" climate city is NOT worth it or cost effective (for the most part).

Cities take FOREVER to build to max level - turn 100's you are running around with a 30+ lvl chars, but only now your cities are level 5.  And truly the big bonuses you gain from the lvl 5 unique buildings aren't really all that helpful to you at this point as you usually have around 40-50 settlements at this point.  So this needs fixing.  My suggestion is that all races growth buildings be doubled the amount given.

Replenishment percentages needs to be upped for certain races (the ones that can't replenish any after battles).  I spend WAY too much time having my characters sitting in cities picking their noses waiting for their armies to be ready to fight again.  When the computer players can have 3x more armies & heroes than you can, the player needs to replenish their armies faster to stand a fair chance.

Supply line mechanic needs major fixing or elimination.  The computer players don't have it and seeing how they ALWAYS are able to have way more armies than the player, how is this a fair system?

Army upkeep now is unfair now that your cities produce 50% less money than in TWWAR2.  You guys in CA truly don't understand how to balance things correctly.
---Normal difficulty level...  Now I understand if people wish to give themselves more of a challenge and they up the difficulty, so THEN cities make less money, army upkeep & supply lines all increased.  OKAY I get that.  But us other people who just play the game for some relaxing fun, things need to be fixed.

Personally I don't know why so many changes have been made to the game mechanics from WAR2 - some I understand, yes.  But most of the system should of just been carried over from 2.  I mean WAR2 has an 90% on steam and WAR3 has what, 70%?  You guys at CA ever wondered why?

Need new, fresh ideas, then how about asking the community OR hiring some modders to address and fix these serious balancing issues.  

My final verdict, the game is a solid 75% with the mods I've installed.   65% without mods.

J'ai installé 150 mods, l'idée est de retrouvé dans mon jeux pas mal d'unités existantes dans le monde de warhammer fantasy mais qui ne sont pas dans le jeu.

Pour que le jeux reste balancé, j'ai variés les mods pour chaque race, pas de mod de cheat ou qui boost l'economie ou bien qui augmentent le systeme de recrutement ou la taille des villes.

Tout changement de la mécanique de gestion du jeu risque de privilégié certaines factions et de rendre obselete d'autres, pareil pour les mod qui  agrandissent la taille des unités si ceux ci ne sont pas adapté au niveaux de la regeneration des unités, cela change completement la mécanique du jeu et peu désavantager pas mal de faction.
Il existe un tas d'overhaul qui rajoute du contenus mais ne change pas le systeme de gestion du jeu.

J'avais adoré les mod radious que l'on retrouvera sur casi tous les totalwar, par contre pas du tout SFO, ce sont deux overhaul majeur qui compilé avec d'autre mod necessite toujours des mod de compatibilité suplementaire pour tout autre modd utilisé, les deux ne sont pas compatible enssemble et souvent incompatible avec la majorité des overhaul existant, souvent même avec les mod de compatibilité le jeu crash, un autre probleme recurant avec ces deux mod , est que à chaque mise à jour du jeu, les createur mettent une eternité pour mettre leur jeu à jour, ce qui fait que l'ont ne peu plus jouer à nos parties en cours durant une longue periode, autant j'ai adoré radious dans ses debuts, la je ne les recommande plus, la compilation de mes 135 mod sont plus riche en contenu que radious et sfo.

Pour les faire fonctionnés les 150 mod sans crash je les ai testé un par un et ensuite je les ai rangé organisé dans le luncher par priorité..


Petite introduction pour les joueurs qui desirent jouer avec des mod existant que l'ont trouvent sur le workshop de steam:
 
les ordres de classement que j'ai effectué sont:

- mod organiser et mixus en premier, ensuite mixer audio
-les mod pour empecher l'ai de cheater ensuite
-les modd graphique et apres les extensions pour map
-les overhaul
-les mod campaign
-les mod d'unités
-les mod d'unités de renom et les mod extended booster

laissé des mod actif lors du lancement du jeu ne vous permettra de joué au campagne en multijoueur que si les autres joueurs ont les même mods, je recomande de désactivé les mod graphique pour les partie multi, histoire de rendre le jeu moins lourd.

Prenez la peine de lire le descriptif de vos choix de modd, pour eviter d'avoir des conflicts.

Les overhaul sont les plus senssibles au doublons, evité d'en prendrent qui ont des changements sur des même type de fonction , verifié si vos overhaul changent le graphisme des unité ou s'ils ont un graphisme particulier qui pourrais entré en conflits avec des choix de mod graphic.

Les mod campaign peuvent avoir le même probleme lors d'ajout de mod campaign qui crée de nouvelle faction, vérifié que le mod choisit ne va pas interferer avec une faction que vous allez jouer ou avec d'autre faction ajoutée, j'ai constaté moins de probleme avec ce type de mod

Les mod unités sont aussi à vérifié avec de les activé, pour exemple radious et sfp pour ne cité qu'eux (d'autres mod overhaul ou campaign peuvent aussi etre concerné) on leurs propres graphismes et statistiques d'untité, évité les doublons...

beaucoup de mod vont ralentir votre jeu au téléchargement et lors des passage de tours de jeu, vérifié d'avoir une machine assez puissante pour pouvoir les faire tourner.

Pour exemple ma machine actuelle, à un processeur i7 13e generation 8 coeurs cadencé à 4.6 ghz; 32 giga de ram, un carte nvidia rtx 2070 ti super 8 giga et le jeu est installé sur un ssd, avec autant de mod j'ai constaté le ralentissement des fin de tour, mais le plus important, les mod fonctionne enssemble et le jeu ne crash pas et je peu poussé le graphisme hormis les ombres et les details fx pour avoir un fps decent.

In Warhammer 3 many fantasy factions clash with one another in an unending show of blood, gore (avallible with DLC, let's not forget that) and tactical master-planning. 

So, let's take that sentence above and apply a bit of critical thinking to each part of it.

It's a 3rd iteration of Warhammer series made by Creative Assembly, so it should be the most polished one, since it's building itself on the tops of giants that were WH1 & 2 + their respective DLC and FreeLC. Easily above 10 DLCs were made for previous iterations of this game. And you know what? Many, many aspects of the game are still broken. Siege battles, units AI's and less often but still, clunkiness of some animations are the most things that currently are in this game. Is it game-breaking? No. Does it make the game less fun? Sometimes, because it can make for the experience to be frustrating.

Now, "many fantasy factions" includes abberations of human condition such as germans, the french, the chinease, fantasy confederated states of america disguised as elves, and manlets, or excuse me, "short kings" as they are called nowdays. And those are not even the weird part. There's undead arabs obsessed with afterlife, rat people, who are just another allegory for asian cultures, or badass texan manlets. There's also facist elves and orks, so your fantasy bread and butter. Sadly, almost for all of them you'd need to spend additional money in order to buy the DLC's that they are included in. Thankfully, there's a couply of sites that helps you finding the best deals. I usually use allkeyshop in order to find those.

Now is the part in which i criticize the fact that they monetised spirit of a franchise when they put the blood and gore dlc under the 5$ dlc. 
I did not liked it.

And here's something about tactics in this game.
1. The best unit in the game is a sister of avelon - a stack (propably all lesbian, but it might be my fantasy) of around 60 woman who shoots magical arrows that pierce anything they contact with.
2. The best Legendary Lord to start is - just like in real life - highly debatable. But if you want to have 2 clear choices i present those two:
- Tyrion - he's a high elven king-general (not the highest king, mind you, he's not in-game as a lord), and HE are the ones to get acces to the sisters of avelon. Also his faction presents the best experience for order faction in Warhammer, without useless confusing mechanics or over-developed economy.
- Be'lakor - he's a first Deamon Lord, he is able to annihilate enemy armies alone, even in Multiplayer. Also his mechanics are extremly friendly and forgiving.
3. Contrary to some opinions on the internet, this game is not a battlefield simulation. Nor does it presents any sort of intellectual challange besides this: How quick can you click right units in a right time. Everything past that is just meaningless overintelectualisation of a really simple basis, But that basis is extremly enjoyable. And it allows you to play the game how you want it to be played in the first place.
You want to Roleplay 16th cent army with an acces to flying units? Play the Empire
You want to play 20th cent army with an acces to flying units? Play the Chaos Dwarfs
You want to stick in one corner of the map and slowly learn ins-and-outs of when click which unit on which unit of an enemy? Play the standard dwarfes
You want to show your friends how fast you can click? Play the rat-mans
You want to minimise the clicking part to the bare minimum and play League of Legends simulator in WH setting instead? Play Be'lakor or Archeon.
You want to annihilate enemy army with one spell? SIKE! That's actually a feture for every faction!

Why is this game good? Because it allows you to play it how you want. And there are hundreds of variables of what and how you can play, even within the same faction.

В першу чергу ви можете спокійно дочекатись знижок і взяти базову гру приблизно за 250-300 гривень. Цього контенту вам вистачить на більш ніж 500 годин. І це якщо ви ще не будете перегравати одні і ті ж самі кампанії. Навіть базових лордів в грі буде десь 12 штук. А якщо ви візьмете на знижках ще 1 і 2 частину, то там будуть доступні майже усі фракції і більшість лордів. Там контенту на декілька тисяч годин.

По-друге відповім на запитання "Чи коштують ДЛЦ своїх грошей, або ж базовий мінімум є достантнім для комфортної гри?".
Так, коштують своїх грошей, але не всі. До того ж на гру дуже часто знижки по 50-75%, а то й на всі 90%. Але якщо ви вже й настільки бімж, то ці длц можна зламати через деякі програми. Називати не буду які, але за 10 секунд пошуку в гуглі ви все знайдете. 
Гра з усіма ДЛЦ в базовій версії коштує щось на кшталт 13к грн. Чи багато це ? Звісно. Але от чи занадто це для такої кількості контенту ? Я вважаю що це доволі виправдана ціна. Є деякі сумнівні рішення розробника на кшталт ДЛЦ на кров, або ж очевидно необхідні базовому лордові юніти закриті за певними ДЛЦ. Але я вважаю що вархаммер це в першу чергу про офігенські маштабні битви і про тактику, а не про "та без цього юніта весь стак гімно". Стак може і гімно, але тільки для змагального мультиплєру, а ви в нього перші годин 500 точно не будете лізти.

Я награв 700 годин, закрив всі фракції на високій, або на легендарній важкості і все ще не спробував й третини всього контенту. Багато де я тупо рашив на чіз механіках, бо хотів позакривати ачівки. Про яку "недостачу контенту" за свою ціну тут дякі взагалі пишуть. Ви взагалі бачили ціну "безкоштовної" гри Сімс ?

Відгук на саму гру писати не бачу сенсу. Вона шикарна, або як кажуть деякі "Аналогов нєт". До людей які пишуть про якісь там проблеми балансу, або особисті враження, я претнзій не маю абсолтно ніяких. Все ж таки це просто справа смаку. Висновок наступний: починаєте з базової версії на знижках, якщо подобається докупляєте перші дві частини і забираєт безкоштовні ДЛЦ для ельфів та бретонії, якщо і тоді не награлись, то докупляєте на наступних знижках інші фракції. Брати нові ДЛЦ для нового гравця сенсу немає ніякого.

[h1]《全面战争：战锤3》：在西方魔幻世界和“万”族作战是什么体验[/h1]

封狼居胥、饮马瀚海、勒石燕然，这可是多少人心中的狂热和悸动，如今现实和平安康的大好局势难以实现封侯拜相，那么在游戏里征战沙场、攻城掠地、一统天下，何尝不是一种新的形式来实现自己这无处施展的开疆扩土之抱负。《全面战争：战锤3》作为一款以西方魔幻题材为主题的大战略游戏，某种程度上确实能够让玩家感受到攻城掠地的战争体验， “万”族林立，“百”国并存，以一己之力，率领玩家铁骑，打下大大的疆土，击败所有的势力，一统这片战锤世界。 

[h1]兵者，诡道也[/h1]

由于这款游戏的战争采用的即时战略的攻防模式，玩家作为上帝视角，即时的指挥自家的军队在战场中战斗，参与战斗部队多，地形开阔面积广，战场局势变化快。因此，在游戏间歇，玩家完全可以去了解一番以《孙子兵法》为首的中国兵书，熟悉一下一场战争应该怎么打。老祖宗传下来千年的行军用兵之道，可不是盖的，完全能够应用在这款游戏之中。

势力之间，只有永远的利益，没有永远的敌人。对外政策，远交近攻，稳扎稳打，先蚕食再鲸吞。必争之地，要如何争，是资源富裕的补给之地，还是九省通衢的交通要塞，或者是抵御外地的防御关隘。兵种搭配，如何选，是单一兵种的莽穿敌人，还是步兵、骑兵、弓兵等多协同作战。攻城之前，围城、强攻二选一，攻心为上还是攻城为上，心战为上还是兵战为上。战场之上，局势变化莫测，更是让玩家成为一个个指挥作战的微操小能手，地形优劣要如何利用，手中部队要如何排兵布阵，兵种克制要如何对阵，敌方士气要如何哒灭，如何打赢包围和包围、突袭和反突袭、支援和反支援等等，全靠玩家自己熟读兵法用于实践。总结，兵者，诡道也，只要能赢，管他用的什么方法，可不是胜者为王败者为寇。

[h1]战争，烧的是钱，要的是资源[/h1]

战争打的是什么，打的是经济，打的是工业制造业。为了维持玩家征战四方的雄图霸略，玩家的后勤补给是断不可能匮乏，后勤断了，那就是要了“第四天灾”玩家这条“战争狂人”的命根子。重军事而不重经济，其结果就会像汉朝那般，“国恒以弱灭，而汉独以强亡”的存在。游戏中，玩家攻城掠地之后，这些城市便是用以提供金钱等各类消耗补给。因此，玩家占领之后，是需要苦心经营的。当然，也可以选择烧杀掠夺甚至是更严重的完全摧毁城池，但是这毕竟只是杀鸡取卵，不利于后期发展，内政系统势在必行。游戏里，采用《文明6》一类的回合制，在一个回合中，玩家完成城镇建设、科技学习、招兵买马、部队行军等操作行动（其他势力在玩家结束本回合后由AI自发行动），这些行动的目的就是稳住已经占有的疆土城镇，不断发展它们，源源不断的为玩家补充更多的资源和兵力，保证玩家前线战场无压力。

实际上，整个游戏的流程，基本就是一个“发展-战争-稳定-发展-战争”这么一个循环过程，但是玩家始终需要记住，打江山易守江山难，毕竟敌人也不是麻瓜，按部就班的等着你来进攻，他们也会进行各种各样的偷袭、攻击、结盟等战略行动的。而且很多地理位置的环境，可能并不适合玩家当前种族生活，需要对其进行改造，但是改造花费时间长、消耗多、敌人不断骚扰等情况。玩家实在守不住，那就毁城吧，毕竟留着给敌人提供补给，不如自己狠狠地、无情地劫掠一波，然后留给敌人一片废土，虽然有些不人道，但是战争不就是这么剧情。

[h1]最后[/h1]

游戏给予玩家的爽点，其实就在于开疆扩土的满足感、奴役万族征服感、万国来朝的自豪感、征战沙场的热血感以及指挥大型战争的成就感，这一切都让“野心勃勃”的玩家感到爽快和愉悦。但是，本作有一点极其让玩家难受的是，游戏任何加载页面的等待时间都很久，每一场战斗开始需要加载一次，结束需要加载一次，这个时间很漫长，玩家迫不及待的战争渴望犹如硬生生的被一盆冷水泼灭，憋屈滴很。不过，游戏某些问题很突出，但是不可否认这款西幻题材的大战略游戏，确实在杀时间的过程中，让玩家感受到了征途霸略的快乐，如果游戏本体和DLC能够便宜一些，绝对值得的。

長めのロード時間は欠点ではありますが、それはゲームの仕様上致し方ないことだと思いますし、その分、戦闘中やキャンペーン中には、途切れることなくとても快適にプレイ出来ています。
もちろん、今後もシリーズ新作やアップデートで、どんどんロード時間が短くなってくれることを期待しますが、個人的にはロード時間は許容範囲内です。
以下、いくつか好きな点や不満点を書いておきます。

【好きな点】
１．細部まで作り込まれた大規模戦闘
　　このゲーム最大の魅力は、やはり戦場での大規模戦闘だと思います。
　　戦場マップや各ユニットは美麗で、細部まで丁寧に作り込まれており、本当に感動するレベルで素晴らしいと思いました。
　　各ユニットには様々な種族、種類があり、それぞれが待機中、戦闘中にも多彩なアニメーションで動いてくれるので、見ていて楽しく、戦闘の没入感を上げてくれます。
　　戦闘の仕組みや操作に若干の慣れは要るものの、シリーズを重ねてきただけあって洗練されており、UIや説明もわかりやすく、とても楽しいです。

２．親切でわかりやすく、ボリューム満点なチュートリアル
　　チュートリアルだけで１つのシナリオが楽しめる作りになっています。
　　また、やれること、やるべきことを段階的に増やしていってくれるので、操作を一つずつ覚えていくことができ、かなり充実したチュートリアルだと思います。
　　チュートリアルのストーリーも個人的に好みなものだったので、WARHAMMERの世界は初めてでしたが、このチュートリアルでWARHAMMERの世界観にがっつり没入できました。
　　ゲームを始める前には、本編開始勢力はキャセイとかを考えていたのですが、あまりにもチュートリアルの出来が良かったので、開始勢力としてチュートリアルに関係が深いキスレフを選んで楽しんでます。

３．魅力的なMODが多数ある
　　Steamワークショップには魅力的なMODが数多く公開されており、不満な要素があればMODを使って改善出来たり、ゲームに＋αの要素を増やしたりできるので、とても楽しいです。

【不満点】
MODを使うことで不満点はほぼ無いくらいですが、要望的なことを書いておきます。
１．公式では日本語対応していない。
　　もし日本語MODが無ければ、このゲームを体験することすら出来ませんでした。
　　どうか今後のシリーズでは公式に日本語対応してくれることを願うばかりです。

２．キャラクタークリエイトがない。
　　このゲームにはキャラクタークリエイトが無いので、自分好みのキャラをロードやヒーローとして作成して登場させるといったことは出来ません。
　　カオス勢力のデーモンプリンスというキャラには、それっぽいクリエイト要素があるようですが、やはり自分の思い通りのロードやヒーローを作ってこの世界で遊びたい。
　　現状、このゲームはDLCで新しいキャラを増やしたりする販売方法をとっているようなので、キャラクリ要素は望み薄ですが、最終のアップデートとかで出来るようにならないかなー、ベルセルクのガッツ風キャラとか作って遊べたら最高なのになー等と思います。

３．日本風勢力が無い。
　　ファンタジー世界なので日本風勢力が無いのは仕方ないのかもしれませんが、中国風キャセイやロシア風キスレフなど多様な勢力があるだけに、やはり日本風の侍を使って遊びたいと思ってしまう。
　　DLCの情報とかを見ても、今後、日本風勢力が追加されるのは望み薄かもしれませんが、もしかしたらと期待はしてしまいます。
　　ただ、公式のバニラゲームには日本風勢力は無いものの、MODでは日本風MODを作ってくれている方々がおられるようです。
　　私自身、まだ初回プレイ中でバニラ勢力で遊んでいるところなので、次のプレイで楽しもうと思ってそれらの日本風MODは未導入ですが、どれもMOD説明や画像を見ているだけでワクワクするほど魅力的なMODでした。
　　私がこのゲームを購入する際、日本風勢力の有無は購入を決めるきっかけにもなりましたし、私と同じような方もおられるかもしれませんので、ワークショップで見つけることのできた魅力的な日本風MODをいくつかご紹介しておきます。
　　　・Roar of the Jade Sea : Yin-Yin, the Sea Dragon
　　　　（キャセイ派閥の一つに日本風勢力追加。見た目もWARHAMMER世界観にマッチした日本風という感じで素晴らしい。特に侍と忍者には一目惚れ。）
　　　・The Ronin, a Bladelords of Nippon Prologue
　　　　（戦闘中に用心棒として現れる侍風ヒーロー追加。めちゃくちゃカッコいい。作者さんのグループは更なる日本風MODを開発中だそう。）
　　　・IEE Nippon Cathay Faction Reskin
　　　　（IEEと呼ばれるImmortal Empires Expanded MODを使用して遊ぶ際に、キャセイ派閥の一部ユニットを日本風にリスキンしてくれる。これも侍がカッコいい。）

長々と書きましたが、これから購入を検討されている方に何か一つでも参考になることがあれば幸いです。
個人的には大満足の神ゲーなので、こんな面白いゲームを世に送り出してくれた開発者の方々や素晴らしいMOD作者の方々に感謝しています。

My favorite RTS/Turn-Based Startegy So far.

Good: 
- Tons of Replayability with 96 playable factions spread across 24 Races with different Battle & Campaign mechanics and Unique start position. For Example the Empire, which I think are one of the Races that have a diverse selection of Legendary Lords :

You got Emperor Karl Franz who started out in Empire's Capital, surrounded by Chaos, Warmonger Green Skins and Undead, he have powerful Elector Count mechanics to aid his nation, by far the hardest Empire faction imo.

Then there's Elspeth who started next to Karl, but instead of Elector Count system, she could teleport with a special building and buffs various Empire's gunpowder units.  

Oh you want to play the Empire but start somewhere else? then there's Volkmar in Deserts of Araby, hunting down the book of Nagash, Gelt far far away in Cathay, idk what is he doing there but he got a powerful colleges of Magic mechanic that could give him ridiculous ability like restoring movement. And finally there is Markus in Lustria, angering the Lizardmens as he try to colonize the jungle continent.

- many units variety, from typical units like spears, swords, halberds. To Dragons, caster lord/heroes with various lore of magics, Gunpowders, Steamtanks, Dinosaurs or the Unending swarm of Rats.

- There are tons of DLC, but this isn't Paradox game where it's mandatory to have all of them for a literal "full experience" or should i say, paywalling things that should've been free. Just play it vanilla, pick which faction you like and buy the dlc for them. The only issues with the DLCs are the pricing.

- The soundtracks are great, most of TWWH1 Races shares the same music, but from TWWH2 onwards to TWWH3 ( Except the Monogods ) each of Races have their own distinctive OST both during battle and Campaign. It's a shame they don't officially release it.

- Game is still supported with content uptades, likely until the next Total War announced.

- MODS MODS MODS, there are new faction mods, UI mods, or anything really. Workshop support in this game is Gold.

bad: 

- Even on Very Hard Campaign and Battle difficulty, if you already "learn" how the AI works, then the Campaign would fell too easy. But thankfully there are mods to fix this to made the campaign more interesting. 

- Playing as a dominantly Guns factions like Empire, Kislev, Dwarfs or Skaven. You'll often have more difficulty in finding a spot for Line of Sight instead of fighting the literal battle lol, LOS is huge issues for this game, probably due to MOST of the map having 'wavy terrains". Tips for this? ZOOM to the ground and pretend you are one of them. 

- Speaking of map, almost every battle map is horrible. Most of them are small, making them harder to play for certain factions, for example the Bretonnians who relies on their powerful cavalry that requires tons of space to move. And idk who design them, but man... there aren't really true "flat map", 80% of the terrain consisted of big hills, medium hills, small hills, and much more smaller hills that are small enough to block your gunpowder unit's Line of sight. 

- Siege are painful as ever, a total war tradition i believe. There are better Total War titles that handles siege way better, but this one just horribly wrong. Every part of the map is a narrow corridor, and a combination of poor Units Pathfinding+ Bad map is just bad, so it's better to just cheese with a single powerful lord or if you're playing as any factions with Bows, then they're your best friends. Or you know, you can just Auto Resolve.

- The AI is also problem, they tend made the game more tedious by Running away on Campaign map. It's like they are designed by Skavens. If you ever experience it, just use Ambush and they will forget where your troops are, but it won't fix the issue really.

The following is to be taken as a review of the collective Triology (Total Warhammer I through III)

This is one of the greatest action-oriented fantasy strategy game there is. It is a combination between a turn-based strategic campaign map and a tactical realtime-strategy battle map.
The turn-based strategic aspect is rather shallow, compared to comparable games such as those from Paradox. Essentially, it is just a way to generate battles between factions.
While the strategic layer is not as deep, it is noting to scoff at. With each DLC and free update more elaborate campaign mechanics have been introduced peaking with the resource-management of the Chaos Dwarf DLC.
It is extremly fun and contains tons of little twists and a massive map called "Immortal Empires" but if you do not intend to play realtime battles may fall short of your expecations.

The tactical battles are where this game really shines. The diversity of races and units and their animations and art styles that have been introduced over the time is mind-boggling. The love for detail is unbelievable and makes each battle very enjoyable. With time, you get to know the advantages and disadvantages of each unit which makes you better after each battle.

Coop
With the introduction of Total War Warhammer III, simultaneous turns on the strategic map have been introduced. This is a godsend and a time saver. Coop campaigns in general are very fun, you can either play together with your friends or against them, both options are great fun. In both cases you can take over parts of the army and play with or against the other human player(s).

Ultimately, this game is fantastic and will most likely be a "classic" strategy game for many many years to come.

Creative Assembly is slow to change but it is finally beginning to feel like they are on the right track for the final installment of the Total War: WARHAMMER series. It has been a long grind to get to where we are now and although things are not perfect, this is the ultimate Old World Warhammer experience out there right now. TWW2 was great and a massive improvement over the first game but it took time to hone and bring home an incredible Total War game. TWW3 is that next step in the long journey and I believe it is in a place now I can confidently recommend it to all lovers of the setting and real time strategy games. 
However.
Though the entry price is average for a game today the hidden costs of this series are startling to new players. To get the full experience of this game you must buy its predecessors as well as their dlcs that released years ago (I would suggest waiting to snag a little at a time during the major Steam sales) and that is a major grudge I and the most of the community share. You can get by fine with the base game but once you start to notice how much is paywalled (units, lords, entire factions) it can be uncomfortable but I wholeheartedly believe MOST dlcs are fair for what they give, especially the ones from the older installments and the games themselves. Be cautious and understand what you're getting into so take time to get adjusted before blowing through cash as this game has a steep learning curve that is absolutely punishing for people unfamiliar with the Total War formula.

Getting really sick of people leaving reviews for reasons other than whether or not the game is good.  Warhammer 3 is an incredible game, and is a testament to where the collectible table top genre can transition to.  Is the price tag rough? God yes.  But Warhammer 3 is effectively a continuation of the previous games, meaning that CA have been essentially working on this "game" for 8 years.  8 years of continuous updates and new content.  It's a given that after 8 straight years of new additions, things (not the base game) will cost more money over time.   Now, they have fumbled plenty, but with their recent mea culpa and what they have done with the last DLC (and the newest one), they have demonstrated a legitimate willingness to hear criticism and improve.

All of that nonsense out of the way, this game is, on its own, a fairly good strategy game, with very interesting factions, some (mostly) interesting new mechanics, and, as always, a beautiful and richly detailed map.  But if you have Warhammer 1 and 2 (plus the rather hefty amount of content for them), this game becomes one of the greatest strategy games of all time, with most of it's biggest flaws being fairly easy to fix with the easy to access list of mods on the steam workshop.  

Also, if you are interested in the game but fear the larger dlc list, there really is no need to buy them all.  Just buy the ones that seem interesting to you.

When this game dropped more than two years ago, it was highly anticipated by me. I have been engaging with Warhammer for almost thirty years ago, starting with the Lizardman vs. Bretonnians box. Game one was a slight disapointment for me, but I still played it for almost 100 hours, Game Two, especially with Mortal Empires was a blast, getting better with every new faction and legendary lord, so over the course of almost 5 years, I sank almost 500 hours into it. I was ecstatic for the release.

When it dropped I could not hide a small measure of dissapointment again, because compared to the old factions, that had received update after update, the new ones felt a bit shallow, plus: Some of the campaign mechanics were clunky as hell and felt forced, rather than enriching the game experience, they got in the way of actually playing it. Luckily mods helped tremendously. 

Then the first DLC dropped and „Champions of Chaos“ was just tremendous, my favorite of the whole series. It took the oldest and least reworked faction and made it into the most fun I have had with the game until then. Shortly after we received the highly anticipated „Forge of the Chaos Dwarves“ and it was a blast (furnace). Honestly I didn’t think anything could go wrong now.

And then ♥♥♥♥ hit the fan. CA’s rather questionable community management disgruntled the fans, Pharaoh (another TW title) was a dissapointment and the new „Shadows of Change“ DLC was overpriced and underdelivered. Three LL’s for 25 Euros, while back in the days of the second game three LL’s were standard (one of them free) for almost half the price. It was ♥♥♥♥ and I was ready to give up on the game.

Luckily: CA turned it around, delayed their DLC plans, patched more content into the game (for free) and really put the work in. „Thrones of Decay“ is a really good DLC. It made the game better, it makes it more fun. I am rather optimistic and can – at this point in time – recommend it wholeheartedly.

《全面战争：战锤3》评测：奇幻战略的史诗终章

作为战锤三部曲的收官之作，本作交出了一份近乎完美的答卷。它将宏大的战略格局、丰富的派系特色与史诗般的战斗体验提升到了系列新高度，为这个传奇系列画上了辉煌的句号。

游戏最令人称道的是其惊人的多样性。从基斯里夫的冰雪女王到震旦天朝的龙裔子民，每个派系都拥有独特的玩法、兵种和叙事背景。战役地图规模空前，混沌魔域与凡世世界的交织创造了前所未有的战略深度。实时战斗的视觉效果堪称华丽，恶魔军团与凡人军队的碰撞场面令人叹为观止。

“超凡帝国”模式将三部曲内容融为一体，提供了战略游戏史上规模空前的沙盒体验。优化和UI的改进让新老玩家都能轻松上手。虽然入门门槛依然存在，但一旦沉浸其中，数百小时的游戏时间转瞬即逝。

《全面战争：战锤3》不仅是奇幻策略游戏的巅峰之作，更是对 Creative Assembly 多年野心的终极实现。它证明了当深度策略与极致想象力结合时，能够创造出何等恢弘的虚拟战场。

Total War è finito con Medieval II ed Empire, ed è un peccato aver vissuto il declino assoluto di questa serie e dei sui sviluppatori.

Siamo passati da: gestione di città, castelli, avamposti, risorse, mercanti, diplomatici, famiglie reali, relazioni con il Papa, Crociate, Jihad, battaglie navali, rotte commerciali, ricerche, sviluppo delle città, controllo della popolazione in giochi di quasi 20 anni fa...
Al nulla assoluto con una bella grafica, delle ultime saghe storiche e della trilogia di Warhammer.

Il problema non è il tema fantasy, adoro la lore di Warhammer ma negli ultimi giochi la gestione degli insediamenti è veramente ridicola e sembra disegnata per un pubblico con una soglia di attenzione che rasenta il ritardo mentale.

Tutte le città sono uguali e hanno a disposizione si e no 5-6 edifici, le capitali qualcuno in più. Tutte le province sono uguali, non offrono qualche tipo di risorsa particolare, hanno tutte 2-3 insediamenti minori e una capitale. 

Battaglie con migliaia di unità che si risolvono in 3-4 minuti di orologio.
Il terreno non fa alcuna differenza strategica.
Durante gli assedi non possiamo attaccare diversi punti delle mura ma solo una facciata.
Tutti gli assedi sono mappe rettangolari con un muro in mezzo. 
Tutte le "battaglie sotterranee" sono mappe rettangolari con uno skybox diverso.
Tutte le unità a parte gli eroi, sono sacrificabili, non serve avere cura del proprio esercito semplicemente perchè le perdite vengono recuperate/rimpiazzate il turno successivo.

La "strategia" di WH è tutta qui: Creare full stack di unità e mandarle ad attaccare l'insediamento nemico più vicino.

DLC che non aggiungono niente al gameplay e che costano più del gioco, con skin per unità ed eroi singoli a 20-30€

Per avere la mappa del mondo completa e poter giocare la campagna "classica", dovrete aver acquistato anche i due precedenti  titoli di WH (altri 50-60€), altrimenti vi attaccate al cazzo!

CA purtroppo non ha più nulla da offrire, le ultime saghe storiche e non, lo dimostrano.

Aver reso accessibile a tutti questa serie, rimuovendo praticamente tutta la parte gestionale in favore di strategia brainless e battaglie blob veloci secondo me ha snaturato fortemente la serie.

Un'altra compagnia consumata dal money grabbing, che è diventata l'unica priorità di questo sviluppatore e questo lo noterete già dal menù principale, oscurato per metà perchè senza DLC non avrete accesso alla maggior parte dei contenuti.

So this game is kind of like the redheaded step child of the franchise, the first game setup an amazing framework, enjoyable mechanics and some of the most traditionally popular factions. 
  
 The second game took everything the first game did right and jacked them up to 11 (the combat, the unique faction mechanics, more factions), and it took the things that the first game didn't so well (siege combat, unique faction quests, general world interactivity) and either did better or straight up fixed them.
  
 The third game attempted to make two major improvements over the second game, siege game-play and over all general world interactivity. While the attempt was amazing and the company's response to feedback on the mechanics were mostly okay (with a few NOTABLE exceptions that reek of corporate interference) the missing Immortal Empires mode at launch, and the lack of factions at launch made the Realms of Chaos mode somewhat dull in direct comparison to the end of the simply amazing state that the second game was already in. The overall general world interactivity was attempted to be addressed by the four realms of chaos which could occasionally experience temporary game breaking glitches and the realms themselves varied from standard and forgettable game-wise to, down right boring and annoying. The siege battles where attempted to be addressed in a way that while favoring the defender still (as they definitely should) ended up making most player vs AI siege battles very samey and boring. While both of these things have been improved and made to feel significantly more enjoyable, the bad taste left in the wake of launch is still in peoples minds. As well as the still notable lack of factions playable in this mode (while I understand that as more lords are added through DLC more factions will be added to the Realms of Chaos mode I still personally only have access too a very small number of the factions I enjoy playing.) Taken as a standalone experience this game was actually rather enjoyable and a solid game deserving a positive review if not a mostly positive review score. However this game was NEVER going to be able to exist without a comparison to the rest of the series.
   
TL:DR The first game was good, the second game was simply one of the best of its type, the third game took major risks to attempt to improve on the few failings of the second game, unfortunately those risk did not pan out as well as CA (the developers of this franchise) had hoped they would. Leaving this game to just be a really good game, that unfortunately has to live in the shadow of its much cooler older brother.

Стрелки с ружьями почему-то могут стрелять навесом, им не обязательно даже выстраиваться в линию, ведь они могут стрелять сквозь стоящих перед ними юнитов да и анимации перезарядки у них нет.

Newest DLC is quality and, while still pricier than that of TWW2, is more fair in how it is sold and the amount of content you get. Really though, lack of content isn't a critique anyone can fairly lob at TW: Warhammer 3. Buy Warhammer 1 and 2 cheap from a third party site or on sale, and you have easily a hundred hours of content between all the factions across all three games. DLC lords add unique spins on each faction, and full DLC races add a lot of new toys, but this is certainly not a situation where you need all the DLC to feel like you're getting a complete experience. Buy the DLC for factions you want to play as and for the lords that sound cool when you want to play them, and give the others a pass.

Overall, highly recommend even if you've never played Total War before.
