Total War: Warhammer III is a game that has truly outdone itself. It's a **bold, experimental final act** that brings the sweeping dark fantasy trilogy to a worthy end. The game excels on just about every level, strategic and tactical, and is filled with surprises and oddities.

The game's campaign is very story-driven, even more so than Warhammer 2's Eye of the Vortex. It introduces interesting campaign mechanics that build up rivalries between its memorable main cast. The game also introduces several new armies that don't play like anything we've seen in Total War before.

One of the most exciting features of the game is the introduction of the Realm of Chaos. Each section of the Realm of Chaos reflects the personality of its patron god. This new feature allows for a type of scenario Total War has never attempted, and it’s refreshing to see the time-tested formula used in new ways.

Despite some notable flaws, such as a somewhat messier campaign progression, Total War: Warhammer III still manages to impress. With multiple factions and legendary lords to choose from, along with a plethora of improvements to existing mechanics, you're bound to have one hell of a good time.

The game has also seen a resurgence on Steam with its highest player count in a year and positive reviews for the new Thrones of Decay DLC. The Thrones of Decay DLC is a no-brainer purchase for fans of Total War: Warhammer III. It gives players a trio of new Lords to learn, a large number of new units to play with, and another reason to sink hours and hours into the game.

In conclusion, Total War: Warhammer III is a brilliant final act with the series' most inventive and unusual factions yet. It's a game that goes big, fully committing to Warhammer's wonderfully over-the-top brand of fantasy.

WH3 is a decent game.
But I think the game desperately needs to focus on making the core experience more fun.
The DLC's are all great for the most part, it adds content that everybody wants and is always a nice addition.
What I'm refering to is just the overall gameplay being lackluster.

Most players never finish their campaigns and it's for a couple of really good reasons.

Reason 1:
- The ''Victory'' is the most underwhelming ♥♥♥♥ you'll ever see.
A screen just pops up, telling you: You won.
And starts playing a timelaps of the areas you conquered.
The end of your campaign should be cool grand battle that really tests your army and skill in order to win.
But no, just sack 30 random settlements and win I guess o__O

Reason 2:
- Battles with little to no strategy.
The game is really fun at the start since most armies you go up against are around 8-14 in army size.
Why this is such an important thing is because the battles with larger number of units tend to 
screw over all forms of strategy and AI logic.
It's basically impossible to micromanage your army of 20 different units and not be super stressed since you can never 
focus and enjoy the spectacle.
The AI also become absolutely brainrotted.
Since there are so many units on the battlefield, the AI can't keep up with everything that's happening.
It often results in massive moshpits where everyone just slams their head in to each other.
You never get these elegant 1v1 or unit vs unit since they're all stuck in each other.
And don't get me started on the siege battles.
It's always super tight corridors, with horrible pathing and invisbles obstacles, and shows every possible jank the game has.
Cavalry and flanking units are awful since they can't move around freely.

Reason 3:
- Lack of a fun endgame.
When you load up a campaing, most players ''want'' to complete it in some sense or feel satisfied.
But this never really happens because it becomes so easy after you've snowballed past everyone.
So it just becomes a boring victory lap where you execute every faction that's in your way.
So the infamous auto resolve comes in to play, where you auto resolve every encounter until you've reach your superficial goal of razing 5 villages etc.
There is no cool send off or risk since if you fail you can just save scum.
That's what I liked about some of these ''RACE'' campaings, everyone felt apart of the game and not just static NPC waiting to get slaughtered by you eventually.

( Main Conclusion )
- So how do we fix these issues?
1. 
First off.
Give a stronger incentive to actually completing a campaign.
Maybe after winning a campaing, you unlock small bonuses for Legendary Lords or items to be found.
Or a playable LL after winning 100 campaing for example.
2.
Make a setting that caps armies at a lower unit count in armies, that slowly over the turns get bigger and bigger.
Certain factions could have bonuses or tech trees that would increase it faster etc.
But something that limits the AI to spam ♥♥♥♥ units.
3.
Add an end times gamemode in to immortal empires.
Where everyone has the same ''goal''.
So there is more of a grand finale at the end.
4.
Remove Daniel The Demon.

As a self-professed fan of the Warhammer universe, I may be a tad biased, but Warhammer III has unquestionably captured my attention in ways few games manage. With (now) over 250 hours sunk into this fantastical strategy realm, I can confidently say that it hasn't lost its appeal for me. Sure, I don't play it every day, but when I do, it's like embarking on a grand adventure anew.

One thing that strikes me about this game is how faithfully it adheres to the lore of the Warhammer universe. Games Workshop, the guardian of this rich narrative tapestry, keeps a watchful eye, ensuring that Creative Assembly doesn't stray too far from the established lore. This commitment to authenticity enhances the immersion, making battles feel like epic clashes straight from the pages of the tabletop game.

However, every rose has its thorn. it's the sieges. Creative Assembly's attempt at city assaults often falls short of expectations, lacking the depth and strategy present in other aspects of the game. Fortunately, the developers have acknowledged this shortcoming and are working on improvements, which I eagerly anticipate. (I hope so...)

Another point of contention is the DLC policy. While I understand the need to monetize additional content, the randomness of what you get for your money can be frustrating. Sometimes, you'll stumble upon a treasure trove of new factions, units, and campaigns for a modest sum, while other times, you'll feel shortchanged for shelling out a hefty amount. It's a gamble that doesn't always pay off.

Despite these drawbacks, I wholeheartedly recommend Warhammer III to strategy enthusiasts and Warhammer fans alike. The blend of grand strategy, tactical battles, and fantastical elements like magic and monstrous creatures creates a captivating experience that keeps drawing me back in.

That being said, as much as I revel in the arcane wonders of Warhammer's universe, I can't help but yearn for the announcement of Medieval III Total War. Perhaps one day, I'll swap spells and sorcery for swords and sieges once more. Until then, Total War: Warhammer III will continue to reign supreme in my gaming library.

CA did not deliver a good game at this third game's launch and commited a terrible mistake with the pricing of "Shadows of Change" DLC soon after in comparison to the content it delivered then.
Still, the mentioned DLC was never updated with a FLC legendary lord which further adds salt to the wound.
Fortunately, the game was revived with the release of Thrones of Decay DLC but the two DLCs that followed, Omens of Destruction and Tides of Torment respectively, did not deliver the same weight in terms of being "fun" with the lord and faction packs they introduced.
I should like to review Tides of Torment Norsca now:
The Norsca rework of the Tides of Torment is a minor succcess in my opinion, but there are caveats:
Sayl himself is rather a forgetabble LL bc of his campaign, not bc of his character, looks or lore.
He has a forgetable copy mechanic; his "unique" mechanic is just a weaker Tzeentch's Changing of the Ways mechanic.
The lord himself is a fun caster lord that can ride a mammot, but he's the only great addition to Norsca along with Beorg Bearstruck and the Fimir Noble.
Regular units themselves are meh.
Marauder bearmen, the Bearmen of Urslo, are tier 2 infantry units that try to feel an unnecessary, in my opinion nonexistent, gap; the gap was already filled with Marauder berserkers, and it's not like regular marauders underperform considering the buffs they can and do get during the campaign.
On top of that, the tier 3 Marauder Champions are just so good of a unit with a lot of in-campaign buff potential that one will ultimately almost always replace any other infantry with these guys 'cause they hold the anvil, the lines, firm.
So, the Bearmen are, again, extremely unnecessary at worst and redundant at best.
The Kurgan Horsemen are conceptually and lore-wise insanely cool, but they underperform in the late game, even if attached to Sayl's army, considering his unique buffs to them, and that's unfortunate that this unit cannot transition to late game.
Imo, it's not that the Kurgan Horsemen don't get kills, they just die a lot getting those kills while other Norscan units don't struggle as much doing the same job.
Norsca's roster is phenomenal overall: solid infantry, great and various monstrous and complementary infantry, fast cav or cav-like monster units, respectable but niche ranged units and many cools monsters are abundant in this roster, so Chimera while very effective is just a buffed Chaos Frost Dragon. Curs'd Ettin if not bc of the Runecaller version would've been too redundant, but they get a shaky pass.
Shaman Sorcerer Lord must've been already added to the game with the original Norsca release or at least should've been added as a FLC lord now for previous Norsca DLC owners.
The new RoR units are meh reskins of previously existing units in terms of uniqueness they bring; they have their uses, no denies. They're just not unique.
The problem with Tides of Torment Norsca is not necessarily incompetent units, but rather uniqueness in terms of the roles they play and the gaps they fill.
They're just a tad bit redundant.
Did I mention there's a conceptually cool but kinda underperforming Dreadmaw, too?
And the Nightmaw? Don't get me started on how frustrating its presence is, a ridiculous wind spell.

So: Sayl ✅️ Shaman Lord ✅️ Beorg and Fimir Noble ✅️ other units? Not very intriguing if not straight unrecommended.

What I like about the game: the voice acting, background music, theme, graphics, relative stability of current build, cool factions that play very differently, general ability to immerse myself in the fantasy.  I also enjoy the tension of the beginning of the campaign, where it all seems like it could either fall apart or work. 

What I'm lukewarm about: I'm not as thrilled with the magic system in TW WH III compared to TW WH II, where a magician could really turn the tide of battle.  Feels like an unnecessary nerf that reduced some of the fun of the game.

What I don't like: siege battles, but I don't really hate them.  Sometimes I actually find them fun, depending on what type of weaknesses they have (and if I have an appropriate answer to exploit it).  The only down side is that a siege battle does take a long time, and I generally don't have multiple hours at a time to plow into a videogame anymore.

In summary: I really enjoy this game, with much more I can say positive than negative.  The most recent Thrones of Decay DLC really breathed some life into the Empire for me, a faction that never really felt that fun to me before this.  If you can pick this game and recent DLC up on one of their semi-regular sales, I would highly recommend it.

Warhammer 3 has grabbed and held my attention in the way I hoped 2 was going to. I ostensibly played Warhammer 2 but in reality this is my first Total War game and it’s awesome!

It plays like two different games baked into one and pulls it off well and at a scale that I now regret not getting into Warhammer 2.

It plays like a 4x game, similar to Civ, where you’re building settlements and expanding next to neighboring factions. There are over 120 factions on the smaller campaign map and about 300 in the combined Warhammer 1 + 2 + 3 map. 

Each of the 24 races play fairly different on the 4x front, offering different mechanics you need to focus on. Some are more beginner friendly and are additive (Kislev, High Elves, Cathay) and some are essential and you’ll lose if you don’t interact with them at all (Skaven, Ogres, Orcs). 

Then there’s the battle system. You build armies composed of 20 different units, each consisting of 1 to over 100 individual units, and can auto resolve the battles. If you do this, then the game literally just plays like a civ game. 

But you have the option to manually take over the army and actually fight out battles. You control the formations, you control when units engage, when they flank, how cavalry goes out, who and what to priority, when to fall back, how and when to use spells, and more. Each of the factions and each of the lords, of which there are over 80 at this point bring something unique to the table, and you are incentivized to manually resolve battles because you can turn an auto resolved defeat into a decisive win. 

The game is huge. So many ways to play, so many units, so many possibilities, that I’m just scratching the surface at 40 hours and see myself playing for well over 300+ over the next couple of years. I hope Sega allows Creative Assembly to continue supporting the game for many years to come because it truly is a one-of-a-kind masterpiece.

[h1] 它不仅是一款游戏，更是一部史诗 [/h1]

这是一款由传奇开发商Creative Assembly，所去打造的一款史诗级的战略经营类游戏，同时也是战锤系列三部曲的最终作，或者称之为集大成之作。目前由世嘉进行代理发行，搬上了steam平台，它的背景及其庞大，并且极具深度，接下来我将向大家具体介绍一下 这款真正的史诗级策略游戏的真实体验。

[h1] 波澜壮阔，风云变幻的奇幻史诗 [/h1]

本作是以知名桌游《奇幻战锤》作为参考，并且加入了全面战争系列游戏的玩法，真正的展现出了一款史诗级的沙盒策略游戏，虽然本作是三部曲的最终章，但是游戏讲述的非常全面，哪怕你没有玩过前作也丝毫不用担心无法上手或者学习成本过高的问题，你只需要去体验这部史诗就好啦，游戏中拥有非常大的战役地图，然后搭配上策略性的战略经营玩法，真的让人无法自拔。

哪怕你没有玩过任何一部前作，你依旧可以去享受这款游戏，在游戏的序章，也就是新手关卡的时候，它会在游戏中告诉你这部游戏真正的故事，当熊神厄孙被恶魔囚禁，而前去搭救的亲王大人也被混沌恶魔所进行同化，最后熊神的痛苦哀嚎，彻底的打破了现实世界和恶魔世界的稳定性，当水非常浑浊的时候，任何一个势力都会企图浑水摸鱼，而真正的全面战争，就在此刻缓缓拉开了帷幕。

游戏采用了全程配音，让人真正的沉浸在这一场战争之中，在这一张巨大的地图之上，你只需要去进行战争就行了，我们可以用各种各样的方法赢下战争，无论是增加军队，还是增加质量你都可以去体验，去真正的融入在游戏里面。在游戏中会存在不同的种族和国家，完全了融入了桌游的背景，可玩性非常的高，每一局游戏，你都会有全新的发现。
游戏的体量也极其庞大，当我第一次下载的时候，上百G的大小确实是吓到我了，在游戏中，我真正的体验到了千人大战和巨大的地图到底是什么样子的，游戏在首发的时候就拥有8个种族10个传奇领主。 游戏的画面也极其精美，说实话我感觉拿它去拍个微电影都是丝毫没有问题的。

说完优点，当然也有缺点，我个人感觉游戏的操作是比较难的，它不像其他的传统RTS一样，可以单独操控一个单位，来进行精细的策略运营，这是一个千人大战的战场，你需要做的是运筹帷幄，排兵布阵，去控制大量的军队来去进行冲锋陷阵，游戏在中后期可能会感觉到有点无聊单调，但是这也是同类型游戏的通病。

游戏拥有创意工坊和各种MOD，极大程度的提高了游戏的寿命。更何况游戏本身的质量就不差，之前推出了腐烂王座系列的DLC直接完成了评价逆转，而这一次的《毁灭预兆》直接来了一手锦上添花，真的算是诚意满满了。
 
[h1] 又来三位全新领主，《毁灭预兆》有点好玩！ [/h1]

作为一款已经发售了两年的作品，没想到它居然还在持续性的更新优化，诚意是真的足，前段时间的腐烂王座系列DLC珠玉在前，这一次的毁灭预兆又怎么可能差呢！本次的DLC玩法上没有过多的变化，最让我惊喜的其实就是恐虐的机制，实在是太强了，不过闲话少说，看看这次的DLC带来的究竟有什么吧。

本次DLC带来的依旧是三位实力强劲的传奇领主，首先第一位就是最臭名昭著的兽人将领：哥巴德·铁爪，这个领主属于直接把大脑和肌肉融合的怪胎，也是绿皮阵营中少有的智力担当，这个特性翻译的很有灵性 “俺计划”虽然名字听上去不怎么好听，强却是真的强，可以混合不同的部队去解锁一些协作增益，各种军队组合能构建出很多种战术，玩法大大提高了，而且随着哥巴德的到来，一只全新的部队也将要出现，其中包括了传奇领主斯纳格拉·毒涎，实力还是挺强的，在哥巴德的DLC中，总共有，1位传奇英雄，1位传奇领主，2类领主与英雄，5种战斗部队，以及3支精英部队。

第二位则是食人魔历史上最成功的雇佣兵，高尔法格·噬人者，是类佣兵的派系，整体的属性算是非常强的，而且长的是真的帅，在特性方面，最主要的就是雇佣合约了，毕竟是佣兵嘛，我们可以通过解决客户的争端，获得各种报酬，还会获得一些随行辅助，作为传奇佣兵，怎么能没有属于自己的兵团呢！高尔法格佣兵团中最值得一提的就是传说中的食人魔王国处刑者，被称为“开膛手”的布拉格，本次的DLC中，总共有，1位传奇英雄，1位传奇领主，2类领主与英雄，5种战斗部队，以及3支精英部队。

最后一位则是被称为最强的放血鬼，猎颅者，它是真的强，特别是它的机制，颅骨披风，我们必须不断的寻找领主，然后击杀他们，把他们的颅骨挂在披风上面，可以因此解锁一些全新的增益，获得升级，听上去平平无奇，但是实际上是真的猛，随便点点点就赢了，完全不需要思考，而且随着猎颅者的到来，还会有九种来自血神魔域的部队加入，其中包括了两位传奇领主，分别是“嗜血屠夫”斯卡尔·血怒 以及“恐虐之怒”席拉·昂菲格里姆，本次的DLC中，总共有1位传奇英雄，2位传奇领主，1类领主，5种战斗部队，以及3支精英部队。


[h1] 闻者不如见者，知之为详 [/h1]
这是一款非常宏达的史诗级策略运营游戏，你可以在这里发动所有的脑细胞，去体验一下真正的策略游戏到底是什么样子的，优美的音乐 全程配音，并且优秀的平衡性，我真的无法想象，为什么会有人不喜欢这款作品，我希望把它推荐给每一个喜欢策略游戏的玩家们。

"The right to discuss is a privilege – it is not an entitlement you earn by playing the game."

Creative Assembly doesn't put the same effort into their games as they did in the past. All maps are previously generated, and don't adjust to where you are on the world map.

AI is absolute trash. Takes forever for ranged units to lock on their target and begin shooting. Many actions don't make sense as far as positioning goes. Steam tanks randomly turn around in place, even after moving them and forcing their facing to a certain direction. You basically have to hand hold every unit, and hope they don't make some idiotic decision regardless of your commands.
If you are using multiple ranged units, they will all lock their shots onto ONE enemy in a unit, meaning additional shots are completely wasted on an already dead enemy. This has been going on throughout all the Warhammer games.

Left Alt + Right Mouse Drag no longer works. Now if you use it, it doesn't keep the same formation and heading, instead it does what it was supposed to, except it reduces your ranks/columns into a skinnier formation.

Most combat seems random. You cannot count on the AI to do the same actions each time. Sometimes they just randomly change up their actions. This is why when you restart a battle, sometimes the actions will be different. I'm not talking about the computer AI, I mean with your very own units, things will change from battle to battle, even if everything you do are the same actions.

This is the only Total War game where I cheat the bank. EVERY other Total War game I had no need to change the amount of money I had to work with, as I always had plenty. This game, if you want a competent army, you'll be paying through the nose with upkeep. God help you if you want multiple armies. In addition, your units can be grossly underpowered. Want to play the most popular race, The Empire? Well get used to everything but Cavalry and Gunpowder troops being underpowered. Infantry? Absolute joke. Ranged Gunpowder units? Well now you think you'd have an advantage, except the AI is awful. I LOVE having my units focus on an enemy for ages before they finally shoot.

There is also very little direction. I find myself wondering what direction I should go in, what enemies are truly my enemies, and should I truly ally with a particular faction or not. Some provinces will not be fully yours, based on what allies you have, regardless of the ability to trade cities now. Some just don't want to budge.

I always find myself disappointed by the Warhammer series, especially Warhammer 3. I never had this issue with older Creative Assembly Total War games. Something has changed, and you cannot count on this company any more. Play the Rome games. Play the Shogun games. Do not play anything recent from Creative Assembly. They no longer fix bugs. They always ship the games in an unfinished state. And you can always expect an abhorrent amount of DLCs added to each game, when much of it should have been shipped with the game at launch.

Garbage company, garbage game, the future is doomed for Total War.

40+ hours and I still feel like I have barely scratched the surface. The amount of content this game has to offer is staggering. Even just the base game could net you 400+ hours of new things to see. I haven't tried any mods yet, but the steam workshop integration looks solid. It's good to see a developer making modding as accessible as possible.

The game play is fairly solid. This is my first TW game, but I found the campaigns to be a good mix between turn based and real time.  With lots to do on the campaign map, and battles offering a fun challenge with lots of variety.

There is a fair amount of depth when it comes to the campaign. You need to pick your friends carefully, since making an alliance with one faction may lock you out of another if they don't like each other, even within the same race. You need to plan out your economy to fund your armies, keep your people happy and manage your relationship to other factions carefully. Planning your the compositions of your armies is quite important. It's not just about getting the "best" units, you need armies you can afford. So it becomes a balance between economics and military strength. Do you build a few really strong armies, or lots of okay armies?

The variety in game play between factions is significant. I've played a bit as Grand Cathay and as the High Elves and they offered very different experiences (need to get WH2 to play as the high elves). You're still doing "Total War" thing, but the strategy is very different and each faction has unique mechanics that offer new challenges and opportunities. 

The graphics are pretty, zooming in to see the model animations can be quite fun, the campaign map itself is well designed. There is a lot of depth

The amount of DLC is both a pro and a con. 

The Pro is that many of them seem quite good (with a couple misses, which happens) and you can still have lots of fun without them. Picking the ones you are interested in when they go on sale, which happens quite often. They all offer a new experience that could lead to hundreds of hours of enjoyment.

The con is the price tag. It's expensive to get "everything". Especially considering that to get everything, you need to purchase both WH1 and WH2, all their DLC and all the DLC for WH3. That being said, you really don't need everything to enjoy this game, since the only thing it does is allow you to play as the factions in the DLC. They are all already on the map, so if you don't want to play as someone, you don't need their DLC. 

Overall, this is a very unique fantasy experience with tons of replay value and lots of ongoing support from the developers. It has definitely made me want to check out some of the historical TW games at some point, but for now I am really enjoying this.

[h1]久闻大名，名不副实[/h1]

《全面战锤3》作为《全面战争》全战系列的集大成者，在继承前作的优良基因的之外，更是在策略深度，种族多样性以及战役丰富度上达到了新的高度，不仅满足了老玩家的期待，更是给新玩家提供了入门的平台以及详细的教程。正值《腐烂王座》的dlc加入，正好入手体验一波，看看这款策略作品是不是真的属于一款名不副实的全战作品。

[h1]战锤世界，背景介绍[/h1]

和其他全战系列不一样的是，战锤世界一直都是虚构的魔幻世界，在这里生活着人类、矮人等24个种族，虽然是虚构的魔幻世界，确是以中世界作为背景，玩家可以在这场战略沙盒的冒险中打造属于自己的帝国。玩家在游戏中充当传奇领主，守护自己的国度避免被其他种族入侵，击败他们，同样也可以选择入侵他们占领他们的国度，主要体现在打战场的把控，特别是对于战场中各个兵种的调度以及资源的配比，在这个魔幻的世界中生存下来，变得更加强大，因此也特别考验玩家的策略性。

[h1]细致入微，新手引导[/h1]

开局就是序章，但是序章的故事特别长，第一是为了让玩家有代入感，逐步了解这个虚构的魔幻的战锤世界，第二是是足够详细细致的新手引导，包括各种游戏界面，操作的指引都很到位，让玩家进一步代入感，这些设定就可以说明这款作品的成功。

[h1]依旧如旧，宏伟叙事[/h1]

进入游戏，序章的故事大概就是基斯里夫所信仰的神“厄孙”被恶魔囚禁，陷入沉睡，而故事里的尤里亲王，率领部队北征时就面临着风雪，一队人马孤立无援，在这时候厄孙的声音响彻尤里的耳畔，体验过了序章之后，就已经能够很好感受到本作作为策略游戏的细节部分以及丰富的内容，而且在前面强大的世界观加持下，能够感受到一种史诗版的感受，不过后续的剧情也是有些出乎意料，其实是受到了邪神“暗影”比拉克的蛊惑，走上了与自己信仰的神背道而驰的道路，而就是在这里，本作的宏大世界就正式向我们玩家敞开了大门。

[h1]游戏机制，大型作战[/h1]

首先是战锤系统一直都是热衷给玩家带来大战场，玩家需要指挥各种大型部队进行作战，并且由于作战部队也有很多设定，包括前排的骑兵，步兵，后排的弓兵，炮手等，让玩家在战斗前的指挥需要进行深度构思，对于不同手头上不同兵力兵种的调度，还要利用所在地形的优势进行作战，以尽可能小的损失取得最大的胜利，因此这也是十分考验玩家的对于战场各个细节的把控。

[h1]兵种系统，技能科技[/h1]

其实这个一直都是全战系列的特点，每个全战系列想要完全深入了解，肯定要对这些熟悉，才能更好打出自己想要的战场结局。首先是战锤3目前一共有24个种族，且每个种族都有自己的独特兵种和英雄树，而且科技树还要更加复杂，对于一些种族的领主还会拥有不同的科技树，并且有些还要额外购买dlc，才能解锁，这也是为什么战锤3被打很多差评的一部分原因。

[h1]环境因素，腐蚀系统[/h1]

环境系统大体可以分成两种，一是选择适合自己或者不适合自己居住的的环境。可以根据自己的情况进行选择可以选择直接摧毁不占领，或者顶着高额的掌控力负增长进行居住。二是腐蚀系统，有着奸奇腐蚀、瘟疫腐蚀、吸血鬼腐蚀等等，如果你本身不是适应该腐蚀的种族，那么这些腐蚀会导致你在此区域行军的时候对你的部队造成损伤，你需要派遣副英雄去降低去除腐蚀。

[h1]总的来说，还算不错[/h1]

排除一些让人诟病的dlc外，其实本体还算是一款不错的策略作品，特别是塑造了一个魔幻的中世界风格的世界，丰富的兵种设定，战争要素的细节考虑以及特别重要的大战场让玩家可以亲自下场指挥宏大的战争，体验一场酣畅淋漓的战斗，加上最近更新的腐烂王座dlc，真的很好玩，希望ca能推出更多好玩的dlc，还有其他dlc快点打折吧。

Ich bin mit "Total War: WARHAMMER III" in die Welt von Warhammer eingetaucht, daher kann ich keinen klaren Vergleich zu den älteren Teilen ziehen, jedoch gibt mir dies, so denke ich, eine Objektivere Betrachtung des Spiels und ist daher kein Nachteil. 

Zunächst einmal es gibt viel berechtigte Kritik um "Total War: WARHAMMER III": 
Zu Release viele Bugs, AddOns werden teils viel zu teuer verkauft, Ladezeiten sind auch mit Modernen PC's unerklärlich lang und ja die neue Kampagne "The Realm of Chaos" ist tatsächlich sehr nerven Aufreibend. 

Jedoch bringt die "Total War: Warhammer" -Reihe eine einzigartige Fantasy Welt mit sich, welche ich so in keinem anderen Spiel gesehen habe. 
Es gibt über 90 verschiedene spielbare Kommandanten und 24 verschiedene Völker/Fraktionen. Jeder dieser Fraktionen hat individuelle Kampagnen Spielmechaniken und spielt sich durch Verschiedene Startpositionen, Befreundete/Verfeindete Fraktionen und eigene Einheiten komplett unterschiedlich. Zudem ist die Welt welche es, in der Kampagne "Immortal Empires", zu Erobern gilt riesengroß und bietet mit jedem neustart unterschiedliche Herausforderungen und Abenteuer.

Die Schlachten in "Total War: WARHAMMER III" sind, meiner Meinung nach, das Kern- und auch das Gelungenste Element des gesamten Spiels. Durch Taktisches Vorgehen und Kennenlernen der eigenen Fraktion und deren Einheiten, ist es jedes mal ein riesen Spaß das Schlachtfeld zu betreten. Auch hier gilt wie auf der Kampagnen Karte jede Schlacht ist durch Terrain, Einheiten, Kampagneneinfluss und den verschiedenen feindlichen Fraktionen unterschiedlich. 

Dazu kommt das Warhammer eine eigene komplette Lore hat, in welche man sich mit Hörspielen, Büchern, Wikis und Videos verlieren kann. Dies macht das Spiel meines Erachtens noch interessanter da ich meine Lieblingscharaktere wie bzw. "Gotrek und Felix" selber auf ihren Abenteuern begleiten kann. 

Nach all diesem Lob muss ich jedoch noch eine für mich Extrem wichtige Thematik ansprechen, welche vielen vielleicht die Entscheidung vom Kauf zu diesem Spiel abnehmen wird. Die Add-Ons. 

Ich habe vorher grob beschrieben wie Viele Fraktionen es in diesem Spiel gibt und das sich genau dadurch "Total War: WARHAMMER III" erst so richtig entfalten kann. Nun ist es jedoch so, wenn dies der Erste "Total War: Warhammer" Teil ist welchen Sie auf Steam kaufen, so besitzen Sie nicht 24 Fraktionen verschiedene sondern lediglich 8. (Ein paar mehr durch Kostenlose DLC's, aber das Argument wird klar.) All diese anderen Fraktionen verstecken sich so gesehen, hinter einer Weiteren Paywall, wenn Sie diese selbst spielen möchten. Entweder durch Kauf von DLC's oder die Vorgänger "Total War: WARHAMMER I" und "Total War: WARHAMMER II".

Alle Kommandanten Freigeschaltet zu haben kostet ohne Rabatte, weit über 200 €.
Deswegen mein Tipp, genau überlegen welche Fraktionen für einen Interessant sind und im Angebot oder vergünstigt Online auf anderen Plattformen kaufen. 

Ich persönlich habe mir alle "Total War: WARHAMMER" Teile und insgesamt 3 DLC's gekauft für ca. 90 € und mit diesem Paket mehrere 100 Stunden Spielzeit bekommen, für meine Rechnung ein Fairer Deal. Dies muss jedoch jeder für sich selbst entscheiden. 

Ich hoffe ihnen hat dieses kleine Review weiter geholfen und ihnen vielleicht die Entscheidung zum Kauf abgenommen.

Total Warhammer III is a grand strategy and turn-based tactics masterpiece that doesn't becessarily takes the series to new heights, but provides a more complete version of the world created by the first and second titles in the series.  Fair warning: for newcomers to the franchise, this is not the Total War experience, but a more unique fantastical concept take on the TW formula; and it is fantastic.
The game's core gameplay loop of managing your empire, recruiting armies, and engaging in epic battles is as addictive and satisfying as ever. The addition of the Chaos Realms and the Realm of Chaos campaign adds a fresh twist to the familiar formula, forcing players to navigate far more treacherous terrain than in previous titles. The game's factions are diverse and well-designed, each with their own unique playstyles and mechanics. The Kislev and Cathay factions, in particular, are a welcome addition, offering a fresh perspective on the Warhammer universe, however the Chaos factions, while varied in theme, are essentially four aspects of a similar concept.  
The battles are as intense and visually stunning as ever, management of settlements can be as micro or macro level as you decide.  It would be remiss not to mention my two significant concerns about the title: later game AI turns between battles can be a little sluggish and most obviously, the exorbitantly high cost of the DLC. This hurts, as with the minimal content it provides, it simply feels like a callous cash grab; something the publishers have a poor record for over many titles. The lack of a more substantial expansion or a complete edition of the game at launch is a missed opportunity, but it is important to recognise that for those who have the previous two core titles-it makes for a tremendously full roster inside this game. The gouging that occurs for Lord or hero characters aside, this is a wonderful way of expanding the options and interaction between all factions.  
~It is an easy recommend - nothing new, but more comfortable, formulaic strategy and developed content from a reliable engine.

Als ich "Total War: WARHAMMER III" gespielt habe, war ich überwältigt von der Größe und dem Detailreichtum des Spiels. Die Kombination aus der epischen Schlachtfeld-Action und der tiefgründigen Strategie in der Kampagne macht das Spiel zu einem absoluten Highlight für Fans von Strategie- und Fantasy-Spielen.

Die grafische Darstellung ist atemberaubend. Jede Einheit, jedes Gelände und jede Schlacht sind mit einer Detailgenauigkeit gestaltet, die das Spiel zum Leben erweckt. Die Animationen sind flüssig und die Effekte beeindruckend, besonders in den magischen Kämpfen.

Die Vielfalt der Fraktionen und ihrer einzigartigen Spielstile ist ein großer Pluspunkt. Jede Fraktion fühlt sich anders an und bietet eigene Herausforderungen und Strategien, was den Wiederspielwert erheblich erhöht. Besonders gefallen hat mir die Tiefe der Lore, die perfekt in das Gameplay integriert ist.

Allerdings gibt es auch einige Kritikpunkte, die erwähnt werden müssen. Die Performance-Probleme und Bugs zum Zeitpunkt der Veröffentlichung waren für viele Spieler frustrierend. Obwohl Patches viele dieser Probleme behoben haben, war der Start holprig.

Die KI könnte in manchen Situationen besser agieren, insbesondere in der Kampagne, wo sie manchmal unlogische Entscheidungen trifft. Auch das Balancing zwischen den Fraktionen ist nicht immer perfekt, was zu unfairen Situationen führen kann.

Insgesamt ist "Total War: WARHAMMER III" ein beeindruckendes und umfassendes Strategiespiel, das trotz einiger technischer Schwierigkeiten und Balancing-Probleme durch seine Tiefe und seinen Umfang besticht. Für Fans des Genres und der Warhammer-Welt ist es ein Muss.

English:

When I played "Total War: WARHAMMER III," I was overwhelmed by the scale and detail of the game. The combination of epic battlefield action and deep strategy in the campaign makes the game a highlight for fans of strategy and fantasy games.

The graphical presentation is stunning. Every unit, terrain, and battle is designed with a level of detail that brings the game to life. The animations are smooth, and the effects, especially in magical battles, are impressive.

The variety of factions and their unique playstyles is a significant plus. Each faction feels different and offers its own challenges and strategies, greatly enhancing the replay value. I particularly enjoyed the depth of the lore, which is perfectly integrated into the gameplay.

However, there are some criticisms that need to be mentioned. The performance issues and bugs at launch were frustrating for many players. Although patches have fixed many of these problems, the start was rocky.

The AI could perform better in some situations, especially in the campaign, where it sometimes makes illogical decisions. The balancing between factions is also not always perfect, leading to unfair situations.

Overall, "Total War: WARHAMMER III" is an impressive and comprehensive strategy game that, despite some technical issues and balancing problems, stands out for its depth and scope. For fans of the genre and the Warhammer universe, it is a must-play.

战锤3新DLC：CA的那谁限时回归！

其实挺感慨的，众所周知锤3先前的DLC是被骂得有多惨烈，在那段时间里，CA不知道是不是因为磕嗨了才做出错误的决策，使得锤3的DLC质量极其低下，并且加上为了回收成本，DLC的价格还相当于本体的三分之一，这种举动着实触怒了忠实的锤粉，还有发售后那些花里胡哨的BUG更伤害了锤粉们的感情。

幸运的是，新DLC腐烂王座的推出，使得CA的那谁限时回归，你看，用心还是能做好事情的不是嘛？

腐烂王座的到来，终于为那些旧世界的种族带来了黎明的曙光。坦白说，战锤3机制本就冗杂繁复，加上新世界那些有趣的玩法，使得许多新玩家觉得，哎嘿，新种族真牛逼嘿！而今能够借此机会将那些被玩家忽略已久的内容重新唤醒在世人前，实在是值得浮一大白。

哦，我亲爱的“墓园玫瑰”

本次DLC更新的了3个传奇势力，接下来有请我们帝国阵营的“墓园玫瑰”埃斯佩斯·冯·邓肯！咳咳，虽然埃斯佩斯女士虽然不是本次更新的正主，但是由于其优秀的素质，实在是令我为之心脏狂跳！哦，尊贵的来自努恩的黑色夫人，希望我能够用我的生命换取你一丝的笑容！

尊贵的埃斯佩斯女士恶名远播，当然，这只是针对帝国敌人的，在帝国敌人的眼中，她就像是潜居在墓园里研究着最邪恶最可怕魔法的黑暗女巫。事实上，埃斯佩斯女士确实在某些时候会痴迷做一些，嗯，不那么能够让人接受的实验，当然，强大的魔法实力是让她能够这么做的保障。很多时候，埃斯佩斯女士并不介意将自己的试验场带到战争前沿，用帝国的敌人来验证自己的可怕想法。

如果你只是以为光埃斯佩斯女士可怕，那就大错特错了，埃斯佩斯女士的坐骑，同样令帝国的敌人闻风丧胆，那是象征死亡与烈焰的红龙，当战争爆发的时候，埃斯佩斯女士骑乘在红龙背上，用手中的苍白镰刀无情地收割着敌人的生命，其惨烈度足以止小儿夜啼。其手中的苍白镰刀亦是一件不凡的发起，能够增强主人的法术控制力和抵抗力，并且会随着主人的使用而逐渐成长。最关键的是，身为大名鼎鼎的墓园玫瑰，当她受到伤害的时候（虽然这个时候很少），她能够直接汲取敌人的生命力来治愈自己，为此，许多人私底下偷偷怀疑她是否还是人类。目前没有人知道真相，因为将这个疑问诉之于口的人，早就在第二天就莫名其妙消失地无影无踪。

此外，埃斯佩斯女士带来的高速机动性相当有趣，允许玩家在帝国境内建造一个叫做莫尔花园的建筑，除了能够招募强力的兵种外，还可以让军队快速在花园之中穿行，随时驰援的机制能够震慑所有敢来侵犯的宵小！

还有我们尊贵的埃斯佩斯女士，拥有渊博的知识，能够使用帝国枪炮学院来强化帝国的火器部队，让这些钢铁洪流再度焕发出新生的光芒，这些知识能够增加弹丸数量、提高远程伤害、爆炸半径等等，让敌人再一次想起被帝国枪炮所支配的恐惧，那是从一片无硝烟中划过的无尽流星雨，将敌人撕成碎片！

信墓园玫瑰者，告别过去的细、短、小！

逃跑吧，如果你能跑出射程的话！

本次更新的马拉凯·马凯森，嗯，就非常适合新人入坑，除了马拉凯带来的强大武力外，矮人机制的变更也使古老的秩序种族从新时代牛鬼蛇神中杀出一条血路。马拉凯作为一名卓绝的工程师，能够给远程部队带来超强的增幅，可见其深谙什么叫做“真理在大炮的射程之内”。

让我们看下，曾经因为研发的产品过于极端（比如坚不可摧，只会爆炸的飞艇）而被驱逐的马拉凯能够给部队带来什么优势。吸取了过去的教训，马拉凯设计出了一系列更加成熟的战争机器，这些钢铁的大家伙能够确保如何以最高的效率去收割敌人的生命，并且拥有敦实的护甲确保自身能够从疯狂的混沌潮流中生存。

还可以凭借自己多年的心得让远程部队减少装填时间并提高准确性，甚至能通过技能大幅提高单位的远程伤害，可见，如果多年前马拉凯没有选择成为一名工程师，那么其肯定是一位足以名载史册的传奇射手，当然，那样矮人就会少一位天才发明家。

以上的加强还不是全部，马拉凯还带来了敌人从未见过的雷霆飞艇，这座令人望而生畏的空中钢铁堡垒就像是一个飞舞在空中的刺猬，或者说是豪猪，庞大的火力体系能够阻止所有敌人的接近，厚重的装甲能够防御绝大多数敌人的进攻，如果出现了那少数的情况，那么飞艇则可以使用特殊的方法，通过一些暴力手段短时间内大幅提速，总之，这是一种令所有敌人头疼的战争机器。

虽然马拉凯将矮人的实力提升到了一个新的高度，但或许关于仇恨机制的改变是更令玩家欣喜的，毫无疑问，新的仇恨机制更加鼓励矮人们去履行仇恨，以此获得相应奖励，矮人爱好者终于可以挺起腰板狠狠地将过去的新仇旧恨一并清算了。

杀了我，我将成为你

关于本次更新的真正主角塔木尔可汗，有着许多的传闻，有人说其是过去叱咤风云的库尔干可汗献给混沌四神的子嗣之一，后来得到了纳垢的青睐而成为了如今的塔木尔可汗，另外一种说法则只在小范围中流传，因为这个真相比较容易将人逼疯，那就是塔木尔可汗其实是一条丑陋狞恶的巨型变异尸蛆，在当年混沌荒原的永恒战场中，其吞噬了无尽的血肉，汲取了数不清的力量，最后成为了如今的模样。

当不管怎么说，没有人会在直面大名鼎鼎的蛆虫之主·塔木尔可汗的时候不被吓得尿裤子。其强大的实力和残忍无比的性格，让其成为了纳垢的双花红棍，并且荣获了各种赐福，这使得它愈加强大。

我们可怖的蛆虫之主拥有着超绝的耐力，不仅是因为其强大的身体素质，更是因为纳垢的赐福，勇士，你最后祈祷不会在战场上遇见这个可怕的肉山。同时，蛆虫之主强大的身体素质还为他带来了卓绝的战斗能力，一斧头下去没有劈不断的东西，如果有，那就两斧子，再加上塔木尔可汗骑乘的蟾蜍龙，一整个在战场肆虐的肉坦，或者说移动的绞肉机，超高的杀戮效率会让所有和它战斗的敌人迅速丧失战斗意志。

然而，更可怕的是塔木尔可汗所拥有的特技，也是因此才有其第二种身份的猜想，那就是当塔木尔可汗阵亡的时候，它会对击杀低于一定血量阈值的敌人，从而寄宿在其体内重新加入战场！事实上，塔木尔可汗现在的身躯就曾经属于恶名昭著的食人魔暴君卡拉卡·碎山。

此外，蛆虫之主可以消耗统治力来招募氏族长，当招募单位忠诚增加的时候，塔木尔可汗可以获得各方面的提升，最终在终焉的战场上，为纳垢带来血肉的祭礼。

和矮人一样，纳垢的机制同样有所改变。

诚意满满，值得一试

总的来说，“腐烂王座”DLC为《全面战争：战锤3》带来了全新的游戏体验。从游戏内容到机制更新再到角色设计，“腐烂王座”都展现出了开发团队的诚意和实力。这次更新不仅解决了帝国和矮人在游戏中的劣势地位问题，也提升了游戏的整体体验。对于喜欢《全面战争：战锤3》的玩家来说，“腐烂王座”绝对是一个值得一试的DLC。

然而，“腐烂王座”也存在一些不足之处。例如，在某些细节上还有待打磨，部分机制还需要进一步完善。但这些问题并不会影响玩家对这款DLC的整体评价。毕竟，“腐烂王座”为《全面战争：战锤3》带来了如此多的新内容和新体验（尤其是相比起过去的DLC），已经足以让玩家们为之买单了。

Est ce que je peux décemment dire que le jeu est mauvais avec autant d'heure de jeu dessus ? Je ne pense pas.

Pour avoir découvert la saga total war warhammer et l'univers warhammer avec cette opus j'avoue être tombé amoureux du jeu très rapidement. L'univers est riche les roasters aussi, c'est beau visuellement et les heures de jeux ne sont pas compter. Je trouve sincèrement que c'est un des meilleurs 4X de ces dernières années. 

Points positifs :

-Visuellement le jeu est beau pour l'échelle des cartes, les animations sont propres.
-Musique et sound design réussit et immersif
-Beaucoup d'heures de contenue de disponible ( même sans les DLC )
-Un contenu très étoffé avec la multitude de DLCs disponibles avec des gameplay variés
-Un multijoueur très appréciable

Points négatifs :

- Quelques bugs à droite à gauche qui peuvent être frustrant ( Pathfinding parfois au fraise dans les cités )
- Obligé de mettre le jeu sur SSD minimum ou le jeu est vraiment lent au niveau des temps de chargement
- Une IA très irrégulière en bataille
- La campagne royaume du chao qui n'est pas forcément très intéressante à refaire comparé à la campagne  empire immortel

Toutefois le jeu reste exceptionnel en terme de travail, certes investir dans tout les DLC n'est pas forcément très encourageant, mais rien n'y oblige et cela peu être fait au fur et à mesure sur les contenus qui vous intéresse vraiment. Même si tout les DLC ne sont pas de la même qualités, la majorité restent bon voir excellent, c'est à voir au cas par cas. Et malgré les problèmes et les polémiques passées du studio je ne peux m'empêcher d'apprécier le travail et l'investissement qu'il propose pour redorer leur blason en proposant des DLC certes cher mais ambitieux, et un contenu gratuit qui reste qualitatif. C'est un excellent total war et malgré la phase d'apprentissage qui peut être très longue le plaisir d'évoluer sur le jeu est indéniable.

Despite having so much pay walled content, Warhammer III often pairs their DLC content with free updates, free reworks, and free factions and units. Schade, dass die Warhammer-Community so negativ ist. Für mich ists eines der tollsten Strategiespiele ever, ich habe gut 1500 Stunden darin versenkt, meinen Steam-Account verloren und mir ein Jahr später alles noch einmal gekauft, trotz des heftigen Preises. Heftiger Preis? Japp, denn Immortal Empires, die "Weltkarte", die alle drei Teile des Spiels vereint, setzt voraus, dass man auch alle drei Spiele besitzt. Puh. Kauft im Sale! Mag das zu Release des zweiten Teils noch als nettes Feature gedacht gewesen sein, ist es heute DER Grund schlechthin, das Spiel zu spielen. Dazu kommen auch noch zahllose DLCs, das mag abschrecken - aber halt, sind die jetzt wirklich etwas schlechtes? Ich finde nicht. Aber eins nach dem anderen.

Warhammer 3: Immortal Empires bietet eine riesige Weltkarte mit Anfangs ~290 Fraktionen, 99 davon sind mittlerweile spielbar. Aufgeteilt auf über ein Dutzend verschiedene Völker, die sich alle mehr oder weniger (teils radikal!) unterschiedlich spielen, die alle jeweils noch einmal über verschiedene Anführer verfügen, die wiederum einzigartige Einheiten und Mechaniken mitbringen. 

Ich bin eigentlich eher ein Fan der historischen Titel, oder dachte ich zumindest. Zum Glück habe ich dem Spiel trotzdem einen Versuch gegeben. So begann ich mein erstes Spiel mit den Bretonen - man stelle sich eine Mischung aus mittelalterlichen Franzosen mit einer Prise "Ritter der Tafelrunde"-Folklore vor. Trebuches, Bogenschützen, Schwert- und Speerkämpfer und eine Kavallerie dazu , so weit, so bekannt aus anderen Total War-Teilen. Nur: Wie langweilig war es bitte in vorherigen Teilen, einfach nur gegen andere Bogenschützen/Schwertkämpfer/Pipapo zu kämpfen? 

In Warhammer mache ich das Anfangs vielleicht auch, erstmal gilt es ja, das eigene Königreich gegen diverse andere bretonische Lords zu behaupten. Aber dann wird es schnell wild. Ich kämpfe mit Waldelfen, die mit Baummenschen Breschen in meine Infanterie schlagen und aus der Luft mit Riesenadlern angreifen. Ich kämpfe gegen eine Flut an Orks und Goblins, dann gegen Vampire und ihre untoten Horden. Gegen Oger, Zwerge, ägyptisch angehauchte Gruftkönige mit wandelnden Riesensphynxen. Gegen Echsenmenschen mit Dinosauriern (lol). Zum Glück sind die Hochelfen mittlerweile meine Verbündeten und erlauben mir, ihre Truppen auszuleihen, denn Wikinger mit Eistrollen und Mammuts fallen aus dem Norden ein, während die schwarzen Archen der Dunkelelfen, schwimmende Festungen sozusagen, an meinen Küsten auftauchen. Hab ich schon von den Rattenmenschen erzählt, die im Untergrund hausen und mich in furchterregenden Massen überfallen? Rattenmenschen mit Gatling Guns, wohlgemerkt...

Die schiere Vielfalt, die Liebe zum Detail bei einem abnormalen Umfang, all das in einem relativ einsteigerfreundlichen, aber doch fordernden Strategiespiel mit Echtzeitschlachten? Mir fällt nichts vergleichbares ein, 12/10 recommend!

___

Die Rattenmenschen (Skaven) gehören übrigens mittlerweile zu meinen Lieblingsvölkern. Die Ratten sind hillarious! Ich mag ihre Voicelines, ihren Soundtrack, selbst die verrückte Ästhetik ihrer Truppen und vor allem ihr Gamedesign, denn hier wird es anspruchsvoller. Hier baue ich nicht nur meine Städte aus, ich baue auch mein Under-Empire, also Städte unter den Städten der Gegner. Meine Ratten sind immer hungrig, und es sind viele. Neben Geld auch Essen zu managen ist daher ein wichtiges Feature; habe ich zu wenig Nahrung, drohen Aufstände und meine Krieger laufen davon. Habe ich viel Nahrung, kann ich dagegen allerlei damit anstellen, zum Beispiel zusätzliche Truppen in der Schlacht spawnen lassen. Braucht man auch, denn die Rattenmenschen sind feige und schwach und rennen meist weg, wenn sie nur scharf angeschaut werden. Lieber aus dem Hinterhalt angreifen (Hrr Hrr), besser auf Masse setzen. Anfangs zumindest, denn währenddessen züchte ich im Hintergrund mächtige Rattenoger und bastle an der Warpfire-Bombe - sozusagen das Warhammer-Equivalent zur Nuke. Großartig!

Für all das braucht man keinen DLC. Es gibt zig spannende, jeweils einzigartige Kampagnen mit hohem Wiederspielwert (klar, jeder hat seine Favoriten bzw. mag die eine oder andere nicht), jede einzelne kann leicht 10-20 Stunden dauern. Dazu kommt noch die eigentliche Warhammer 3-Kampagne, die ebenfalls sehr gut ist, aber einen deutlich geringeren Wiederspielwert besitzt. Wer dann, und damit meine ich: nach +250 Stunden, immer noch so begeistert ist, dass er mehr will - well, der freut sich dann so wie ich, dass es all die DLCs gibt, die eben noch einmal neue Völker spielbar machen. 

Und damit zurück zum Anfang: Ich empfehle, dieses Spiel nicht als "puh, das brauch ich alles?? wie frech!" zu betrachten, sondern stattdessen erstmal einfach einzusteigen und sich dann, wenn es einem eben gefällt", wow, das gibt es alles? wie cool!" zu denken. Dass ein Großteil der Spieler, die hier negativ werten, es auf mehrere hundert Stunden Spielzeit gebracht haben, spricht glaube ich für sich.

It's sad to see how far this series has fallen since the days of Medieval 2. I'm not even talking about all the features that have been removed over the years. Or the shrinking number of playable factions. I'm not talking about the poor gameplay design that sees huge numbers of units become immune to the key gameplay mechanic of the series, which has simultaneously been crippled by the damage bonus to broken units being reduced to almost nothing.

I'm talking about just basic functionality as a computer program. How often does it crash to desktop? Every few hours. How often does it freeze? Several times a turn. Does it stay on the menu you select? No. But even all that might be tolerable if it weren't for the load times. They're so bad that you end up avoiding playing the battles just so you won't have to sit through two more five minute load screens for each one. And if you're doing that, then you end up playing it like a 4X game, which it was never meant to be and so it doesn't have the complexity to be enjoyable that way. So then you're just slogging along not getting anything out of it, until you give up. And for all the massive patches that come out every few months none of them seem to care about fixing any of the problems that keep it from being fun.

There's so much to love about this series, so much that it has done well. But this game just doesn't pull it off. It really is sad.

It depends if you already like the wh2 formula then wh3 should not be worse and will give you more contents and some QOL. But if you don't like wh2 formula, wh3 changes may not be enough to make you love this game.
Also i can sum the main difference from the 2 games as you can decide if you find it worth it:
-Realm of chaos campaign map replace the vortex some like it some hate it (I do like it but it bored me faster than vortex since survival battles are the same at each playthrough)
-Survival battles are a new special battle mod that you can do in custom or in some quest battles or through the realm of chaos campaign in order to claim Daemon souls it involve using tickets to improve your units, replenish their life, amo wind of magic, building wall towers and call reinforcement
-Siege battles now use supply tickets that allow the defender to build wall and towers during the battle, attackers can capture some area to reduce the ticket output. Some like it some hate it(i find it better than game 2 but still need big improvement in siege battles imo like remove pocket ladders and polish units pathing, also they should make wall more wide)
-Mp battles have a new mod call domination where you can win by holding control area and where you call reinforcement from your reinforcement pull(chosen before the match) in exchange of tickets that you earn passively. Some love it some hate it(I love it it's less blind counter than standard battles and more manageable since you don't start with a too big army)
-Authority now give some buff/debuff depending of how much you are high on/low of and somewhat stay stable by itself by nerfing the gain of autho when too high and buffing when too low. (Most people hate it and i find it meh like progressive buff/debuff is cool but autoregulation make stabilize his empire trivial so too ez to snowball)
-Corruption is now trivial to clean or spread so it's not rly a mechanic anymore except for the attrition stuff when fighting in foreign realms
-Wind of magic gain has been revamp in a good way even if few people still don't like it
-Auxilaries and items can now be fused to improve their tiers and you earn plenty of them(it's a little too much imo since it's time consuming to manage them every turn)
-Character level cap is increased from 35 to 50 but some char don't have enough skill node to have any effect above a certain level... (It's bad for me as it means you have all skills anyway so not rly choice and it makes char even more op)
-Older faction such as DE, Empire, Dwarves and Chaos warriors have been reworked and it's mostly better than before esp for CW even if imo they became too op and rely too much on vassal which is a bugged feature in all TTW except if you use mods to fix it.
-The game has now a ton of mods both new and imported from previous game, some of them have a rly high quality
-9 New races playable with mostly funnier campaign mechanics than older races even if not balanced enough so every faction are op except kislev, tzentch and ogres :p
-2 new mini campaign game mod available on mp only one pve coop oriented (2 players kislev vs nurrgle and one pvp FFA oriented map with a score based map where after the turn 50 the player with the most points win the game)
-In game prologue is cool and the most narrative thing we have in total war xD even if he doesn't rly teach you enough how the true campaign work imo

The previous games and DLCs constantly go on sale. Unlike other games where my time and money are wasted when they release a new one, this title carries it over. My previous game experience and dlc helps me in the newer one. I see complaints that it is a high hurdle to play the newest game but honestly every faction isn't for everyone. Why wouldn't you buy the 3rd game for sale as it has gone on multiple times and get your feet wet before deciding to drop a bunch of money on DLC you might not even like? You don't need any of the DLC's to play the game and if you just really really love dwarves you can pick those up and who needs the rest? 

As of writing this, the game is on sale for 50% off, the barrier of entry is 30$. Find who you love and go from there. I am a major fan of the Undead factions and have been awaiting Nagash for far too many years now. I expect my playtime will double after his release. When Tomb Kings, Vampires, and Vampire Coast get more DLC I will probably buy it with no hesitation. Is it perfect? No.  Is it expensive?  Yes (Make sure sure you get it on sale since with all DLC it's $400 USD).

It's also the most comprehensive Total War simulator of an entire IP (Warhammer Fantasy) we'll probably ever see.  Years of work have gone into this franchise so the approximately $230 USD (on sale) price tag is absolutely justified.  I've spent 1400-1500 hours playing this trilogy, something I have never and will never again do with a single player game.  The sheer scope of different factions and play styles is refreshing and brings me back time after time.

Is it frustrating sometimes? sure.  There are bugs, units won't do what you want during battles, it feels like the AI cheats sometimes, the list goes on.  None of that can take away from the thrill of discovering a new faction or mechanic and charging into battle with their unique rosters!

Creative Assembly isn't perfect either.  They've definitely gotten lazy at times during the development but hopefully as of May of 2024, they've come to appreciate the past success and future potential of the Total War Warhammer Trilogy.  In my opinion, this series is something special and if this genre of grand strategy is your cup of tea, do yourself a favor and try TWWH.

For those who are familiar with the previous two Total War Warhammer games, this one has finally reached the level of quality we came to expect at the end of Total War Warhammer 2. Those of us of who were here at the beginning had to suffer through all sorts of bumps and burns along the way as the developers struggled to keep the game stable, along with adding in new content and balancing out the old. To put it mildly, it was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. And the less we speak about the DLC controversies, the better. The point is that after the tidal wave of complaints and backlash, Creative Assembly have finally managed to drag the game where it should have been at launch.

To those of you who are new to the whole franchise? This is a turn-based/real-time strategy game based on the Games Workshop's long running Warhammer Fantasy universe (one they've yet to try and ♥♥♥♥ up with their DEI bullcrap). Unlike most other Total War games, this one is set in a fantasy setting, where they've mixed normal troops you've come to expect in the series with magic, monsters and whatnot. The game also offers a rather robust character system that gives the game's lords and heroes light RPG-elements, as you level them up and open up new skills and abilities for them. The game has two campaign modes - one set in the smaller more story-driven map and another free-for-all massive world map that actually consists of the entire world of Warhammer Fantasy. There are 24 different factions in the game, and almost each of them play so differently from each other that when you play with them, you'll feel like you're playing a different game each time you switch a faction. Also, in some cases within a faction you might have lords - your main hero you play as - that when compared to the rest of the lords within the faction can feel like they don't just flip the board; they change it completely. The best way to familiarize yourself with what this game is like is to go and watch some gameplay videos on YouTube if you're unsure if this game is for you, but the only way to be sure is to actually play it yourself. The big issue I have - and many others - is that vast majority of the old factions are locked away unless you own the previous two games and have bought their DLCs. This sucks big time, but it is what is. If you do buy the game and like it, I highly recommend looking into them and buying the ones that interest you the most. I'd recommend buying them on sale, because they can be bit expensive in some cases.

Since I've been a fan of the franchise for over thirty years now, I've bought them all - even the bad ones, or ones that were bad when they first launched. CA's have been busy fixing those that were broken or lacking in some ways, and now - for the first time in Warhammer 3 - I feel most factions and lords are beginning to feel like they're balanced.

Playing the game with friends can be fun, but if you play the campaign mode, I need to stress the fact that the game can get tad slow the further into the campaign you get - as you will inevitably expand and have more and more armies on the map, and more battles you need to deal with. If that doesn't bother you, then this just might be the strategy game for you.

[h1] 新版本《腐烂王座》能否让褒贬不一的《全战3》重新翻身？[/h1]
《全战3》作为一款经典游戏，想必大家都不会陌生，最近推出了全新版本《腐烂王座》并首次将DLC拆成了三份分别售卖，方便玩家根据自己的喜好进行购入，三款DLC分别为帝国阵营的“埃斯佩斯·冯·邓肯”、矮人阵营的“马拉凯·马凯森”以及纳垢阵营的“塔木尔可汗”。
	这三位领主分别有各自独特的能力与自身所独有的、强大的派系效果，帮助玩家来更快的组建部队，下面就来为大家一一介绍下三位传奇领主。
[h1]【墓园玫瑰】“埃斯佩斯·冯·邓肯”[/h1]
 
“埃斯佩斯·冯·邓肯”是一位强大的法师，坐骑是一条猩红龙，选择这位传奇领主后，可以解锁【帝国枪炮学校】强化炮兵与火药部队，并且通过【紫晶军械库】招募到专属的紫晶部队。同时该领主还可以在任意城市中建造【莫尔花园】，通过进入莫尔花园页面，可以花费金币传送到任意花园中，实现快速移动。
 
[h1]【蛆虫之主】“塔木尔可汗”[/h1]
作为纳垢势力的领主，“塔木尔可汗”的相貌可以说更容易让人接受，作为一名近战型领主，身披盔甲手持巨斧，更像是一位兽人战士。当等级达到15级时获得坐骑“布勃博洛斯”，一头威猛的科莫多巨兽，这时的“塔木尔可汗”甚至有了一些帅气~~完全可以凭借一己之力大量杀伤敌军。
 
该领主的特色是可以招募氏族长，这些氏族长相较普通英雄更加的强大，玩家只需不停的战斗，累计足够的霸权就可以进行解锁，这些氏族长全都有各自的特色，如第一位【玷污者】凯兹克，天生就骑乘“腐烂兽”同时还携带紫色武器与紫色护符，是玩家强大的助力~！
 
当解锁氏族长后，还可以继续消耗霸权来解锁其氏族专属部队。

[h1]矮人“马拉凯·马凯森”[/h1]
提到矮人，大家脑海中一定会浮现那些身材矮小，留着大胡子喝着啤酒的矿工与火枪手。而这位传奇领主“马拉凯·马凯森”却是将属性点点在了科技上，作为一位发明家，他为矮人带来了【飞艇】这一强大的战争机器。类似于海盗的船，玩家可以对【飞艇】进行升级从而达到可以随时随地的招募部队。
 
同时作为一位传奇领主，“马拉凯·马凯森”还可以开启自己的专属冒险，通过冒险打败预期的敌人，为部队进行升级。
 
整体看，飞艇的随时补兵外加完成冒险的能力提升，“马拉凯·马凯森”的部队相较其他矮人领主能力更加的强悍，并且有更强的作战持久力。

[h1]总结[/h1]
此次【腐烂王座】版本的更新相较之前无疑是比较成功的，将DLC拆成三部分也可以减少玩家花费的“马内”只要购买自己喜欢的领主即可。同时这三位领主的能力也是有目共睹，确实做出来各自的特色。
个人比较喜欢【蛆虫之主】和【矮人】出生点的位置比较有利，发展起来没有太多的障碍。当然并不是说帝国弱，骑上猩红龙的女王还是蛮帅的。
目前DLC还没有折扣，但45元的价格还是可以接受，选一个最钟爱的先入手玩起来，其余的等折扣也是个不错的选择~~~

Graphismes et Ambiance

Les graphismes sont superbes, avec des paysages variés et des unités détaillées. L'ambiance sonore est immersive, renforçant l'impression d'être plongé dans un monde épique.

Gameplay et Stratégie

Le gameplay reste fidèle à la série, avec des batailles en temps réel passionnantes et une gestion stratégique en mode campagne. Chaque faction a ses propres forces et styles de jeu, offrant une grande variété et une rejouabilité élevée.

Nouveautés et Améliorations

Les nouvelles factions comme les Royaumes du Chaos, Kislev et Cathay ajoutent des mécaniques de jeu uniques. La carte de campagne est vaste et offre de nombreuses possibilités de conquête.

Multijoueur et Communauté

Le mode multijoueur est amélioré avec plus d'options de personnalisation et de coopération. La communauté est active, ce qui promet de nombreux contenus additionnels et mises à jour.

Conclusion

Total War: Warhammer III est un excellent jeu de stratégie qui ravira les fans de la série et les amateurs de l'univers Warhammer. Avec ses graphismes impressionnants, son gameplay profond et ses nombreuses nouveautés, c'est un must pour tous les amateurs de jeux de stratégie.

Note : 9/10

En résumé, Total War: Warhammer III offre des heures de plaisir stratégique et des batailles épiques mémorables.

As a veteran player, I always play on the hardest difficulty, and some factions offer a truly unique and distinct experience that wasn’t present in earlier installments. This forces you to rethink your strategy and even restart the campaign to figure out how to succeed with a faction that cannot win in direct combat. Well, it can fight, but victory will be out of reach unless you master its specific mechanics.

However, there are downsides too. Without mods, the game doesn’t look as good as it could. One particularly disappointing aspect is the absence of "little people" who used to simulate life in the game, making the map feel rather lifeless and lacking atmosphere.

On the bright side, the developers recently released a new DLC, which brought a much-needed rework to the Empire. This is a significant improvement that really changes the gameplay experience. And if the team continues to listen to player feedback, the game definitely has great potential for success.

Overall, the game is worth checking out, but it could benefit from more attention to detail, especially visually. If you enjoy challenging gameplay and interesting mechanics, this game might be a great fit for you, especially with mods.

Я провел немало времени за этой игрой и прошел множество интересных моментов. Хотя базовая ("ванильная") версия не вызвала у меня особого восторга, важно отметить, что новые механики и карты в этой части действительно впечатляют. Разработчики сделали серьёзный шаг вперёд в плане разнообразия геймплея.

Стоит понимать, что игра, особенно за некоторые фракции, может оказаться довольно сложной. Я как опытный игрок всегда выбираю максимальный уровень сложности, и некоторые фракции предоставляют уникальный и самобытный опыт, которого раньше не было в серии. Это заставляет переосмысливать тактику и даже рестартить кампанию, чтобы понять, как пройти за фракцию, которая не способна побеждать в прямом бою. Здесь нужно уметь пользоваться уникальными механиками каждой фракции для достижения победы.

Однако, есть и недостатки. Без модификаций игра выглядит не так привлекательно, как могла бы. Особенно огорчает отсутствие "маленьких человечков", которые симулировали жизнь в игре в прошлых частях. Это делает карту довольно безжизненной и не такой атмосферной, как хотелось бы.

Но есть и положительные моменты — ребята из команды разработчиков выпустили новое DLC, в котором мы получили очень важный реворк Империи. Это большое улучшение, которое действительно меняет восприятие игры. И если разработчики будут прислушиваться к отзывам игроков и дальше, игра определённо имеет все шансы на успех.

В целом, игра достойна внимания, но хотелось бы видеть больше деталей и проработки, особенно в визуальном аспекте. Если вы любите вызовы и интересные механики, то эта игра может вам понравиться, особенно с модами.

[h1] 生人勿近外表下的桥梁 [/h1]
《全面战争》系列虽然已经有多部作品，但老实说，在《全面战争：三国》之前，国内的大部分玩家对该系列的印象仅仅是停留在“听过，但没玩过”。最根本的原因可能在于，战略游戏所共同存在的高上手门槛，一副生人勿近的模样很难让人起亲近的心思，被现实压力压得对待游戏都只能有忙里偷闲、小小放松一下的玩家，也不想在游戏内再被复杂的系统教育一通

而实际上，《全面战争：战锤3》也算得上是系列中最繁杂的机制了，特别是中古战锤本身题材相较于其他背景的系列作更加的有了自由创作的空间，本身桌面游戏的复杂规则尽管在游戏内得以简化，但管中窥豹的一点点种族大熔炉也足够复杂

简单来看，单单战锤所具备的种族差异构筑的系统复杂度也足够令人头疼，不同单位以及侧重方向决然不同的战术对策、不同英雄庞大的法术和技能、随之带来的大地图之上的不同的经济养成系统，这一切都构成了基于种族而产生的特殊机制和完全不同的玩法内容。这也就是为什么在社交平台几百小时的玩家也总是称自己只是一个初入门径的老手，每次重开一次对局，游玩一次新种族，《全面战争：战锤3》都能给玩家带来相当新奇的游戏体验

可玩性高固然是件好事，但从一体两面的角度看，玩家往往需要花上足够多的时间才能逐步领会游戏机制，感受到游戏的醇厚魅力，而作为新入坑玩家面前的丰富内容却反而容易成为拦路虎

在这种情况下，《全面战争：战锤3》堪称之为教科书级别的序章教程就显得格外重要。它不仅仅是将游戏内容填鸭式的传递给玩家，而是通过数小时的时长、根据恢弘世界观序幕的一角引导玩家根据剧情发展一点点的熟悉并活用游戏内容。也正是在这润物细无声的引导下，玩家在经过几小时的游玩，总会发现在初看颇显晦涩的游玩内容逐渐显得有章可循，甚至天赋异禀的玩家还能挖掘到一些更细微之处的玩法。而作为“战锤”系列的第三部作品，在剧情以及世界观的引导上，时刻穿插的对话文本和精美的CG演绎，对于新入坑的玩家而言，通过作品之间的精巧衔接，也不总是容易升起畏难情绪

[h1] 种族大熔炉 [/h1]
虽然自动战斗仍是不喜即时战术玩法的玩家的最佳选择，但这更多的仅是在实力对比相差悬殊时比较适用，而在实力相当或是想要以弱胜强，数值博弈则显然不够看。并且，作为可以说《全面战争》系列最具特色的一模块内容，一味的选择跳过战斗可能对游玩体验也会造成伤害

而相对于其他的即时战术游戏，《全面战争》系列虽然也存在一些需要玩家细微操作之处，但更多的是集中在玩家对排兵布阵、地形和兵种克制的运用上，而不用对于一些资源的经济性拉扯搞得战术变得不再发挥更为重要的效果

相对于其他《全面战争》游戏由于历史背景不能最大化脑洞，中古战锤本身的奇幻色彩给了“战锤”最大的发挥空间，英雄的各种夸张技能和法术、除了最为基础的近战、远程以及骑兵外更为细化的兵种单位划分、不同种族带来差异化明显的局内大方向的战术选择，让不同喜好的玩家都能在游戏中找到心仪的单位，并让它们大放异彩

[h1] 砸吧砸吧 [/h1]
《全面战争》系列一向以慢热著称，它的乐趣并不在某天某时某刻的突然鸡血，而是贯穿在玩家可能长达数月里上百小时、在熟悉机制后不断克服游戏内出现难题的成就感。中古战锤的奇幻背景和在前两作作品的经验积累下，《全面战争：战锤3》的丰厚内容所呈现的巨量内容让它成为一部绝对值得在长时间里慢慢品味的作品

全面战争：战锤3——史诗级战场纷争，你来扮演上帝！
命运大典，揭示了过去、现在与未来的诸多秘密。相传，只要能得到它，便能获得支配世界的力量。
但没人知道，拥有这本大典的人将会遭受怎样的诅咒。它规定了：能熟练使用该书的人，只能服务于他人。现在，这本书将世界分裂，化成碎片化的机会吸引着不同的种族前来争夺利益，选择你的队伍，在群雄争霸中大展拳脚吧！
初次接触全面战争系列便是最新的第三代，实打实的讲，操作压力着实不小，这就好比将学者置身于宽敞的图书馆一般，五车之书，半山之文，慌乱之中根本不知从何入手。
幸好系统为新入坑的玩家提供了序章战役，在循序渐见中为玩家的征程保驾护航，引导玩家一步步熟悉这片大陆上的战争法则。
在战役模式中，共分为3大篇章，序章为新手教学篇，引导玩家快速熟悉规则；中篇为混沌魔域篇，鼓励玩家扮演任意种族开始一场规模宏大的世界战争；末篇为巨型沙盒，为玩家提供纯粹的，开放世界战略游戏目标，这也意味着，此时的玩家已经具备了操作全面战争世界的能力。

⭐指挥作战，不单单靠人海战术
在通常情况下，作战队伍之间的人数差距绝对是影响战局胜负的关键因素，但绝不是唯一，如果纯粹靠人海战术取得胜利，玩家亦不会有很大的成就感。
兵种：以斧兵、矛兵、剑士为代表的近战士兵，单兵作战能力强，适合相互厮杀；以弓箭手、火枪手、飞行孽妖等单位为代表的远程兵，适合躲藏在队伍后方，在敌人奔袭的过程中不断消耗其有生力量；骑兵适合冲阵，矛兵适合反冲锋，远程输出高，但惧怕近战士兵的突袭，兵种与兵种之间相互克制，互相制衡。
领主：不同种族的领主拥有各自不同的天赋技能以及主动技能，这些技能对与战场的局势改变也有一定的作用。要么在破釜沉舟之际提升士气，要么在作战途中利用范围法术对敌方重要兵种进行减员。
作战获胜、或者完成特殊任务目标后，领主都会获得对应奖励，种族不同，获得奖励的方式也不尽相同；人类领主可能会获得战甲、武器、随从等，而混沌恶魔则会得到4方魔神的馈赠，为自身的头部、胸部、尾巴、腿部等身体部件进行强化。
领主综合能力强大，一旦身败离场，战役即将宣告结束。
相关数值：武器威力、近战攻击与近战防御，在原有固定命中率的基础上，兵牌战力在综合计算后的总命中率也会影响其作战能力，护甲强度、破甲值、物理抗性、魔法抗性等，都充分证明了本作在数值面板体系上有着近乎严格的计算流程。
阵型：你可以随心所欲的将小队编成自己想要的阵型，一般来说，系统默认的“一字长蛇阵”是中规中矩的模式，但该阵型队伍调动过慢，在人数众多时还可能会引发单位之间的碰撞；是故，各项均衡的正方形矩阵更加适合情况多变的战场。
战术：地形的影响，可能为某些兵种带来难以预估的好处，尽可能扬长避短，用己所长来取得优势。率先清理掉对我方团队威胁性最大的兵种，利用阵型来为远程兵创造良好的输出环境，及时使用领主技能提振士气或清理战场，阻止地方增援部队前来扰乱阵型等，都是不错的战略思路，在均势局尤为重要。

⭐治大国如烹小鲜
总的来说，单次战役不过是整场战争的一个缩影，一个转折点，在大部分时间内，我们还需要扮演上帝，一面纵观全局，一面为自己的势力谋划未来。
拥有第一座主城后，除了接下来要完成的既定任务，你还应该为辛苦建立起的家业保驾护航。
外交：利用外交界面洞悉周边版图范围内与己方交好的势力，努力发展关系，争取未来合并为一体；同时维持与中立势力的关系，尽可能用条约来束缚他们，这样，便可以大刀阔斧地对敌对势力展开进攻。
前期的思路当然是能交好切勿交恶，在自身实力弱小的情况下，韬光养晦至关重要，在干掉敌对势力后便要潜下心来，暗中搞发展；如果出现关系非常要好的势力，待时机成熟后便可通过外交手段劝其入伙，也就是我们口中所说的“收编”。如此，不费一兵一卒，不刀剑染血便可扩大势力，何乐而不为。
战略同盟、通行权、互不侵犯条约等，都是外交的手段，中立势力会根据你的综合实力来为他们的条件增加/扣除砝码。（比如，对方主动愿意在支付1200单位金币的基础上换得和平条约）
版图观察：当本回合结束后，世界上其他区域的势力也会做出相应动作，如果看到敌对势力方向向我方派出了英雄，那么一定要做出相应举措应对。
发展：主城及其他城镇都可以在属于玩家的回合内进行发展，升级建筑是最有效的途径之一。
如果觉得当前战力不够，那就招募第二位领主及军队，开辟新的战线，由于人口过剩的缘故，领主在城邦中招募的速度及成本都划算很多；
倘若军队的维持费用过高，从而产生赤字，则根据需要，可以适当削减领主麾下不太重要的兵种，直到扭亏为盈。或者，升级集市等能够直接增加税收的建筑物，也能改变窘状。如果阶段性任务目标是信仰强度，那么建造些教堂、信仰森林之类的，也无伤大雅。
总之，你侧重于哪方面的建筑，它就会在对应领域回馈于你。要么建筑费用减少，要么部队补员速度提升，根据实际情况，可以将建筑侧重点均匀分布在各个城镇中。
行军状态：不同的行军状态决定不同的属性加成。如果着急赶路，或者去救援，则可使用“强行军”状态，虽然会有疲劳惩罚，但兵贵神速；如果周围没有城镇，在部队减员的情况下可以用安营状态来恢复补员；而如果你预知了敌人动向及路线后，可以用“埋伏”状态改变队伍，这样，在战斗伊始，己方便处于优势之中。
科技：无需赘述，无论是某某部队战力+？，亦或是领主统领力+？，都是百利无一害的选项，选择当前环境下最需要获得的科技，等待几回合后研发成功即可。
英雄：不可多得的宝贝战力。有的放在城邦能增收、增员、增发展，放在野外能搞破袭，刺杀敌方前来“阻挠补员速度”的奸细，收编在自己的部队中，英雄们也是不错的战力。  

⭐宏大史诗级战场
这个绝对是本系列值得肯定的地方。只要打响战斗后，点击屏幕左下角的“战争视角”，便可近距离观看双方厮杀的过程，玩家可以自由的进行视角调换和视角缩放，第一时间掌握战局情况。
人类弓箭手的漫天箭雨，骑兵的野蛮冲撞，巨人、冰熊的振臂一挥，色孽投弹手、震旦炎龙炮的弹幕攻击...每一秒都有生物被撞飞，每一刻都能听见金铁交鸣之音。个体在战场上显得是如此渺小，哪怕是领主，如果不看头顶上的圆形徽标，也会被淹没在茫茫铁骑内。
在攻城战时，你还能看到早已就位的工程梯被交替掩护着带向敌方城墙之上。率先用弓箭手解决掉驻防守军后，工程提便可顺利贴靠墙面，兵力能源源不断通过云梯输送至城内，而此时的侧面战场，我方伏兵也给予了敌方援军当头一击，在领主的勇气咆哮下，胜利就在眼前。

⭐庞大且丰富的种族兵团
也可以近似的理解为曾经红色警戒中的诸国，只不过这里用种族来替代了。
每个种族都有其独特的背景故事及对应兵种，各自擅长的领域也有所不同。以华夏文明为原型的震旦天朝不仅需要快速平息本土兽人的侵袭，还要时刻提防着外面的混沌四神，本土老鼠人倒反天罡，企图大兴杀戮之道，震旦天朝以龙炮开路，玉弓手输出为先手，派龙马骑士及盾兵截杀，战事连绵不休；
信奉混沌四神，野心庞大的混沌恶魔生来便长得骇人听闻。每当有一座城池陷落，它们都会将其先给四神之一，以得到恐虐、色孽、纳垢以及奸奇的赠礼，哪个魔神得到的赠礼多，你的魔王得到的部位强化就多（有可能还会得到一条长着巨型大嘴的蛇头尾巴）；
头脑简单、四肢发达，善于作战做苦力却不善于经营势力的巨型蜥蜴人，还有集合疾病与脏乱于一身的鼠人，它们向来不受人待见。老鼠人的发家史本也不光彩，从不刚正面，只会打远程，铺天盖地硫酸雨，猥琐偷袭数第一；
还有我们最熟悉的基斯里夫——这个信奉祖国母亲，信奉凶神厄孙的冰雪民族。虽然是架空历史，但给我的感觉就像是中世纪的魔改维京人（可他们的其中一位领主又叫女沙皇）。故事的序章讲的就是基斯里夫族群一位领袖率军冒险，拯救被困凶神的事情。
如果所有种族都介绍一遍，篇幅恐怕冗杂且长，暂且先到这里，况且，以本作内容庞大的程度，远不是我一篇文章便能讲清的。

正如网上提到过的，《全面战争：战锤3》是一部非常宏大的即时战略类游戏，你可以把它看作是“文明6+三国志+红色警戒的融合体”。试想一下，当恶魔、兽人、矮人、人类、精灵、食人魔、吸血鬼等各式各样的部队集结在某片荒原上时，打起仗来是何等的惊心动魄、气势恢宏，而这史诗级的战争全都要听从你的安排。
选择你中意的派系，挑选你心仪的朋友，快来开启一局紧张刺激的全面战争！

Overall, I came away a little disappointed. Most of the new factions feel underwhelming compared to what Warhammer II introduced. Factions like the Lizardmen and Skaven are still some of the most creative and engaging in the entire trilogy, which makes many of the newer additions feel less distinctive by comparison. That said, the prologue is genuinely excellent easily the best Creative Assembly has ever done. It’s tightly paced, well written, and does a great job onboarding new players without feeling like a chore. I’d really love to see more structured, narrative focused campaigns like this in the future, even if they’re shorter, self contained DLC experiences. One or two of these would go a long way toward offering something meaningfully different from the standard sandbox campaign.

The campaign map itself is massive and visually impressive, but beyond sheer scale, it doesn’t feel like enough has changed. Sieges, diplomacy, and several of the new systems sound good on paper and are welcome refinements, but they don’t fundamentally alter how the campaign plays compared to Warhammer II. Much of the core experience still feels very familiar.

It also doesn’t help that some of the most interesting content is locked behind a paywall. The Chaos Dwarfs, in particular, stand out as a noticeably absent highlight. From everything I’ve experienced and observed, they offer one of the most fleshed-out and mechanically interesting campaigns, which only makes the base game feel less complete without them.

There are also ongoing technical and balance issues that drag down the long-term experience. AI behavior can be inconsistent, and patches sometimes feel like they fix one problem while introducing another. Even now, the game still feels like it’s catching up to where it should have been at launch.

My biggest issue, though, is the persistent feeling of “been there, done that.” As a conclusion to the trilogy, it works. When viewed as a single, massive package across all three games, the scope and ambition are undeniably impressive. At the same time, that structure feels deliberately fragmented in a way that pushes DLC purchases, which leaves a somewhat bittersweet impression. Despite all of that, it’s still an amazing experience overall. With all the DLC included, the sheer amount of content is extraordinary even if, in my opinion, it ends up being significantly overpriced.

Total War: Warhammer III Review: A Fun, Memorable Experience with a Daunting Campaign

Score: 8.5/10

Creative Assembly’s Total War: Warhammer III is a grand strategy game that successfully blends the expansive lore of Warhammer Fantasy with the deep tactical gameplay of the Total War series. It delivers a visually stunning and strategically rich experience that fans of both franchises will find deeply satisfying. However, its epic campaign, while immersive and rewarding, can be lengthy and cumbersome, making it a challenge for players to see through to the end.

Gameplay and Mechanics: 9/10

Total War: Warhammer III excels in offering complex and engaging gameplay. Players command vast armies, manage cities, and engage in diplomacy as they strive for dominance in a richly detailed fantasy world. The game features a diverse array of factions, each with unique units, abilities, and playstyles, ensuring that every campaign feels fresh and different. The real-time battles are thrilling, with a blend of tactical depth and visual spectacle that few other games can match.

The addition of new mechanics, such as the Realm of Chaos and survival battles, adds further depth and variety to the gameplay. The strategic layer is complemented by a robust AI, which provides challenging and unpredictable opponents, keeping players on their toes.

Visuals and Art Design: 9.5/10

Visually, Total War: Warhammer III is a feast for the eyes. The game’s detailed unit models, stunning battlefields, and grandiose magic effects bring the Warhammer world to life in spectacular fashion. The art design captures the dark, fantastical aesthetic of Warhammer Fantasy perfectly, making every faction and environment feel distinct and atmospheric. The attention to detail, from the intricate armor of units to the sprawling cities, enhances the immersive experience.

Sound and Music: 9/10

The sound design in Total War: Warhammer III is top-notch. The game’s orchestral score, composed by Richard Beddow, perfectly complements the epic scale of the battles and the dark fantasy setting. Voice acting is strong across the board, with distinct and memorable performances for each faction leader. The sound effects, from the clash of swords to the roar of monsters, further enhance the immersion and bring the battlefield to life.

Campaign Experience: 7/10

While the campaign in Total War: Warhammer III is richly detailed and offers a deep and rewarding experience, it can also be lengthy and cumbersome. The sheer scope of the game means that campaigns can take dozens of hours to complete, which can be daunting for some players. The Realm of Chaos mechanic, while adding an interesting narrative element, can sometimes feel like a repetitive grind, interrupting the flow of the campaign.

Managing an empire across multiple fronts, dealing with constant threats, and juggling diplomacy and economy can become overwhelming, especially in the late game. This complexity, while part of the game’s appeal, can also lead to fatigue, making it challenging to maintain momentum and see the campaign through to its conclusion.

Conclusion:

Total War: Warhammer III is a grand strategy masterpiece that offers a memorable and engaging experience. Its deep gameplay, stunning visuals, and rich lore make it a standout title in both the Total War series and the Warhammer universe. However, the lengthy and sometimes cumbersome campaign can be a significant hurdle, requiring a substantial time investment and persistence to complete. Despite these challenges, the game’s strengths far outweigh its flaws, delivering an epic and unforgettable experience for strategy enthusiasts and Warhammer fans alike. With a score of 8.5/10, Total War: Warhammer III stands as a testament to the power of combining grand strategy with fantastical storytelling, even if it demands a lot from its players.

I have over 1800 hours in the 3 games and have been playing since war-hammer 2 came out, First and foremost it is undeniable that the quality of the dlc since war hammer 2 has diminished, the dlc in the second game set a ridiculously high bar and they have not been able to recreate that magic in a while. The main story ( if you want to call it that) poorly implemented and untested, functionally making this game half dead on arrival. The game made a resurgence when immortal empires came out though. The closest they came to a war hammer 2 dlc moment was the chaos dwarves story which felt like a step in the right direction. Despite all the negative things ive said i have 900 hours on this game why is that, Simple. Immortal empires a huge sandbox with a huge selection of playable lords, A ton of races encouraging so many play styles with such good art direction and sound design.  you like the undead we got a race for that, you don't like being evil, Here play undead Egyptians with giant constructs , you like the ocean? here have undead zombie pirates with walking ships and giant cannons. Humans, dwarf, elves of all kinds, world ending demons, all are present. the bones of this game are extremely solid and my love of fantasy keeps me coming back. i might recommend the second game slightly more but overall i would recommend this game on immortal empires. Total war has a history of releasing as a mess and by the end of its support makes a grand come back and is a complete game that is widely loved. And the final thing ill mention that make makes me recommend this game is the modding support. want more units here you go, want mods to change where you spawn here you go, want different lords and hero, we got a mod. Hell do you want to completely change the game with a overhaul mod. We got you covered. the community is so dedicated and really makes this game shine. I don't think you will be disappointed if you buy this game. P.S Tomb kings are by far the coolest thing ever. Side note: im aware of the AI issues like standing around there cities and constantly sacking but never capturing enemy cities. while its unfortunate and should be addressed i cant deny that at the end of the day i still have lots of fun. it wouldnt make sense for me to give a negative rating and still put in constant hours. plus even with the issues i still think there is good value all around.

My play time is entirely from the Prologue/Tutorial, which was well done and pretty fun. I'm probably going to continue playing this game for a while, mainly with my brother in co-op. However, the reason for not recommending this game came from looking into the different lords to choose from and deciding who I want to play for my first real campaign.

What sort of terrible person(s) made the decision to lock away some of the lords in the way they did? The catalyst for me making this review was seeing the Skaven. Three lords are locked behind DLC, which while I hate DLC when compared to being able to play and unlock content over time, it's a stupid part of this world now and I begrudgingly tolerate it. Another two lords are locked behind owning the second game in the series! Why!? I own the first, skipped the second, and decided to grab the third on sale only to find out that there is content, not locked behind DLC but instead locked behind having to own a game that I have no interest in owning!

The final and sixth lord combines these practices in an even odder way and says I must own the second game and one of a selection of DLC. Why is the character included in multiple DLC options if not for the sole purpose of padding out each DLC, but then inherently devaluing each of the other DLC as they now have a lord unlock that would already be unlocked by purchasing another.

I want to believe there are good, passionate people behind Total War who care about their game. But the person(s) who makes the big decisions has soured my taste for the series and I will probably never buy another game from this series as I doubt this practice will cease.

EDIT: I forgot to include that I had been hoping each playable race would give at least one lord to choose from purchasing the base game. The fact that there is at least one entire race blocked from being playable after purchasing the game is just gross.

Me encantaría recomendar este juego. Lo digo en serio, a mí Total War: Warhammer me encanta. Le eché cientos de horas al TW:W2 y me lo pasé muy bien incluso como jugador casual. En momentos bajos de mi vida, una campaña del TW:W2 me ha ayudado a mantener la mente ocupada y me ha hecho más liviana la carga que llevo a cuestas. Lo he pasado muy bien con ese juego y, a pesar de tener algo de reticencia, me decidí a probar el 3.

Y lo que me he encontrado es que han metido un montón de mecánicas, unidades y facciones nuevas muy interesantes, que están muy bien. La mayoría de decisiones que veo que han tomado son muy buenas, y las que no me han gustado las he podido revertir fácilmente con sencillos mods. Más de lo mismo, mucho más contenido y en general algo que en teoría debería gustarme.

Pero se acabaron las buenas palabras. Las batallas son como siempre, sin una diferencia notable en rendimiento, pero el mapa de campaña funciona fatal. Todo va muy lento, los turnos de la IA pasan aún más lentos que en el 2 y es increíble como una batalla donde miles de soldados se reparten ostias entre sí va muy fluido mientras un mapamundi con ciudades y banderas de ejércitos me va a pedales. Todos los procesos en segundo plano de mi ordenador se vuelven locos. Antes mi pequeño "vicio" era echar campañas de TW:W2 mientras me ponía listas de reproducción de YouTube de fondo. Ahora con el 3, esta cosa consume tantos recursos que ni siquiera soy capaz de buscar en Google por qué Archaon ahora está interesado en el mercado inmobiliario sin que Google Chrone y TW:W3 luchen entre sí por ver cuál peta primero. Un día de estos me va a acabar dando un pantallazo azul, me lo veo venir.

Pero esto no es la razón por la que escribo esta reseña. No, señor mío. La razón por la que escribo esto es por pura impotencia ante los crashes. Literalmente, a momento de escribir esta reseña, echar puntos de habildad a Señores/Héroes es como jugar a la ruleta rusa. El juego aleatoriamente crashea al asignar puntos de habilidades, una tarea extremadamente rutinaria que cualquier jugador de TW:W hace en cada maldito turno.

Me encantaría recomendar este juego, en serio. Al momento de escribir esto llevo 50 horas y seguramente le echaré más, pero os juro que la mitad de ese tiempo son pantallas de carga y habría que añadir otras cuantas horas por tener que reiniciar el juego después de cada crasheo. Y no, no juego desde una GameBoy, mi ordenador tira del TW:W2 como la seda, y ese juego visualmente era más agradable en el mapamundi. Quizás sea cosa mía, pero en el nuevo veo los modelos del mapa más suavizados y menos detallados, y aun así peta muchísimo más el juego en el mapa de campaña (Conste, en el modo batalla, el juego sigue funcionado igual de bien que el 2, eso se lo admito).

Ahora en serio, dejo comentarios activos. Si alguien me recomienta un mod, una configuración o algo para que el juego no crashee y funcione mejor, yo le doy mil gracias y hasta me planeteo editar esta reseña. Si no, no puedo recomendar a nadie jugar a este juego en lugar de a TW:W2. Las facciones y unidades nuevas a duras penas compensan las molestias de un juego que funciona tan mal. Ojalá lo arreglen y optimizen y yo pueda retractarme de esto, pero no tiene mucha pinta de que las cosas vayan a salir bien.

En fin, eso es lo que quería decir. Si no has jugado antes a esta saga, juega al 2. Si como yo jugabas al 2 de antes y te planteas jugar al 3, espero que esto te ayude a saber dónde te metes. Ahora no hay vuelta atrás, ya me da palo volver al 2 y tener menos contenido a costa de mejor rendimiento. Igual no deberías cometer el mismo error que yo.

I can only somewhat recommend this game, here are some pros and cons before deciding to buy it. 

pros: 
- very fun and engaging campaigns, every legendary lord feels (relatively) unique to play. 
- Your campaigns never get boring, there are many things to do before you get bored. If you do get bored, every legendary lord (there are many, trust me) is its own campaign, so the experience feels new every time
- good replayability.

P.S: I really wanted to list out a lot of good things about this game, but there's really not lol, I still personally enjoy it.

Cons: 
- The wait time for everything is needlessly long, every battle loading screen takes about 2-4 minutes, and every turn takes 1-2 minutes. And starting a new campaign is also very long...
- The game demands a LOT of hours to really start to enjoy it, for reference it took me about 10-15 hours just to finally start to understand the game's features and mechanics. You really need to read everything about each faction/lord to play them to their full potential. 
- The game is... pretty janky. There are times where the controls are just all over the place. It's hard to explain exactly what, but when you experience it you'll know exactly. 
- The DLCs are absolutely atrocious. I won't deny, I have bought most of them myself, that does not mean anyone has to do it as well. Most of them are overpriced for what they offer. This makes the game feel like (it is) just another attempt at a money grab, buying the game hoping for your favorite Warhammer characters, only to find out it's behind a paywall feels very scummy. 
- Some factions are just straight up weaker than others. Like they are in the same race, but this one faction is just weaker than this faction because the better faction is straight from a dlc. It's almost like a pay to win, you pay for absolutely broken characters while leaving the less wealthy people a stray, being stuck with the base game. 

This game holds a special place in my heart, which is why I hold some bias toward recommending it. The game demands a lot of hours, but when you put the hours in, it's very fun. If you don't enjoy long learning curves, this game is not for you. Hope this helps for new potential buyers, know what you are buying.💓

Cathay was my trial period. Oxyotl and the Lizardmen an experiment. Valkia and the Chaos Faction a slaughter fest. But Kislev got me hard. Never have I struggled so to... just barely survive. It seemed like the final test: an awful economy, wide open borders in all directions, enemies everywhere, especially once the Empire crumbled, and a very limiting starting roster. Diplomacy was necessary - keep factions alive just to act as buffer states, use all allies for protecting key choke points, so that my armies could be always on the move. I couldn't afford to keep them standing, ever. 

Warhammer shines in many ways, with an awe-inspiring roster of different factions, heroes and playstyles. But far too often it is just a couple of interesting hours initially, followed by a long, grindy snow balling. Kislev got it right, where the heat was kept up well beyond 100 turns. 

I kept the forces of Chaos at bay, united Kislev under one banner,  put the Chaos Dwarfes on their place, freed Boris, and helped the Empire come back on its feet. I was the chain that held, when others would have broken. The wall which stood firm, when others would have crumbled. Now I can rest and let Warhammer 3 keep its very special place in my heart.
