Bonjour, je vais essayer de détailler les différents points positifs et négatifs de Total War: Warhammer 3 rapidement.

POINTS NÉGATIFS :
Le coût des DLCs : Le jeu de base est déjà riche, mais pour accéder à toute l'expérience, il faudra souvent passer par la case DLC. Cela peut vite rendre le jeu onéreux si on veut profiter de l’intégralité des races et des campagnes disponibles. Il faut donc être prêt à investir si on veut vraiment tout explorer.

La complexité des factions : Chaque faction possède son propre gameplay, ses mécaniques spécifiques et ses défis. Si cette profondeur est un atout, elle peut aussi devenir un obstacle pour les nouveaux joueurs ou ceux qui n'ont pas le temps de tout maîtriser. Cela demande du temps et de la patience pour comprendre les subtilités de chaque race.

Configuration matérielle exigeante : Le jeu est assez gourmand, surtout pour profiter des graphismes au maximum. En particulier, un SSD est presque indispensable pour éviter les temps de chargement interminables. Si votre PC n'est pas à la hauteur, l'expérience peut vite devenir frustrante.

Quelques features retirées : Certaines petites touches présentes dans les opus précédents ont disparu, comme les discours des généraux avant les batailles. Cela peut sembler mineur, mais ces éléments contribuaient à l'immersion et leur absence est notable pour les fans de la franchise.

POINTS POSITIFS :
Un contenu immense : Total War: Warhammer 3 est une véritable mine d’or pour les fans de stratégie. Le mode Empire Immortel est un chef-d'œuvre de sandbox, offrant une liberté totale dans un monde gigantesque. Avec 96 factions, 560 colonies et plus de 1200 unités différentes, il y a de quoi s'occuper pour des centaines d'heures. Chaque race est unique, avec des mécaniques propres qui apportent une vraie diversité dans les parties.

Une réalisation technique impressionnante : Que ce soit en campagne ou en bataille, les environnements sont magnifiques et les unités sont détaillées à l’extrême. Le jeu offre des moments visuellement époustouflants, que ce soit lorsque vos armées s’affrontent dans des batailles épiques ou que vous explorez la carte de campagne. C'est un régal pour les yeux, surtout si vous avez une machine capable de faire tourner le tout à fond.

Une profondeur et une rejouabilité infinie : Avec ses innombrables factions, ses campagnes riches et ses stratégies variées, Total War: Warhammer 3 propose une expérience mature qui saura tenir en haleine les joueurs les plus passionnés. Que vous préfériez dominer par la force, par la diplomatie, ou par la magie, chaque partie sera différente et vous n’aurez jamais l’impression d’avoir fait le tour du jeu.

Le mode multijoueur coopératif et versus : La possibilité de vivre des campagnes en coopération avec des amis ou de se mesurer à eux en versus ajoute une dimension supplémentaire à l’expérience. Cela permet de redécouvrir le jeu sous un autre angle, en travaillant ensemble pour triompher ou en se défiant dans des batailles épiques. C'est une véritable plus-value pour les amateurs de stratégie en équipe.

CONCLUSION :
Total War: Warhammer 3 est un bijou de la stratégie, proposant une profondeur rare et un contenu gigantesque. Certes, il n'est pas exempt de défauts, notamment en ce qui concerne les DLCs et les performances matérielles nécessaires, mais ce qu'il offre en échange est colossal. Creative Assembly a réussi à créer un jeu qui sait captiver sur le long terme et offrir des expériences uniques à chaque partie. Si vous êtes prêt à investir du temps et de l’argent, vous découvrirez ici l’un des meilleurs jeux de stratégie de ces dernières années.

Bref, pour moi, un excellent jeu, et probablement mon préféré. Le plus dur sera de convaincre ma femme d'y jouer !

Hello, I'll try to quickly break down the positive and negative points of Total War: Warhammer 3.

NEGATIVE POINTS:
The cost of DLCs: While the base game is already rich, accessing the full experience often requires buying DLCs. This can quickly make the game quite expensive if you want to enjoy all the races and campaigns. Be prepared to invest if you want to fully explore everything.

The complexity of factions: Each faction has its own gameplay, specific mechanics, and challenges. While this depth is a strength, it can also be an obstacle for new players or those without the time to master everything. It takes time and patience to understand the nuances of each race.

Total War: Warhammer 3 is a gem in the strategy genre, offering rare depth and an enormous amount of content. Using  ranged gun units are annoying,  because you have to try and fail to figure out where  your unit can shoot from and where they cant. Total War: Warhammer 3 is a ambitious entry, a brilliant epic strategy game that will enthrall both seasoned strategists and newcomers to the franchise. While this latest installment in the Total War series sets a new benchmark for grand strategy games, featuring an impressive blend of tactical depth, diverse factions, and stunning artistic design. It also bears marks of a troubled development cycle, having faced significant challenges during its production. Creative Assembly has delivered a game that, though needing some fine-tuning, and possibly another full year of development time, still has potential to captivate fans of the Warhammer universe.

From the moment you embark on your campaign, the game captivates with its breathtaking and meticulous attention to detail. The landscapes, ranging from lush forests to desolate wastelands, immersing you in the rich Warhammer world. The Immortal Empires campaign is the real gem here, offering a rich experience that players will treasure. This campaign builds upon the maps and mechanics from Total War: Warhammer 1 & 2, providing a more fulfilling experience for those seeking the expansive gameplay the series is known for.

The strategic gameplay is where Total War: Warhammer 3 truly excels. The blend of real-time battles and turn-based strategy creates a dynamic and engaging experience. Each faction offers unique playstyles and abilities, ensuring that no two campaigns feel the same. The combat mechanics are both intuitive and deep, with a satisfying balance between unit management and battlefield tactics. The AI presents a formidable challenge, adapting to your strategies in a way that keeps every encounter engaging and exciting.

Narratively, the game shines with its rich storytelling woven into the fabric of its gameplay. The lore is expertly integrated, bringing the Warhammer universe to life through compelling characters and faction-specific quests. The voice acting is top-tier, adding depth to the narrative and making each encounter feel significant. The dialogue is well-crafted, offering moments of intrigue that enhance the overall experience.

In summary, Total War: Warhammer 3 is a noble attempt at merging intricate strategy with a vast, immersive world. While it has the potential to be the standout title in the franchise, the game is hindered by a rushed development that left some aspects lacking. It is an experience that fans of the franchise will likely appreciate, yet it falls short of the high bar set by its predecessors. While there is potential for greatness, it is clear that this installment needed much more time and care to address its shortcomings and fully realize the epic vision it strives to achieve. Prepare for an epic journey filled with potential, but be aware that a few bumps along the way may require patience from its players.

Depois de acumular mais de 1300 horas e 100% das conquistas lá vai a análise:

Total War: Warhammer III é um jogo que, como seus predecessores, oferece uma experiência profunda e envolvente. Vamos analisar os aspectos positivos do jogo em várias áreas:

Jogabilidade
A jogabilidade em Total War: Warhammer III é altamente satisfatória, com uma combinação robusta de estratégia em tempo real e por turnos. As mecânicas de controle de unidades e gerenciamento de exércitos são refinadas, permitindo um grau considerável de personalização e profundidade estratégica.

Variedade de Raças e Facções
O jogo brilha em sua diversidade de raças e facções. Total War: Warhammer III expande o universo de Warhammer Fantasy com a adição de novas e distintas facções, cada uma com características e estilos de jogo únicos.

Mecânicas
As mecânicas do jogo são sofisticadas e oferecem uma experiência estratégica rica. Cada facção tem sua característica e mecânicas únicas, sejam rituais, contratos, seitas demoníacas ou sistema sofisticado de vassalização/confederação.

IA do Jogo
A inteligência artificial em Total War: Warhammer III é notavelmente aprimorada em comparação com os jogos anteriores da série. A IA mostra um comportamento mais inteligente e desafiador, adaptando-se às estratégias do jogador e oferecendo uma competição mais sólida. Isso resulta em campanhas mais dinâmicas e batalhas mais imprevisíveis.

História
A narrativa e o lore de Total War: Warhammer III são profundamente enraizados no universo de Warhammer Fantasy, oferecendo uma rica tapeçaria de histórias e eventos. A inclusão de histórias específicas para as novas facções e a continuação das tramas das facções anteriores ajudam a criar uma experiência mais envolvente e contextualmente rica.

Possibilidade de Rejogabilidade
A rejogabilidade é um dos pontos fortes do jogo. Com a variedade de facções e raças, cada uma oferecendo diferentes campanhas e estilos de jogo, e a diversidade de estratégias que podem ser empregadas, Total War: Warhammer III oferece uma quantidade considerável de conteúdo que incentiva múltiplas jogadas. Cada campanha pode se desenrolar de maneira diferente com base nas escolhas do jogador e nas interações com outras facções.

Total War: Warhammer III se destaca por sua complexidade e profundidade, oferecendo uma experiência que é tanto estratégica quanto imersiva. A combinação de uma jogabilidade sólida, uma variedade impressionante de facções, e um mundo vibrante e detalhado contribui para um jogo que é cativante e oferece uma excelente rejogabilidade.

[b]Como nada é perfeito, é evidente alguns problemas[/b]:

Desempenho
Desempenho e otimização não é das melhores, o jogo é pesado, sem um SSD você vai sofrer.

Balanceamento
Desbalanceamento entre facções tanto na campanha quanto no PvP, principalmente no PvP, alguns facções são queridinhas e recebem update e ajustes com frequência, já outras (Elfos nobres, bretônia, Norsca, Elfos da floresta, demônios do caso) estão esquecidas.

IA
IA foi bastante melhoradas comparado com os jogos anteriores, os update estão focando em melhoras a tomada de decisão dos inimigos, mas ainda sim existe situações sem sentido.

Curva de aprendizado
Um jogo que explode informações na sua cara o tempo todo e não te dá tempo suficiente para sintetizar tudo que lhe foi dito. Tutoriais fracos ou ausentes, muitas mecânicas não são devidamente explicadas.

DLC - Conteúdo extra
Absurdamente caro e, dependendo da DLC nem vale a pena pelo fato de não adicionar tanto conteúdo. Comprar DLC assim que é lançada te da um powercreep absurdo com a tal raça ou facção, depois de 3 atualizações a CA vai rebaixar o desempenho dela. [strike]DALE CREAMPI NELAS[/strike]

It’s time to give a review. First, I’d like to mention that I really enjoy TWW3, and I would recommend it—except when it comes to the story. However, I can’t give a positive rating overall. CA should do a better job of putting themselves in the community’s shoes, which means everything that gets criticized should be carefully looked into. If this gets changed, I can give a positive review, but as it stands, I can't! Think about how much money I’ve spent as a player, with all the DLCs—and I own all of them. For that amount, I expect a game to be released without needing to criticize it!


For my part, I’ve noticed since TWW1 and TWW2 that there has been no focus on the story, unlike what we saw in Dark Omen. As a result, I don’t care about the campaign, but rather focus on PvP! You could take inspiration from other games like MWO, which has various game modes.


TWW3 has more than enough different game modes, but not all are used for ranked play! Personally, 1 vs 1 land battles are completely fine with me, but what bothers me a lot—massively—is that I can’t load my army builds. It’s fine that we only learn which faction the opponent picked after they’ve locked it in. Most of the time, it’s better to select a faction first. That way, the opponent can’t just counterpick, which is great, because that already annoyed me in TWW2. But please give me the ability to use all the army builds I prepared for the selected faction! It doesn’t make sense that once both players have chosen their factions, I can’t load my army builds anymore. You need to fix this! I don’t want to manually adjust my army every time. Isn’t that what army builds are for?


And please, add a story for TWW3, like in Dark Omen. That’s really not asking too much. I’ll leave out the other criticisms I’ve already mentioned in TWW2, but just fix what you realistically can.


Also, a ranked mode with more game types wouldn’t hurt. Sure, you can do siege battles in multiplayer, but conquest in ranked mode? That’s just not fun. You have to hold the center of the map? Sorry, but that’s really not enjoyable. As for domination mode, I still need to test it before I can say anything.


Come up with at least five PvP modes that are actually fun: land battles, 2 vs 2, and siege battles would be great for ranked play. I’ve already shared my opinion on conquest, and I still need to test domination. It’s probably similar, except with three points to hold. Well... the mechanics seem to be similar in that regard. So why have conquest with only one point? Doesn’t make much sense to me. And if someone says, “But you can do 2 vs 2 in ranked with invitations,” well, you have to know the players and add them on Steam to set that up, which isn’t a possibility for everyone!

Immortal Empires is phenomenal. The fantasy world of Warhammer is so cool to explore and dive into, reading lore one second and then stepping into the shoes of your favorite character the next. As of this review there are 100 different lords to play, and each feels different and unique, so there really is hundreds, if not thousands of hours worth of content here. It's really satisfying to watch your faction grow from a single city to a sprawling empire that's as big as you want it to be. The sandbox really is awesome. It's worth noting that mods make the game even more customizable, and are super easy to use even in terms of compatibility and getting set up, which is always nice. 

Of course though, the battles is what makes total war total war, and they're fun too (minus the sieges, but hopefully that gets fixed one day). You can play sandbox battles with whatever combination of units/upgrades/maps you want, but the battles in your campaigns feel so much more awesome. Total War: Warhammer 3 had the potential to be an incredible game, but unfortunately, the sheer number of overpriced DLCs has completely ruined the experience. While the base game offers some great mechanics and visuals, it feels like a skeleton of what it could be, constantly pushing players towards purchasing more content just to access essential features, races, or factions that should have been included from the start.

The constant barrage of paid content creates a sense that the developers are prioritizing profits over player experience, fragmenting the community and making the game feel like a cash grab. Instead of releasing meaningful updates or refining gameplay, they keep locking critical content behind expensive paywalls. The cost of keeping up with all the DLCs quickly adds up to far more than the base game itself, which feels exploitative.

At this point, the game feels incomplete without spending a fortune, and that’s just not in the spirit of what a Total War game should be. It’s disappointing to see such an otherwise great game bogged down by greedy DLC practices.

tl;dr: Unequivocally the best RTS game on the market. The central gameplay loop is unique enough between factions to remain interesting for outrageous amounts of time, while being approachable/arcadey enough that the average gamer can pick it up easily enough.

Graphically there are some hiccups such as lighting being too bright in snow, but overall this game is absolutely gorgeous.
Content-wise there is enough to keep even the pickiest player interested. With the addition of Immortal Empires as playable for all owners of this edition, you can experience content from all 3 games and see first hand how well they've done with balancing. Older factions may not be as polished nor have as many mechanics as newer ones, but the overall balance is so well done that most players will struggle to name more than 2 or 3 factions out of the 24 available factions that need a touch-up.
There are hundreds of mods available on the mod workshop, and even if you only explore the more polished ones you could easily double your playtime with what players have posted.
Multiplayer is fantastic. I don't personally recommend doing a campaign with more than 1 or 2 people just because waiting on 7+ battles every single turn in your 8-person coop is a bit boring, but if you did decide to do a massive multiplayer campaign like that the game handles it flawlessly. I can count on 1 hand the number of multiplayer errors I've experienced, and since the game autosaves every turn they aren't that big of an issue.

I recommend this game because it's a blast but I warn you. If you play this game with mods, if you want to play a campaign at all you'll be very frustrated. You're forced to save your campaigns on a specific drive which cannot be changed.  On my drive I have around 10GB free but when I launch a campaign it drops to around 1GB and steadily decreases. 

It wouldn't be so problematic if the game didn't crash so frequently, which happens regardless of you using mods or not. A method that helped was to hard-link the save location to another file in a separate drive. I just overwrite my current save every turn and every battle to prevent losing too much progress. (Sometimes it doesn't register and you lose a few turns of progress, (*ALWAYS DOUBLE CHECK*)

Another are the frequent updates which cause mod incompatibility. It causes mods to crash your game on startup and usually take over a month to resolve, which wouldn't be an issue if the game wasn't updated so frequently. It would be appreciated if the devolopers showed some more love to the modding community. It's very frustrating being unable to play with mods for over a month when you can generally only play for a couple months with mods before they're made redundant again.

The DLC's  are overpriced. Things should be cheaper or free, not to mention needing to own previous titles to play certain factions or have more units. This is a well documented issue, but unfortunately this is Games Workshop. They love money. They won't change.

But with all issues aside the game is a lot of fun. The campaign mechanics are unfortunately lackluster and there aren't a lot of choices when it comes to building within your territory. It comes down to just industry and military, everything else is secondary. There aren't a lot of mechanics to make the campaign interesting unlike previous Total War Titles. The victory conditions often chalk down to "murder the map please". I recommend using a mod to alter the victory conditions. Setting is great though, voice acting is immaculate. Holy moly this game is fun, regardless of what I just stated I can't stop coming back to it. It's my go to game when I'm burnt out on everything else and I highly recommend it if you're patient enough to deal with the issues.

But the game still was one hell of a diamond in the rough, and the developers and modding community have been great at refining the game to make it as good as possible.

This game also was my introduction to Warhammer and I came into it from a historical total war angle expecting not to like it, and initially I didn't because its so unfamiliar to the older games because factions have powerful single-entity lords and heroes, wizards that can devastate armies, and weird unit types like monstrous infantry or flying artillery. But if you stick with it you'll find its not just the rock-paper-scissors of infantry-artillery/archers-cavalry, it that wizards can punish blobbed up infantry, cavalry and chariots can carve though loose infantry, missiles can devastate single entities and lords, single entities and lords kill weaker lords or wizards and can mess up enemy formations, and good infantry can either hold your position on the defence or steadily roll over your opposition if attacking. Its so delightfully complex.

And then there's the factions that are genuinely unique, which is good both when you're playing them or fighting them. If you're playing as Khorne a fight against Slaanesh, Tomb Kings, or Dwarfs is going to be quite different even though you're playing as the same faction, as you're limited roster of powerful melee with moderate speed has to adjust to overwhelming speed from slaanesh that can outmanoeuvre you, lots of chaff infantry, wizards and powerful constructs from tomb kings that could wear you down, or the Dwarfs can obliterate you with gunfire and artillery if you can't silence their guns fast enough. And there are near infinite combinations of factions and army compositions so theres so much replay value.

I could go on and complement its visuals and animations, its stability for such a huge game, or the campaign features but I won't. What probably is more useful is to say what this game is not: Its not a story rich game (except the sandbox story you create yourself), its not perfectly balanced, the AI is not genius and immune to exploits, this game is not hard (but I also like playing Attila Western Rome Legendary so maybe I have no measure for this). If those are deal breakers, this game probably isn't for you.

Final point: DLC. Its pretty overwhelming how much there is, so my advice is it's not neede to enjoy the game and if you do want it wait for a sale as thy're often 50% off. The best value in my opinion is buying games one and two on sale as they're often about £10 and each gives you 4 more immortal realms factions (5 if you include the free Bretonia DLC), followed by the race packs with tomb kings as the best one, then beast-men or wood elves, then chaos dwarfs, chaos warriors and vampire coast. Norsca and Ogres are in the worst state as race packs that might change with updates. Then the other DLC is mostly down to faction preference, but the Prophet and the Warlock and Thrones of decay I'd highlight as particularly good.

I enjoy getting home from work and playing it, the prices for things are pretty expensive, but on the bright side most new characters offer entirely new ways of playing the game, each focusing on playing differently in some way; whether that be using different kinds of units, or focusing on achieving different goals, most every unit will have something for you. Want to spread a plague to as many people as possible while gaining rewards for it? Play Epidemius. Want to hide nuclear bombs under settlements and detonate them at any time you choose? Play Ikit Claw. Want to cause as much unbridled mayhem as possible? Play the Beastmen. Want to eat a lot of gross food (Including your enemies?) Play Grom. Want to focus on large units? Small units? Fast units? Stealthy units? There are lords for all of these different playstyles that gives this game untold replay-ability. I reccomend picking this game up when it is on sale, and researching which dlcs youd be most interested in. I'm slowly acquiring them as I play, and I enjoy every moment of it.

I can't really speak to the latter, but any drama related to how CA supposedly "made a youtuber quit" seems overblown and irrelevant how the good or bad the game is.
I agree that on higher settings the game pushes even high end GPUs beyond what seems reasonable (I have a 3060TI and it's usually cranking and I play on moderate-high settings). 
Lastly, the price of the game is not unreasonable when you consider the time you'll likely spend playing.  Consider a price of a movie ticket ($15-25 these days?) that gets you about 2 hours of entertainment.  You can pickup most of the DLCs on sale for $5-10 and get upwards of 10-20 hours out of a campaign depending on how you play.  The vanilla game is completely playable with two unique maps that have  different mechanics and campaigns, plus a challenge mode which I haven't even touched yet with 800+ hours spent playing.

Does the game have downsides? Yes. Has CA made questionable decisions in the past with pricing and how they treat the community? Yes. Is it still worth buying and playing if you're a fan of total war style strategy games or a fan of warhammer fantasy? Absolutely. Take the negative reviews with a grain of salt because a lot of them are biased and driven by emotion.

[h1] Ну что ж, пришло время и описать мои мысли по поводу этой игры. [/h1]
Начнём с хорошего. Ещё в детстве, играя в игры типо героев 3 и "кингс баунти", мне очень хотелось управлять не просто пешками с красивой циферкой, символизирующей количество юнитов в отряде. Нет, народ, как говорится, желал хлеба и зрелищ. И вот, спустя годы, включив телеканал "GameShow" (ныне "телеканал E"), я увидел нечто удивительное, интригующее, воплощающее старую мечту в реальность. Это была TW: Rome 2, но тогда я этого не знал, да и вряд ли бы купил эту игру в противном случае, так как всё моё окружение играло в шутеры, а потом ещё и пошла волна популярности королевских битв. Вообщем я задвинул её в долгий ящик. Но вот, однажды, мне Steam порекомендовал уже TW:WH2, как игру, с меткой "тоже есть динозавры"... (Гениальные алгоритмы, я просто похлопаю).

Так или иначе, я начал знакомство со всей серией TW. Игры этой серии никогда не стоили дёшево, поэтому я, желая попробовать, поставил пиратку. И вот меня затянуло, недаром двойка считается лучшей игрой серии, по крайней мере на момент её выхода. Пик популярности линейки и прибыли взлетел именно с ней.

Но сегодня не про вторую часть. Зачем же столь долгое вступление? А затем, чтобы показать интригу и потенциал, который, к сожалению, не раскрыт до конца в 3 части серии.

[h2] Поговорим о плюсах. [/h2]

1) Разнообразие.
Под ним я понимаю буквально всё. Расы, механики, модельки, эффекты, спецэффекты и так далее. В первые 50 часов буквально глаза разбегаются.

2) Богатый бекграунд. Что бы не говорили хейтеры, коих у вахи полно, лор тут действительно уникальный и своеобразный. Особенно он увлекает на фоне, к примеру, того же варкрафта, где лор давно скатился в соплежуйство и лобызания орды и альянса. Тут классическое тёмное фентези [spoiler] (и нет, не из-за цвета кожи) [/spoiler]: кровь, кишки, мясо, все плохие, война не закончится никогда [spoiler] (магию убрать, и будет прямо реализм) [/spoiler]. 

3) Как я упоминал выше, это глобальная стратегия, грамотно соединившая в себе карту обычную, и непосредственно карту поля сражения между пешками-полководцами.

4) Система ресурсов. К примеру, мясо скавенов, рабы у гномов хаоса, скверна у хаоситов, которая с недавних патчей, наконец-то, стала важным атрибутом, влияющим на ваш успех в компании.

5) Магия. Тут даже объяснять ничего не надо.

6) Открытость игры к сообществу мододелов. Моды на текстурки, на юнитов, на карты, и даже на целые пользовательские фракции.

7) Недавно разработчики начали помимо крупных обновлений и длс запиливать мини фичи, наподобие "глубин" у гномов, исправление культов хаосопоклонников и так далее. Это однозначно радует, разнообразие компаний как никак.

[h2] Но дьявол кроется, как всегда, в деталях. [/h2]
Теперь о минусах.

1) Самый главный минус, из-за которого я вынужден опустить палец вниз - система монетизации.
Мало того, что региональный ценник перестал в один момент существовать как явление, дак это пол беды. Если вы захотите поиграть, к примеру, на скавенах (самая проработанная раса) в 3 части, то вы словите проблемку. Для игры за 3 лордов нужно купить 2 часть. Но как так, вы же купили третью!?  А вот так вот, а остальные только в длс, причём в длс сразу 2 лорда минимум. И ладно, если это длс, например, "The Prophet & The Warlock", в котором оба лорда и их механики вылизаны и завёрнуты в фантик от конфетки. А что, если в фантике будет какашка? Вопрос остался без ответа. Или ещё один пример. При игре за монобога хаоса у вас не будет половины реально ценных отрядов, если вы не приобрели длс "Champions of Chaos", дающее половину ростера очень ценных юнитов каждому монобогу из 4. Вам не нужны юниты оставшихся 3 богов, а только одного? Хех, ну вы поняли. Недавно цена ещё и просто так выросла, хоть теперь игроки добились возможности покупки лордов по отдельности.

2) ИИ.
Ох, сколько боли в этом словосочетании. ИИ хоть и совершенствуется потихоньку, но глобально он всё ещё на уровне условного "Рима 2". За примерами долго ходить не надо. ИИ, прущийся 2 стеками к тебе, когда его столицу сейчас снесёт другой, враждебный ему, ИИ.
Упёртость и тупость союзного ИИ вассалов. Яркий пример - Накай, у который отдаёт все захваченые поселения отходят вассальному ИИ. Он не способен ни на что, даже помойная армия рассыпающихся вампиров может разнести его поселения, а армии он делает. Поселения тоже ИИ вассала не интересуют без вашей указки, только руины, и то лениво так, с пинка под зад. Вассал птица гордая, пока не пнёшь - не полетит. Более того, если он съел нужное тебе поселение, он его не отдаст, о чём далее.
ИИ очень не любит отдавать поселения. О чём бишь я, к примеру, у вас отношения 300+ с ИИ, вы в военном союзе, просите его отдать город, который ему ничего не даст, а у вас там уникальная постройка. Дак вот он не отдаст, даже в размен, как правило. Ну что за бред? Ещё смешнее, когда это ещё и твой вассал. Типо, алло, ты мне тут как бы рабом приходишься, а вот нет, симпуй по уникалке дальше, или объяви войну вассалу. Мдам.

3) Поломанность и баги.
Это не столь критично, по сравнению с предыдущими двумя пунктами, однако, нельзя закрывать глаза на подобные минусы. Особенно их ощущают любители онлайн битв, нежели любители соло кампаний. И ладно, если у вас неправильные цифры натиска или не срабатывает статус эффект яда - такое чинят очень быстро. А вот хитбоксы юнитов и их атак иногда вводят в ступор. Это касается только контента, вышедшего с 3 частью за редким исключением. Например, ледяной змей Кислева, наверно, самый яркий пример. Из-за необычной змиеподобной модельки урон его собственных атак просто не проходит по врагу, хотя визуально ещё как должен. А вот сам змей получает по балде исправно. 

4) Ну и, напоследок, про казус годовой давности. А именно - про отмену русской локализации длс гномов хаоса. Поступок действительно свинский [spoiler] (иронично) [/spoiler]. Хоть, скажем так, оплошность была исправлена, но неприятное послевкусие осталось, хоть тут скорее всего сыграла банальная жадность и нежелание терять прибыль.

[h2] Итого [/h2]

I think I gave it a pretty good chance, but this just really sits with me as a downgrade to its predecessor. And it's for a lot of big and small things. I came to the title after the big CA mental breakdown, and whatever you want to call its launch (pretty standard for most modern games now), so that's not even what weighs me down. I'll start with some of the larger, broader issues I have, and then trickle down to some really tiny details.

So one thing I heard claimed about this game is that they improved balance. Sounds pretty cool, but it really does not feel like it. Nor did media making its way to me confirm that. I held off on buying this game, and just watched Legend's videos for the most part while enjoying and working on 100%'ing Warhammer 2. Thunderbarge memes aside, I did not expect the game to rapidly shift towards feeling like spectacle was its main appeal. But when I started bland with a choice like Kislev on Hard for my first campaign, I was treated to watching my first enemy dreadquake shot partially hit, and still take out half a unit card of Ice Guard. That just set the tone for everything else. Winds of magic got the cap of 30 removed, which means Tzeentch is free to throw four vortex spells at you simultaneously, with army abilities, and unit abilities. On top of dreadquakes being spammed, Hashut gets a pseudo nuke and dreadquake barrage, which are also army abilities. Remember when Ikit got a nuke, and it was a massive deal? Then they started using Ikit's workshop as a base for many different faction mechanics? They just started giving nukes to people. Cataclysm spells are also a thing, and the result is that infantry armies can be rendered into a liability once you start facing certain (many) factions. Eventually as Kislev, I started getting tired of constantly mass-micro managing my guard units, just to have one volley of arrows deal a third of an iron daemon's health. 

And the amount of other random crap thrown in on the campaign map to annoy you just doesn't help. Tzeentch can, without warning or counterplay, zap an army for 5 turns of attrition and no replenishment. And swap settlement ownership. Also force war, which if done right after you make peace, lowers your reliability rating. Slaanesh, though possessing many ways to negate seduction budgets, can force your units to switch sides. If this happens to your rank nine handgunners, say goodbye. All the while we have factions like Norsca and Bretonnia that still have not been touched for a rework, and lack any of this, just sitting there, rotting for years now. So with almost everyone getting a big red button, monstrous artillery duelling lords and winning, and every random hero and lord getting far over 1k damage, I don't see how balance has gotten better. It's weirder, much more brutal, and not counter by cavalry having better mass values.

I could continue rambling on about weird junk like magic resist getting changed to spell resist, but I feel like I need to say that I could probably tolerate that if I didn't immediately dislike everything else from the UI text and design changes to the new unit cards. And no, I'm dead serious on that. I don't like the new settlement UI layout, I don't think animated UI backgrounds were necessary, and every time I see one of the new units I just stare at the card because the art style is completely different. It looks like a mod, not official content. I went so far as to share my screen with someone since I was complaining in VC, and he has never touched the series, yet was able to spot the new unit cards with a little over 50% accuracy. I get that you couldn't possibly get the same artist, or maybe someone wanted higher quality art, but at least re-do the old ones, too. Or make a conscious effort to try and mimic the old ones.

But man, that isn't even the end of the weird stuff with them porting things from the previous games. 3D portholes just look terrible for old models. The lighting in 1/2 was very clearly tuned with the models or vice versa, but in 3 the old models just look terrible. Skin looks like half-dry plaster at some angles, and the materials lost a lot of their quality on base models as well. So much so I sought out a mod that thankfully fixed most of it. Dwarfen metals particularly just lost all luster and were discolored. And one of the things that is just the worst are the factions they split up. Grombrindal needed voice lines... I don't know if they're AI generated, but I do not want to see Grombrindal pop up in my diplomacy window. 

Also they taught the AI to rat. Which made it immensely more stupid. I know the AI wasn't exactly "smart" before, but at least it stood its ground and was consistently aggressive. Now Festus will force march past your armies to sack a minor settlement, try to help his main army out with others, and essentially kamikaze his whole faction. I would expect this on easy, but this is just normal to see on Hard. The AI will leave settlements when it does not have the advantage, conceding large parts of its territory for nothing. Essentially, I don't enjoy the battles as much, nor the campaign map, and the new mechanics don't make up for it. I applaud them for making the Empire actually fun to play, rather than managing 20 AI toddlers that get nuked by random Skaven. But that's about it.

I got the game on a pretty steep sale, got some alright hours out of a handful of campaigns, and I'm laying it to rest. Perhaps when work ceases and mods become more stable (pretty bad timing on saying this granted what you just did in 5.2.6), I might come back. Maybe then the DLC will seem reasonable on sale, since I'd currently have to spend over 100 USD to get everything already.

Footnote: I can't say much on the technical side, but I know a ton of people dump on 3 for performance. I can't say it's absolutely terrible, as in battle I think it's pretty comparable to 2 now. The campaign map gets weird dips for me, though. Might be because they changed it from just a game map to almost more of an animated game board. Gyrocopters fly around, ton more particle effects. But I never had a save corrupt or anything, which is also moderately common. With how often hotfixes drop, and rollbacks now being eradicated, just be frugal with your mods. Grab some fixes and you should be fine. In the end I feel like load times got a bit longer, and that's maybe the most substantial pitfall, but a new SSD will probably fix that for me.

From someone who grew up playing the civilization games (here and there, I skipped a few) and countless other strategy games, this is something phenomenal. There are so many options to choose from and different ways of playing the game that offer thousands of hours of replayability. Bought it while it was on sale and a few days later I picked up most of the DLC. I mainly play the Immortal Empires mode with a buddy and also solo and I am having so much fun. The experience has been very difficult, but also very rewarding. Each faction (and there are a LOT) plays differently with different mechanics that take time to learn and more time to master. Once mastered or even just on the journey of mastering them, (because I'm far from a master with only my 50 hours played at the time of writing) the game starts to change and twist. I have loved playing as the Vampire Counts and the Warriors of Chaos. I recently started another playthrough as the Chaos Dwarfs aka the Chorfs and that is an entirely different beast. I've been a fan of Warhammer since I discovered the universe some years ago, but only played a few of the games here and there. My time now is divided between Space Marine 2 and this game and I am a very satisfied customer. I highly recommend this game. Sale value or full price, you won't regret it. For those that aren't a big fan of mapping everything out on a battlefield, this game can be played like Civilization with a feature called auto-resolve. Just make sure you have "doomstacks' with good armored units and you're good to go. Across my campaigns I've spent a major part of my time auto-resolving (because I'm playing in CO-OP Immortal Empires) most of the time and don't want to disrupt the flow. I maybe write a review like once a decade, but here it is.

Honestly after putting 40 hours into WH3, I can say I really enjoy it!

For me I only play immortal empires, and I enjoy throwing some good mods in the mix too. Makes for a pretty fun experience.
Performance wise (atleast for my system) it is a step up from WH2 which is shocking given the graphical improvements and vastness of the campaign map, so If you want to expand your mortal empires to include all the chaos factions and whatnot, I'd say definitely give WH3 a try!

One of the best games ever created in the RTS genre, this title shines in its current state. It's addictive and always fresh, with each playable race offering a unique experience. The game boasts numerous on-point features and the most enjoyable learning curve of any Total War game. The campaigns are incredibly fun and ambitious, keeping me engaged from the moment I first stepped into the Total War universe.

As a newcomer to the series, I find myself unable to stop playing. The depth of strategy and the richness of the world continually draw me back in, offering new challenges and experiences with each session.


The only minor drawback is the reliance on mods to enhance certain aspects of the game, such as the UI, AI, or map layout. While these mods undoubtedly improve the experience, it's somewhat disappointing that the developers haven't incorporated similar improvements into the official release. This could be seen as a missed opportunity on their part. However, I'm not against modders and their contributions; I simply believe that if the base game were perfect, we wouldn't see so many mods focused on what should be basic improvements.
Despite this small critique, the game remains an outstanding achievement in the RTS genre.

Die Trilogie Total War : Warhammer 1 bis 3 ist Teuer bietet dafür aber extrem viel Inhalt und viel Möglichkeiten Zeit darin zu verlieren.

Diese Rezension steht für die Gesamte Trilogie mit all seinen bisher erschienene DLC Inhalten. Es würde sich zwar lohnen die beiden Vorgänger Spiele separat zu bewerten, da es sich aber um eine Trilogie handelt und im Dritten Spiel alle vorherigen Spielinhalte ebenfalls verwendbar sind, reicht ein Blick auf das Große Ganze. 

Für mich als Fan von Total War seit den ersten Rome Teil und als Fan von Warhammer ging mit dieser Trilogie ein Traum in Erfüllung. Ich wünschte mir solch ein Crossover schon zur Zeit von Total War: Medieval 2. Manchmal können Wünsche auch in Erfüllung gehen. 
Das wird auch der Grund sein warum ich mir alle 3 Spiele + alle DLC Inhalte geholt habe. Alles zusammen ist schon ein wenig teuer gewesen, bereue ich deshalb den Kauf ? Eher weniger da ich fast alles Brav mir im Sale gekauft habe und der Spielspaß den ich bisher hatte das Geld wieder Wett macht. 
Und wenn Spielzeit und Spielspaß kein gutes Argument für die Kosten ist : Stellt euch vor ihr Kauft euch stattdessen eine Armee für das Warhammer Tabletop, für die Regelwerk, Farben und Regimenter/Figuren legt man im Endeffekt mehr Geld auf den Tisch, so habe ich das nun alles in Digital. Womit ich allerdings nicht sagen möchte das TWWH3 gut das Tabletop einfängt und abbilden. 

Was es aber gut einfängt ist die Fantastische und Umfangreiche Welt von Warhammer "Fantasy", womit ich nun auch endlich zum eigentlichen Spiel komme. 
Sofern ihr das komplett Packet habt erwarten euch 24 spielbare Fraktionen, hat man sich für eine entschieden wählt man noch einen Lords/Helden aus mit den man dann seine Kampagne bestreitet. 
Man hat die Qual der Wahl, da sich die Einzelne Fraktionen schön unterschiedlich spielen und die einzelne Lords/Helden bringen oft auch nochmal kleinere Mechaniken mit sich. 
Und da ist Ansicht für jeden Geschmack etwas dabei : Du willst als wütende "Kuh-Herde" durch das Land ziehen und Marodieren dann sind die "Tiermenschen" etwas für dich. Oder willst du lieber die "Good Guys" das "Imperium der Menschheit" spielen die mit einer Ausbalancierten Armee aufwarten wo das Zusammenspiel stimmen muss um zu Siegen ? 
Oder doch lieber Piraten ? Vampir - Piraten ! Ja richtig gelesen, Vampir Piraten. Das ist eine sehr ulkige, Lustige und Spaßige Fraktion. Das kratzt natürlich nur die Oberfläche an, aber wo wäre denn da noch der Spaß am Selbst-Entdecken wenn ich jetzt alle Fraktionen hier einfach aufliste.

Gespielt wird mit Vorzug die "Immortal Empires" Kampagne, das ist die Große Sandbox Kampagne mit allen Fraktionen auf einer Großen Welt Karte. Im Grunde wetteifert man mit den anderen Fraktionen um die Vorherrschaft, Ziele setzt man sich selbst und der Weg ist die Geschichte die man Erlebt. Letztendlich artet es in einen Krieg aus, was hast du auch anderes erwartet bei "Total War = Totaler Krieg". Zumeist ist es so das wenn man ein Feind von der Landkarte gefegt hat der nächste schon auf dich wartet. 
Und so führen wir Echtzeit Schlachten mit Monstern und Magie und ethlichen Möglichkeiten der Kriegsführung, da jede Fraktion ihre eigenen Spezialitäten und Taktiken mitbringen. Wir erobern und verwalten Siedlungen oder reiße diese einfach ganz nieder. Und wir Leveln unsere Helden, skillen diese und rüsten sie mit ein wenig Ausrüstungskram aus. Das Spielgeschehen auf der Kampagnen Karte findet Rundenbasiert statt. 
Zudem gibt es noch ein paar Aufgaben-Schlachten die meistens ein wenig Lore erzählen und spezielle Herausforderungen und Belohnung bieten. Diplomatie gibt es auch, diese ist aber eher Bodenständig und nicht sonderlich Komplex.
Damit wäre zum Gameplay schon das wichtigste Gesagt und da ich diesmal nicht so Ausarten möchte mit meiner Rezension folgen jetzt noch ein paar Plus und Minus Punkte :

Plus/Positiv:
+ Tolles Setting
+ Gute Warhammer Franchise Umsetzung
+ Guter Soundtrack
+ Unglaubliche Vielfalt an Fraktionen, Einheiten, Helden
+ Cineastische Schlachten
+ Hübsche Kampagnen Karte mit viel Details und Landmarks (manchmal mit kleinen Textbeschreibungen dazu)
+ Viel Liebe zum Detail vorallem bei den Einheiten Modellen
+ Endlose Spielzeit durch Sandbox
+ Ethliche Mods von "Total Overhaul" bis zu extra Einheiten und schönerer Grafik ist für jeden ein Mod dabei
+ Multiplayer, sowohl Gefechte als auch die Kampagne können zusammen oder gegeneinander gespielt werden.
+ Für mich ein wahr gewordener Kindheitstraum

Minus/Negatives:
- (Man kann den Preis für das Komplett Paket als Minus werten
,das selbe gilt für eine derartige DLC Politik)
- die Diplomatie und der Aufbau/Verwaltungs Part des Games kommt zu Kurz und ist zu Simple gehalten im vergleich zu zb. TW Medieval 2
- Die KI hat manchmal derbe Aussetzer sowohl auf der Kampagnen Karte als auch auf den Schlachtfeld. 
Ist in meinen Augen allerdings bei jeden TW ein Problem
- Die KI wird auf höheren Schwierigkeitsstufen nicht schlauer und besser, sie bekommt einfach mehr Buffs an die Hand und Cheatet mehr (spawnt zb. vollständige Armeen auf die Karte)
Dies ist ebenfalls in allen TW Games ein Problem
-KI hat keine Wirtschaft und kann sich deshalb Armeen Leisten welche sie eigentlich nicht bezahlen könnte. 

Trotz der Schwächen in der Verwaltung, der Diplomatie und der KI ist die Total War Warhammer Trilogie + alle DLCs ihr Geld wert. Für mich als Fan von Warhammer steht das außer Frage. Ich empfehle es deshalb auch jeden Warhammer Fan weiter so fern er bereit ist für den Preis. 
Fans der Historischen Total War Games sollten wiederrum eher mit bedacht zugreifen. TW Warhammer ist anders als die Historischen Spiele, ob schlechter oder besser ist jedoch eine Individuelle Entscheidung. 
Fans von Strategie spielen können ebenfalls gern zugreifen solange ihr eher was seichteres, Casual - Mäßiges sucht seid ihr hier richtig. Fans von Komplexer Strategie (zb. Paradox Fans) können auch auf ihre Kosten kommen, wenn auch dann vielleicht mit Hilfe von Mods. 

So nun ist es das aber auch gewesen, ich habe das Thema zwar nur angekratzt und man kann sicher noch viel mehr schreiben, aber so reicht mir das hier auch erst mal. 

Danke für's bis hier her Lesen !
Habt noch ein tollen Tag.

The biggest downside? The DLC. If you want access to all the units and factions, you’ll be spending hundreds of dollars. Almost half of the factions are locked behind paid DLC, which feels a bit excessive. While the base game is solid, it doesn’t quite feel complete without them.

That said, it’s still a great game, especially for strategy lovers, but I wouldn’t recommend it to people who aren’t already into the genre. It's easy enough to get into once you learn the basics, but the depth can be daunting if you're not used to games like this.

Je vais séparer cette review en deux parties :

1- La campagne classique
2- La campagne Empire immortel

========
Classique

Les histoires sont simples et intéressantes.
Les 4 domaines sont faciles à parcourir et donnent envie de les faire, mais après plusieurs campagnes, cela devient répétitif et lassant. La carte est courte, mais il y a tout de même du contenu.
Les 4 démons et leurs mécaniques de campagne sont bien pensées et collent parfaitement aux personnages :
    Nurgle est en mode épidémie virale.
    Khorne (le meilleur) se concentre sur le carnage et la destruction à grande échelle.
    Tzeentch est plus stratégique et nécessite une bonne compréhension et plusieurs essais pour bien saisir les subtilités.
    Slaanesh conquiert principalement par vassalisation, ce que je trouve très cool et stratégique en début de campagne.

Quant au personnage principal, le prince démon, le système de personnalisation est top : c'est un personnage tout-en-un, avec un style de jeu polyvalent.

Un point bonus, mais à double tranchant, qui concerne la bataille finale. Elle est longue et amusante lors des premières tentatives, mais après cela, elle devient fastidieuse, car on se retrouve à répéter les mêmes stratégies pour réduire au maximum le temps passé en bataille.

===============
Empire Immortel

Non intégré dès la sortie, mais ajouté plus tard, c'est de loin mon mode préféré, à condition d'avoir le mod suivant :

    Victory Conditions Overhaul

Pourquoi ? Parce que ce mod apporte un fil conducteur pour les actions de campagne des personnages pris en charge. Cela permet également de faire des campagnes amusantes mais plus courtes si l'on n'apprécie pas vraiment le seigneur choisi.

La carte est immense, et une conquête complète prendra énormément de temps.

C'est là que la nouvelle fonctionnalité diplomatique que j'adore entre en jeu :

    L'échange de colonies !

Grâce à cet outil, les accords deviennent plus stratégiques et permettent d'écourter la campagne. 
En mode légendaire, connaître les factions et maîtriser cet outil est fortement recommandé ! C'est particulièrement gratifiant d'avoir un vassal avec plus de 30 colonies et de jouer en mode 'Horde' pour capturer et offrir les colonies !

En ce qui concerne le reste, les DLC sont un peu chers, mais bon, c'est CA. Cela ne veut pas dire qu'ils sont de mauvaise qualité, mais il vaut mieux les acheter en promo.

Une bonne suite que je recommande pour passer plusieurs centaines d'heures !

The game is expensive, on its own paying 60 usd for a game is something that AAA titles are used to at this point. That's not the problem. The problem is that the monetization of the game including lord packs, races packs, and other dlc are locked behind extensive (and expensive) paywalls. Even on sale, these will cost you a ton of money for the races and lords you might want to play. 

So yes, the game is extremely fun and I would highly recommend it to anyone, even those new to the genre of strategy games, and the world of Warhammer, but your expectations should be to spend more than the $60 price-point printed on the front.

Warhammer 3 is probably in the list of some of the best strategy games ever made (even though Starcraft 2, AOE2, Rome total war are probably higher ranked for the time they where launched in). At the same time it is also the most expensive, because you have 290dollars in DLC's. That is probably why it had a ton of downvotes and mixed reactions here on steam. For the base game of warhammer 3 you literally get a slap in the face, because you can not make half of the units and you can not play with the majority of the factions, everything is behind a paywall. Just imagine playing chess, without the queen, the knights, the rooks and the bishops.Everytime you would love to have those you can grab your wallet and that destroys immersion and instead of playing the game you end up just playing it less then you would have. You even decide to play Linewar instead.

Honestly the best strategy I have ever played (and I started with classics like Age of Mythology, Warcraft, Rise of Nations etc. back in my kid days). Like any game, it has it's faults, and if you are just starting out you won't even notice most of those. What it is lacking is long term goals in your campaigns, so you have to set those for yourself (talking turn 100+). Start with at least Normal difficulty, do not go lower as it gives you a fake boost in power where you will: 1) Auto resolve 99% of your battles and learn nothing from them, or get to enjoy real time planning and unit micro management, and 2) Get discouraged when you eventually bump up the difficulty and realize you suck, 3) get bored really fast. All of this will result in you disliking the game and not seeing it's true potential.

This is a review for those who aren't really into the world of grand strategy or strategy games in general. This is coming from a person who simply enjoys strategy games casually and I hope this just adds a different take to the game.

So pros and cons of Total War Warhammer III;

PROS:
- The best entry point in the whole Total War: Warhammer franchise. Warhammer 2 is also amazing, but a lot of the stuff there is also found here with a lot of quality of life adjustments that the second one needed.
- All the factions are here. Daemons, Elves, Dwarfs, Ogres, etc. this basically encompasses the whole Warhammer franchise.
- Has an amazing tutorial for those who are new to the Total War series. Most of the skills you learn here can be applied to a lot of other grand strategy games and obviously other Total War games.
- It's welcoming to casuals that can turn you into a core strategy gamer. Yes, it has diplomacy, espionage, empire building, but it's not as complicated as a lot of the other Total War games, so you can easily understand a lot of the main mechanics here and discover more of what the game can do as you play more and more.
- Absolutely stunning visuals. Other Total War games are great too, but the world of Warhammer is jawdropping. Magic, sorcery, the lore, the world even the troops, it's basically visual eye candy.
- Ungodly amounts of replayability. No seriously...SO MANY FACTIONS with each faction having different Leaders ("Lords") with different start positions on the map and different skills, buffs, etc. If you're bored with a race, faction or lord, go ahead and choose another for another adventure, maybe try and see how a different race plays, etc.

CONS:
- Maybe you've heard but the AI isn't really the smartest in the game. You're either playing against a dumb AI that may not move, make questionable decisions, or flatout get destroyed by you. Higher difficulties may make the AI a little more aggressive, even defensively aggressive. But difficulty boils down to them having more money or stats in general.
- If you want to play other races, you have to fork over some cash. You'll have access to the game mode called "Immortal Empires" where you can choose which faction to play as and conquer as you like and face off against ALL factions, BUT if you want to play certain factions, you're gonna have to purchase Warhammer 1, 2 and the DLCs depending on which faction you want to play. You'll get the base factions found in the 3rd game, but if you want to play the "dwarfs" or "Dark Elves" you'll need to get the DLCs or games they're associated with.
- Diplomacy is MUCH BETTER, but AI diplomacy is still questionable. You finally have a number indicating how likely your offers or demands will go through, so long as the number is on the green your offer or demand will be accepted, BUT just like in battles and conquest, the AI will ask, nag, threaten, and request the most wildest things EVEN if you decline or even have a grand empire that far exceeds their power rank. They will pester you in the weirdest ways. And even if they become your vassal or ally and ask them for help to attack something or coordinate something, it may not come into fruition until WAY later OR it might not even happen at all.
- Main campaign outside "Immortal Empires" is lackluster. it's there for lore and it's interesting, but the stress of the looming countdown feels like it hinders your progress to play.

Overall, amazing game and still HIGHLY recommended for people who haven't experienced this before. Yes there are cons, but it pales in comparison on how fun the game is and how much hours you'll sink into this if you give it the time.

Last time playing Warhammer games was the one called "Warhammer: Dark Omen".

Now after playing this one, it feels a massive jump. I like it and especially enjoy the "Immortal Empires" mode.

Although the cons for this game are especially the load of DLC's you have to get for this game and getting all these, will cost you a hefty sum.

This game will devour your time. 

Getting started with it is slow, painful and frustrating. There is a ton to learn. The "tutorial" is decent, the Prologue will teach the basics, but the main part of the game, Immortal Empires, doesnt teach much and is way more complicated.

Immortal Empires is where most players spend their time. Its just the entirety of the Old World map, and the factions/sub-factions all start in predetermined locations. It is basically "conquer the world" mode. Which, given the random aspect of the AI factions, will likely be never the same twice. It requires a bit of awareness of who is getting too powerful and how your diplomacy is with them. The macro game is a bit complex, but the micro - the battles - are really fun. 

My favorite factions are the Lizardmen (dinosaurs!) and Dwarfs. Dwarfs have a ton of fun gunpowder units and are excellent at turtling, their little legs take a while to chase stuff down. 

I spent nearly 7 months playing Immortal Empires, nearly consistently. It is addictive. There are so many factions + subfactions, that you will be eager to try them all and their best units take many turns to get to. Before I finally learned the game, I refunded Total War 1 & 2 twice. TW3 once. It can be rage inducing to learn, but they make mods really easy to implement, which can help greatly during the learning process. 

Highly recommend, but just be aware that they charge a bit for the different factions spread over all three games. I probably spent nearly $200 (on sale) unlocking all factions and sub-factions. 

Get TW3 and go through the tutorial, you should be able to get a feel for it and if you are interested in it before the refund window is up. Try it for yourself, you may spend countless, emotional, hours playing it.

When Total War Warhammer III came out, I saw that it was received poorly compared to the previous entry and decided to wait to play it because of that. I had played the last game and did enjoy my time, but it had some issues that pushed me away from it. Following that, at some point, I finally looked into the game with more depth, saw that it had fixed a lot of its initial issues, and decided to finally give it a try. And I am happy to say that several years after release, a lot of the previous complaints at launch I saw have now been addressed, and I had an absolute blast playing it.

The gameplay is so complex that it is hard to summarize because I want to add tons of detail, but I know I will be leaving something out. However, in the simplest terms, the overworld of the game plays like a less in-depth Civilization series game with a big focus on lords, heroes, and combat; whereas, the battles that you get into are the most realistic (as far as that word applies to fantasy) RTS battles that you can ask for. There is so much here, to the point where I 100% understand why this game is over 110 GB (for now, mind you, they will add more DLC if it is anything like the last game). The amount of depth in the maps, the absolute variety of units and the unique fighting styles/animations they have, the advanced AI that is needed, the crazy number of lords they have built up over 3 games, and so much more all suggest to me that this game could easily be 220 GB, and I would still understand the file size. So here is the breakdown. What is good? The combat, overworld, variety in play and units, AI, map design, and way more. What is bad? The games feel like slogs once you reach 10-15 hours in or so of a campaign. It does wear thin when you are doing upgrades over and over again on cities, and just doing battle after battle for little reward when you just want to kill Be’lakor and be done with it; this is a common problem that is shared amongst many grand strategy games, though, so it is kind of to be expected. There is also a lot to the UI, and it can be overwhelming (once again, like many other grand strategy games). The UI has many improvements over the previous game that I specifically wanted to play TW:W3 for, but there are some big steps back, like the damn alert bar on the side and the mission info just below them suck, for example. Sometimes the camera gets stuck in odd positions in combat. The controls can be annoying and hard to fully grasp in combat as well, but a lot of that comes from the game's depth. And finally, the fact that you can’t cancel the movements you queued up several turns ago to make adjustments while the animations are occurring is super annoying and caused me many a headache; I am sorry that I forgot about them, I had 1000 other things to do. There are a lot more little issues than those, but Steam will not let me make 30-page reviews where I break down every little thing. But here is what is important. Despite the issues that I have with it, this game was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun that I had the worst “one-more-turn syndrome” that I have ever had in my life, the kind where you forget to eat all day, and barely leave your chair. This game is not perfect, but I would be lying if I didn’t say it was masterfully crafted. There is so much to this game that I will just never experience, I simply just don’t have the time, and I am not sure I ever will. It is a massive and wonderful mix of a turn-based grand strategy game and a grand-scale RTS, and I could gush about it for hours.

As far as the story goes, this game has a wonderful tutorial/prologue that has a great story that builds up a wonderful scenario for the main campaign to take place in. However, the main campaign itself falls short in its writing and has far less depth than the tutorial. Honestly, I know this could be an unpopular opinion, but you should have only been able to play either as the Tzarina Katarin of Kislev or [spoiler] Yuri Barkov – the Godslayer [/spoiler] of the Daemons of Chaos faction. They are the ones that have the most investment in all of this, and I would have liked to see a more focused story rather than making it a muddled mess of factions with similar goals. I would have loved to see a campaign broken into pieces, focusing on chapters of their journeys rather than the small amount you get in the long single-map main campaign. That would have meant they absolutely would have needed to have the Immortal Empires content on launch to still allow for the freedom that the playerbase craves in picking their factions (an initial major criticism), to be fair. The story could have been so much better, but they wanted to stick to the formula too much, and I think that was a poor choice. With that said, it is not bad; there is just less story depth than I would have liked. To add insult to injury, you have to play the campaign way too many times if you want to experience everything, and that only gives you story at the start and finish anyway. If you are interested in the stories, I would just look them up online and choose to play Tzarina Katarin of Kislev for your first (and probably only) run through that campaign. Coming at the story from their perspective feels like the intended ending based on all of the other ones I watched, but I could be biased. That being said, we all know that we are around to get to play our favorite lords, and they tried to make it work, but I just don't think they stuck the landing. The reality is that the main campaign is good, but it could have been so much more.

The sound design is great. The sound effects in combat sound like war in the most gruesome real ways possible, the overworld has such a vibrance to its idle soundscape, and the voice acting is a bit campy, but fun. The music is kind of hit or miss, but some of those battle tracks are absolutely killer. It is just such a grand presentation, and I love it all. Beyond wanting some more really powerful music, I am so happy with the sound design.

I am also very impressed with the graphics and performance of TW:W3. I have a beefy computer, but even then, I expected the literal thousands of units on the field with these grand and beautiful battlefields to melt my GPU. However, at 1440p max graphics, I never dropped below 100 fps even in the messiest of battles. It is downright impressive when you realize how detailed units are, the crazy amount of fluid animations they have, and the sheer number of them, with all of the AI wizardry and sound processing in the background added to that mix. It is nothing short of phenomenal. The stylization is great, the world and colors are so vibrant and varied, and the scale feels right. I do think that this game’s implementation of Anti-Aliasing is pretty weak, and this is most noticeable when examining lords like those of Kislev who have fur on their coats. I would love to see this game use DLSS to clean that up a bit, but I think it would create way too much artifacting during battles just because there is so much going on, so I am not sure it would ever be possible. Despite this, the game is still gorgeous in my opinion.

I am still pretty new to this whole series, and I am sure that series veterans have way more nuanced opinions on the game, but as a relative newcomer, I can say that if you have not played this series yet and want to, this one is beginner-friendly with its great tutorial and prologue with a lot of quality of life changes that makes it better to play than the others even if it is rated lower than the past entries. I love this game; I love it so much I uninstalled it so that I could actually get my work done. If that is not high praise, then I don't know what is.

The Dark Elves' blend of cruelty and cunning contrasts so sharply with the Vampires' raw power and corruption—it keeps you on your toes every time you switch sides.

What's fascinating is how the developers avoided making factions feel like mere recolors. Instead, they've infused each one with unique mechanics that demand new strategies. It's like learning a different game with every playthrough. The Dark Elves' emphasis on slavery and sacrifice adds this dark economic twist, forcing you to balance immediate gains against long-term power. On the other hand, the Vampires' reliance on necromancy and corruption turns the battlefield into their playground, where they overwhelm foes with relentless undead hordes.

Have you explored the Skaven yet? Their underhanded tactics and affinity for chaos bring another layer of complexity. Utilizing their undercities and warpstone weapons can be a game-changer, literally undermining your enemies. It's wild how each faction not only requires you to adapt but also to rethink your entire approach to conquest.

The depth doesn't stop at faction mechanics, though. The way the game integrates lore into gameplay enhances the experience tenfold. It's not just about winning battles; it's about immersing yourself in a living, breathing world where your decisions have weight and consequence.

Would I recommend getting Total War: Warhammer 3? Definitely not.
Am I having fun playing this game? But of course.
Now you may wonder why this guy with nearly 800 hours playtime in Warhammer 3 and hundreds of hours in part 2 and 1 would not recommend this game although it's really fun for him.
Well, I'm on board of the Total War: Warhammer train since part 1 and got my hands on nearly every dlc with just a few exceptions. I am having a great experience playing this game because i can enjoy pretty much all the content there is.

If you're new to the Total War games and just bought Total War: Warhammer 3 you have access to 7 races which to choose from (Kislev, Grand Cathay, Khorne, Nurgle, Tzeench, Slannesh, Demons of Chaos). There are a total of 24 races to play. So after spending 60 Euros (at least that was the price in my region) you have access to less than 33% of all the races.
But then you be like "Oh, but i wanted to play Skaven, they're my favourite" for example.
Don't you worry, just get your hands on Total War: Warhammer 2 which still costs 60 Euros. Getting this game unlocks 4 races for you to play (Skaven, Lizardmen, High Elves, Dark Elves). At this point i should mention that all content from the previous games is available in the third part, so buying the previous games doesn't mean one has to launch the older games but instead unlocks the content for the current game.
Great, you can now play the Skaven. But wait, after selecting the Skaven as a race to play, basicially half of their clans and units are still locked because you do not own the corresponding dlc's.
But still no need to worry, just pay more money to get the dlc's to unlock the complete Skaven roster.

By now i think everyone still reading this understands what I'm getting to here. The Total War: Warhammer series is great and fun experience if you have payed a lot of money and have access to all the content.
If you are just going to buy the base game be prepared to only have access to a tiny fraction of the content there actually is. The are better games you could be spending your money on. The AI is insane. Terrible decision making which we can see now through the ally system. Province management is incredibly dumbed down compared to what we had a couple decades ago. Typical battles take less than five minutes. Sieges are annoying, not challenging (unlike a couple decades ago).

A personal bugbear of mine is how the world is falling apart and nobody cares: Daemons are all over the map, even Ulthuan. Skaven empires, greenskin warlords and chaos marauders left, right, and center. In my Franz campaign I spent the first 25 turns going from battle to battle preventing the empire from falling apart from about ten different factions. While it proved an interesting experience, the fact that nobody is willing to work with anyone is rather jarring. Even non-aggression pacts and trade agreements are hard to come by, despite both of us being the same race fighting monsters, sometimes the same enemies. Won't even sign a trade agreement unless I give them a couple turns worth of income. And don't get me started on how the AI is allowed to ignore the economy because otherwise it would always bankrupt itself.

Is TW:W3 a good game? It is... [i]if you're already a fan of Total War games[/i]. I think it sits around the top 3 in the series for me, considering the level of polish this one has. Right now, I'd argue only Dynasties is as well thought out and expansive, albeit it has also lost a lot from previous games (i.e.: I miss unit formations such as those in Three Kingdoms).

Is TW:W3 a fun game? It is... [i]if you can gloss over its many inconsistencies and odd design choices[/i]. Battles are great. [b]When they work properly[/b]. Units will randomly bug and get stuck, they won't fully obey your orders and you'll find them being obliterated because you only have two commands to give: move and attack. You're supposed to employ them to perform advanced tactics, but unit control is still too sluggish and a lot of times won't really do what you were trying to. And I'm speaking about normal battles here, forget about making sieges work because they're absolutely broken. Expect to have your units annihilated without you being able to do anything because they got stuck in a half-opened gate or went down the wrong street due to the poor pathfinding.

Also, diplomacy still sucks big time, even if it's a massive improvement over older titles.

Is TW:W3 worth it? Yeah, no. Discussing whether the game is good or not has nothing to do with its worth. CA has one of the worst business models in the entire industry, rivaling Paradox. You can't just buy Warhammer 3, you [i]really[/i] want to buy the previous 2 and their respective DLCs if you want the full experience. Which would be fine and alright, [i]if they weren't at full price[/i]. If each game was 30€ and no more than 8€ per DLC, I'd be convinced to pay for them, but asking a grand total of 380€ (so far) for all the content. [b]You need 3.49€ to have blood enabled in a war game[/b]. That's the level of disrespect CA has towards Total War players.

You can fuel it if you want with your money, but I'd implore you to wait for sale or look elsewhere for the full experience, because the really, [i]really[/i] don't deserve the money they get.

I'm a long time lover of Total War Games. I started way back in the mid 2000s playing the original Medieval Total War and Rome Total War. 

What I loved about the games was the epic gameplay that really made it feel like you were managing a country. Managing unrest and all sorts of other unforeseen variables gave me a sense of accomplishment, and challenged me in a fun way that gave the games infinite replay. 

Some of the newer iterations of Total War became too complicated to follow, and the game felt more like work than play. But I would say Total War Warhammer III captures the essence of the original Total War games with incredible complexity, and the main difference is the system organization for the game. 

Onboarding and learning curves for this version of the game went quickly. The tutorial is much more effective in this game than others in the Total War series. And the task manager at the bottom right of the screen helps keep track of a lot of minutia without it becoming a micro-management game, a problem I felt as the complexity of Total War games expanded.

I stopped playing Total War games for a number of years, because there was too much to keep track of to play the game casually. 

But this latest iteration I feel has not compromised on the complexity that makes Total War games what they are. Instead the game helps the player have more fun by giving the player tools to easily make a lot of small decisions quickly and without having to remember everything for themselves. 

It's fun. It's less of a commitment to start a new campaign, and the different playable races and factions offer significant differences in the experience of the game. The key to keeping the complexity of the game fun has been the added task management options this game has.
