[h1] Total War: Warhammer III [/h1] — це третя і завершальна частина епічної стратегії від Creative Assembly, яка втілює культову фентезійну всесвіт Warhammer у межах механік серії Total War. Ця гра поєднує глобальну покрокову стратегію зі складними та масштабними битвами в реальному часі, пропонуючи новий погляд на знайомий світ.
[h2] Основні особливості гри [/h2]
Сюжетна кампанія: Криза Кисліва та боротьба за Вихор Хаосу
Total War: Warhammer III пропонує значно розширену сюжетну кампанію, яка сфокусована на епічній боротьбі між різними расами за доступ до Вихор Хаосу, що відкриває ворота до царства Хаосу. Гра занурює гравця у конфлікт, де центральну роль відіграє загадковий бог-ведмідь Урсун, і кожна раса має власні причини й інтереси в цьому конфлікті. Кампанія майстерно вписує фентезійні теми Warhammer в стратегію, поєднуючи політику, магію та постійні битви.
[h2] Ігрові фракції [/h2] : різноманітність та унікальність
Однією з головних переваг Total War: Warhammer III є величезний асортимент фракцій, кожна з яких має унікальні механіки та війська. На старті гравцеві доступні:
[h2] Кислів [/h2] — царство, натхненне руськими мотивами. Їхні потужні ведмежі війська та сильні маги роблять цю фракцію грізним суперником.
[h2] Великий Катай [/h2] — східне імперське царство, яке ґрунтується на китайській культурі. Вони використовують магію Іньянт, щоб підтримувати баланс на полі бою.
[h2] Чотири фракції Хаосу [/h2] — Слаанеш, Тзинч, Кхорн та Нургл. Кожна з цих фракцій має унікальні війська, магічні здібності та власні цілі.
[h2] Демони Хаосу [/h2] — армія, що об’єднує елементи всіх чотирьох богів Хаосу, дозволяючи гравцям створювати свого особливого лідера.
[h2] Бойова система [/h2] : знайома глибина та нові виклики
Серія Total War завжди славилася масштабними битвами, і Warhammer III не став винятком. Основні механіки залишилися знайомими для шанувальників серії: формування армій, тактичні маневри та управління ресурсами. Однак, творці додали кілька нових елементів:
[h2] Портали Хаосу [/h2] , які з’являються на карті та дозволяють гравцям взаємодіяти з царством Хаосу.
[h2] Облоги [/h2] — система облоги зазнала значних змін: тепер гравцям потрібно активніше використовувати захисні структури, барикади та тактичні пастки.
[h2] Битви за Вихор Хаосу [/h2] — новий тип епічних сутичок з різноманітними умовами та завданнями, де гравець відчуває справжній тиск хаотичних сил.
[h2] Графіка та атмосферність [/h2]
Візуально гра вражає детальністю та стилізацією. Художники Creative Assembly постаралися передати атмосферу світу Warhammer з його похмурістю, величчю та епічними ландшафтами. Кожна фракція має свій унікальний стиль, який відображається в дизайні армій, архітектури та магічних ефектів. Аудіосупровід вдало підкреслює напругу та епічність подій, особливо в ключових битвах.
[h2] Мультиплеєр та можливості кастомізації [/h2]
Warhammer III пропонує кілька цікавих нововведень для фанатів мультиплеєра. Основною фішкою стала спільна кампанія на 8 гравців, що відкриває нові можливості для кооперативної гри та складних PvP-сутичок. Також гравці отримали більшу свободу у кастомізації своїх армій та лідерів, що додає грі варіативності.
[h2] Моди та підтримка спільноти [/h2]
Модифікації завжди були невід'ємною частиною Total War, і Warhammer III продовжує цю традицію. Creative Assembly активно підтримує розробників модів, забезпечуючи інструменти та постійні оновлення, що гарантує тривалий інтерес до гри та постійне її оновлення завдяки спільноті.
[h2] Total War: Warhammer III [/h2] продовжує розширювати свій світ завдяки численним DLC, які додають нові фракції, лідерів, війська та інші цікаві можливості. Нижче наведено опис ключових DLC, що вже випущені або заплановані.
[h2] 1. Champions of Chaos [/h2]
Це DLC є одним з найбільших розширень для гри. Воно додає чотирьох нових легендарних лордів — кожен представляє одного з богів Хаосу: Кхорна, Нургла, Тзинча та Слаанеша. Кожен лорд має власний набір унікальних механік і доступ до нових військ. Основна увага в цьому DLC приділена фракціям, які присвячені конкретним богам, що додає більше глибини та варіативності для гри за Хаос.
[h2] 2. Forge of the Chaos Dwarfs [/h2]
Це DLC вводить у гру легендарну фракцію Гномів Хаосу. Вони відомі своєю темною майстерністю у виготовленні зброї, жорстокістю та прагненням до завоювання. Гноми Хаосу отримали власних легендарних лордів, механіки розвитку, нові війська та магічні здібності.
[h2] 3. Immortal Empires [/h2] (безкоштовне оновлення для власників усіх трьох частин)
Цей контент є однією з наймасштабніших кампаній, яку пропонує Total War: Warhammer III. Він об'єднує карти та фракції з усіх трьох частин трилогії в одну велику кампанію, створюючи наймасштабніший ігровий світ, доступний для гравців.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3311177933
[h2] 4. Shadows of Change [/h2]
Це DLC додає до гри нові можливості для трьох фракцій: Великого Катаю, Тзинча та Кисліва. Кожна фракція отримує нового легендарного лорда з власними механіками та цікавими здібностями.
[h2] Плюси гри Total War: Warhammer III [/h2]
Різноманіття фракцій та унікальні механіки: Гравець може обрати з широкого асортименту фракцій, кожна з яких має власні особливості та ігрові стилі. Це дозволяє кожен раз відкривати новий досвід, що зберігає інтерес до гри.
Захоплююча сюжетна кампанія: Кампанія, пов'язана з Вихором Хаосу і подіями в Кислеві, інтригує та додає додатковий рівень драматизму. Сюжет став більш комплексним і захоплюючим порівняно з попередніми частинами.
Поліпшена система облоги: Нова механіка облоги значно глибша та варіативніша, що вимагає стратегічного підходу до оборони та атаки. Це робить облоги цікавішими та більш тактичними.
Кооперативний мультиплеєр на 8 гравців: Можливість грати кампанію разом із друзями робить гру ще більш захоплюючою, відкриваючи нові можливості для кооперативного ігрового процесу.
Візуальна атмосфера: Гра вражає своїм опрацюванням візуальної частини — деталізовані армії, епічні пейзажі та яскраві магічні ефекти підсилюють занурення в світ Warhammer.
Підтримка модифікацій: Традиційна підтримка модів і активна взаємодія з фанатською спільнотою забезпечують тривалий інтерес до гри та постійне оновлення контенту.
[h2] Мінуси гри Total War: Warhammer III [/h2]
Проблеми з оптимізацією та продуктивністю: Багато гравців стикалися з проблемами продуктивності, особливо під час великих битв або на старіших ПК, що може впливати на ігровий досвід.
Високий поріг входу для новачків: Гра має дуже багатий набір механік та систем, що може стати проблемою для нових гравців. Вона вимагає часу на вивчення та освоєння всіх аспектів.
Повторюваність деяких елементів: Незважаючи на різноманіття фракцій, деякі елементи гри можуть стати повторюваними під час довгих кампаній, особливо в багатьох вторгненнях Хаосу.
Невелика дизбалансність фракцій: На момент виходу гри деякі фракції відчувалися сильнішими або слабшими через особливості армій та механік, що впливало на справедливість гри.
Складність керування великими арміями: У масштабних битвах іноді виникає хаос через кількість юнітів та одночасне використання магії, що може ускладнювати контроль та управління.
[h2] Підсумок [/h2]
Total War: Warhammer III — це масштабне завершення трилогії, яке піднімає планку фентезійних стратегій на новий рівень. Гра пропонує захоплюючу сюжетну кампанію, різноманітні фракції, глибокі механіки та розширені можливості для мультиплеєра. Вона вдало поєднує знайомі механіки серії з нововведеннями, які дозволяють відчути світ Warhammer ще глибше. Це чудовий вибір як для давніх фанатів серії, так і для новачків, які прагнуть пізнати світ Warhammer у всій його величі.

Total War: Warhammer III – это впечатляющее завершение трилогии, которое предлагает игрокам уникальный и захватывающий опыт. Разработчики из Creative Assembly проделали отличную работу, объединив эпические сражения с глубокой стратегией и богатым лором вселенной Warhammer Fantasy.

Графика игры поражает своей детализацией и атмосферой: от огромных армий, состоящих из разнообразных юнитов, до потрясающих ландшафтов и городов. Каждая битва ощущается как настоящее сражение за судьбу мира, а анимация и визуальные эффекты добавляют реализма происходящему.

Геймплей сочетает в себе элементы глобальной стратегии и тактических боев, что позволяет игрокам проявить свои навыки в различных аспектах ведения войны. Кампания богата событиями и выборами, которые влияют на исход конфликта, делая каждый игровой процесс уникальным.

Отдельно стоит отметить разнообразие фракций и их уникальных механик. Каждая из них имеет свою историю, стиль боя и цели, что делает игру еще более интересной и многогранной. Введение новых рас, таких как Кислородные демоны и Хозяева жизни, добавляет свежести и разнообразия в уже знакомую вселенную.

Мультиплеер также заслуживает внимания. Возможность играть с друзьями или против других игроков по сети открывает новые горизонты для любителей стратегических игр. Режим кампании для двух игроков особенно интересен, так как он позволяет совместно пройти весь путь к победе.

В целом, Total War: Warhammer III является достойным завершением серии и обязательным к приобретению для всех поклонников жанра. Это не просто игра, а настоящий шедевр, который подарит вам множество часов увлекательного геймплея и незабываемых эмоций.

TL:DR Great game, I think it is now the best in the series. Very expensive if you get all the addons, would wait for sales. Whilst I have 189hrs on TWW3, TWW2 - 1k hrs, TWW1 - 400+hrs.

One of the best points of this game for me is the Immortal Empires map which lets you go around the Old World and back. It is entirely possible to complete a campaign and not have to deal with some of the other factions. Granted my play is heavily biased towards the Empire (favourite faction, I rarely get bored with them), and for that I cannot recommend Thrones of Decay enough on that front as it really improves the state of play for them.

For those that want something more varied you have every race from the Old World to choose from, Beastmen, Elves, Bretonnia, Dwarfs, Chaos Dwarfs, Demons, Dark Elves, Skaven (Yes yes), Greenskins, Vampires, Tomb Kings, Norsca, Warriors of Chaos and more. 

The mechanics are smooth, and this is a game that you can always come back to and try something new, and with teh balance tweaks they have done most of the units and combinations are viable now which is awesome. 

The primary downside is to get all the factions will cost you £130 just for the main games full price, however I have seen some cracking prices at sales (picking up TWW1 & TWW2 for £19.98 - pre 04/11/2024 - and £39.97 for all 3 is a BARGAIN) Whilst I own all the DLCs you could save a few pennies just picking and choosing the ones that cater to your favourite factions.

Zero regrets with getting the game on release, CA have really come through in the end despite hiccups. If you are a fan of Warhammer, this game gives some great little lore drops and easter eggs, all while you rampage to bring everything under one banner.

[h3] Short version: [/h3]
This game is (in my opinion) the definitive warhammer fantasy experience. Despite the flaws listed below, this is a huge and great game that I highly recommend! Combined with total war warhammer 2, I have played for over 2k hours as of this review, and I'll gladly go for several thousand more.


[h3] Long version: [/h3]
This game offers an amazing variety of armies to fight as and against. For example, you can play as lizards riding dinosaurs, crazy man sized rodents taking science and warcrimes to a new level, or scentient green fungi known as orcs (and this is just scratching the surface, not to mention modding). This variety is captured beautifully by great graphics and animations. For example, you can have a T-rex RKO a hellpit-abomination. The voice acting is great, and the sound effects really bring the fantastical creatures to life. 

That being said, the music can be lacking at times. It's alright, but it pales in comparison to for example Medieval II total war (see duke of death for example).

This game offers what is easily the best total war multiplayer campaign experience, through simulateous turns with up to 8 players. Also, multiplayer campaigns is a way to get around the questionable battle AI, by replacing it with your friends or whatever you want to call them.

Speaking of, AI will allways be a problem in complex strategy games, and this is no different. As of this review the AI has a tendency to be a bit cowardly on the campaign map, and it struggles to build empires. There are some campaign features that the AI just does not interact with. In battle the AI is often questionable, if not worse, and it is often abuseable (especially with magic). The AI has long struggled with using magic, but there are some spells that it spams to great effect. 

When it comes to difficulty options, campaign difficulty gives the AI cheats, while battle difficulty changes behaviour on the battlefield somewhat (note that lower battle difficulties give the player bonuses in autoresolve, up to 300% on easy)

I haven't really played too many siege battles, as I tend to avoid that, but they need a full rework. You'll likely never experience a satisfying defensive siege due to the AI refusing to lauch the assault without overwhelming odds. On the other hand you'll fight plenty of offensive siege battles, and they tend to feel samey. Offensive siege battles can almost always be cheesed, and cheesing sieges is straight up boring after a while. It doesn't help that the AI doesn't know the concepts of concentrated defence or sallying forth. The AI will almost never set foot outside the walls. Sieges are easily the most janky part of the game, especially when it comes to pathfinding and line of sight for ranged units.

While there is a lot of DLC, you don't really need to buy it. It is better to wait with buing any DLC, and then you can buy DLC later for the factions you like once you have tried out the game a bit.

CA has been doing a fantastic job with updates lately, and as of this review I'm optimistic, after the bumpy ride warhammer 3 has been so far.

On the game itself though, you can fight each battle using the Total War mechanics or you can lean more towards auto-resolve and focus more on the grand-campaign mix. You of course can do a mix of both, which is what I end up doing. I have to say the "tutorial campaign" is actually really good and while I'm an expert in no means, having gotten this game a few days ago, it's a really smooth on-boarding process compared to other grand strategy games like EU4, etc. Overall, I recommend this game, but know it's a time and money sink (but what games aren't nowadays except PvE extraction shooters?)

Pros:
Hybrid Turn-Based + Real-Time Strategy. Best of both worlds in 1 game.

Graphics are future-proof, not trying to be photo-realistic and instead going for a visually appealing 3D cartoon aesthetic similar to what you could expect from Blizzard games.

Insane amount of variety especially if you own the trilogy of games. You can expand this even more with DLC too.

Ability to do custom skirmishes, or relive battles from previous warhammer games, plus a wealth of quest battles separate from the campaign modes to do.

Multiplayer support

Do not need to install the other games or their dlc's to have access to the content. You simply need to own the games\dlc's in your steam library.

Cons:
Denuvo DRM has a slight impact in performance (not enough to recommend avoiding buying this game, but a little bit bothersome)

In-game anti-aliasing is terrible, highly recommend combining matthew's reshade preset (found in steam community) with either SMAA or DLAA reshade plugin. This gives the game a nicer colourful look, and much better fidelity overall. AA still not great even with reshade, but much better than vanilla. After a while you stop noticing the bad AA with the reshade stuff in place. Without it, the AA is an eyesore.

DLC prices are very expensive, if you are going to be buying any DLC the warhammer 1 and 2 bundles are the best value for money. 76% sale you can get both for around £30 ish while warhammer 3 dlc bundle is around the same price on 76% sale alone + offers less content than either of the previous bundles. Also does not include Thrones Of Decay, unlike the other bundles for the previous games which include all DLC.

Game balance is quite poor, not the worst I have seen but not great either. This leads to multiplayer lacking variety, with people choosing the limited pool of meta factions more often than not. If you are strictly single-player like me, consider this a nitpick. If you are buying this game for multi-player, then check out some balancing videos and see what you think before you buy.

Verdict: 9/10

Reasoning: If I could buy an ultimate edition for £100-£120 which included all content from the previous games + all dlc + all future dlc for warhammer 3, the game ditched denuvo, and they add dlss\dlaa support so we could ditch TAA\FXAA , this would be a 10/10 for single player, 9/10 for multi player. If game balancing got better, would be a 10/10 all-round. One of the most fun strategy games I ever played, one of the most in-depth games I ever played (of any genre), and game is packed full of good content. Just a few minor nitpicky things + 1 major flaw (Ridiculous DLC paywalls such as paying just to see blood.....) holding it back from a 10/10 for me.

Honestly I wish I could give this a "mixed" or an "average" instead of either a "yes" or "no". On it's own,however,  this is not worth the price tag.

To be succinct, the game has enough negatives that outshine the positives. Let's cover both sides (these were the most significant in my experience with the game):

1. Questionable  design decisions: Here I'm looking at you, Realms of Chaos. To be brief, it's just not fun and the game design works against the player and against the core design of total war games. You are actively discouraged to expand and conquer  due to the Rifts of Chaos mechanic. Coupled with how the economy works, you will not be able to field more than 1-2 armies before the first rifts open. From then, you will have to basically micromanage 2 "maps" (as your Legendary lord ventures into chaos to try and get the demon prince soul). It basically becomes a hassle and you get to barely scrape by before Chaos armies come through the rifts and invade your provinces if you don't rush to close them. Now remember, you can only field 1-2 armies realistically, and rifts open all around your realm, which means... you WILL lose provinces, and if that weren't enough, the corruption from chaos kicks in, and it's no joke either to clear that corruption. Added with the ticking clock element of having to rush chaos ASAP, it becomes a race that is significantly stacked against the player way too early. Back in Shogun 2, Realm Divide made sense, it provided an adequate challenge at the point in the campaign where the player would be ready for it. Here, it feels contrived at best.  Allow me to exemplify: 

In one of my campaigns, I was doing decent to get the Khorne Realm soul... won 5 battles in a row, didn't lose a single army unit, encamped to replenish, was a turn away from fighting the guardian... only to have Goldtooth rush into the chaos realm, win one fight, and in the next turn he rushes into the guardian fight, wins, the realms close, I get kicked out of chaos with empty hands, making 2-3 hours of work... pointless. It's extremely demotivating for the player. The randomness of it all, while thematic, makes for a poor gameplay experience. It says volumes that one of the most popular mods for this game is one that completely deactivates the campaign conditions and mechanics (Ursun does not roar, so the game becomes a sandbox).

2. Battlefield mechanics:
2.1 AI behaves erratically, at points ignoring units completely, at others not knowing who/what to attack but I didn't have too much issue with that. Let's face it, AI in Total war games was never the best when it comes to this (though TWW2 had significantly better AI, especially for the generals, at least in my experience). 
2.2 Sieges: They've always never been the best, but now they are even more frustrating. Being allowed to build towers and fortifications WHILE the battle is ongoing is just nonsensical. That should be allowed only  during the deployment phase of the battle. 

3. System:
3.1 Loading times are still an issue. Having to wait 2-4 minutes with specs above the recommended still proves this game has significant issues with it's aging engine and optimization. Although, it seems that the most glaring issues from launch have been fixes, as I didn't experience some of the worst ones noted then.  
3.2 Campaign map has frame rate drops, especially when snow falls. 

Now for the positives:

1. Graphics: amazing. Chaos realms look fantastic and have ton of character to them. Each realm looks distinct and interesting in their own chaotic ways. Kudos to the graphics designers and artists here. The rest of the main campaign map also looks pretty good. 
2. The Prologue campaign: excellent narrative for a prologue campaign that teaches the basics of TW mechanics and provides a cool background for this game's setting. Only hurt more that the realm of chaos campaign after it was such a contrasting experience.
3. Diplomacy: Well look at that, finally I get told WHY my deal is rejected or accepted and I can base my proposal in game parameters, instead of a simple "low/moderate/high" likelihood of success. Not nearly developed like a paradox game diplomacy, but still, a step in the right direction. 
4. Immortal Empires*: the one big reason to play this, especially if like me, you own the previous 2 games and has a bunch if not all the DLC. Finally we have the largest Warhammer map ever, and god it's fun. It's everything you wanted for the grand campaign we've been wanting ever since the fist game came out. 

* Immortal empires did not ship with the game at launch and is ONLY worth it if you have the previous games and DLC. Having almost 70% of the content and leaders locked behind those paywalls is otherwise a turn-off. Here in Japan the base came goes for 7,000 yen (and they lowered it after all the debacles) and the Shadows of Change and chaos dwarfs still go for 3000 each, lol.  

All in all, this is a very mixed bag. I focused a lot on the negatives, as they are the main reasons why I am in the end giving this a negative but it does have good points. However, as a standalone game, it does not justify it's price tag. 
I got it on sale and still I might continue to play it, but only for immortal empires.  

Edit 11/2024:

Played more and finally dragged myself to finish a Realm of Chaos campaign. God that was BAD, both in terms of mechanics and narrative. Here are some highlights.

1. Glitches, bugs: got so many weird bugs and glitches both in battle and campaign. Units not attacking, units glitching, a hero outright vanish from the army it was attached to, sieges being an utter and complete mess, etc. etc. My personal favorite: In the last campaign of Realm of Chaos the chaos army glitched so much it was insanely easy to win. Be'lakor just flew around the battlefield not attacking a single unit until his health was 10%. Half his army had issues with path-finding and could not reach my units. Clearly little to no QA was done here or was outright ignored. Unbelievable that at least some of this stuff has not been fixed in over 2 years.

2. Narrative: Honestly, sort of lame ending for a game that had a good prologue campaign. No spoilers, but it was quite generic and I think more could have been done to give it some flavor, especially for Kislev. There are also some plot holes that are never addressed in this narrative. 

3. A lesson for the future? CA, please think twice about these arcade-like modes in a game design that does not work well with it, or make it it's own thing entirely. Again, for realms of chaos, the best strategy is to not to play this as a TW game. 

4. Engine: as people much better articulated than I have said, CA, it's time for a new engine. This engine is collapsing over its own weight. I keep having significant issues despite well above recommended settings, and loading screen time are atrocious.

Total War, itself, is a franchise I feel comes close to realizing the potential of a genre of media to it's fullest. 

With this installment, we have seen the culmination of the greatest amount of content they have vested in a title to date. I have been with the Warhammer installments almost since the beginning, and through ups and downs, it has mostly improved. 

I truly enjoy this game, and hope for more fleshed out combat and strategy components in future titles.

I'm re-writing my review having now played 364 hours of this game. I've got a pretty good feel for it, and the basic situation compared to Total War: Warhammer 2 is as follows:

Campaign - significant improvement on WH2, many QoL features that make it much easier to play. Still lots of annoyances (crazy retreat distances for example) but generally it's much better

Field Battles - significantly worse than WH2 for so many reasons:
 - Units will tarpit by default. The AI does so just for lack of strategy, it used to be the case in WH2 but they fixed it so that it was actually fairly difficult to convince the AI to tarpit its infantry, now it just piles all the infantry in a big tarpit ready to be nuked to a spell (or an actual nuke).
 - Your units will tarpit - because the AI tarpits its units, it's not uncommon for you units to fight 2 enemy units at once. When one of those breaks your units pursue, and end up just bunching up against the other unit. In fact generally moving units around they end up snagging on things and just forming into a massive bubble.
 - Units fail to maintain cohesion and end up getting sprawled across the battlefield, the game will attempt to draw these units back together, but one model being stuck somewhere else confuses the game and it just runs it back into combat. 
 - AI speed difference is absurd. It's always been the case to some extent, but in WH3 it's got silly; Don't even bother with skirmishing as you'll need a good 30% speed advantage over a unit to outrun it. I'm not sure if it's continually charging, something about your unit crashing into itself, or just a straight cheat, but trying to outmanoeuvre the AI is not viable any more.
- missile units can no longer effectively target. If you're using a firing arc unit, telling it to directly shoot causing it to start turning and reforming its position repeatedly to directly face the unit. in WH2 it would fire if that unit were within its arc, now it will try to get it dead centre. The general advice is just to leave them on fire at will and hope. As for missile cav, they take the "kill bob" strategy, where bob is the guy on the very left hand corner of the enemy troop. Everyone hates bob and targets him with every single missile, massively overkilling him. Generally - missile units suck now.
 - Single entities get snagged on a model - in WH2 it was always frustrating how the AI Lord could cut through your troops like Moses parting the red sea, whereas you try it and it's only with repeated clicks that you can gradually force through. It's now much worse. A single model gets snagged in your entity and you'll be clicking around trying desperately to free yourself from it as the rest of the unit catches up.
 - The "Leave no man behind" attitude of the units remains where if a single model is still caught up in a unit (which it usually is) then unit will all disregard your orders and charge back in. This is worse than WH2 because of the total lack of unit cohesion and the ease with which models get snagged. Once you're in melee you just have to stay there, getting forces out is a massive undertaking.

Sieges - oh god why? I understand what they were trying to achieve, but this isn't the way to do it.
 - The pathways through the settlement are too thin with too much deadspace on the borders that you cannot effectively layout a single unit, you have to rely on the AI pathing to just snake your models through. This destroys most strategy and makes sieges just a dumb grind.
 - The AI finds this even more challenging and ends up just piling its units into you such that you can exploit the AI (and if you want to avoid the grind you have to) by doing things like just running around the other side of the fortress and attacking that (or leave them hidden in some trees and surprise).
 - The gate bug still exists, and is more annoying, never try to barge down the gate with multiple model units as some of your models will glitch through and get killed while the rest stand there not sure what to do. Trying with an SEM may work but will more likely accidentally glitch through before knocking the gate down.
 - Tower control is plain odd, it's not clear how it decides who controls an area, I think it might be unit "value" rather than count, it's really wierd though and the AI might take control of a tower by moving a single model back into the control area.

Overall - WH2 is a better game by a long way, the campaign in WH3 is better, but the battles are incredibly frustrating and littered with bugs. CA are not fixing this, they have shown no intention of even acknowledging the problems even though they did fix some of it in WH2.

CA has been alone carrying the charge of keeping alive and innovating the RTS/TTS/RTT genre. And now with Warhammer 3 they have reached the pinnacle of their home-grown formula of the mix between 4X , and Real time. I played the old total war games back in the day but they never clicked particularly due to not-so-good art and sound. I was always more inclined towards AOE and COH coz they felt more satisfying. But Total war warhammer feels like as if warhammer and TW were made for each other. TW3 is a very high quality game as compared to previous TW games and every other RTS game available today. It looks phenomenal and has a very good implementation of PBR so it's photorealistic and fantastical at the same time.
Turn based expnasion is very addicting and is such a sandbox that there are multiple ways to play, not to mention that every faction is very different. So replayability is insane and AI is good enough to surprise you especially if you are a new player like me.
If you are new like me, I suggest don't pick any other total war but this. It's way better and looks much better compared to TW2 and TW1. You will either not play this game for months or will play it forgetting every thing else for months. YOu should be fine with 4K Ultra if you have anything like a amd rx 6800xt like me or nvidia equivalent or more. Plus a ryzen 5 5600x or better.
DLC practices are less courteous, so I don't recommend buying them or even the full game outside of a sale.
For the best exp I recommend these DLCs:
-Elsipeth - thrones of decay (you get empire in its full glory)
-Prophet and the warlock
-Plus Bretons(they are free)
-don't buy ogre kingdoms because i guess a new ogre DLC is coming
-chaos dwarfs

And do know that buying a DLC for a faction let's you use it completely with a few units disabled so don't think you need the old games or all DLCs of a faction to play them. Like getting Elsepeth gives you empire and lets you play it completely just without a few lords and units.

Epic battle simulator with a terrible kingdom management overlay that sours the experience.

The battles are epic, they are engaging, they are almost worth the price of purchase (if you have the money...). The amount of factions, units, etc are truly incredible. The aesthetics of the game are incredible. If you can throw money around and want that experience, totally worth it.

However the maaaajor flaw hits you very soon into playing: the kingdom management aspect of the game is D-tier. It will frustrate you to no end, where you save-scum because a single lost battle can (and will) ruin an entire game because most games are built around having a single army stack (because of how economies work). The AI has omni-present knowledge and they get artificial buffs (to balance against humans that are generally better). Furthermore, the AI armies know how to perfectly out-pace your armies/harass your lands.

All of that leads to a game that pushes the player towards an early land grab/steam roll from the player - and if you get behind that curve (meaning 1 loss) it is a slog or likely game ending. Add to that, that the politics system is abysmal and you realize the overall kingdom management system is just an frustrating flaw that gets in the way of really incredible battles that we all want.

Then you add in the fact that battles can be "auto resolved". The terrible part of this is most auto resolves favor the player AND when you auto resolve and win - every single enemy unit dies. When you fight manually and win, enemy units can run away and escape - meaning most of the time the enemy army gets away to some extent and can remain a real threat. This incentivizes players to NOT want to experience the best part of the game... the battles! The player constantly has to choose - "do I fight this awesome battle and then have a worse experience in the kingdom simulator because the enemy basically gets away? Or do I choose auto resolve, completely killing every enemy unit, but then skip what I came for... the battles...?" TERRIBLE design which in the end spoils the entire campaign mode. 

The novelty of the game is great at first, and it lasts a very long time. However once you see the flawed mechanics of the kingdom simulator for what they are, the gig is up and the "game" isn't really a game anymore.

Without all or at least most of these products, this game feels quite barren and you notice the AI of the same fractions have a lot of units , lord types etc. that you simply do not have. -Warhammer Fantasy map is not completed (despite its huge size) parts are still missing



In Summary: 
Despite huge scale of the game world and high diversity of units and maps, i do not recommend this game to potential new players. Dieses Spiel ist eine großartige Frechheit. Es ist generell sehr hochwertig und macht Spaß. Allerdings ist es immens Teuer. Möchte man alle Inhalte des Spiels besitzen muss man auf Steam stolze 488 Tacken hinblättern. Durch 18 DLC´s in einer ungefähren Preisspanne von 308 Euro bietet das Spiel zwar sehr viel Inhalt ist aber so schon lächerlich teuer. Dann gibt es da noch eine (in meinen Augen) einfach nur gierige Frechheit. Diese betrifft die Standartfraktionen der vorherigen Teile. Will man die die Orks oder die Hochelfen, sowie die Skaven oder die Echsenmenschen und die Vampiere oder Chaoskrieger spielen muss man sich die vorherigen Teile kaufen. Da diese auf Steam jeweils 60 Euro kosten kommt man auf 180 Tacken. Außerdem ist das Grundspiel Warhammer Total War 3 ohne DLC`s oder Vorgängerteile nur sehr limitiert genießbar. Permanent bekommt man die DLC Fraktionen präsentiert. In jeder Kampagne und bei jedem Neustart von egal welchem Spielmodus. Es fühlt sich an als hätte man 1/3 vom Spiel gekauft und diese Einschätzung ist technisch nicht zu wiederlegen. Wichtig zu erwähnen ist, dass das Spiel gut läuft und ich sehr viel Spaß daran habe. Die gegebenen Fraktionen Spielen sich gut und sind sehr detailreich ausgearbeitet. Sie unterscheiden sich in Spielweise und Spielerlebnis extrem. Sogar innerhalb von Fraktionen und je nach Kommandant ändert sich das Spielerlebnis stark. Es wirkt qualitativ hochwertig und liebevoll gestaltet. Auch erwähnen muss ich, dass ich die Vorgänger der Reihe, also Warhammer Total War 1 und 2 bereits besessen habe als ich mir den dritten Teil gekauft habe. Mir war gar nicht bewusst, dass die Vorgängerteile in Dlcs umfunktioniert wurden als WH TW3 raus kam. Dieser Tatsache ist es auch zu verdanken, dass ich dieses Spiel niemals weiter empfehlen könnte, ohne auf diese horrenden Preise einzugehen. Denn dadurch kann ich das Spiel nur mit sehr wenigen meiner Freunde spielen was einen riesigen Part Spielspaß nimmt und mich mit einem Gelegenheitstitel zurücklässt, den ich meist Spiele, wenn ich gerade alleine bin und das für einen Titel für den ich im laufe der Zeit rund 300 Euro ausgegeben habe. Damit fehlt mir noch immer viel Kontent. Dafür hätte ich mir 5 Trippel A Titel kaufen können. Nichts desto trotz wird, wie bereits erwähnt, sehr viel Qualität geboten. Das Spiel ist prinzipiell sehr gut, allerdings habe ich bei den Preisen und der Umgangsweise mit dem Kontent der Vorgängertitel schon gedacht das Games Workshop von EA aufgekauft wurde. Es erweckt den Anschein als wäre den Produzenten die Community egal. Es sei denn sie können wie eine Cashcow gemolken werden. Diese Verkaufspolitik ist ein weiterer Grund dieses Spiel nicht direkt zu empfehlen, obwohl ich wie gesagt selber sehr viel Spaß mit der Reihe und dem Universen von Warhammer habe. Dem Spiel selber würde ich mit all seinen Inhalten eine sehr gute persönliche Bewertung geben. Quasi eine 9/10. Aber es ist ein sehr teurer Spaß. Daher lasse ich es einfach sein das Preis-Leistungsverhältnis ebenfalls zu bewerten. Für jeden der genügend Investieren will, wird sehr viel Kontent, mit sehr hoher Qualität geboten. Für Warhammer-Fans oder Fans von Strategiespielen wird wirklich viel geboten.

Наиграл пока 91 час. До этого прилично играл во вторую часть игры. Так что могу провести какие-то сравнения. Сыграл компанию-пролог за Кислевитов и на карте "Империя бессмертных" за Великий Катай. Фракции достаточно интересные. Каждая со своим древом развития. За прототип взяты славяне и китайцы соответственно. Прикольно. 
Переработана система защиты городов. Добавили возможность построек барьеров и защитных башен в процессе обороны поселений. Наверное больше в плюс, чем в минус, но когда тебя штурмует большая армия или две, то нет времени контролировать всё поселение, а атаки идут с нескольких сторон, как правило. И соответственно приходится то ли отрядами командовать пытаться то ли постройки эти возводить и где-то что-то постоянно упускаю. На любителя, может просто не привык ещё.
Что поразило на старте большой компании так это 240+ фракций. Карта не просто большая - она огромна, играя за Катай я даже не дошёл до территорий высших эльфов, не говоря про тёмных в левой части карты, как мы знаем из 2 части игры. Добавили некоторые фишки, например: можно армии чужого игрока, нарушившей вашу границу, выдавать предупреждение об этом и дать 2 хода на убраться восвояси. По взаимодействию с игроками добавили функций.

Total War: Warhammer III (TWWH3 for short going forward) Is the natural progression of the prior two games, Bigger map, more factions, more units. With that said lets begin with what i think are some of the positives of this game.

The inclusion of several factions and or races that i believe should have been present since the first game (Kislev, and specific Chaos god Factions) 

Changes made to several factions start locations, avoiding overwhelming bloat in some areas. Such as moving Mannfred Von Carstien, Balthazar Gelt, and Alberic de Bordeleaux away from Bretonnia and The Empire, As with new additions to the game such as Festus the Leechlord, The Changeling, Kislev, Elspeth Von Draken, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Maneater, the area is quickly becoming very full. 

The Inclusions of the new races to the game is a breath of fresh air that while some still need help and some work, i think overall has been good for the game. 
---Kislev: Strong Hybrid units and bear cavalry as well as two new lores of magic allows the player to build skirmishing forces that are able to soften the enemy before meeting the lines of well armored infantry. Overall, a rating of 7/10. I think personally their early game is their weakest point. The only Kislev faction ive been able to play and not want to drive my head through my desk early game is Mother Ostankya. Who plays very differently compared to Tzarina, Kostaltyn, and Boris. 

---Daemons of Chaos: Oh. How badly i want you to be better. A very unique faction and genuinely, an incredibly fun campaign. IF not for your neighbors. Starting Daniel next to Malus Darkblade is the biggest cucking ive ever seen. Even with changes to Malus's agression and the inclusion of Epidemius there. it feels like starting a Daniel Campaign is like playing five finger fillet. Youre gonna get cut eventually. and its gonna suck. 5/10

---Grand Cathay: A perfect example of a well balanced faction on launch. Their whole mechanic of ying and yang is about balanced armies. The Dragon Legendary Lords perfectly encapsulating the faction. Miao Ying boosting Ranged units, and Zhao Ming boosting Melee units. They were the first new faction i logged serious hours on. and i continue to find myself booting a campaign up for them just to see those sweet sweet Fire Rain Rockets. 9/10

---Khorne: Khorne plays exactly how Khorne Should. Unfiltered Agression. Load into the battle. Target the enemy. charge. Strategy boils down to Smashing units into the backs of enemies and using Skarbrand to kill any heros or lords they have. If you enjoy making Black Orc Doomstacks with Grimgor. Youll like Khorne. 10/10 (though not my taste)

---Nurgle:Slow, Tanky, Infectious. Nurgle is a slow burn. Units are slow, Battles can drag on. It is a training exersize in patience. the patience to brew the perfect plague. to infect the right settlement or army. Nurgle is a brilliant faction that in my opinion plays so differently to any other that it is truly one of the few truly 'unique' factions in the game. 9/10

---Ogre Kingdoms: At Launch, awful. i wanted them to be good so bad. but they struggled. The camp and bounty system was clunky. now however, after some changes and a new legendary lord. The faction feels good to play. And i highly reccomend it. 8/10

---Tzeentch: Do you like being a massive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ all the time? Play Tzeentch. If you play Tzeentch in a multiplayer campaign. youre likely to lose a friendship. Changing of The Ways is the most Chaotic thing ive ever experienced and the AI will use it to hurt you in ways you cannot imagine. 10/10 very thematic. Still hate Tzeentch though.

---Slaanesh: Slaanesh is strange. Ive played large swathes of Slaanesh campaigns fighting maybe. one battle every fifteen turns. Using Heros to just. dominate other factions from the safety of my capital.  Thematic? very. Interesting to play and interact with on the campaign map? Ehhh? 6/10 gameplay. 10/10 thematic.


Now. onto a few things i dont care for. 

There are areas of the game that just. feel like theres too much. Too many Legendary Lords stuffed into one or two areas. I play with mods that make the map larger. adding more space between legendary lords. Because nothing feels more. bluh. then hitting turn 50 and realizing that some BIG name characters are gone because they just got gooned early. In all my time of playing theres some factions ive seen. maybe once unless i play them. Cronee Hellebron is a great example of this. I cant remember a game ive played that she lives past turn. 15? unless I am playing her or Malakith. 

The game isnt perfect. and it probably wont ever be. CA/GW does some scummy ♥♥♥♥ occasionally, pushing for how little dlc they can release for the maximum amount of money. They abandon factions, Vampire Coast and Tomb Kings havent seen really anything since release if i remember correctly. Power creep is hamstringing factions. Dark Elves are suffering from changes to their economy and the power creep between games. 

That being said, I do love this game. even with all the.....funk that it has. alot of these issues are fixed by the community. through mods and workshop content. and really i think the Community is the best part of it. While i do think that some of the community can be annoying by an large it is just that. a Community. There are people who create PVP tournaments. You can make friends in discords and just talk about factions you like and the gameplay you employ.  Overall would i reccomend this game? Yeah. Id reccomend it to people who enjoy Total War games. but this style of game isnt for everyone. Its alot of trial and error. and it has some of its elitists that are gonna preach and soapbox that theres a 'right' way to play it. The only Right way to play a total war game is how you want to play it. If you wanna beat the game using only teir 1 units. do it.

7/10  This game possesses the best and worst (laziest/cheapest) aspects of any Total War game I've ever seen.  The battles are epic (some of the best I've ever played in a Total War title), but the siege battles have been completely trashed, especially if you're defending.  Utterly broken mechanics in sieges, weak-cookie-cutter towns (even the capitals), and for some reason, the cities are actually smaller than in War 1 and 2.  Sieges have been a mess ever since back in the day; a new ENGINE is required.  

Most of the buildings aren't even clipped properly into the ground!  This is basic stuff.  And after "three" games and ten (10) years of development, it's absolutely unacceptable.  I've created better foundations in my settlements in Fallout 4.  I've seen better lava effects in the original DOOM (1993).  

The A.I. does work well in most situations, however.  

The "cinematics," if you can call them that, are nothing more than a still image with over-the-counter animation software so it looks like things are moving when they really aren't.  Unfortunately, this has become a standard with lazy game developers these days.  If you compare the cinematics from old Blizzard (Starcraft 2, Diablo 3), and of course, Larian Studios' Baldur's Gate 3, you can instantly tell a difference.  

The price for this game is also astronomical.  We're talking $250.00+ for the "full" version.  Beyond Ridiculous.  Gamers are forced to pay for different factions and even characters within factions, and it's pathetic and just plain Greedy.  It'd be like charging per character in a fighting game.  And I'm not even going to touch on the hands-off approach to building up your settlements that has been completely reworked and dumbed-down, especially visually, since at least Rome 2.  

Mods are also hit or miss, and there's no real consensus about what works well and what doesn't.  

War 1, 2, and 3 are basically the same game.  1 is the Alpha, 2 is the Beta, and 3 is, unfortunately, the "full" version.  If you're not absolutely in love with the Chaos factions, you'll have a better time with War 1 and 2.  Even on a discount, this game is a hard MAYBE.

So what about this game? Based on a huge fantasy world with many characters, stories and places? Overall, the places part was good for a total war game. There were many locations, areas - deserts, mountains, jungles. The category variety was on point. The variety INSIDE those categories, however, was lacking. Too much repetition of the same battle and siege maps. However, regardless of the repetition, those maps were beautiful, and sometimes, I would just admire the sights of this fantastical world. Campaign map is also nice, with its sights to see- gives small introduction to some areas or events that have transpired in the game. Helps one immerse themselves in the game and world a bit more. Is there enough lore? Well, the current vanilla amount is a good start, but more game lore would be nice. As for characters, again - same as with the other two categories - good start, some improvement from the third warhammer game (there were two others), but, taking into consideration the capabilities of modern technology and the availability of lore, sadly a bit lacking. Without going into too much detail, for example, theres this faction/race which, on the map, has MANY subfactions, with only a minority playable, but the greatest disappointment is that the leaders of those factions only get generic character models, which is something that really breaks the immersion for me. Same applies to agent units - these are special units that can be both in the army and perform actions on the campaign map - same deal as with the previous two topics: the category variety is good, but the visual variety WITHIN categories is lacking, taking into consideration how far the gaming industry has come. Once again - it is GREAT to see the amount of areas on the campaign map, nice to see some lore interface where one can read up about a few areas on the map, and the fact that there IS quite a few faction leaders that ARE named, unique in design, and interesting to play. However, the WITHIN-category variety of all these is lacking, all things considered. I do not believe that the game creators are justified in maybe releasing Total War Warhammer 4, without first properly delivering what they owe to the fans of this massive world. In summary - good enough, but really not perfect.

Audio/sound. I am no expert in any of the fields that I am describing, so I will only share my views in everything from the perspective of... you guessed it - myself. I like that campaign music changes based on where you look on the campaign map. Nice feature, adds immersion. Same as for faction specific music in battles. Good that there is uniqueness. Is it enough for the modern gamer? I don't think so. The quality of sound is nice, there are many things happening - combat explosions and swashbuckling, all in the foreground of nice battle music.,... that you hear OVER and OVER again. More would definetely be nicer, as in a normal campaign, you are intended to play quite a few battles. Voice acting is great - characters and races both have  their uniqueness, accents and what they say. And what they say is linked to, for example, how they feel about your faction diplomatically. Nice dialogues, well-enough written, even variety isn't really a problem here. In summary - as with the previous topics - audio NEEDS more variety.

Gameplay. This will be divided into two subsections - campaign and battle. To begin with, the campaign gameplay. Having played a few campaigns already, I can say, at the very least, that the campaign outcomes of OTHER factions (non player) are not predictable - with the exception of very few factions, it becomes quite difficult to say how the world map will look like during any particular playthrough, so that is nice. Adds replayability to the campaign. Campaign difficulty basically determines how aggressive AI is towards the player and how much will they spam unit stacks (armies). There is quite a leap (at least as much as I have seen), from easy to normal - AI actually begins to act strategically, by moving their armies in such a way that it can create quite a few difficulties. Anything above simply improves their strategy and make them more of a threat to you. However, the downside is that the most visible consequence of higher difficulty is not how smart the AI becomes, but rather how many stacks they send against you, thus making the game technically harder, but in a grindy sort of way. But I can't think of how to improve on that, so I can't rate this too negatively. There is increased customisability of the campaign itself, which is what I approve of. 
Now for the meat of the game - battles. Where this game (not only 3, but also the other 2) shines is the variety of gameplay you are faced with in battles. Due to the fact that there are such things as magic, ranged units, melee units, cavalry AND those split into quite a few different types on their own, based on the faction you play and the one you play against, there is quite some serious variety in what you will encounter and what you can do. Naturally some factions are better and some things than others, some can't do some things at all (efficiently I mean), but overall, there is a great replayability in this variety of advantages, disadvantages of units per faction, as well as the variety of the units themselves and how they play. The battle AI is now even more customisable than in other total war games - you can independently manipulate how SMART the AI is, as well as what bonuses/mali they get. That is quite begginer friendly, as it allows you to, for example, play against a hard AI, meaning that they will be reactive, take quite smart decisions in the rock-paper-scissors style of match ups, but you might also choose to make their stats a bit weaker, so the game becomes more forgiving to you. Again, I will be honest - I am no pro, I make loads of mistakes, but I also don't play this game to absolutely master it - so the fact that I can enjoy just the more challenging AI, but with weaker units, really does make it more playable. However, due to the campaign and battle difficulty changes being possible for the duration of the whole game, it also allows one to tailor the game to be playable as one likes it. I think the strong point, with regards to the other two topics discussed here, is the gameplay, as it really has become quite improved and customisable in comparison to past releases of the same and different total war games. Is it balanced and easy? No, but neither should it be for the very simple reason that various factions and races retain their uniqueness through their strengths and weaknesses. 

In summary of summaries, although this game could do with more within-category variety for visuals and audio, those are still very beautiful and a pleasure to witness. As for gameplay - it really has improved over time, especially in the field of campaign and battle AI - making each playthrough quite unique and quite interesting. As a balancing factor to the disadvantages of missing content - one has to remember one simple fact: the modding community exists and is fantastically active. Developers may not necessarily hear and see everything, but the deficiencies within this game, although not really that major, are more than fully compensated by the existence of modders. Is it logical to add modability to the rating of a game? Yes - developers can't always see everything, but if infrastructure is made (and there is) for the community to contribute to the betterment of the game, then its a very welcome development. 

I like this game, and whilst I may not recommend getting the whole franchise when its not on discount - and it really is too expensive when it isn't, but thats just my opinion - I do recommend the game overall for those that like warhammer fantasy genre and want a total war game with quite significant replayability, randomness and quite a bit of fun.

Comparing this one with TWWH:2, which I've got 440+ hours in:

- Runs worse.

I haven't been able to run #3 on as high graphic settings as #2 and I'm really not sure what's making it harder to run when there's seemingly less detail inherent in the art style.

- Siege Battles...
Was excited for the overhaul of them with #3, but city gates are bugged out so that nothing seems to be able to pathfind or shoot through them once they've been torn down, and units that did tear it down seem to sit stuck in the archway. Pathfinding across cities doesn't factor in barricades or bridges, so if you try and walk a bunch of stuff too far ahead they'll likely all bunch up on the corner of a bridge, thinking they need to walk down an impassable cliff.

Irritating that sometimes they'll stay up if you move your cursor over the dialogue box from hovering over a button, and othertimes they refuse to (especially on the hero & lord experience page). Especially annoying when they appear to the right of a button and so completely cover up an adjacent one, so you've got to mouse off in another direction to then be able to hover over the next. #2 doesn't do this.

- Nitpick.
The sound design bothers me; the strange inverted booming sound effects and flappy wad of plastic sheeting sounds on menu buttons.
Esc Menu layout is just no. A simple list in the middle of the screen like #1 & #2 is much better.

The third installment of the Total War: Warhammer Series, and by far my favorite. Now there have been some major ups and downs for this game, especially given just how great Warhammer II was, but the developers have been doing a lot to fix/improve on their mistakes. In it's current state, minus some outdated factions that are currently being worked on in future updates, this game is amazing. The scale is insane, and if you're a Warhammer nerd, especially a Warhammer Fantasy nerd, this game is an instant purchase. If you've never even looked into Warhammer and wanted to learn about it, it's definitely worth the buy. The lore is insanely deep, and you can tell that this game has developers that really love Warhammer. Now for first time buyers, I'm going to tell you the one catch with this game. When the first game came out, they released DLC, and when the second game came out, you had the first game's DLC come with it if you bought it. They did the same thing when Warhammer III released. As someone who bought the first game and all of the DLC and then the next game with all of its respective DLC, I came into Warhammer III with 5-6 years worth of DLC. If you are a new player who hasn't played any of them, you are behind on around 8 years or ~$300 worth of DLC. Obviously that's a no go for a lot of people, especially in this economy. However, this game is on sale a lot, and all of that DLC can be bought for anywhere from 25-75% off depending which one it is which is huge. To anyone looking to get into this game, whether you are a fan of Warhammer or even someone looking to get into it, definitely get it, but get it when it's on sale and help yourself out. This game is easily a game you can sink thousands of hours into and not get bored, and if you can lower the cost for those thousands of hours, then definitely do it. I hope this review helped, and hopefully, you enjoy the game as much as I do.

Total War: Warhammer III è la conclusione di un viaggio epico, una fusione magistrale tra strategia su larga scala e l’universo oscuro e brutale di Warhammer Fantasy. Un titolo che non solo soddisfa le aspettative dei veterani della serie, ma le supera, offrendo un’esperienza grandiosa, intricata e profondamente coinvolgente.
Al centro del gioco si trova il Caos; non solo come elemento narrativo, ma come forza motrice della profondità strategica. Ogni fazione, dai regni mortali ai Signori Oscuri del Warp, è caratterizzata da meccaniche e obiettivi unici. La campagna immerge il giocatore nel Regno del Caos, una struttura narrativa ambiziosa che intreccia decisioni strategiche a momenti di pura meraviglia narrativa.

[h3] Innovazioni nella strategia e nella guerra [/h3]
Sul fronte gestionale, Warhammer III espande le classiche meccaniche di Total War con innovazioni come le battaglie d’assedio rinnovate, combattimenti in scenari più variegati e l’introduzione delle battaglie di sopravvivenza, dove il giocatore deve resistere a ondate di nemici in ambientazioni surreali e infernali. Queste aggiunte rendono ogni scontro un’esperienza più tattica e cinematografica.
Anche la diplomazia ha ricevuto un aggiornamento significativo, con un sistema più dinamico e opzioni avanzate per gestire alleanze e vassallaggi. Ora è possibile reclutare unità da fazioni alleate, aggiungendo un ulteriore livello di profondità strategica che premia la pianificazione a lungo termine.

[h3] Un universo visivamente e narrativamente straordinario [/h3]
Tecnicamente, il gioco è sbalorditivo: le mappe pullulano di dettagli, ogni razza è caratterizzata da un design che ne cattura l’essenza alla perfezione e la colonna sonora amplifica il tono epico della campagna, dando peso a ogni battaglia e svolta narrativa.
Ma ciò che rende Warhammer III davvero unico è la sua attenzione alla longevità. Con l’espansione Immortal Empires, la mappa diventa un campo di battaglia globale che unisce i contenuti dei titoli precedenti, creando un’esperienza sconfinata, quasi infinita. È un omaggio ai fan più fedeli, un tributo all’intera saga Total War: Warhammer.
E per coloro, come me, devoti al Signore del Mutamento Tzeentch, preparatevi a un’esperienza che incarna l’inganno e l’imprevedibilità del Changer of Ways. Manipolare gli eventi, padroneggiare la magia e rovesciare il destino con astuzia e inganno è pura gioia per chi ama la strategia più sottile.

[h3] Conclusione [/h3]
Total War: Warhammer III è un capolavoro della strategia, una celebrazione tanto della profondità tattica quanto della ricchezza dell’universo di Warhammer. Non è solo un gioco: è un viaggio epico, che ricompensa chi è disposto ad abbracciare il Caos e a emergere vittorioso.

Total War: Warhammer 3 : Une immersion totale dans un univers fantastique

Total War: Warhammer 3 est une véritable pépite pour les amateurs de jeux de stratégie. Ce troisième opus de la série nous plonge dans un univers fantastique riche et détaillé, où chaque faction possède ses propres mythes, légendes et unités uniques. La variété des factions, allant des guerriers nordiques de Kislev aux démons du Chaos, offre une expérience de jeu toujours renouvelée.

Une profondeur stratégique inégalée

Le jeu brille par sa profondeur stratégique. La gestion d'un empire ne se limite pas à la conquête militaire. Il faut également gérer son économie, développer ses technologies, et entretenir des relations diplomatiques avec les autres factions. Le système de magie, particulièrement réussi, ajoute une dimension tactique supplémentaire aux batailles. Chaque sort peut influencer le cours d'un affrontement, rendant chaque combat unique et mémorable.

Un univers vivant et évolutif

Total War: Warhammer 3 ne se contente pas d'être un simple jeu de plateau numérique. C'est un monde vivant et évolutif, où les événements se succèdent et influencent le cours de la campagne. Les quêtes sont nombreuses et variées, offrant aux joueurs la possibilité de découvrir les secrets de l'univers de Warhammer.

Une rejouabilité infinie

Avec une telle variété de factions, de campagnes et de mécaniques de jeu, Total War: Warhammer 3 offre une rejouabilité infinie. Chaque partie est une nouvelle aventure, où les joueurs peuvent expérimenter de nouvelles stratégies et découvrir de nouveaux aspects du jeu.

En conclusion

Total War: Warhammer 3 est un chef-d'œuvre du genre. Son univers riche et immersif, sa profondeur stratégique et sa rejouabilité en font un incontournable pour tous les fans de jeux de stratégie. Si vous cherchez un jeu qui vous fera passer des heures de plaisir, ne cherchez plus, Total War: Warhammer 3 est fait pour vous.

Les points forts :

Immersion totale dans un univers fantastique
Profondeur stratégique inégalée
Variété de factions et de mécaniques de jeu
Rejouabilité infinie
Graphismes époustouflants
Les points faibles :

Courbe d'apprentissage peut être abrupte pour les nouveaux joueurs
Quelques bugs mineurs peuvent être rencontrés
En résumé, Total War: Warhammer 3 est un jeu qui saura satisfaire aussi bien les fans de la série que les nouveaux venus.

Сел «на часок» посмотреть кампанию — очнулся через три дня, армия в астрале, демоны захватили холодильник, а Кислев требует уплаты налогов. Да, это Total War: WARHAMMER III — игра, где стратегический гений борется с желанием просто смотреть, как твои великаны пинают крыс.
Но перейдем к делу !
[h3]Плюсы: [/h3]
[list]
[*] Эпичность зашкаливает. Каждая битва — как финал “Властелина колец”, только вместо орков у тебя демонические спруты и медведи с пушками. Короче Максимальное [b] Фэнтази [/b] вам обеспечено! 
[*] Фракции — праздник души. Хочешь завоёвывать мир ради славы? Играй за Кислев. Ради разврата? Великий Слаанеш ждёт тебя с обнимашками. А хочешь Войну ради Войны ? Добро пожаловать к Хаосу!
[*] Мир огромный, как аппетиты Нургла. Кампания «Империи Смертных» — это не просто карта, это полноценный отпуск на 200 ходов минимум.
[*] Медведи. Серьёзно. Огромные. Боевые. Медведи.
[/list] 
[h3]Минусы: [/h3]
[list]
[*] Оптимизация… где-то там, в варп-пространстве. Иногда даже твой ПК вызывает Великих Демонов, чтобы помочь загрузить бой. Оптимизация игры оставляет желать лучшего - частые просадки FPS и тормоза
[*] AI — странный. То герой штурмует твою столицу с одной отрядной кошкой, то заключает мир с врагом, который его же сжёг. ИИ противников часто ведет себя нереалистично и предсказуемо, проходя одну кампанию из-за бага с порталами, я каждый раз видел как ИИ противника выбирал один и тот же ход на протяжении трех кампаний ( одной фракции ) 
[*] DLC-бог. Кажется, уже скоро даже кнопка “Начать кампанию” будет продаваться отдельно.
[*] Твоя личная жизнь. После 100+ часов ты понимаешь, что у тебя есть армия, но нет друзей.
[*] Возможный и Серьезный Баг в Кампании с порталами, который руинит сильно прохождение и заставляет заново проходить ее... 
[/list] 
[h3] Итог: [/h3]
Total War: WARHAMMER III — это стратегическая одиссея в мир, где демоны воюют с пингвинами, а каждый ход — мини-драма. Бывают лаги, баги, DLC на DLC и конечно в первые 2 часа и не узнаешь всего, ведь пока ты узнаешь все, и пройдешь до багов, до точки где Кампания ломается, но пройдет много времени, и приходится откатываться на 5 - 15 ходов назад, спустя больше 50+ часов игры. 
Игра конечно огромна, но явные ошибки могли бы отполировать.

Gra wprowadza nowe rasy, takie jak Kislev, Kataj, armie Chaosu (w tym dedykowane frakcje dla każdego z bogów Chaosu) oraz Demony Chaosu. Kampania "Chaos Gate" skupia się na walce o dominację w piekielnych wymiarach, co wprowadza unikalną dynamikę i nowe wyzwania strategiczne.

Mechanika rozgrywki została dopracowana, a bitwy są bardziej widowiskowe niż kiedykolwiek. System oblężeń zyskał znaczące ulepszenia, a nowe tryby gry, takie jak Immortal Empires (dla posiadaczy poprzednich części), oferują ogromne mapy i nieograniczone możliwości podboju. Dodatkowo multiplayer został wzbogacony o opcję wspólnej kampanii dla większej liczby graczy.

Czy polecam? Tak, ale z pewnym zastrzeżeniem. Gra jest wybitna dla fanów serii i Warhammer Fantasy, oferując gigantyczną zawartość i niesamowite bitwy. Jednak początkowo cierpiała na problemy techniczne i balans, choć większość z nich została naprawiona w aktualizacjach. To idealna pozycja dla miłośników epickich strategii i ostatnia szansa, by w pełni doświadczyć mrocznego, fantastycznego świata Total War. ⚔️🔥

A combination of Heroes of Might and Magic 3/4 (Turnbased, city building, heroes & armies, dark-ish fantasy) and Age of Empires (RTS, Tactical Battles). 

This game touches my sweet spot in terms of a re-playable masterpiece, especially the Immortal Empires mode. There are over 90 different factions to play with in Immortal Empires, each faction has their own heroes, units & playstyle. There will be certain units shared between factions (Human faction, Dwarf faction, etc, but due to the starting location difference in addition to the quests & heroes being unique, it will feel different each time).

The game is split into 2 parts: 
- The turn-based kingdom building
- The RTS combat.

The kingdom building will include the building of infrastructure, making sure your army upkeep doesn't exceed your income, diplomacy with different factions, managing race-based faction powers (Most factions have unique systems that play differently), researching technology and also the movement of your heroes/armies.

If you're too lazy to do RTS combat, then there's the convenient "Auto-battle" option which will do the battle for you. Please note that this feature is biased towards high armor units and frequently notes that you lose the fight, even though it might be an easy victory if done manually. But if you don't want to participate in the RTS, you can generally focus on just building a tanky army with lots of armor and ranged, and just steamrolling the campaign.
Note: Some factions don't have too many high armor units or don't have units that translate well into auto-battles, especially early (Skaven, Slaanesh, etc) in those cases it's best to try and overwhelm your enemies with multiple armies, until you get those units that have high armor value and stats.

It's hard to explain how much love and care has gone into the animation department in this game. Even though I think Auto-battle is fine, I still recommend you to check out the battles for the unit animations (especially the huge units), the amount of money gone into animating an awesome Kaiju fight in the battle is unreal. Not to mention the feeling of your heroes/lords leveling up and becoming killing machines is hard to describe. Some lords can become strong enough to solo entire armies and that's simply a sight to behold.

It's simply a joy to start a new game, you'll slowly feel your characters progress, your kingdom grow, until you become a behemoth of that world, where you can simply flood enemies with armies and get enemies to spam for peace every turn, where you know for a fact that they're out of options and they'll soon be out of life. This also is related to the awesome Warhammer Lore that this game is based on, all the factions act a certain way. The Human knights act honorable, but hate people who're untrustworthy, Dwarves hold grudges and are unlikely to forgive/forget, Lizardmen are pragmatic, the Skaven are backstabbers and cowardly. I feel the brutality of the Warhammer world is really well conveyed in this game, and this definitely adds to the atmosphere of this game.

Negatives:

The DLCs - there are waaay too many DLCs released. Please note that the DLC's on this game don't only include the DLC for Warhammer Total War 3, but also the DLC for Warhammer Total War 2 and also Warhammer Total War 1. To unlock certain factions you will need to throw out cash, which can become hundreds and hundreds of dollars/euros. Thankfully if you don't own the DLCs you can still fight against those factions, but that's still kinda messed up that close to half of the factions in Immortal Empires are inaccessible to you even after you buy this game.

This game has a good amount of bugs, some systems might have the game crashing, experiencing a memory leak, etc. Thankfully there's an autosave feature which minimizes any loss (unless you just completed a difficult RTS battle and find out that the game crashed afterwards). I recommend putting the game on a SSD to make sure the load times would be fast. Some people don't experience those crashes/bugs, so it may be hardware related on my high-end Intel CPU. Some bugs have been reported 2 years ago, but I still experience them (Lord stuck in a enemy hero after combat, reported like 2 years ago, but I just recently experienced it)

Summary: Amazing game, awesome gameplay loop, buggy but the overall game is good enough to ignore those issues. 9/10.

I'd like to preface this by saying that you DON'T need all the DLC to enjoy the game, You should only buy whatever you're interested in actually playing, I have almost 1000 hours as I'm writing this review and I have not played all the Legendary Lords.

The game features grand battles with a lot of unit and tactics available to keep you entertained, with fairly distinct races. The AI on the campaign map isn't great, but is relatively fun to play against, it can sometimes do annoying things like running around sacking minor, undefended settlements, but it's something that you can learn to deal with. That being said, the game can lack challenge in the endgame even with endgame crises enabled. After the latest AI recruitment changes however, the AI recruits fairly competently for the most part and you can still have fun, challenging battles in the later stages of the campaign(which is the main focus of this game)

Personally, I do have issues with the siege battles in this game, but I don't hate them like most of the community does, for one on the defensive side, you can very much do a lot if you know what you're doing and on the offensive side I'm just treating them like a puzzle, if the AI concentrates here - I go there, cast magic here etc. It's not exactly challenging unless your army is wholly unprepared for it(for example full of gun units without artillery to destroy the walls). The main issue of siege battles is the pathfinding, especially while using ladders. Unless you really NEED TO use ladders for whatever reason, I'd recommend just not using them and destroying a gate and going through it, you'll thank me later.

Although there were some downs with this game, especially at launch and during Shadows of Change, the community managed to put enough pressure on CA that they've actually addressed a lot of the problems with the game and they are still continuing to patch the game, which hopefully will fix at least the main remaining issues(clunky ranged units turning very slowly, line of sight issues, pathfinding issues etc.)

Total War: WARHAMMER III – це не просто гра, це справжня стратегічна пригода, яка запрошує тебе у світ величезних битв і неймовірних фентезі-історій. Якщо ви любите стратегії, епічні бої і фентезійний всесвіт, то ця гра здатна вам сподобатись та повністю захопити вас, що надасть незабутні враження.

Що справді захоплює у Total War: WARHAMMER III – це масштаби битв. Представте собі тисячі юнітів, що зіткнулися в запеклій сутичці, де кожен солдат має своє місце і свою роль. Тут є місце для тактичного мислення і глибокого планування, що надасть вам можливість керування та випробовування різних тактик бою: як від гучних атак кавалерії так і до до могутніх магічних заклять, від захоплення ворожих фортець до несподіваних поворотів бою. Кожен момент на полі бою це просто всплеск емоцій та вражень. Уявіть, як ви пускаєте лавину демонів на ворога, або викликаєте страшного хаосного бога, що топче все на своєму шляху.

Ще одна крута річ — це глобальна карта світу. В Total War: WARHAMMER III ви не просто б’єтеся в одних битвах, а ведете цілу кампанію, будуючи імперії, укладаючи союзи або розв’язуючи війни. Вибір фракції визначає ваш стиль гри. Хочете стати правителем людей, борючись за мир і стабільність? Чи, може, вам до душі хаос і безжальні демони, що прагнуть підкорити світ? Тут ви можете обрати те, що вам до душі. Кожна з фракцій має свою унікальну механіку: це і неймовірно цікаві сюжетні лінії, і незвичайні способи ведення війни. Гра дозволяє вам реалізувати різні стратегії, від дипломатичних угод до повного знищення ворогів. І це все у величезному, відкритому світі, де кожне ваше рішення може змінити хід історії. Кожного разу граючи навіть за одну і ту ж фракцію, ви отримаєте різне проходження.

Графіка в Total War: WARHAMMER III просто вражає. У грі прекрасно поєднується візуальна складова: величезні карти, продумані деталі ландшафтів і, звісно ж, самі бої, що захоплюють своєю динамікою. Технічна частина гри справляється з відображенням тисяч юнітів на полі бою, що є неабияким досягненням для такого жанру. Кожен персонаж, кожна армія виглядають дуже деталізовано, а магічні ефекти, різноманітні монстри та армії демонів додають атмосфері ще більше величі.

Висновок: це просто круто! Total War: WARHAMMER III* — це та гра, яка не просто вражає своїми масштабами, а й захоплює і тримає в напрузі кожен момент. Якщо ви хочете відчути себе справжнім полководцем у фентезійному світі, якщо вам подобаються епічні битви, глибока стратегія і безмежні можливості для творчості — ця гра створена саме для вас. І кожен новий бій, нова перемога або поразка, кожний прийнятий стратегічний маневр — це ще один крок до того, щоб стати справжнім володарем всесвіту Warhammer.

Warhammer 3 — это игра, где у тебя есть только два состояния:

1. “Ещё один ход и спать”
2. “Уже 6 утра, но у меня же скоро откроется портал в Ад, нельзя же всё бросить!”

Ты начинаешь за какую-то фракцию, думаешь: «Ну, у меня тут армия, пара деревень, всё под контролем». Через пять ходов твои деревни уже горят, армия сдохла от холода, а на горизонте скачет демон размером с пятиэтажку, и орёт: «Здарова, сосед!»
Игра за демонов — это как вечеринка: у тебя есть Кхорн (главный качок, который орёт и бьёт всех), Нургл (толстый дед, который разбрасывает сопли), Слаанеш (красавчик, которого твои воины смотрят дольше, чем на карту) и Тзинч (колдун, который думает, что он самый умный, пока не прилетает Кхорн и ломает ему лицо).
Игра за людей — это как ипотека: у тебя много проблем, денег нет, соседи хуже, чем в реальной жизни, а демоны не дают расслабиться.
Битвы — отдельная тема. Ты расставляешь войска по уму, строишь тактику… и смотришь, как твои копейщики бегут в сторону, потому что у них стресс. “Да-да, ребят, понимаю, на вас идёт стая монстров с клыками размером с КамАЗ, но может хоть чуть-чуть постоим? Нет? Ну ладно…
В итоге Total War: Warhammer 3 — это симулятор боли, ужаса и неожиданного веселья. Ты будешь кричать, страдать, ржать и всё равно нажимать «ещё один ход».
Оценка: 10/10. Игра, которая научила меня бояться даже паузы.

Die regelmäßigen Updates bringen nicht nur neue Inhalte, sondern auch spannende Balance-Anpassungen, die das Gameplay frisch und herausfordernd halten.

Die neuen Fraktionen und Einheiten, die mit den Updates eingeführt werden, sorgen dafür, dass es immer etwas Neues zu entdecken gibt. Das zeigt, dass sie sich wirklich um die Spieler kümmern und das Spiel zu einem noch besseren Erlebnis machen wollen.

Die Grafik und die Atmosphäre sind einfach atemberaubend, und mit jedem Update fühlt sich das Spiel lebendiger an. Total War: Warhammer 3 ist nicht nur ein strategisches Meisterwerk, sondern auch ein Spiel, das sich ständig weiterentwickelt und mich immer wieder überrascht.

Ich kann es kaum erwarten, was die Zukunft für dieses fantastische Spiel bereithält! Wenn du ein Fan von Strategiespielen bist, dann ist Total War: Warhammer 3 definitiv ein Muss. Vielen Dank an das Team für all die harte Arbeit und die tollen Updates!

If your C: drive starts getting low on space while playing this game or the previous ones, you can find and delete old save files all at once under C: > Users > (Your Username) > AppData (folder might be hidden) > Roaming > The Creative Assembly > Warhammer 3 > save_games.
