This game gets a lot of hate - some of it justified, especially on the corporate financial side of things. However, what it does well it does really well like no other:

After a long day's march, your dwarves begin digging into the top of a hillside overlooking a long valley below. Your scouts have determined a large horde of skaven are sulking in the shadows somewhere nearby. You do not know yet if they will give battle in the morning or will instead cowardly skulk off during the night, but it's best to be prepared for a fight regardless.

Your left flank is densely wooded and covered by a few detachments of veteran Longbeards and Rangers. Their lines have to be uncomfortably thinned out to cover the broad front before them but the terrain should make a big attack unlikely. Not to mention rats are notoriously too hasty and uncoordinated to make good such a venture. Visibility is poor however so who knows what will be unveiled in the underbrush when the morning fog lifts.

You are strongest in the center flank, among the ragged ruins of an ancient castle near the top of the hill where you have made your encampment for the night.  The approach is difficult with many cliffs and boulders funneling any would-be attackers into a few narrow channels. Your Ironbreakers and Warriors find an eeire silence as they steadily work to fortify their positions before dawn, the quiet only broken by the occasion sharp, high-pitched screech echoing in the distance. Just above their location a couple of regiments of Quarrelers have been stationed to provide much-needed ranged cover for any scrum that may occur.

On the right flank you find a steep, open slope that would provide any hopeful assailant easy access into the heart of your position.  Here you decide to make your rat trap. At the base of your position you place your unfortunate bait, a skirmish line of stout and steady Miners. Behind them you place your spring, heavily armed Hammerers who are always eager to join then finish a fight. On a bluff overlooking them all you place your deadly and explosive Thunderers. You are optimistic that your firepower advantage can shock and break your enemy before their vast numeric superiority overwhelms you.

Your reserves are located In the rear on a grassy plain on the very top of the hill.  A detachment of unruly, death-seeking Slayers await to be rushed into combat to plug any holes that enemy monsters may make. Three batteries of organ guns prepare to paint the palette of enemy forces with iron spray from their barrels. Your lone Gyrocopter attachment is ready to lumber off to any location that is requested.

As the darkness finally lifts you find yourself peering into the distance, searching for any sign of the enemy. You don't have to look for long. The adjacent hillsides are awash with ugly, putrid rat men, quite visible despite the gray of the morning. You make a quick estimate and figure that the vermin horde must easily number into the tens of thousands. According to the last count from your quartermaster, you have 1753 dwarf ready for duty. The day should be very interesting....

[h2]前言[/h2]

谈起大战场策略类游戏，永远绕不开的就是CREATIVE ASSEMBLY制作的全面战争系列。无论是早期的罗马还是幕府将军还是最近两年的三国亦或者战锤系列都带给玩家们符合对应题材极致的幻想。但如果真要讨论全面战争系列哪一部最好玩，对于笔者来说一定是三国以及战锤，三国是因为描绘的是中国的历史以及演义风格的战斗而战锤就一定是那数不清的派系兵种以及将领们千奇百怪的技能和特色。

[h2]杂谈碎碎念[/h2]

目前来说，战锤3就是目前全面战争战锤系列的集大成之作，涵盖了前两作几乎所有的派系玩法并更新了些许内容，莫非是因为战锤1+战锤2=战锤3？[spoiler]1+2=3  [strike]不是[/strike][/spoiler]

那说回游戏内容，对于锤三来说最让人在意的还是以全面战争框架下带来的史诗战斗体验。锤三则延续了系列一贯的实时战斗系统，但在细节和战术层面有了明显的变化。

[h3]战斗系统的深度与复杂性[/h3]

首先就是游戏内的单位种类更加丰富，不仅有传统的骑兵、步兵、弓箭手等，还加入了大量魔幻的特色单位，例如巨兽、魔法生物和神祇等，这使得每一场战斗都充满了可能性和史诗体验。而玩家在指挥时则需要综合考虑兵种克制、地形因素以及战斗阵型等多方面的因素。

另外就是锤三的魔法系统了。相较于传统的《全面战争》系列，在锤三中魔法的运用会更加频繁且影响巨大。不同的法术可以在战场上产生不同的效果，从控制敌军到增强己方士兵的战斗力亦或者领主的变身能力，每个阵营的魔法特点都有所不同，这给玩家带来了极大的战术选择空间。

[h3]种族与阵营的多样性[/h3]

锤三继续强化了种族和阵营的多样性，不同种族之间不仅在单位、建筑和科技上有所差异，而且各自的玩法和策略也完全不同。例如，帝国军队注重兵种的平衡与资源的管理，而混沌势力则依赖强大的魔法与神祇单位进行压制性攻势。而每个阵营的游戏节奏、战略目标以及战斗方式都非常独特，极大地提升了重玩性。

尤其是“混沌四神”阵营的加入，为游戏带来了全新的挑战。玩家需要管理各个神祇的信仰和力量，做出战略决策来加强自己的阵营。与此同时，新的地图和任务系统也使得每个阵营的游戏体验更加丰富。

另外锤三的震旦阵营肯定会让身为中国玩家的我们眼前一亮！毋庸置疑，震旦就是古老神秘的东方王朝，但震旦坚守的长恒在奸奇的侵略下已然出现了缺口，而内部的城市亦有反叛军的存在可以说是真正的外忧内患开局。不过游戏前期的难度并不大，主要是跟发展方向相关，只需要确认发展方向即可~


[h3]AI以及游戏表现[/h3]

说到这里，我还是想谈谈CA的技术力，或许有玩家没有注意过在如此恢弘的战场下，CA仍然可以做到每个士兵的姿态以及面孔的多样化，让玩家几乎感受不到战斗之间的僵硬，或许只有这样细致入微的表现才使得游戏能有如此成功吧。

而游戏的AI也是有了显著的提升。笔者曾经尝试用最高难度打了一把，结果被AI虐的体无完肤。肉眼可见的是高等级的AI会利用根据地形、兵种搭配以及魔法使用等多方面进行更为智能的战术调整，AI会尽可能的利用阵容克制来与玩家战斗。一场战斗下来手忙脚乱，也不出意料地输掉了，当然估计千小时的大佬们应该可以应对这样的场景吧。

[h2]总结[/h2]

总的来说，《全面战争：战锤3》是一款深度和广度都极为出色的策略游戏。从战斗系统到大规模战役的策略层面，从种族和阵营的多样性到魔法的引入，每一项都为玩家提供了丰富的玩法选择和自由度。如果你是《全面战争》系列的老玩家，或是喜欢深度策略和奇幻元素结合的玩家，那么锤三绝对是值得一试的佳作。

I will say this: This is one of those franchises that has a cult fanbase. The people that like these games care a lot about them. For that reason, reviews and opinions about this game, and others in the franchise are very exaggerated. Criticism for TW games seems endless. There's always a problem, there's always a design choice people are unhappy about, there's always hate for the devs. But many of those criticisms come from people that try to find problems and complain about them. If it wasn't ___. It would just be another thing, they will never be happy with it. 

The game is good. Awesome strategy game, and the Warhammer universe is a great setting for a TW game. Mods help to keep it fresh, and generally the updates and DLC have been decent.

Again, the content model for this game is sort of a barrier. You must buy content for the old games to have access to it in these games. And to own DLC for TWW 1 and 2. You must own those games to begin with. 
That can be a big investment if you want the content but you're starting fresh. However if you've BEEN playing the games and purchasing content, it's actually a nice system.

I'd keep an eye on large sales when considering buying the game/games and the DLC. Or purchase third party keys at a discounted price.

For those put off by the DLC prices, you don't really need any of them to enjoy the game. The only thing I'd strongly recommend buying in addition to this would be Total War: Warhammer 1 when it's on sale for ~$6, as that adds the Empire, Dwarfs, Vampire Counts, and Greenskins to play as on the Immortal Empires map in Warhammer 3. (Which is basically the massive sandbox mode of the game) There's also free DLC for Warhammer 1&2 that you can add to your steam library and use in 3 even if you don't own their base games, which among other things gives you the Brettonia faction.

As for the game itself, it's quite good. It's been quite a few years since I played Shogun 2 and Medieval 2, but with about a hundred hours in the former and thirty or so in the latter I think I'm at least decently familiar with the series, if not a hardcore fan. The game bears many mechanical similarities to the past games (particularly Shogun 2) but is primarily set apart by it's more varied, fantastical, and notably less squishy unit roster as well as its more unique factions and campaign mechanics. That said, the previously mentioned lack of squishyness is actually one of the game's biggest turn-offs for me. Unit health (particularly with some single/low entity units) generally feels a little high for my liking, leading to things like a full musket salvo on an exposed enemy or a cavalry charge into an enemy flank generally feeling at least a little more underwhelming in terms of casualties and damage than I feel it should, particularly coming from a series that (to the best of my knowledge) previously didn't even give individual soldiers health stats over just giving them live/die armor saves when they're hit. Still, I don't find it straight up bad and it's rather subjective at the end of the day, the game overall is still great.

Un des Total War les plus aboutis à ce jour, qui a connu un départ compliqué avec une optimisation un peu aux fraises et des DLC aux tarifs discutables.
Néanmoins, le jeu est maintenant dans un très bon état, avec une pluralité de factions énorme, une map gigantesque où les situations de départ et le déroulement des campagnes peuvent changer du tout au tout.
Chaque faction possède son style de jeu unique et des affinités stratégiques distinctes autant sur la carte de campagne en tour par tour qu'en bataille en temps réel.

L'IA se fait plus intelligente et un peu plus vicieuse que par le passé, ne patientant plus tranquillement en attendant de se manger de l'artillerie, les volées des tirailleurs ou des sorts. Demeure néanmoins le problème des doomstacks en très difficile, où l'IA peut sortir des armées à composition ridicule rendant le combat ennuyeux/frustrant (les nains avec plein de dirigeables et hélicos, par exemple). La résolution automatique des batailles mériterait aussi d'être revue, certaines factions étant bien trop avantagées là où d'autres sont trop lésées (Mon armée de squelettes avec un seigneur vampire ne pourrait pas tomber 4 unités de berserkers sous cocaïne en armure ?). Cela rend malheureusement certaines factions, bien qu'agréables à jouer, un tantinet rébarbatives, la majorité des batailles devant être jouées manuellement pour éviter la perte d'armée ou d'une unité stupide.

Visuellement, le jeu est beau, malgré que le moteur commence à montrer ses limites au niveau de la physique et de certaines animations. On regrettera aussi le manque d'animations de duels, excusé par la multiplication des squelettes à animer et les moyens réduits de Creative Assembly depuis le temps.
La bande-son est qualitative et les doublages aussi, l'immersion est réussie et l'identité de chaque faction est bien traduite au niveau visuel et sonore.

Despite the ups and downs that Warhammer III and Creative Assembly on the whole have gone thru over the last couple of years, I think this game is the pinnacle of the Total War series. 

I say this as someone who first got into the series with Medieval Total War (2002) and who put multiple thousands of hours across the 20+ year lifespan of the series. Rome and Medieval 2 were the games I played the most - but this was before I had a business and a family. 

I now have close to 800 hours in WH3, and every time I start a new campaign and get into new faction or lord mechanics, I still often find myself contemplating the journey that starts with the first Medieval (no campaign movement - just hop army token from one province to the next) and ends with WH3, with all the campaign shenannigans, flying unit, lores of magic, etc. 

If you have never played TW Warhammer and find yourself at a loss about where to start, my suggestion is to do a bit of research and find a factions that sounds like it would fit your playstyle, then get yourself all the DLCs that have content for that faction. This will be a portion of the total price tag for all three games and DLCs - and will still give you hundreds of hours of absolutely fantastic gameplay.

Enemy combat AI is passable. Even decent, but the campaign so clearly cheats. Enemy factions will go from a crushing defeat, to full strength in a couple turns. Diplomacy is irrelevant when there's so many factions all trying to kill you . No matter how well you play, the battle of attrition is theirs to win.

✅ Factions Feel Completely Different – Seriously, playing as Khorne and then switching to Tzeentch feels like two different games.
✅ Immortal Empires is Insane – Once you unlock it, you’re basically playing the biggest Total War game ever made.
✅ The Battles Are Just Fun – Giant monsters, magic, and total chaos. Watching a Hell Pit Abomination wreck enemy lines never gets old.
✅ So Many Strategic Options – Diplomacy, ambushes, economy—there’s always something to manage.
✅ The Warhammer World Feels Alive – The art, music, and voice acting bring everything together so well.

A Few Things That Annoy Me
❌ Late Game Can Get Slow – Turns start taking longer, and some battles feel repetitive.
❌ Too Many DLCs (But I Still Buy Them...) – Warhammer and Total War fans know the deal. The game is amazing, but expect to spend more money on extra content.

Final Thoughts
I keep coming back to Total War: Warhammer 3 because no two campaigns ever feel the same. Whether I want to build a massive empire or just destroy everything in sight, it always delivers. If you love strategy games, especially Total War, this is easily one of the best.

For a game of this magnitude, there are frankly inexcusable issues that CA simply refuses to fix. This is the third game in the series and has been out for some time, yet basic campaign mechanics literally do not work. 

For example, vassals, especially ones made from minor factions, do not work. They will simply AFK on their main settlement. Additionally, they seem to be largely incapable of winning battles. I once had to reload due to two full stacks of vassals being wiped by an injured tier 1 unit and generic lord. This is made worse by the fact that THERE ARE FACTIONS DESIGNED AROUND VASSALS!!! Chaos is almost unplayable, as they are incentivized to give their stuff to vassals, who will never do anything. Sure, you can try to order them, but 1) it barely works any better than their standard AI. 2) You have to give them orders to attack a specific army or settlement, rather than generic orders or stances such as "be aggressive or defensive". This is only made worse by 3) YOU NEED TO USE A RESOURCE TO ORDER YOUR OWN VASSALS, meaning you are unable to micro them into being useful (not that it would be possible even with unlimited points given how poorly they work). 

Another example is the diplomacy. Want to get a trade agreement with a faction that's not of your race? I hope you're okay with wasting potentially hundreds of thousands of gold to get them to agree. But, if you give them a settlement, no matter how insignificant, they will likely do anything, including become your vassal (for as much good as that will do you). This does not seem to be effected by how much land or armies they have. On top of that the diplomacy is bare bones and hasn't changed functionally from Rome 2.

Lastly, there are antiquated mechanics CA is simply too lazy to update. The biggest thing that comes to mind are rogue armies; full stacks of random, often high tier units (that make 0 sense lore wise; Lizardmen wood elf pirate raiders? Really?) that will wander around your border with impunity until they decide randomly to begin attacking your settlements, often when your armies are on the other side of the map fighting real factions. If you're especially unlucky, they'll attack you early enough in the campaign to essentially make it unplayable, as they start with full, high tier armies for free. 

Bonus: The DLC practice is known to be predatory and excessive. Want the full roster for your favorite faction? I hope your fine with buying 1-2 DLC for it. 总结：非常好玩，但是慎入

如果你是一个战争+经营+策略类的PVE玩家，这个游戏极度好玩。战争大场面、绚丽的火焰和魔法、差异极大的阵营玩法和思路，宏大的故事叙事，这款游戏基本上能满足你所有的需求！

但是，慎入……因为这是一个超级消费陷阱。游戏70%的乐趣在于超凡帝国模式（你可以理解为全球攻略模式）。这个模式你可以和队友联机（出乎意料的是，国内开加速器后链接状况还不差；最保险的方式是下载Radmin VPN虚拟局域网联机），你也可以单机自己玩。这时候你将面临最核心的消费陷阱：你玩的阵营一般都是基础包，只有该阵营的基础部队、领主和英雄。在你没买入DLC前，你遇到同阵营的DLC的传奇领主，你甚至无法通过外交方式跟他合邦！而这些DLC不但包括3代的DLC还横跨1代和2代。比如我玩的蜥蜴人我就要买二代的3个DLC才补全！跟基础包比起来，完全体的阵营直接让你的兵种类型翻倍，运营架构也更加复杂和耐玩。

总而言之，如果你不是该类型的深度玩家，切记慎入！如果你是PVP玩家，这款游戏也极度不推荐，所谓平衡性稀烂，新DLC的阵营会严重超模。仅推荐：深度经营类PVE玩家（其实经营也只是配料，战斗爽才是核心内容）

As a longtime fan of the Dark Elves, I was initially disappointed to see them nerfed in Warhammer 3. Their economy, previously overpowered due to slave mechanics, has been toned down significantly, making it harder to amass wealth quickly. Their legendary lords, while still powerful, feel more vulnerable, and their armies require more tactical management rather than brute-force domination.
However, despite these nerfs, playing Dark Elves is still incredibly rewarding. The challenge of balancing economy, public order, and aggressive expansion adds a new layer of depth that wasn’t as pronounced before. They remain a powerhouse in naval warfare and aggressive raids, and once you master their new mechanics, they still offer one of the most fun and dynamic experiences in the game.
Longevity and ReplayabilityWith over 200 hours played, I can confidently say Warhammer 3 has incredible longevity. Every playthrough feels different, thanks to the variety in factions, starting positions, and strategic possibilities. The Immortal Empires campaign (which combines all three games into one massive world) is an absolute game-changer, offering an almost infinite amount of content for those who love grand strategy.
Multiplayer has also seen improvements, with better co-op mechanics and new features that make playing with friends more engaging. Whether you’re competing in PvP battles or working together in a co-op campaign, Warhammer 3 ensures there’s always something to do.

Final VerdictTotal War: Warhammer 3 is the definitive Warhammer strategy experience. The improvements in map size, mechanics, and faction diversity make this game a worthy successor and a fitting conclusion to the trilogy. While there are some balance issues (especially for longtime favorites like Dark Elves), the game is still a masterpiece in the strategy genre.
Pros:
Vastly improved campaign map with more strategic depth.
Reworked siege battles that feel more engaging.
Diplomacy is finally meaningful and useful.
Unique faction mechanics that make each playthrough distinct.
Immortal Empires offers near-unlimited replayability.
Great improvements to AI and battle mechanics.
Cons:
Some factions, like Dark Elves, feel weaker than before.
Occasional performance issues and bugs.
Realm of Chaos campaign can feel a bit ''scripted'' at times.
Overall, if you’re a fan of Warhammer, strategy games, or both, this is a must-play. It may take some time to adjust to the new mechanics and faction changes, but once you do, Total War: Warhammer 3 offers an incredible experience that will keep you coming back for more.
Final Score: 9/10

DLC policy and CA being a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ company aside, the game is really just held together by duct tape and its a genuine miracle its functional.

Granted I've on Linux through Proton - another issue being its lacklustre native Linux support, the performance is an absolute nightmare. Medium settings 1080p on the Immortal Empires grand campaign map yielded me ~30-40fps on an RX6600, 1440p High is 40-60fps on my current RX6800. CA's previous titles, Attila and Rome II have noted performance issues on Linux using Proton, but from what I've gathered this is a lesser problem in their newer titles. However this is not the only issue, but one of many. The game itself has bugs, poorly implemented mechanics and features, outright missing animations and more. Empire handgunners, mortars, free company militia ALL LACK RELOADING ANIMATIONS. How can they screw up on something this basic when Medieval II managed to do it swimmingly on a 32bit engine in 2006 designed for PC's MAGNITUDES slower than what we have today. This game is supposed to be pure eye candy - you're supposed to be dazzled by the epic duels between lords, the impact effects of magical weapons, it is SUPPOSED to distract you from the fact its an unbalanced, cheesy joke of a grand strategy title. It's the allure of form over function yet they fail at even accomplishing this. Gore effects, which cost money (Blood for the Blood Gods III) mainly to keep the game's age rating down, are so ugly to look at, its only when zoomed out where it looks remotely acceptable.

The siege overhaul that came with TW:WH3 is also a poorly implemented, often FRUSTRATING mechanic that makes the auto-resolve button a greater temptation than its ever been. Pathfinding is utterly broken, careful maneuvers entirely broken by palisades the enemy AI placed. Indirectly they've made the AI a real challenge, but not by making it any more competent (its not) but by giving it abilities and mechanics that break up your own unit cohesion. Yes, pathfinding and unit formations have been notoriously bad since Rome II but I think Warhammer 3 is the first game where I actively avoid particular engagements because of it.

These are just a few issues to ♥♥♥♥♥ about among a twenty page list of problems this game suffers and for each update that fixes something, the update also happens to break something. I'm honestly surprised that the CUHMINITEE is so easily pleased and swayed by CA, make a bunch of meagre promises, a slight adjustment to their pricing model and the seals start clapping again. The game is still in an early access state or at the very least feels like it, the release had a LOT of issues and granted most of those are fixed, but the game has always been held together by duct tape and the number of oversights are just astounding. There are indie studios with 1% of the budget that are more passionate and jump at the opportunity to fix a bug or oversight that has been discovered. And perhaps it always does come down to it, CA know they have a cash cow and the franchise, or in particular the IP will sell regardless of its numerous issues. There's really no market incentive to create a more optimised or polished experience, especially if the community are there to fix it (the Community Bug Fix mod is highly recommended).

As someone who has played every game in the Total War: Warhammer trilogy extensively, not to mention all the other Total War titles, I can confidently say that this is the most ambitious and polished entry yet.

The game builds on the strengths of its predecessors while introducing new mechanics that add depth and replayability. The factions are incredibly diverse, each offering unique playstyles, mechanics, and lore-rich experiences. Whether you prefer the brutal hordes of Khorne, the cunning deception of Tzeentch, or the disciplined ranks of Grand Cathay, every campaign feels fresh and distinct.

The Immortal Empires mode is a dream come true, seamlessly merging all three games into one colossal sandbox. The sheer scale of the world, combined with the improved diplomacy, battle mechanics, and customization options, makes this the definitive way to experience Total War: Warhammer.

The Realms of Chaos campaign, while divisive, provides a narrative-driven challenge that forces you to adapt and stay engaged. Meanwhile, the AI improvements and UI refinements make managing large empires smoother than ever.

Visually, the game is stunning, with gorgeous battlefield environments, detailed unit models, and spectacular spell effects that bring the Warhammer world to life. The soundtrack is equally impressive, perfectly capturing the epic and dark fantasy themes.

While not every game has been perfect, Total War: Warhammer 3 has evolved significantly since launch, with patches and DLC continually refining the experience. I know the price of the DLC's have been a sticking point but well worth it if on sale. The dedication from the Devs on expanding and balancing the game ensures that it remains engaging for veterans and newcomers.

If you’ve enjoyed the previous games, Total War: Warhammer 3 is an absolute must-play. With its deep strategy, thrilling battles, and endless possibilities, it’s the ultimate fantasy strategy experience.

Ich bin ein bisschen zwiegespalten. Nach 3 Jahren wird das Spiel immer noch für 59,99€ verkauft. Nach langer Wartezeit war es dann endlich Mal im sale (60%) und ich konnte mir einen ersten Eindruck verschaffen. Zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt habe ich den Prolog und den Anfang der ersten Kampagne gespielt.

Da es mein erstes "Total War"-Spiel ist, habe ich keinen Vergleich. Für mich fühlt sich alles zuerst etwas zäh an. Es wird viel erklärt (auf der Oberweltkarte wurde ich andauernd unterbrochen, was den Spielfluss stört), die Schlachten fühlen sich deutlich länger an als es nötig zu sein scheint und der Gegner fällt mir gern in den Rücken (was mich mehrfach einen zweiten Versuch hat starten lassen). Generell ist jede Schlacht machbar. Die Lernkurve fühlt sich nur etwas zu lang und flach an, um wirklich in Fahrt zu kommen.

Musik und Geräuschkulisse sind wirklich gut gelungen. Die deutsche Vertonung kann sich sehen lassen...wenn sie zu hören ist. Denn manchmal wechselt das Spiel zwischen zwei Sprechern und während der eine deutsch spricht, höre ich vom anderen nur englisch. Die Untertitel kann man zwar anschalten, nur ist die deutsche Übersetzung teils richtig mies. Es ergibt schon alles Sinn, doch die epische Geschichte wird sehr stumpf übertragen.

Optisch macht das Spiel viel her, wobei die Designer mir etwas zu viel Freiheit in die Oberwelt gesteckt haben. Allein der Prolog war ein leichter over kill an fliegenden Felsen, Schädelburgen, Lavagruben, usw. Das hätten sie auch etwas simpler halten können. Ihr wisst schon...es ist Fantasy. Aber irgendwann ist es deutlich zu viel davon.

Die Story nehme ich dem Spiel noch nicht ganz ab. Klar, Warhammer Fantasy ist (genau wie 40k) ein ewiges Prügeln zwischen den einzelnen Völkern und ab und zu gucken auch Mal die Dämonen vorbei. Nur hat die komplette Aufmachung nicht den Hauch von Originalität, sondern wirkt wie eine Mischung aus Warcraft 3 und Diablo 2. Ein Prinz der im eisigen Norden böse wird? Check. Ein alter, weiser Mann, der mit seinem Buch Weisheit verbreitet? Check. Und das alles bevor die Kampagne richtig los geht. Das ist ein Start, der mir starkes Kopfkratzen bereitet.

Nach drei Jahren ist den Programmierern auch technisch noch etwas durch die Lappen gegangen. Zum einen habe ich sofort auf über 10 Zwischensequenzen Zugriff, ohne diese freigeschaltet zu haben. Zum anderen muss ich im Prolog einen Charakter opfern, der danach noch dreimal mit mir gesprochen hat. Keine gute "wenn...dann..."-Programmierung.

Ich werde dem Ganzen noch etwas Zeit geben und hoffe alles wird besser und zugänglicher. Eine Empfehlung kann ich noch nicht aussprechen, doch dafür bin ich auch nicht wirklich qualifiziert.

O engenho humano, sempre ávido por domar as vicissitudes do tempo e da história, encontra neste título um artifício engenhoso, onde a tática e a reflexão caminham de mãos dadas, como se a própria guerra, em seu rude esplendor, se convertesse em arte. Longe de ser um simulacro inerte das campanhas de outrora, o jogo resgata, com destreza e elegância, o espírito belicoso dos primeiros Total War, conferindo-lhe um fulgor renovado, mas sem macular a essência que o fez célebre.

O que se vê, portanto, não é um simples retorno às raízes, mas antes um requinte meticuloso dessas mesmas estruturas, aprimoradas sem a impaciência do ímpeto juvenil que, em sua pressa de inovação, por vezes se afasta do que há de mais sólido em sua tradição. Aqui, o peso das decisões não se esgota no ímpeto das batalhas, mas reverbera nos corredores do poder, onde a diplomacia se impõe não como capricho, mas como necessidade. O equilíbrio entre a pólis e o campo de Marte nunca se mostrou tão bem engendrado.

O esmero na ambientação não se limita ao detalhe pictórico, mas adentra o domínio da evocação histórica, tornando cada campanha não um mero exercício de conquista, mas um entrelaçar de destinos, onde impérios surgem e fenecem ao sabor das escolhas do jogador. Há, no movimento das tropas e no fervor do embate, um rigor que transcende o simples deleite lúdico, elevando-o a um exercício quase literário, como se cada batalha fosse um capítulo de uma epopeia que se escreve a cada carga de cavalaria e a cada guinada da fortuna.

Se outrora a série, em seus primeiros lampejos, encantou pela audácia e inovação, este título retoma tais virtudes com uma maturidade que se nota em cada pormenor, como um veterano que, após longas campanhas, regressa não com o ardor dos jovens, mas com a sabedoria dos que já viram o destino oscilar entre a glória e a ruína. Mais do que um jogo, um tratado sobre o poder, a guerra e a eternidade.

Итак, я провёл немало бессонных ночей, погружаясь в мир Total War: WARHAMMER III и исследуя его глубины. Я сражался с демонами, сдерживал натиск орд и пытался понять, что же происходит в этих мирах, охваченных хаосом и психоделическими видениями. И теперь я готов поделиться своими впечатлениями.

Что же это за игра?
Для тех, кто ещё не знаком с Total War: WARHAMMER III, это третья часть эпической трилогии, объединяющей масштабную пошаговую стратегию с тактическими сражениями в реальном времени во вселенной Warhammer Fantasy Battles. Здесь огромные демоны сражаются с воинами в тяжёлых доспехах, а маги разрывают реальность на части. Всё, как мы любим!
Плюсы этой игры:
1. Эпический размах, невиданный ранее.
2. Огромная карта. Просто огромная. Восточные земли Катая, ледяные пустоши Кислева и, конечно же, ужасающие миры Хаоса — мир стал невероятно большим и разнообразным. Хочется исследовать каждый уголок, завоевать каждую провинцию и установить свой порядок (или хаос) на этих землях.
Фракции. Восемь фракций, каждая из которых представляет собой уникальный игровой опыт. Здесь и китайская супердержава Катай, и русские медведи Кислева, и все четыре бога Хаоса со своими демоническими армиями.
Царства Хаоса. Это глоток свежего воздуха, хотя и с примесью гнили. Механика прохождения через порталы в царства демонов, чтобы спасти или поработить бога-медведя, действительно впечатляет. Каждое царство — это уникальное испытание, и прохождение их ощущается как отдельная мини-кампания.
Юниты. Они прекрасны, брутальны и разнообразны. Художники CA постарались на славу. Каждый юнит выглядит потрясающе, и наблюдать за их схватками в бою — одно удовольствие. Особенно удались демоны: мерзкие, страшные, но невероятно крутые.
Оптимизация. Это больное место всей серии. Да, патчи немного улучшили ситуацию, но до идеала ещё далеко. На больших битвах FPS может проседать даже на мощном оборудовании.
Кампания. К концу она может наскучить. Механика с порталами в царства хаоса поначалу увлекательна, но к середине кампании она начинает утомлять. Особенно если вам не нравится постоянно отбиваться от набегов демонов.
Баланс. Он… есть? Некоторые фракции кажутся явно слабее других, а некоторые юниты — слишком мощными.
Новички. Будет непросто. Если вы никогда не играли в Total War, то WARHAMMER III — не лучший выбор для начала. Игра сложная, механик много, и разобраться во всём сразу будет нелегко.
Вердикт: замах на рубль, удар на копейку… нет, на полтора рубля!
Несмотря на все недостатки, Total War: WARHAMMER III — это отличная игра. Эпический размах, разнообразие фракций, потрясающая графика и захватывающие сражения — всё это делает её одной из лучших стратегий последних лет. Да, проблем хватает, но Creative Assembly активно работает над их решением. Если вы фанат Total War или Warhammer, то WARHAMMER III обязательна к покупке. Если вы новичок, то будьте готовы к трудностям, но оно того стоит.

So, I've spent a lot of sleepless nights diving into the world of Total War: WARHAMMER III and exploring its depths. I've fought demons, held back hordes, and tried to understand what's going on in these worlds of chaos and psychedelic visions. And now I'm ready to share my impressions.

What kind of game is this?
For those who are not yet familiar with Total War: WARHAMMER III, this is the third installment of an epic trilogy combining large-scale turn-based strategy with real-time tactical battles in the Warhammer Fantasy Battles universe. Here, huge demons are fighting warriors in heavy armor, and magicians are tearing reality apart. Everything we love!
The advantages of this game:
1. Epic scale, unprecedented before.
2. A huge map. It's just huge. The eastern lands of Cathay, the icy wastelands of Kislev and, of course, the terrifying worlds of Chaos — the world has become incredibly large and diverse. I want to explore every corner, conquer every province and establish my own order (or chaos) on these lands.
Fractions. Eight factions, each representing a unique gaming experience. There is the Chinese superpower Katai, and the Russian bears of Kislev, and all four gods of Chaos with their demonic armies.
Realms of Chaos. It's a breath of fresh air, albeit with a touch of rot. The mechanics of going through portals to the demon realms to rescue or enslave the bear god are really impressive. Each kingdom is a unique challenge, and completing them feels like a separate mini-campaign.
Units. They are beautiful, brutal and diverse. The CA artists did their best. Each unit looks amazing, and watching them fight in battle is a pleasure. The demons were especially successful: nasty, scary, but incredibly cool.
Optimization. This is a sore spot throughout the series. Yes, the patches have improved the situation a bit, but it's still far from ideal. In big battles, FPS can sag even on powerful hardware.
The campaign. She might get bored by the end. The mechanics of portals to the realms of chaos are fascinating at first, but by the middle of the campaign it begins to tire. Especially if you don't like constantly fighting off demon raids.
Balance. Is he... there? Some factions seem to be clearly weaker than others, and some units are too powerful.
Newbies. It won't be easy. If you've never played Total War, then WARHAMMER III is not the best choice to start with. The game is complicated, there are a lot of mechanics, and it won't be easy to figure everything out at once.
Despite all the drawbacks, Total War: WARHAMMER III is a great game. The epic scale, the variety of factions, the stunning graphics and exciting battles — all this makes it one of the best strategies of recent years. Yes, there are enough problems, but Creative Assembly is actively working to solve them. If you are a fan of Total War or Warhammer, then WARHAMMER III is a must-buy. If you're a beginner, then be prepared for the challenges, but it's worth it.

I love the Total War Warhammer series and believe this is where the franchise is shining. I wish a Dawn of War dark crusade-esq RTS (aka modern 40K) would come in this format, but for the earlier medieval era of Warhammer this delivers. 

The factions, animations and units are great and the new mode is interesting, but not exactly what I was after. I want the Mortal campaign style all out war, not racing to an objective or lose kind of scenario. I understand this might not be everyone's cup of tea, but the game has this and so I am happy. 

There are some issues, such as your allies and companions A.I. is not the brightest and can leave you strung out despite good relations and their impending doom. I also feel like diplomacy in this game is non-existent. You can be a much superior faction, have all the cards, and it wont matter half the time because the faction you wish to parlay with want your left leg, right arm and first born son to just have a non-aggression pact. 

However, this game still delivers a fun and addictive RTS and for anyone about Warhammer this is a no-brainer. Whether its fighting for the empire, waging war for the waagh or collecting skulls for the skull throne, its got the warhammer goodies and I really enjoyed my time playing this.

ESPAÑOL:

Habiendo jugado Rome: Total War (lanzado en 2004) y considerándolo uno de mis juegos favoritos de todos los tiempos, tenía grandes expectativas para Total War: Warhammer 3. Como fanático de la saga, compré Warhammer 1, 2 y 3, junto con numerosos DLCs para disfrutar la experiencia lo más completa posible.

Sin embargo, mi experiencia con Warhammer 3 fue profundamente decepcionante. Intenté jugar con las facciones recomendadas para principiantes, pero siempre terminaba siendo abrumado por otras facciones de manera irreversible. Cuando lograba hacer algún progreso en la campaña, inevitablemente aparecían ejércitos enemigos que arruinaban mis avances. Probé al menos cinco razas con diferentes héroes, pero el resultado siempre fue el mismo: frustración en lugar de diversión. Nada que ver con la experiencia estratégica y gratificante que ofrecía el Rome: Total War original.

Además, el control de los ejércitos en las batallas me pareció un caos absoluto. Gestionar mis unidades de manera efectiva resultaba complicado y torpe, haciendo que cada enfrentamiento se sintiera más como una lucha contra la interfaz que contra el enemigo.

En general, siento que este juego representa una involución para la franquicia. Lamento haber invertido tanto dinero en un título que me resultó tan poco disfrutable y aburrido.

ENGLISH:

Having played Rome: Total War (released in 2004) and considering it one of my favorite games of all time, I had very high expectations for Total War: Warhammer 3. As a devoted fan, I purchased Warhammer 1, 2, and 3, along with numerous DLCs to experience the game in its most complete form.

Unfortunately, my experience with Warhammer 3 was deeply disappointing. I tried playing with the beginner-recommended factions, but I was always overwhelmed by other factions in an irreversible way. Whenever I managed to make some progress in the campaign, enemy armies would suddenly appear and destroy my advances. I tried at least five different races with various heroes, but the result was always the same: frustration instead of enjoyment. It was nothing like the strategic and rewarding experience of the original Rome: Total War.

Moreover, controlling my armies in battles felt like total chaos. Managing my units effectively was cumbersome and unintuitive, making every encounter feel more like a struggle against the interface rather than a true tactical challenge.

Overall, I feel that this game is a step backward for the franchise. I regret spending so much money on a title that turned out to be so unenjoyable and dull.

This is the most important game in the overall trilogy and one of the best product Total war has ever released, but the entry fee is down right violent. In short this is easily an A to S rank game for people who like this specific type of strategy games so easily 7 or 8/9.

In terms of gameplay you are divided into two different modes being the grand campaign and the battles which gives an intresting balance between macro and "micro" gameplay. 
In the grand campaign you are typically tasked with the management and growth of cities while transporting armies to cull and conquer thy enemies. What's made unique here is the massive variety in both factions, playstyles, and mechanics that make most nations feel drastically different. Paired with the fantasy elements of diverse building and territory and youll find each faction often has very different priorities leaving a constant evolving game of entertainment despite is relative simple interactions.
In the battle game mode you are zoomed into a battlefield where you guide massive block of hundred to thousands of soldiers in a grand conflict. This is the most iconic portion of Total war games and is made more interesting with the fantasy aspect. Typically these battles rely on careful placement of troops which often makes real historical examples of strategy valuable even in a video game simulation, but Warhammer allows the aspect of immense variety from horrific beasts, land sweeping spells, variable technological advancements, and awe inspiring lords and the entire model is flipped on it's head with immensely deeper and more amusing gameplay and strategy. 

Story wise, this game is rich in history as it feed off the establish lore of the warhammer fantasy series that easily fill libraries. This leaves the world full of weird yet interesting characters like the rat hordes of skaven or the swashbuckling schizo vampires of the pirate seas. These variety is truly endless and allows for an ever expanding game much to the detriment of players wallets. Warhammer 3's story line and base factions are kinda basic as it takes a heavy focus in the northern regions with the humans and demonic factions reside, but this is compensated by a feature that will be discussed further down.

Graphically the game looks very wonderful especially for a strategy game which are not known for quality. This is especially appreciated for a game with assets as unique as warhammer. Where I can find fault is often some simple variation like grand campaign structures or simple soldier variation can often be lacking.

Now for the most important part and weirdest portion: microtransactions. Total War Warhammer works on a simple model of game assets that additional units and factions from DLC, but Warhammer 3 is very different from how they performed other games as it has a grand-er campaign call mortal empires which instead introduces EVERY SINGLE FACTION into the game in one massive board from the entire trilogy. The issue is to play it you must own all three games. SO I highly recommend waiting for a sale.
The benefit to this system is you do not need to install the older games nor their DLCs to have access to them as they are all preinstalled into the 3rd game, but you do need to own the game/ DLC and have it in your library for the game to acknowledge access to said content. This does mean you should look through DLC content of the prior games for things you specifically want especially since older games had heavy focus on certain factions. 

Modding is also very well supported in this game both in multiplayer and singleplayer. This game specifically has and extremely high amount of mods especially considering the inclusion of old content, so it's something I highly recommend as it can greatly fill any qualities of gameplay that feel lacking.

Title: "Total War: WARHAMMER III - Prince Yuri's Journey: From Hope to Despair... But Mostly Despair."

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)

Review:

Step 1: Start your journey with Prince Yuri, the "brave" hero of Kislev, ready to find the lost god Ursun and save the day.
Step 2: Realize that the Chaos Wastes are an absolute nightmare, your army is starving, and morale is lower than your hopes for survival.
Step 3: Watch as your army begins questioning your sanity. Even your brother starts looking at you like, “Bro, we’re all gonna die.”
Step 4: Pray to Ursun for guidance, because that’s what all good leaders do when they have no idea what’s happening. Suddenly, Ursun’s like, “Yeah, keep going, bro. It’s gonna get worse.”
Step 5: Fight off a bunch of Chaos freaks in the town of Beacon, because clearly, this is what you need when you’ve already lost half your men.
Step 6: Chase a guy named Skollden, who’s apparently the main villain, like “Nah, I don’t have better things to do.”
Step 7: Beat Skollden at Dervingard, then take his cursed sword (because that’s what every good hero does—pick up cursed items).
Step 8: Realize Ursun’s call is getting louder, but also realize you’re probably gonna die in the process. Guess what? It only gets harder from here!

Prince Yuri’s campaign is basically a survival simulator where hope is an illusion, your army is falling apart, and Ursun has very questionable “guidance” for you.

But hey, at least you’ve got a cursed sword to definitely make everything better. Right?

TL;DR: Total War: WARHAMMER III: Play as Prince Yuri, the guy who thought finding Ursun would fix everything, only to discover that everything is just chaos, betrayal, and death. But at least you get a cool cursed sword, so... yay?

Total War: Warhammer 3 ist der krönende Abschluss der epischen Strategiespielreihe, die Fantasy und komplexe rundenbasierte Strategie vereint. 

Schon die Vorgänger haben eine beeindruckende Tiefe geboten, doch dieser Teil toppt alles mit seiner riesigen Welt, den fantastischen Fraktionen und den intensiven Echtzeit-Schlachten.

Eines der Highlights ist die Kampagne, die nicht nur durch ihre epische Story besticht, sondern auch durch die einzigartigen Spielweisen der verschiedenen Völker. Jede Fraktion hat ihre eigenen Mechaniken, Einheiten und Strategien, was die Wiederspielbarkeit enorm erhöht. Besonders gefallen hat mir die spielerische Freiheit, die es ermöglicht, unterschiedliche Wege zum Sieg einzuschlagen.

Grafisch setzt Total War: Warhammer 3 ebenfalls neue Maßstäbe. Die Detailverliebtheit der Einheiten, die beeindruckenden Zaubereffekte und die epischen Schlachtfelder lassen das Warhammer-Universum lebendig werden. Doch diese Grafikpracht fordert auch ihren Tribut: Das Spiel ist anspruchsvoll, was die Hardware betrifft. Ich empfehle dringend eine SSD und eine starke Grafikkarte, um das volle Potenzial auszuschöpfen.

Der Mehrspieler-Modus ist ebenfalls ein echtes Highlight. Gemeinsam mit Freunden riesige Kampagnen zu spielen oder sich in epischen PvP-Schlachten zu messen, sorgt für unzählige Stunden Spielspaß. Besonders die Koop-Kampagne macht mit mehreren Spielern richtig Laune, da man zusammen strategische Pläne schmieden und umsetzen kann.

Allerdings gibt es auch Schwachstellen: Die KI ist nicht immer auf der Höhe, was zuweilen frustrierend sein kann. Manche Fraktionen sind anfangs schwer zu meistern und verlangen viel Einarbeitung. Zudem kann die Performance auf weniger leistungsstarken PCs manchmal zu Wünschen übrig lassen.

Insgesamt ist Total War: Warhammer 3 ein herausragendes Strategiespiel, das Fans der Reihe und des Warhammer-Universums begeistern wird. Es bietet taktische Tiefe, eine beeindruckende Inszenierung und einen hohen Wiederspielwert. Für Strategie- und Warhammer-Fans ein absolutes Muss!

I wish the Steam review system had a "neutral" score... but here we go. I'm playing this "trilogy" religiously ever since launch, 30 minutes, 1 hour almost every day, even published mods in the workshop. Looking at the time wasted, it can be interpreted I love this toxic drug, it entertained me, etc.. but the numbers are deceiving, the concept of "waste" can be considered one of the many flaws of Total War as a franchise since they switched to the Rome 2 engine, currently TW is at its lowest, nonexistent optimization, flawed engine, overpriced as hell, godawful PR from Creative Assembly and so on.

Warhammer "3" is nothing more than a glorified expansion of TW Warhammer "1" released all the way back in 2016ish, this game is almost 10 years old and it shows. Completely dependable of mods to be enjoyable, offers double A production value and charges premium prices for EVERYTHING (literally, even the blood effects are paid separately). Mods are a whole nother can of worms, very similar to Bethesda (I consider Creative Assembly the poor cousins of Bethesda, they share the same exact issues, but one is triple A, the other double A), it's a nightmare to organize, these supposed "2000 hours"? Just bu11sh1t, artificial... I lost more time organizing the mod menu, testing what works, what doesn't, if compared to actually playing and enjoying the game. I lost count how many times I played for a while, 10, 15 turns or so, the game crashes and I have to reorganize the mod list from scratch, testing one by one like a complete idiot... here it comes a superficial "patch" or yet another DLC adding reskins? The mod list explodes again. It's like my own personal circle of hell, the definitive guilty podcast/brainless game.

When it finally works, 300 mods or so properly setup? Again, just like Bethesda games, the Warhammer "trilogy" becomes very fun and engaging. But you need infinite patience to reach this scenario. This "third" game features a sandbox world map of the Warhammer Fantasy setting, that is enticing, but the performance is horrendous, each turn takes a full minute to load right at the get go, it gets progressively worse as the sandbox keep cycling (so again, the time wasted factor, a typical 100 turns campaign? You waste at least 4 to 5 hours just waiting for the turn completion)... if heavily modded? Oh boy, just double the waiting, the Rome 2 engine is a sin against humanity.

So, I can't be neutral, if heavily modded, this game is a 8 out of 10. "Vanilla", no mods whatsoever, no egregious DLCs, etc.. 5 out of 10. Overall, even with all my time wasted, I know people consider "time" as "currency" in this hobby, hours of "content" = value... but quite honestly, between giving a thumbs up or down for this dream Fantasy game infested with predatory DLCs? You see the thumbs down, but it's actually a closed fist. For strategy fans, TW pretty much has a pseudo monopoly, we don't have a choice, literally the only strategy game with a proper 3D "war" engine. So, if you are either a strategy or a fantasy fan in general (this take of Warhammer has everything, no wonder it's so popular and addictive, every single fantastic creature and folklore imaginable), then buy this crap on a heavy promotion, like 75% discount at least (as an expansion should be priced), be rational and DON'T support the predatory monetization, Creative Assembly is one of the most anti-consumer devs in the market, CA and Paradox treat us like cattle, don't let them abuse your love/addiction to the strategy subgenre

One of the few games where you can watch fantasy battles play out where there is a good combat system lying underneath. I don't care for the Warhammer lore, but since it is pretty much just a collection of standard fantasy and cultural tropes, you can just consider it to be "a" fantasy world and pick and choose which parts you are interested in.

While the game has a number of issues, many related to the old underlying technology, you can tell the people working on the game care for it and want to make it good, and it was mostly mismanagement that was affecting its development to poorly. (That is the case with most game developers/tech companies these days. CEOs are eternally greedy.) Glad that they came around after the Shadows of Change update.

A giant improvement (mostly overlooked due to drama) was the AI changing in (Shadows of Change I think?), which made the game so much less rote, making it so that even in the first 10 turns, you don't always follow the same path.

It's less of a long-term game since most of the content is within the first... 50 turns? The game gets really bogged down with leveling up lords/heros that it always pushes me to start a new one rather than try to complete a specific campaign. 

This game will never be perfect until they make a new engine that properly supports modding and also that doesn't make your video card melt simply from viewing the main menu.

But despite all its issues, it is a really solid game that you can play however you wish and get a lot of fun out of it.

一、游戏性：被数据异化的战略艺术
《战锤3》的底层逻辑暴露了EA对"全面战争"系列的致命误解：它不再是一场关于征服与信仰的博弈，而是一场精密计算的数值狂欢。

1. ​​「胜利条件」的陷阱
​资源通胀危机：新增的"血魔法"与"混沌腐败"系统本应丰富战略维度，实则演变为无脑囤积资源的军备竞赛。玩家被迫在地图上投放大量低效建筑只为兑换性价比存疑的单位，战略纵深被压缩成Excel表格的数值对冲。
​兵种相克沦为数学公式：龙族骑兵对兽人的压制力随等级提升呈指数爆炸，而非基于战场动态的战术选择。一场千人会战可能因敌方领袖装备了+5斩杀的腰带而瞬间逆转，系统性崩坏让"以弱胜强"的浪漫主义彻底死亡。
2. ​​「多人合作」的伪命题
​盟友即耗材：联机模式下盟友的AI行为充满黑色幽默——当你急需援军时，他们大概率正在你的边境无脑推进，用你的领土当练兵场。合作机制更像是在服务器后台运行的大型MMO，缺乏真正的协同叙事。
​匹配机制的羞辱：低配玩家与满级氪金佬同屏作战时，体验如同用玩具剑对抗重机枪。EA所谓的"动态难度平衡"，实则是将付费玩家的数据优势武器化。
​二、视觉奇观：资本堆砌的虚妄神殿
《战锤3》用4K分辨率与实时光线追踪编织了一具华丽的黄金笼子，可惜玩家不过是笼中雀。

1. ​场景设计的意识形态
​景观霸权：从燃烧的帝都到冰封的北境，场景美术完美复刻了战锤IP的哥特式美学。但当玩家需要反复横穿同一片风景屠杀NPC时，这种美学沦为了 performance 的燃料——每一帧都在提醒你："看，我们烧了多少钱！"
​单位模型的空心化：龙族鳞片的反射光效堪比珠宝店橱窗，但角色面部表情永远凝固在程式化的愤怒与狂喜中。即便是巫妖王这样的终极BOSS，其战斗动画也像是被AI生成的抖音神曲MV。
2. ​技术缺陷的皇帝新衣
​帧率刺客：在2K分辨率下，《战锤3》勉强能维持30FPS，但开启"史诗"画质后，战场会突然陷入PPT式卡顿。更讽刺的是，游戏内甚至没有帧率限制选项——EA宁可让玩家忍受锯齿画面，也不愿牺牲那几毫秒的GPU性能。
​物理引擎的笑柄：巨龙轰塌城墙时，碎石块会以完美的抛物线落入玩家脚边；千人军队冲锋时，士兵们保持着诡异的6足兽式步伐。这些"电影级"特效背后，是连基本碰撞检测都懒得优化的敷衍。
​三、叙事自杀：消费主义对IP的肢解
《战锤3》的剧情像是从漫威宇宙剪接的废料拼贴，连原作最核心的黑暗基调都被稀释成快餐式的过家家。

1. ​角色塑造的扁平化
​英雄模板复刻：新登场的精灵王子与人类女武神共享同一套成长树与台词模板。他们的"悲剧命运"沦为装备商店的促销文案——"购买此角色皮肤，解锁限定哭泣动画！"
​反派的人设崩塌：混沌帝君不再是无尽的混沌本身，而是变成了会发表励志演说的直播主。当他在屏幕上大喊"赐予我力量吧！"时，你会错觉自己正在看《英雄联盟》的皮肤展示视频。
2. ​DLC预售的阴谋
​本体即众筹：游戏本体包含的"完整战役"实际上只是《战锤2》的简化版，真正的内容需要购买售价40美元的DLC《皇帝陨落》。这种"买椟还珠"的营销策略，让《战锤3》沦为了EA年货线的又一个韭菜田。
​剧情断层的嘲弄：结局直接跳转到《战锤4》的预购页面，连彩蛋都变成了充值页面的广告。当玩家以为自己参与了史诗叙事时，才发现自己不过是资本齿轮上的润滑剂。

Total War: Warhammer III – это одновременно грандиозное завершение трилогии и игра, которая на релизе вызывала вопросы. Сейчас, после множества патчей и DLC, она наконец-то чувствуется цельной и проработанной.

✅ Плюсы:
✔ Глобальная карта – огромная, насыщенная, особенно с режимом "Империи Смертных". Теперь можно править ВСЕМ.
✔ Разнообразие фракций – Катай, Кислев, Демоны Хаоса, Дао-Тан – каждая со своими механиками и стилем игры.
✔ Дипломатия и управление стали сложнее и интереснее (но ИИ всё равно иногда делает странные вещи).
✔ Битвы стали эпичнее – осады переделали, появились новые возможности, но ИИ всё ещё иногда не справляется.
✔ Легендарные лорды и кастомизация – особенно прокачка Демон-Принца.

❌ Минусы:
❌ Оптимизация – на старте была ужас, сейчас лучше, но всё ещё требовательна к железу.
❌ Сюжетная кампания слабая – беготня по реалмам Хаоса может раздражать.
❌ ИИ местами тупит – особенно в осадах, да и в дипломатии бывают моменты 🤡.
❌ DLC-шный кошмар – многие крутые фракции за пэйволлом (но мы-то знаем, что это стандарт для TW).

🎭 Вывод:
Если ты фанат Warhammer Fantasy или серии Total War, то брать однозначно стоит, особенно с DLC. Если ты новичок – лучше начинать с Total War: Warhammer II и потом идти в третью часть.

⚔ Оценка: 8/10 (Если есть DLC – 9/10)

💰 Стоит ли брать по фулл-прайсу? – Только если ты очень любишь Warhammer. Иначе жди скидок.

This is a fun game, however it's no Total War game. 
If you play this as an RPG and treat even mid tier units as acceptable casualties that sometimes get nuked without you even noticing, it's quite fun. But it's nowhere near what you'd expect if you played other Total War games. Even heavy infantry is extemely squishy against projectiles, every battle revolves around heroes, magic, high mass cavalry (and giant units) and massed missile troops. 

Maps are too small. Microscopically small. Medieval 2 (2004) had huge maps with interesting terrain while maps in Warhammer 3 are so small you can't pick your terrain. You need the entire width of the map to engage the enemy in larger battles, you can't play around specific terrain features of your choosing. Large, mongol style horse archer armies are great against some factions in theory but fail because the map is too small to evade, so your fully upgraded hobgoblin wolf raiders can get caught by much slower ogre bulls simply because the entire map is covered in ogre bulls and there's not enough real estate for evasion. I would give this an middling rating rather than positive or negative, but as there are only two options... I've played quite a lot of the campaign, and overall this game is a bit of a frustrating mess. There are lots of good bits but equally there are a fair few negatives. The game is split between a strategy style campaign map where you move your armies about and try to form an empire, managing your economy and various other factors as you do. When you meet an enemy army you then play an RTS style battle. The problem is both of these sections are rough, feel half baked and poorly play tested, with endless unbalanced content being added without the fundamentals being sorted out.  
The campaign first. Positives, conquering territory is quite fun, it looks ok in that kind of overly saturated pastel colours (the Dawn of War III look) way that games like to sport nowadays (although I think Warhammer II looked better personally). The negatives... god it is an exercise in grinding and torture to play on the higher difficulties. Difficulty comes not from clever AI but from slowly grinding down one enemy after another. Diplomacy is quite frankly broken, and factions will either like you or hate you regardless of your relations if the AI wants someone to attack you in the back. Getting in a defensive or military alliance with another faction is an excuse to use them to make you go to war with random enemies as they 'get attacked' by a faction that is nowhere near them, but strangely has three stacks next to you settlements. Yes congratulations Creative Assembly competitive AI is all about attacking you at the opposite end of your empire to the one you've just been fighting on all the time, and timing it so it happens just before the enemy you've been fighting before can be completely wiped out. Great fun watching some legendary lord and three other stacks who you previously had not problems with, suddenly decide to attack you in the back wrecking all the settlements you've painfully spent the pathetic amount of money you've won, because CA can't think of anything cleverer to do to make things more competitive. This happens everytime, you can time it, one settlement away from wiping out your enemy, boom some random declares war. AI units wander over territory's owned by other factions they're at war with to attack you ignoring their undefended settlements. Allies fall asleep on the campaign when you are both at war with someone. Chaos factions, despite being no longer being the end game crisis of choice, seem to all act as one, not really fighting each other, and if you end up fighting one they all eventually pile in. There are countless other ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to deal with. Fighting some factions is the definition of grind, you can fight battle after battle but the enemy will magically keep pumping out units, even if they are down to a couple of settlements (Nurgle is the main culprit here). There is almost never a 'decisive' battle, where you break the back of resistance. There is an auto resolve, which is a joke, and useless if you have a faction that likes using trash units. It also likes forcing you to fight certain battles even when you know you are way more powerful than the enemy. Winning a campaign is strangely an uncelebrated affair as a simple text screen declares you have won, with no fanfair or some screen of your lord in triumph. If you want to go and conquer the whole map, good luck as it is huge and will take some time for no reward..
Ok the battles themselves, they look great (albeit very intensive on the graphics card), it can be a lot of fun, but god the balance is all over the place. Some units or legendary lords are totally overpowered, and there is a tendency for power creep with later released lords being way better than the ones released with Warhammer 1. There are some ridiculous magic spells and nukes that have massive area of effects and can literally wipe out your entire army if you are clumped together, which is really fun if you have a rubbish army you need to clump with to get results (how about limiting spell damage to 25 - 50% of health max CA, it would really make playing with trash less sole destroying). There are way too many unit melting abilities and enemies in the game, which means half your army can literally disappear in the few seconds you look away at some other part of the map. Then again other spells seemingly have little effect (gaze of nagash anyone - literally useless). Tactics are virtually pointless (beyond cheesing the retarded battle AI or hiding in a wood), as the bonuses you get from flanking or charging are often completely negated by some units just being OP. There is no way a couple of units of trash will beat a really good unit using good tactics, which seems a shame. CA nerf okay lords, but seemingly let others that really need a nerf go unaltered (Tarmukhan I'm looking at you, you or your army at least, need a massive nerf). I could go on with the gripes but wont... The AI also commits the (IMO) cardinal sin of knowing where your units are all the time and knowing where they are going, which again limits tactics somewhat. The main problem with battle though is actually controlling your units. Clicking on the flag above your units or the unit itself to select them is often blocked by a invisible hit boxes from units in front, forcing you to whiz the camera about to try and zoom in. The same problem happens when you try and target an enemy unit. Even when you tell a unit to do something they often stop randomly or get caught up in an enemy unit and ignore what you telling them to do forcing you to constantly reissue commands. Your more powerful units will often stop duelling the enemies powerful units and start fighting trash usually getting themselves killed. The AI never has this problem strangely enough and often magically disengages from the centre of large melee blobs whenever it feels like it. This game really needs a toggle that forces the unit to just do what you tell it too, ignoring any distractions, even if it is to its detriment. I would turn it on permanently. A game that purposefully ignores what you are telling it to do is a major frustration. There are also some siege battles where you have to fight in a town. These are awful and the auto-resolve loves forcing you to fight them, meaning they are sadly mostly unskippable. 
Basically the game feels like CA haven't actually play tested properly, they keep adding things to it, which is great, but never sort out the fundamental issues. It is also quite buggy, flying units go in slow mo while chasing fleeing enemies, fire at will is, at the time of writing, broken. If you conquer too much of the map, and have too many items in your inventory the game likes to max out the CPU/GPU when you view the inventory screen and then crash. There are many more. 
Is it worth it? Sort of, there is a lot of content (at a price - god lawks they even charge for the privilege of seeing some blood), but getting every pack, even on sale, is going to set you back a fair amount. It's also a lot of Warhammer, so if you like the table top this will be up your alley (Games Workshop have no idea how to balance their game either!) It would be nice to have a bit of customisation, perhaps being able to limit the map to certain areas to simplify things or removing certain factions from the game. For a beginner the immortal empires campaign is completely overwhelming, with hundreds of factions each with their own random abilities and mechanics to get your head round, so being able to shrink things down would probably be more fun for a beginner. 
Overall a good game at the core, somewhat ruined by a engine that needs some serious tweaking. Warhammer II was probably a better game overall, but now lacks the content of the third, and I actually preferred the slower, more tactical, battles in Warhammer I myself, even if it lacked some of the funky effects of the latter two entries.

Total War Veteran from medieval 2, Rome, Rome 2, Shogun 2, Empire, and Pharaoh. 

Get. This. Game. 

I have a total of about 800 hours of my life spread across Warhammer 1, 2, and 3 (with the latter having  almost 600 hours at time of writing). The amount of replayability, diverse gameplay, cutting edge battles, abilities, mechanics, and units this game has to offer, you would be a FOOL to not get this game if you are a Total War lover. 

That being said, I have some gripes. The story campaign (Realm of Chaos) is a total snoozefest and the endgame of Immortal Empires doesn't have as much weight as previous installations had (such as realm divide in shogun, mongol invasion in medieval). The diplomacy is alright but there are some nuances missing that Pharaoh Dynasties expands upon (understandably since its a newer game). You do lose out on city management and importance of trade items that a lot of other titles focus on such as medieval, empire, and shogun, as this game focuses a lot more (imo) on battles. Which, if you like the battles of total war, you need this game. You could be losing a match hard but because you've got a spellcaster, it turns the tides. 

But if you're looking to give your time to learning each race unique mechanics, you will have so much fun playing. Even playing a faction within a race can yield you some amazing differences. For example, I'm a big vampire and vampire coast player- one faction will have you mainly fighting elves and the other will have you fighting humans. One focuses more on a specific unit and the other focuses on plundering. Each faction is quite unique and offers so much variability such as playing with just heroes, making a one man doomstack, recruiting only certain units. 

I give this game a 9.2 out of 10. If there was more emphasis on diplomacy and city management, it would be a 10.

Warhammer 3 ist der würdige Abschluss der Total War: Warhammer-Trilogie und stellt alles, was die Serie so besonders macht, auf beeindruckende Weise unter Beweis. Als Spieler wird man in eine Welt geworfen, die vor epischen Schlachten, faszinierenden Fraktionen und einer dichten, lebendigen Geschichte nur so strotzt. Hier sind einige Gründe, warum Warhammer 3 ein absolutes Meisterwerk ist:

1. Atemberaubende Grafik und Detailverliebtheit
Schon bei den ersten Minuten wird klar, wie viel Liebe zum Detail in der Welt von Warhammer 3 steckt. Die Umgebungen sind atemberaubend und reichen von frostigen, gefährlichen Gebirgen bis zu dunklen, chaotischen Landschaften. Jede Fraktion hat ihren eigenen einzigartigen Stil, und die Models der Einheiten und Charaktere sind unglaublich detailliert.

2. Faszinierende Fraktionen und neue Spielmechaniken
Warhammer 3 führt nicht nur bekannte Fraktionen weiter, sondern bringt auch spannende neue Völker ins Spiel, darunter die mystischen Chaosgötter und die Kriegsmaschinen der ostasiatisch inspirierten Cathay. Jede Fraktion spielt sich anders und erfordert neue Strategien und Taktiken. Besonders die Chaosgötter bieten eine völlig neue Spielerfahrung mit dunklen Ritualen und einer einzigartigen Wirtschaft. Das Hinzufügen dieser Fraktionen gibt dem Spiel eine enorme Vielfalt, die nie langweilig wird.

3. Tiefe und fesselnde Kampagne
Die Geschichte, die sich um die Welt von Warhammer 3 spinnt, ist düster, spannend und voller Wendungen. Die Kampagne bringt die verschiedenen Fraktionen in ein interessantes und konfliktreiches Setting, das dich ständig fordert, taktische Entscheidungen zu treffen und neue Gebiete zu erobern. Das große, offene Endgame lässt den Spieler viel Freiheit, das Spiel nach eigenen Vorstellungen zu gestalten.

4. Eine beispiellose Schlachtenintensität
Die Total War-Serie hat schon immer für ihre epischen Schlachten bekannt, aber Warhammer 3 hebt das noch einmal auf ein neues Level. Ob du nun mit Tausenden von Soldaten in einer gewaltigen Feldschlacht kämpfst oder gigantische Kreaturen gegen riesige Armeen antreten lässt – das Schlachtfeld ist dynamisch, packend und strategisch tiefgründig. Die Möglichkeit, auf den massiven Schlachten zu zoomt und das Chaos hautnah zu erleben, ist einfach unbeschreiblich.

5. Verbesserte KI und anspruchsvollere Herausforderungen
Ein weiteres Highlight von Warhammer 3 ist die verbesserte KI, die nun noch ausgeklügelter ist. Gegner reagieren klüger und stellen dich vor neue taktische Herausforderungen, wodurch die Wiederspielbarkeit immens steigt. Die Mischung aus cleveren Allianzen, Intrigen und feindlichen Übergriffen hält die Spannung konstant hoch.

Fazit:
Warhammer 3 ist ein herausragendes Strategiespiel, das sowohl alte Fans als auch Neulinge in seinen Bann ziehen wird. Mit einer atemberaubend schönen Welt, spannenden Fraktionen und einer fesselnden Kampagne bietet es alles, was man sich von einem epischen Fantasy-Strategiespiel wünschen kann. Wer sich für tiefgehende, taktische Kämpfe und ein lebendiges Universum begeistern kann, wird in Warhammer 3 zweifellos viele Stunden unvergesslichen Spielspaß finden.

Total War: WARHAMMER III — Великолепный, но не без шероховатостей ⚔️

Игре однозначно есть за что поставить лайк. Она масштабная, эпичная, атмосферная — настоящая кульминация всей трилогии Total War: Warhammer. Кампания за Империю Хаоса, осады, масштабные битвы, разнообразие фракций — всё на высоте. Особенно радует Immortal Empires — огромное полотно для стратегов и любителей лора.

👍 Что понравилось:

Масштаб и глубина кампании.

Яркий визуальный стиль и проработка фракций.

Отличный саундтрек и атмосфера.

Постоянные обновления и DLC (если не считать цену).

⚠️ Но есть нюансы:

Оптимизация всё ещё местами хромает: даже на хороших системах бывают подвисания.

Искусственный интеллект в битвах временами странно себя ведёт.

Некоторые механики усложнены без особой нужды, особенно для новичков.

Монетизация: игра уже дорогая, а контента прячется за платными дополнениями всё больше.

📌 Вердикт:
Это игра, в которую хочется возвращаться, особенно если вы фанат Warhammer Fantasy. Но чтобы получить от неё максимум, придётся мириться с багами, ждать патчей и, увы, открывать кошелёк. Тем не менее — это всё равно один из лучших Total War’ов последних лет.

Would I recommend this game Warhammer III to you? short answer yes. long answer well maybe, 
So for a single player game it's amazing if you like grand strategy with a skill based combat system. If you like grand strategy games such as civ, stellaris, crusader kings or hearts of iron i bet you will have a blast in Wh 3. The gist are the same, you start off small and build up your empire conquering the world, reacherching tech, building buildings in your cities, choosing your armies. A turn based empire manager with a different but good combat system.

The campaign: You pick a race to play as and the world has one world campaign. Some campaigns are amazing, others fall short 8/10.

The combat: there still room to improve for the company CA especially when it comes to sieging a fortified settlement. There is a desire for more map variability as some are still pretty bad, boring or have no terrain you can play around. The open world combat experience is kinda simple: your army is lined up on one side and the enemy is on the other side. It's up to you to use your units in an effective way to win. Most unit’s work like rock paper scissors. Example horses or big unit’s is bad vs spears, in the game this is a large unit vs anti large unit, kinda simple. combat 8/10 seaging 6/10

The expansions: this game suffers or thrives depending on how you see it on expansion and extra content. To be honest you don't need any of them. unless you want to experience a specific race and their unique starting location there is no need to get any of them. Sadly tho CA limits some functions and mechanics on the base game when you don't have the major expansions. which in my experience have led to hilarious and game breaking unintended game mechanics. That can be abused or suffered from them. I'd rather see them fix the core problems that the community have been asking for instead of dropping another lord for 20 dollars/euro or you're equivalent. As the game has been out for 3 years, I would expect my units to be able to walk through an open gate instead of climbing a ladder over a wall 200 meters away to get inside the enemy fort. 4/10

Buildings: some races have unique ways of building there stuff some i like alot but what i think most suffer from is choice, its kinda odd how i cant build Tall or wide there is just one form of building unless you want to rush a tec, recruitment building, hero, or a quest. I can't really go as tall as I can in stellaris or in civ, I kinda can go wide but it's unstable and the wider you go the more armies you need. undefended territory will be attacked if you cant defend it, it will be taken. it feels linar 7/10

Multiplayer campaigns: Me and some friends tried the multiplayer when the game came out but it suffers from the same problems as other grand strategy game multiplayer games have. Dsync, longer games, slower games. it probably would be alot of fun just to play 2-3 players but as we were 8 players on the first week of the game it was impossible to get past turn 10 in 8H. na/10 

Multiplayer pvp battles: this one works most of the time, not much to say i didn't play them alot.  na/10

Overall as a single player game i would give it a 8/10

Immortal Empires is the greatest (and most expensive) fantasy strategy sandbox of all time

Is it perfect? No. Is it good? Absolutely. Is it expensive? Yes, Because with the extremely slow bugfixes, poor communications and overpriced DLCs with little content this game doesn't deserve the best strategy games of all time.

Pros:
There are many factions to play as. Finishing the game takes very long time. Contains multiple scenarios of how to achieve victory. It has so many different mechanics and units, the battles and the campaign map are stunning. It's not perfect but they have really come a long way from warhammer 1. Super addictive, and there have been so many small but noteworthy additions that work. Like sieges now cause attrition. If a rival nation lord is parading your lands, you can threaten war if they don’t leave pronto. The sieges with supplies introduced a more protected asymmetric warfare for even more trickery with the defending army. I have sunk over a hundred hours in Immortal Empires Campaign, the maps is so BIG! I played The Empire faction with lord Elspeth Von Draken and it was a joy to hear the gunpowder fire, tank engines, and cannons every time I fought, although I had to buy the full DLC first to be able to enjoy all the lords and units of The Empire. The game is made with the feet, if it wasn't for the steamworkshop I would give it a meh. THANK YOU MODDERS FOR SAVING THIS GAME FROM THE NEGLECTFUL MANAGEMENT OF The Creative Assembly.

Cons:
DLC's are too expensive. Unfortunately,  I have to say the CA's DLC practices were a breath of fresh air. Not because they're great (I'm not giving you that much credit CA), but because none of the main game mechanics were DLC locked so I could just get the factions I liked and play the game worry free because I still can fight all factions in the game even I don't buy the DLC's, I just can't play as them. So, buy the DLC for the faction you want to play, you don't have to buy all the DLC's. It could be so much worse. The game's optimization has improved, but bugs haven't been fixed and there are rarely any quality of life updates because they only focus on updating DLC ​​and creating new units.

Außerdem finde ich die Kampagnen-KI katastrophal.

Kleines Beispiel:
Ich spiele das Imperium mit Karl Franz und bekämpfe die Orks, die inzwischen eine ganze Nachbarprovinz direkt vor der Nase meiner Hauptstadt von einer anderen Imperium-Fraktion erobert und besetzt hat. Ich ignoriere die erste besetzte Stadt und bewege meine Armeen daran vorbei nach Norden wo zwei volle Ork-Armeen warten um die erstmal zu vernichten bevor ich dann die Siedlungen wieder befreien will. 
Tja, Pustekuchen. Während ich mit dem Kampf gegen die Orcs beschäftigt war, haben sich zwei Armeen einer unwichtigen Bretonen-Fraktion (das andere große Menschenkönigreich) von ganz weit weg mitten durch meine Länder bewegt (Ohne einen militärischen Zugang mit mir auszuhandeln, der eigentlich nötig gewesen wäre...) und hat mitten im Herzland des Imperiums die von den Orks besetzte Stadt erobert. 
Jetzt habe ich mitten im Imperium, das ich laut Zielvorgaben eigentlich vereinen soll, eine Stadt, die unter der Kontrolle der Bretonen ist. Um diese abzukaufen müsste ich utopische Summen Geld ansparen, und wer wie ich Wert auf Immersion und etwas Roleplay legt, kann den Bretonen auch nicht den Krieg erklären. So ein brutal unnötiges Dilemma, und solche Situationen rauben mir dann die Lust weiterzuspielen. 

Das war nur ein kleines Beispiel. Es macht einfach nichts Sinn, was auf der Karte passiert in meinen Augen. Und bei einem Spiel, das so sehr vom Charakter der einzelnen Fraktionen und dem daraus entstehenden Storytelling im Verlauf einer Kampagne leben sollte, ist das ein extremer Dämpfer.

Normally, I try to write out long detailed reviews going over things I like, things I don't, and things I would like to see. I'm not doing that here. I'm not going to talk about mechanics or gameplay, or any of that. If you like fantasy, if you like big battles, buy it. Because Immortal Empires is available to everyone now, see what factions you like and then decide what additional DLC you want to get from there. 

I first learned about Warhammer from Dawn of War. I played a Warhammer mod for Medieval 2, and back then I didn't know what Warhammer was. I vastly preferred the LOTR mod or Hyrule Total War because, well, I knew those, I didn't know Warhammer. Here I am now, with over 1000 hours in this game, and quite frankly, I still know very little about Warhammer. I just know I'm a heretic because I love Elves in fantasy and that holds even here in Warhammer. Eldar were my favorite, aside from Sisters of Battle (who doesn't love nuns with guns?), in Dawn of War, because they were literally teleporting space mages. I am what I am. Even after learning that apparently the Elf hate is, I think, because the Elves with their debauchery summoned Slaanesh that basically screwed the Imperium when it screwed the warp? That said, that's 40K, this is fantasy, and there's a lot of factions to choose from.

I never thought that I would willingly play a faction of rats, and yet the Skaven is one of the most delightfully fun factions I've ever played in a game. They are ratsh- insane and I love them. Grand Cathay is my favorite faction, (I wonder what's the only other Total War game where I have over a 1000 hours in that wasn't lost due to platforms ending service); followed by Khorne, then it's a tie between Skaven, Slaanesh, and High Elves. I don't think I've ever played a game, where sometimes you're more than willing to move just about any faction to that number 2 slot, because you actually like them all. It's honestly to a point where I'd put just about the rest of the game in the number 2 slot. Hell the only ones I don't like is Nurgle and Vampire Coast. Nurgle has more to do with I just hate how the map looks in Nurgle corruption and the units are disgusting. Vampire Coast, I mean, I just prefer the Counts, never was a pirate guy. I guess I could put Ogres and Chaos Dwarfs even further below since I never bought their DLC and while I'll probably by Chaos Dwarfs eventually, I don't see myself ever playing the Ogres honestly. They had a really awesome and catchy trailer, but, well, see what I said about Nurgle.

Then there's mods; and I always believe that steam workshop and mod support greatly enhances the replayability of a game. There are some games that are hard carried by it's mods, to the point that you become baffled when someone likes the poorly written vanilla game that breaks it own's rules, then there are games that are just enhanced by the mods from really passionate fans. Like I said, I know very little about Warhammer. I use very unlorefriendly mods, anything that's aesthetically pleasing, I'm probably using. I have freaking Ryuuko Matoi from Kill la Kill and Saber as lords in my game. I have a faction full of weird succubi that's actually really well made. Slaanesh vs Miao Ying, I played it. Corruption I played it. Total Warmaidens, I don't play without it anymore. Don't google those btw, unless you know what I mean. What am I even talking about at this point? I don't know, I have a 1000 hours in this game, that should be the only thing you need to see for whether I recommend it or not. But I'll stop typing here.
