Сюжетна кампанія базової гри — найслабша частина. Реальне м’ясо починається з Immortal Empires, де масштаб настільки абсурдний, що стратегічне мислення йде на задній план, а виживання стає головною метою.

Фракції надзвичайно різноманітні. Грати за Нургла — це як керувати гниючим годинником. За Катай — як намагатись втримати баланс на вершині айсберга. Грінскіни — суцільний хаос і драйв. Кожна кампанія — це окрема гра.

Глобальна карта прекрасна. Бої — кінематографічні, хоч бери й знімай. Але є проблеми: оптимізація не завжди на рівні, ШІ часто дивує абсурдними рішеннями, а баланс — це окрема гра з Тзінчем.

Це гра, яку варто купувати не заради конкретного режиму, а заради досвіду: стотисячних армій, зради союзників, кривавих облог і моментів, коли один загін орків рятує імперію від загибелі.

Не ідеальна. Але грандіозна. І якщо ти вже відкрив портал — назад дороги нема.

IA:
Oui — dans Total War: WARHAMMER III avec le DLC Tides of Torment, Dechala, the Denied One est devenue notoire pour être extrêmement puissante en bataille, à tel point que dans certaines parties elle peut détruire plusieurs armées ennemies à elle seule, y compris celles menées par des légendaires comme Balthasar Gelt.

🔥 Pourquoi Dechala est si forte

Très hautes stats et mobilité : Dechala est un Seigneur légendaire unique du Chaos dédié à Slaanesh qui combine haute vitesse de mouvement, dégâts en mêlée massifs, et capacités débilitantes en combat rapproché.

Compétences mortelles : Ses styles de combat (« Dance of Destruction », etc.) lui permettent de tailler des unités en pièces rapidement.

Unités de soutien puissantes : Son armée est composée de troupes très agressives (champions, slaangors, Preytons, etc.) qui accentuent sa force globale.

Mécaniques de campagne fortes : Elle génère des avantages uniques (corruption, décadence, structures spécialisées) qui accélèrent sa domination sur la carte.

💥 Des exemples concrets de domination

Des joueurs rapportent qu’elle peut littéralement balayer des armées complètes, même lorsqu’elle est en infériorité numérique, grâce à sa vitesse, ses dégâts et ses résistances, ce qui inclut des victoires individuelles contre des forces nombreuses commandées par des seigneurs puissants comme Balthasar Gelt.

Dans certains cas de campagne, Dechala a vaincu des stacks entiers du joueur, écrasant et détruisant plusieurs armées sur plusieurs fronts sans aide substantielle d’alliés ou de renforts.

D’autres témoignages de la communauté confirment qu’elle peut devenir une véritable machine à tuer si elle est laissée libre de croître et de recruter.

🧠 Conseils si tu joues contre elle

Ne fonce pas tête baissée avec uniquement des unités lentes ou non spécialisées — elle éclate facilement l’infanterie pure.

Évite les compositions trop défensives : face à elle la mobilité est essentielle.

Certaines unités antichars ou armes lourdes peuvent aider à la ralentir, mais une bonne stratégie de bataille reste cruciale.

Total War: WARHAMMER III is a massive fantasy strategy experience that combines empire management, diplomacy, character development, and enormous real-time battles into one remarkably deep package. Developed primarily by Creative Assembly and published by SEGA, it represents the third major entry in the Warhammer branch of the Total War series and expands heavily on the concepts established by its predecessors. Its greatest accomplishment is the sheer variety it offers, allowing players to control civilizations and supernatural armies that differ substantially in appearance, campaign mechanics, military composition, and battlefield tactics.

At the campaign level, the game asks players to manage settlements, construct buildings, recruit armies, research technologies, conduct diplomacy, develop powerful characters, and decide how aggressively their territory should expand. These systems are closely connected, so a strong military means little without an economy capable of maintaining it. Expanding too quickly can expose poorly defended provinces, while remaining passive gives neighboring powers time to grow. The result is a satisfying strategic rhythm where short-term military opportunities must constantly be weighed against the long-term stability of an empire.

The Realm of Chaos campaign provides a more narrative-driven experience centered on an escalating supernatural conflict. Kislev and Grand Cathay stand alongside the terrifying forces associated with the Chaos Gods, while the customizable Daemon Prince offers an especially distinctive campaign. The Daemon Prince can equip different body parts and receive abilities connected to the Chaos powers, giving players considerable freedom to shape both his appearance and battlefield role. Each major faction also possesses unique mechanics, encouraging players to learn different economic, diplomatic, and military approaches rather than simply repeating the same strategy with a new army.

Real-time battles remain the centerpiece of the experience. Infantry formations clash while cavalry attacks exposed flanks, missile units fire from protected positions, artillery pounds distant targets, and enormous monsters smash through conventional troops. Heroes, Legendary Lords, flying creatures, and spellcasters make engagements even more unpredictable. Successful commanders need to understand terrain, morale, fatigue, unit matchups, positioning, flanking, and the proper timing of special abilities. Magic can completely alter a battle when used effectively, whether by damaging concentrated enemies, disrupting formations, strengthening allies, or weakening dangerous targets.

The extraordinary diversity of the armies is one of the game's strongest qualities. A disciplined human force can play completely differently from an army built around daemons, monsters, magic, or highly specialized units. This asymmetry extends beyond combat because factions have individual campaign systems that influence expansion, resources, recruitment, and diplomacy. Starting another campaign therefore feels more meaningful than merely choosing a different location on the map. Learning how to exploit a faction's strengths while compensating for its weaknesses provides much of the long-term satisfaction.

Immortal Empires significantly increases that longevity. This enormous sandbox brings together a vast collection of factions and territories into an open-ended campaign where players can establish their own objectives. Conquest, diplomacy, defensive alliances, economic development, and personal rivalries can produce unpredictable stories without requiring the player to follow a tightly scripted route. For anyone primarily interested in the classic Total War experience of building an empire and gradually dominating a gigantic strategic map, Immortal Empires is arguably the most compelling part of the package.

Multiplayer adds another substantial dimension. Players can participate in competitive battles or undertake campaigns cooperatively, making it possible to experience grand strategy alongside friends rather than limiting multiplayer to isolated battlefield encounters. Different multiplayer formats accommodate players interested in direct tactical competition as well as those who prefer the slower progression of a shared campaign. Considering how lengthy a normal Total War campaign can become, cooperative play can provide an especially memorable experience for a dedicated group.

Visually, the game benefits enormously from the freedom provided by the Warhammer universe. Frozen kingdoms, corrupted wastelands, elaborate cities, magical landscapes, grotesque daemons, dragons, gigantic monsters, and colorful magical effects create a battlefield spectacle that historical strategy games cannot easily reproduce. Zooming from a broad tactical overview down to individual warriors fighting beneath towering creatures remains impressive. Sound design reinforces the scale through roaring monsters, artillery impacts, massed soldiers, magical attacks, and appropriately dramatic music.

The enormous scope also creates drawbacks. New players face a steep learning curve because they must understand economic management, diplomacy, construction, recruitment, character progression, faction-specific mechanics, and real-time tactics. Campaigns can become complicated once several wars develop simultaneously, and managing numerous settlements and armies eventually introduces considerable micromanagement. Artificial intelligence can occasionally make questionable strategic or tactical decisions, while units sometimes require additional attention when navigating crowded battles or responding to commands.

Performance can also be demanding, particularly during large engagements or when using higher visual settings. This is not a lightweight strategy game, and its combination of detailed battlefields, numerous units, effects, and enormous campaign environments can place considerable pressure on hardware. The amount of additional content available across the broader trilogy is impressive but potentially expensive for players determined to build the largest possible collection of factions and Legendary Lords.

Steam Deck compatibility is a notable limitation. Total War: WARHAMMER III is not officially supported for Steam Deck and should primarily be regarded as a desktop PC experience. Unofficial experimentation and compatibility-layer changes may produce varying results, but its demanding performance requirements, complex interface, large-scale battles, and control-heavy strategy gameplay make the handheld a poor choice compared with a conventional PC setup. Players purchasing specifically for Steam Deck use should therefore approach it with caution rather than expecting a reliably optimized handheld experience.

Ultimately, Total War: WARHAMMER III succeeds by combining an enormous strategic sandbox with wonderfully excessive fantasy warfare. Its complexity can be intimidating and its technical demands are significant, but few strategy games offer comparable faction diversity, campaign scale, battlefield spectacle, and replay potential. Immortal Empires further transforms an already substantial game into a long-term strategy platform capable of supporting hundreds of hours of experimentation and conquest. For players willing to invest the time required to understand its many interconnected systems, it delivers an exceptionally rewarding blend of grand strategy and real-time warfare.

战锤3这款游戏，我个人认为，购买还是很值得的。
       从2000年开始游戏的发展来看，红警2和星际争霸，是一代人的回忆。虽然里面只有军队，但是没有领导军队的首领（或英雄），但依然是一代经典，那时候电脑里面必装的游戏。同时期的暗黑破坏神2，确是只有英雄，没有军队，也是大家经常网吧联机打的游戏之一。
       魔兽争霸3的出现，直接将英雄和军队紧密的联系到了一起，每个英雄有自己独特的技能，同时还可以带一批军队参战。战锤系列依然沿用了这一玩法，但是这样有可能出现游戏英雄等级到50以后，游戏作战玩法大多重复。面对很大的地图，不停的重复操作上一回合的操作过程，次数多了之后，多少会对游戏感到乏味，虽然战锤3有很多不同派系、不同英雄可以选择，但是，同一国家（或势力）到英雄50级以后的重复操作，难免让人从开始的新鲜感逐渐过渡到感到乏味。
       战锤3推出很多新的DLC在不断的更新着各种派系的玩法，期待这些玩法来给玩家带来持续的新鲜感。不知道是否能够出一款这样的DLC，骑马与砍杀2的战斗和攻城系统+战争传说的扎营系统，通过做任务（骑马与砍杀1和2中有）和战争，来赚取金钱，用来维护自己的军队、在交通要道之上（或附近）购买土地，然后在这片土地上建设自己独特的城堡或堡垒。如果是山地则建成关隘，如果是平地则依靠河流建成城堡。关隘和城堡用来征兵和训练军队、保护后方的城市，而城市的功能则是用来收税赚钱，每年给自己国家的贵族根据等级发放金钱。而不同的英雄则拥有不同的技能，利用自己的技能和带领的军队取得战斗的胜利。

全战系列的头牌，亲儿子。
虽然D加密，虽然优化很垃圾，虽然DLC很离谱，虽然。。。等
但是能满足玩家同时操控万人同屏开展中古战锤大战的作品，差不多也就仅此一家了。
所以只要玩法尚在，美术不掉队太狠，本垃圾依旧还是会玩一玩的。

There's going to be a lot of asterisks here, but at the end of the day, I absolutely recommend this game. The community loudly, frequently complains (oftentimes they're right to!) and that might put you off, but to be honest this game is FABULOUS. It's the best of the total warhammer games because it fixes the things about the past games that irks me, has EVERYTHING, and the new problems it introduces are not worse than the problems of past TWH games.

Great new factions, great new stuff. If you've never played a game like this before it can be very overwhelming, and even if you're used to playing historical total war it can still be quite tough to learn how this game differs from it. Stick with it and you'll find something wonderful here for you, though!

The modding community is EXCELLENT and I strongly recommend looking into it if you get this game.

The asterisks I mentioned earlier however are all dollar signs. Yes, you can play every faction in every total warhammer game in this game, in multiplayer, with your friends - and with massive awesome improvements like having everyone able to participate in battles that you play out and don't autoresolve (in past games you either autoresolved or wasted your friends' time, here you can elect to give them control over this or that unit or set of units in your army, or they can even try to take up the other army's side and fight you! It's GREAT. Giant, giant improvement, favorite change for sure!)

Yes, you can do this. However.

The price tag is [i]severe[/i], and it's very difficult to know whether or not you'll enjoy a faction without playing at least a few hours of them. At time of writing, without sales involved, you're spending several hundred dollars to get the 'complete' package, and new DLCs are also not cheap at all.

So if you want to get this game, spend strategically. Wishlist, wait for sales. The game is excellent, and having access to ALL the games and ALL the factions and being able to play out the campaigns for the different factions in past games (I think total warhammer 2's campaign is especially neat, I just don't like its gameplay nearly as much as this game) is well worth a significant price tag, we're talking hundreds and hundreds of hours spent having a blast here, and many more with friends - but your wallet's going to feel it.

       除了游戏中的细节，游戏内每个种族都有着自己的科技树、建筑体系和外交策略，玩家可以根据自己的喜好选择不同的种族进行游戏，体验多样化的策略玩法。

Total War Warhammer 2, but expanded. I would say that the jump between 1 to 2 is far bigger than 2 to 3, but this game is the definitive way to experience Total War Warhammer. You have now the option for a campaign which spans all 3 games of factions, many having been updated for the new entry.

Now, it is Games Workshop, and those older factions do require you to have owned the older games (and DLC, for their DLC factions). It can be considered a game which makes the older entries to the series an expansion. But that means it's going to be very expensive. This game is £50, more in dollars, and the older games aren't the cheapest in the world. I do fully recommend getting these games as cheap as you can so it only makes the dent in your wallet that one game would.

The game is being actively developed, for better or for worse, as a number of factions seem to be left in the dust as part of GW's usual schemes to get money out of you. More factions get added, for a price, and they do sometimes make good changes that are healthy for the game.

The game is going to need you to put it on an SSD, just like 2. The first TWW was easily run on even quite old hardware, but 2 and 3 have upped what you need, with battles being painful to enter and exit on and SSD, but near impossible to do within 5 minutes on an HDD. That, and the actual battle maps being able to field more units (while very fun) can be hell for your machine.

Get it if you're already stuck well into Total War Warhammer, otherwise, I think it's just not worth what they're asking you.

Total War: Warhammer III - тяжело описать простыми словами, на бумаге это масштабное стратегическое продолжение серии, которое дарит игрокам богатый и детально проработанный фэнтезийный мир. Игра сочетает классическую тактическую стратегию с масштабными битвами и глубокими элементами ролевой игры. Но с другой стороны эта одна большая палата психбольных, шизиков и людей с особенной натурой. Атмосферности можно не ждать, ведь каждая ваша катка будет похожа на приём грибочков и до гриммдарка вам будет плевать. Цирк абсурда и маразма вот атмосфера этой серии игр. 

Но всё же хочется выделить для себя заметные плюсы :
Графика и дизайн, Визуально игра выглядит потрясающе, особенно новые модели фракций и локаций. Детализация юнитов и окружения, иногда ловил себя на мысли, что явно уделяю бою меньше времени, разглядывая порой хорошие модельки, а порой заметно халтурные. 
Механики кампании кажутся на первые мгновения явно неплохими, да и у многих фракция ныне очень много чего интересного, чего стоят мои любимые Гномы Хауса, с целой новой экономикой внутри самой игровой экономики, баланс между фракциями в целом устойчивый хоть и стоят фракции на тонкой грани баланса. 

Новые фракции и кампании, конечно тяжело обойти стороной многие фракции которые добавили, приятно увидеть тех же демонов хаоса, полноценный кислев. В целом к этому нареканий у меня нет, новые фракции может и казались пустыми на старте, но именно сейчас они более чем забиты механиками и юнитами. Давая вам потратить ещё сотню часов на одно и то же. 

Масштабность по моим меркам кажется только увеличилось и с грядущим ДЛС это станет только ещё краше чему конечно я рад, надо понимать что эта линейка игр как бы не нравилась историческим Плеерам других частей. Всё же не про ваш ебанный реализм в фантезийной то вселенной. И не надо винить что именно ваха губит их игры, просто надо понимать что на подобного рода рубиловки спрос больше. А то что вы дрочите уже десяток тысяч часов в тот же Рим 2 или Аттилу, не значит что вы массовый потребитель. Да и ваха видно что лучше приносит бабки нежели ваши Римы, тут винить разрабов не намерен. Да и ругать фентези за упрощение это уже шиза. 

Улучшена система дипломатии как говорили разрабы, может так и есть, но бот как был тупым так и остался и многие механики на дипломатии может и были хороши, но реализовать их трудно. Но сам факт улучшения есть. 

Ну и как же без Минусов! 

Долгий запуск и технические проблемы, они как были и на старте так и сейчас есть в этом традиция сохранилась, даже со всеми тех пачами, игра имеет много багов любит ломаться, да и ближе к лейту превращается в слайд шоу которое ещё и растягивается до пиздеца. 

Так же выделю желание компании впихивать всё больше и больше фракций когда сами масштабы карты уже этого не выдерживают, от чего комично смотреть на абсурдные спавны лордов которые там и не было даже по лору или логике. Переизбыток лордов во фракциях, при не желании менять на корню масштабы карты, будут приводить к тому, что миноров начнут скорее всего в целом выпиливать из игры. Ведь всеми силами видно что разрабы ну очень не хотят работать над изменением пропорций карт и локаций на них. 

Что изменилось по сравнению с двумя предыдущими частями? 

Новые фракции и сюжетные линии, конечно номинальные, но видно что некую сюжетку всё же пытаются реализовать. Что интересно но в рамках такого жанра больше рудимент. 

Графика и интерфейс заметно скакунли как и требования, но картинка и правда сочнее и ярче, особенно с прибытием самих сил хаоса. От чего банально хотя бы не устаёшь на все смотреть даже после сотни часов.

The game is very alluring, yet the gameplay is not convincing, or maybe just not my cup of tea anymore.
I've played TW since the original Shogun and was a huge fan in my teens and early adulthood.
I'm more of a history than Fantasy afficionado and had no prior knowldege of the WH setting.

Yet the WH setting is what draws me to this game and tempts me to buy dlc (on sale), yet the gameplay turns me away.

The giganric, trilogy spanning Immortal Empires world map is gorgeous: beautifully detailed, 288 factions across multiple races with a huge variety of units, leaders and magic. It's beautifully detailed

But I think over the years, the TW formula has gone stale. Battles have become more and more fast paced, and requires too much fast paced micromanagment with the inflation of magicial abilities. Why design all these cool units and animate them when I never have the time to watch them in battle? This has become a thing for me. I wish I could have the AI fight and watch, with the ability to intervene at my leisure. Yet the AI is, after all these years, not competent enough, that I could watch this without a heart attack.
Siege battles have been a problem so long, I think at this point you have to lose all hope when it comes to WH.

So most of the time, it's autoresolve, which is again not working in the TW series, which has been real time battle first, turn based strategy second franchise.
WH does not have enough meat on its bones in the campaign to compensate. It's no Paradox title. It offers variety since each race, and often each lord has its own gimmicks. Again, this is very alluring, yet the core campaign gameplay offers little depth.
Again, the AI is as bad as ever, maybe even worse than in battles. Yet this is compensated by cheesy gameplay and massive cheating by the AI in higher difficulties to offer a challenge. The higher the difficulty, the more they will gang up on the human player. If you love this sort of challenge, you'll probaly find good fun and replayability.

Yet again, the campaign suffers for being too fast paced. Basicially, it's all about the 20-40 turns, where you need to overcome the challenges above, if you mastered this phase, you'll likely be so strong that it will become tedious busywork.
WIth this many factions, it becomes a fast paced Battle Royale, where factions die like flies and others are blobbing.

Because of this, the campaign is long decided before you unlock the late game units, techs and magic which is unfortunate.
This is the core problem of many strategy games: to make the endgame engaging. In WH:TW this is really pronounced.
Depending on the difficulty level, it's more a master-your first 50 turns game than a deep, immersive strategy game.
And so, every time I'm drawn to revisit this game, my initial enthusiasm is through the roof, and plummets within the first few hours.
It's like a fly trap, luring you in to buy more dlc, only to leave you disapointed. 

CA is celebtraing 25 years of Total War, yet the company is at it's lowest point. There are few game series with this many titles, and at this point the only  thing that keeps Creative Assembly afloat, are their shady business / dlc practices. 
The game franchise has been in need of a new engine and focus for so long. After heavy turbulences, they want to announce a new 'era of TW in December.' It may be their last chance to really turn the tide. As a longtime fan, I'm rooting for them.

First, the TL;DR:
Good game, decent support, bad DLC monetization, plus the team takes their time getting to overhauling factions that need it.

And now, the long version:
Alright, the Pros
-Arguably the best of the 3 Total War: Warhammer series, though I'm partial to the 2nd.
-The Immortal Empires (IE) campaign is huge with so factions to choose from and play.
-The team behind the game is (mostly) receptive to community feedback, overhauling older factions, balancing both under-powered/overpowered units and leaders, and releasing new factions and leaders somewhat consistently.
-Multiplayer is now more than 2 players, allowing schmucks like me to host 4-5 people in single IE campaign, just make sure your buds have a decent computer and good interned connection, expect long 'load' times.
-Visuals and Audio design is good.

The Cons:
-The Elephant: Monetization of the DLC. Yes, they now offer each new faction separately, but the price is still egregious considering all new 3 factions per DLC drop is still ~$36CAD when DLCs in the past (TW:WH2) were much easier on the Steam Wallet. 
-The 2nd Elephant: For new players, the ability to play factions beyond the games initial ones will run you up a nice, fat bill. Veteran players that have been playing since TW:WH1 and/or TW:WH2 have access to the starting factions from those games and any DLC they purchased is brought forward, which is nice for not having to buy it twice, but new players need to fork over a lot of dough for the full experience with 3.
-Updates and hotfixes still break your old saves. I know there is update rollbacks, I'm still peeved by this.
-Crashes have been more frequent with each addition or update, even if you start a new campaign after an update.
-The faction support has been lacking for certain factions in this game like Kislev and Cathay. And abundant for others like any of the Chaos daemons. As a Kislev player, I'm not bitter....
-Siege Battles: They still suck. TW:WH1 and 2 didn't have perfect siege battle setups, but I found them more tolerable then in 3. Attacking in a siege still sucks (Butt-Ladders, exploitive attack angles, flying armies laugh at walls) and defending a siege is chore at best (still can't customize your garrison with the units you get from structures, walls are terrible to fight on, towers do next to nothing).

Rating: 6/10
Conclusion: Looks good, sounds good, gameplay is mixed, monetization is still crap. It's still, overall, the best in the series, but, its not the perfect game of the 3. Creative Assembly is far from the worst of video game devs, but the corporate side of them are still greedy as balls. If you enjoyed the previous entries, this game is worth your time, maybe not so much your money, wait for a sale. If you're a new player that's curious, throw this and the previous 2 games on your wishlist and wait for all 3 to be on sale, it's not worth it otherwise.

Background: - 
I grew up watching my best friend play Rome: Total War on a crappy Compaq laptop. That aside, I have very little experience with Total War. I've played Shogun 2 (for a bit, which was great) but if it boils down to games that are 'role-playing a civilisation', I'd always veered to Civ V, and then later - EU IV. Which wasn't to say Total War sucks or is worse than those games - but I've always been more interested in why Marc Anthony challenged Augustus, instead of whether I could win the War of Actium through better tactics/prep-time. A good price on Warhammer 3 came recently this year. I've always had Warhammer 1 and 2, but had difficulties running it prior to my current PC set-up. Those issues were resolved, hence why I decided to give it a bona fide try again in the probably more improved Warhammer 3. 

Review: - 
I wrote a long essay on what I liked and what I disliked in like, my first 20 hours of gameplay - but I'll just summarise the salient points: - 

1. The game has a lot of complexity and the in-game tutorials aren't that helpful. But strategy games are known to be quite non-intuitive. You're going to need a both a willingness to try things out (and screw-up) and a few Youtube videos - but it's not rocket science. You don't need an excel sheet. 

2. The game is fun, and more importantly losing is fun. You can easily pinpoint what went wrong, what kind of non-optimal decisions you're making, and then find out what's the optimal thing to do in that situation. 

3. Sieges suck. Any battle that's not taking place on an open field sucks to play because there's too much micro-managing. Can you get better at it? Probably. Challenges for a different day. Thankfully the game has auto-resolve.

4. Factions play extremely different from one another. Which gives the game variety, strategic depth, and also flavour. If you're playing as Undead Pirates - you literally feel like undead pirates. It's great. 

5. DLC kinda feels like gouging, and having a lot of (fun) additions to the game locked behind a paywall (and not even a cheap paywall...) isn't optically good. I'm not happy with it, but at the same time there's little to no competitors who aren't doing the same thing. Civilisation has the same problem, and Paradox is probably the most egregious offender. FWIW the DLC isn't essential, but it does affect my enjoyment of the game somewhat - knowing that there's a part of a game that I paid for that I have no access to because the developers add things in piece-meal fashion.

Tl;dr buy on sale. Game is good quality and I'm really having a lot of fun! - but you'll need the lower prices just to make the thought of buying the DLC palatable.

《生化危机2重制版》运用RE引擎打造，画面提升堪称惊艳。从警察局那昏暗潮湿、墙壁上斑驳的油漆，到下水道中流淌的污水和散发的腐臭气息，每个场景都刻画得细致入微。在光影效果上，游戏堪称一绝，手电筒的光在黑暗中摇曳，丧尸被照亮时那扭曲的面容和狰狞的表情，让人心惊胆战。雨滴打在地面上溅起的水花、玻璃上滑落的雨水，这些细节让整个浣熊市更加真实，恐怖氛围被渲染到极致。人物建模精细，里昂的坚毅、克莱尔的勇敢、艾达·王的神秘，都通过面部表情和肢体动作完美呈现，让玩家仿佛真的置身于这场生化危机之中。

Great game, but there are a few important things you should know before buying.
1. Some Warhammer lore helps
Knowing the basics of the Warhammer Fantasy universe really enhances the experience and helps you understand the factions and story.
2. Real cost = Base game + DLC + TW1 & TW2
DLCs add new factions, legendary lords, and units. I recommend only buying the ones you're interested in — and only during sales (on Steam or from trusted key resellers).
3. Steep learning curve
This game takes time to learn. For beginners, I suggest:
• Set the campaign difficulty to Easy,
• Battle difficulty to Hard,
• Battle stat modifier all the way to the left (this gives you the biggest boost in battles).
If you're confused about the difficulty system, I highly recommend this video by LegendofTotalWar:
👉 https://youtu.be/k9ZAbYI_gOk
summary: fantastic game, but it takes time, patience, and some extra cash to get the full experience. If you love strategy and fantasy.

Gabe debería permitir una recomendación neutra a los juegos y WarHammer 3 es un buen ejemplo, por que tiene de lo mejor y lo peor al mismo tiempo.

Tiene diversas facciones y cada una tiene una mecánica diferente de juego, lo que hace que cada facción nueva que pruebes sea una novedad y desafió nuevo. Aun tengo pocas horas de juego y recién voy en mi primer facción, pero vengo de mirar muchas campañas en YT donde se aprecia esa diversidad. 

Tiene una mecánica de diplomacia muy buena, en comparación a otros juegos que eh experimentado, casi perfecta. tus acciones afectan el gusto de otros reinos hacia ti, entre esas acciones esta la de que tu amistad con un reino le llega a sus amigos eh iras en una cascada de relaciones, negativas y positivas con esa mecánica del "amigo de mi amigo",  lo que te permite relativamente evitar conflictos que no deseas, aun que también agravar los que ya tienes. Eh llegado a través de la diplomacia a transformar un posible enemigo en un buen amigo que funciona como muro de protección en una zona de mi reino y lo tengo en una guerra contra un enemigo molesto que lleva decenas de turnos ocupado solo con el (le hice la guerra proxy al juego jajaja).

Luego tiene un surtido de todo, varios héroes para subir de nivel y objetos mágicos que conseguir para hacerlos fuertes, un sistema de mejora de tecnología para todo, un sistema de mejoras de asentamientos con varios efectos en la campaña, diversidad de tropas para hacer ejércitos a tu gusto y manera. Un poco de humor con facciones radicales, desde los que te quieren esclavizar, prepararte como un platillo de cena, o abusar sexualmente de ti aparentemente (te estoy mirando a ti elfos negros).

Ahora es cuando hablamos de lo peor y es muy malo. Lo primero que veo tras instalar el juego y empezar mi primer campaña que no sea el tutorial es que toda esa diversidad de reinos que jugar, la mayoría de los que me interesaban, están bloqueados por ser un dlc. Osea, apenas comienzo el juego y lo primero en lo que te deparas es en que compraste siquiera un tercio de juego. Y vez cosas como que te recomienda comenzar a jugar con los altos elfos por ser "facil" y este es un dlc. 

Lo segundo y agrupo dos cosas es el desempeño del juego y el crasheo. Se supone que mi pc a pesar de todo debería de manejar el juego bien, pero cada ventana de carga es como para ir a tomarse una siesta y tienes una ventana de carga al entrar y salir de una batalla, lo que me obligo a optar por hacer mas batallas auto-resueltas que jugar las batallas en si, enserio, deben de ser como 5min cargando. Luego están los crasheos, jamas se me a crasheado tanto un juego en la vida como con este, me paso que en un turno, no importara que, había un reino amigo que quiere ofrecerme un tratado y el juego se crasheaba ahí constantemente, me vi obligado a cargar antes de terminar ese turno, para ofrecerle un acuerdo antes y evitar que el me lo ofrezca mas adelante, pero si eso no funcionaba iba a tener que buscar ayuda en internet de como reparar eso, por que se me iba a quedar ahí la campaña para siempre. Justo hoy vi como un YT para eliminar un crasheo parecido se vio obligado a eliminar toda una facciones de la faz de la tierra jajaja. 

Lo ultimo es un poco la diplomacia y la inteligencia de tus enemigos juntas. Dije que es buena pero al mismo tiempo desde que estoy en mi campaña actual e estado en un constante avance de territorio a través de guerras defensivas, voy unas 9 guerras defensivas vs 3 que recuerde haber declarado personalmente, siendo dos de ellas futuras guerras defensivas inevitables. Estoy jugando con los Kiev que son humanos buenos y trate de ayudar a los humanos buenos como pude pero terminaron arrollados por facciones viles, por esta misma tempestad de facciones malvadas que se van todos a una. Ahora estoy en un punto que declararme la guerra es una sentencia de muerte y con la diplomacia e logrado aplacar potenciales enemigos y quizás poder en el futuro elegir mis guerras, pero e visto morir a todos mis amigos en el camino jajaja. Sobre lo de la inteligencia, ademas de esa torpeza de ver buenas facciones ser devastadas de la nada, me paso de tener un enemigo que me pide la paz y un par de turnos me declara la guerra, mal para el que tenia ya dispuesto 2 ejércitos cerca para invadirlo y rematarlo, cuando llego a su tierra, le ocupo dos territorios que directamente estaban vacíos, el hizo unos ejércitos mas o menos buenos y no mejoro su territorio, no tenia ninguna amenaza eminente y se fue a una guerra que no necesitaba sin siquiera hacer que invadirlo fuera mas difícil que solo golpearle fuerte y pedirle la paz para que deje de molestar.   

Y es eso todo, Warhammer 3 es muy divertido pero tiene unas nanas muy graves,no sabes si decir de darle una oportunidad o mejor buscar otra cosa mas que no arranque pareciendo una estafa,que crashee y tarde menos en cargar.

- you are very familiar with Total War mechanics
- you own the 2 previous titles and their DLCs

- This game is a pass for me. It has deep lore, mechanics, fun battle, and cringey dialogues.

Total War: Warhammer III è, sulla carta, il coronamento di un progetto titanico: un mondo fantasy sconfinato, eserciti leggendari, battaglie su larga scala e la possibilità di plasmare un impero a propria immagine. E in effetti, quando funziona, il gioco sa essere spettacolare.

La possibilità di seguire scenari già scritti o costruirsi il proprio dominio da zero è uno degli aspetti più affascinanti: ogni fazione ha identità e meccaniche uniche, e l’universo di Warhammer viene reso con una cura che è difficile non apprezzare. La direzione artistica è sontuosa, e sul piano visivo Total War non delude mai.

Tuttavia...
Arrivano subito i dolenti accordi: l’intelligenza artificiale è il tallone d’Achille. Sia quella nemica che quella alleata (sotto il tuo comando diretto) spesso prendono decisioni inspiegabili. In piena battaglia può succedere che unità chiave si disperdano, fuggano in maniera poco plausibile o ignorino i tuoi comandi nel momento peggiore.

Le battaglie, per quanto spettacolari, diventano spesso caotiche. Non in senso positivo, ma in quel modo frustrante che ti fa perdere il controllo. Ritirate continue, armate che si sfaldano e rincorse senza senso da una parte all’altra della mappa compromettono l’esperienza tattica, lasciandoti con una sensazione di "confusione gestita male".

Per un veterano della saga — come chi ha vissuto i fasti di Medieval II, Shogun, Rome — l’impressione è che Warhammer III sia ambizioso, ma ancora lontano dall’eccellenza tattica che ha reso celebre Total War. La componente fantasy ha portato una ventata d’aria fresca, ma ha anche appesantito un sistema che fatica a gestire così tanta complessità.

🔧 In sintesi:

+ Universo Warhammer reso in maniera magistrale

+ Possibilità di personalizzazione e varietà delle campagne

– IA carente, spesso irritante

– Battaglie troppo caotiche e mal gestite dal sistema

= Un colosso affascinante, ma con le gambe ancora fragili

I am a former passionate Total war fan (circa 2008 Rome Total War) - I've played Total War Warhammer, Total War Warhammer II and now Total War Warhammer III (about 900 hours on this game and thousands on the second entry). I used to play VH/VH on WH2 but switched to N/N for WH3 as I haven't spent nearly as much time on the game. 

if you're a fan of the series and are considering the purchase of this game or it's DLC, then this review is written with you in mind. If you're new to the series - skip to Conclusion/TLDR at the bottom if, well, it's TLDR. 

1) Launch: 
This entry to the series has been a disaster from day 1. There are tons of reasons why, but I suggest that you give some youtubers like LegendofTotalWar a watch (I'm not going to rehash it here). 

Honourable mentions to the poor launch performance, price increases for DLC and content cuts for DLC. Many of these issues remain.

2) Current state of the game: 
It has improved somewhat from launch (you can only go up from there) but is still nowhere near as enjoyable or interesting as WH 2. WH3 is inferior to it's predecessor in many ways. 

This is because 

2.1) CA has actively been nerfing every fun game system. The wind of magic system and bonuses thereto? Changed for the worse. Trait farming? Pointless. Ranged units OP? ♥♥♥♥'em. Make your lord/unit type a doomstack? Nah fam, how about some goblin ballistas reusing existing models?  I could go on but I'll stop here, 

2.2) CA has actively been nerfing every single fun mechanic for races from the first and second games. High elf factionwide bonuses that incentivises you to continue playing? Nerfed. Ikit's workshop? Nerfed. Vampire counts' free skellies? Nerfed. Not to mention even third game races being clearly inferior or unplayable on launch.

There is a clear preference on the balance for DLC races - that's always been there. The difference from the balancing in game 2 however is that instead of introducing new races with powerful mechanics, they've proceeded to nerf every single race not covered by the currently released DLC to make them more powerful by comparison. I recently quit a Clan Skryre campaign in absolute disgust as a result of how they've nerfed Ratling gunners from WH2. 

3) WH3's strengths
The graphics are excellent
The maps are stunning
The music slaps in a very pleasant way. 
Sounds on the map and combat are well done and very impressive.
Diplomacy rework (though copied from Three Kingdoms) is very well done and the way alliances are created and allied units recruited is visionary. 

All of the above facets of the game are excellent. 

4) Conclusion (TLDR):

Do not buy this game or it's DLC unless it's at a price level that you can afford to waste. Or literally set your money on fire. IT IS NOT WORTH IT'S COST, EVEN ON THE CURRENT 66% SALE (speaking as a peasant living in a third world country). Ain't that much fun either if I'm honest.

If you're new to the series and can afford to spend some money, I can recommend WH1, WH2 and *most* of the DLC for those games (I'm looking at you Chaos Warriors). The state of play at the end of the second installment was excellent and very fun to play. You do miss out a bit on the journey of WH2 as it grew over the years, but it's still a solid recommend from me. 

PS. This review is pending future DLC releases and updates. If required, I will update this review for fairness. The game's trajectory (and CA's quite frankly) for the past 3 - 5 years suggest to me that this is highly unlikely though. Will have to find a new game to scratch my Total War itch :(

Ahoy, Swoonds here.
Do you like being overwhelmed?
Do you enjoy having thirteen armies, each micromanaged by an immortal cockroach of a faction leader who speaks entirely in reverb and roars?

Would you like to spend 400 turns fighting over a single bridge in Cathay, because some AI named Ku’gath just sniffed in your general direction?

Well congratulations.
Welcome to Total War: Warhammer III, a game so large, so absurdly overloaded with systems, menus, spreadsheets, and bugs, that it essentially simulates an actual Games Workshop boardroom meeting.

What is this game?
Warhammer III is the culmination of years of DLC bloat, three game installs, five culture packs, and a working knowledge of ancient Norse demons.

You play a faction. There are over 80.
Every single one is:

Overpowered

Undertuned

Glitched

Or just horrifyingly fun.

You pick one. Maybe you're feeling spicy.
You pick Skaven, the race of radioactive rats who view the Geneva Conventions as suggestions.

Or you play Kislev, a nation of drunk ice mages and literal bears.

Or you play Chaos Dwarfs, which are like normal dwarfs, but angrier, more enslavey, and somehow Italian.

The Campaign
The campaign in Immortal Empires is literally infinite.
You will never finish it.
You will never win.
There is no peace.
There is only turn-ending.

You begin with one city.

You press "End Turn."

35 minutes later, after watching 92 factions shuffle units around like blind chess players having a stroke,
it’s your turn again.

You raise an army.
You go to war.

Then you realize:
“Oh. There are 900 minor factions. And they all hate me. And Ghorst just declared war on me from across the continent.”

Who’s Ghorst?

He’s a necromancer who rides a coffin like it’s a convertible and throws zombies at you until the game crashes.

And that’s just one guy.

Combat
Combat is Total War. You know what to expect.

Form lines.

Micro flanks.

Hit "Start Battle" and immediately pause to micromanage 22 different flying units, spellcasters, and cavalry charges before your GPU melts.

You try to play tactically.
Your archers hold the hill.
Your cavalry flanks.
Your magic rains fire.

Then Khorne shows up, turns off your UI, disables magic, and begins windmilling through your entire frontline like a blender filled with razor blades and heavy metal.

You cast a spell.
It miscasts.
Your wizard explodes.

You sigh, reload the autosave, and continue feeding orphans into your empire's war economy.

Factions (aka Who Do You Want to Suffer As?)
Tzeentch –
Micromanage teleporting pink bird demons who cast time-space nonsense spells that make your enemies confused, then make you confused, then crash the game.

Nurgle –
Play as a walking disease factory with slow, rotting units and a growth system based entirely around... waiting.
Very fun. If you're a Buddhist.

Cathay –
The only faction that cares about balance.
You try to balance Yin and Yang.
It’s peaceful. Zen. Serene.

Then Skarbrand teleports in and cleaves your harmony in half with an axe the size of a truck.

Ogres –
Eat meat.
Move fast.
Die quickly.
And throw cows at people.

Dark Elves –
Capture slaves. Torture them. Make money.
The only faction where your economy depends on human suffering.
Jeff Bezos would be proud.

Dwarfs –
Short. Grumpy. Hate magic.
They don't even ride mounts.
They waddle into battle with artillery that evaporates your enemies.
Except when it bugs out and fires backwards.

Skaven –
You press one button.
It spawns 400 rats.
They all explode.
Victory.

Vampire Counts –
No ranged units. No artillery.
Just wave after wave of corpses and necromancers with anime-tier healing powers.
Get hit? Just resummon your entire army for free.

Magic
This game has 8 lores of magic.

Each one has:

Buffs

Debuffs

Damage

Vortexes

And at least one spell that turns the battlefield into an acid rave of particle effects and glowing diarrhea.

Don’t worry about learning them.
Just pick whatever spell looks the dumbest and cast it 50 times a turn.

The enemy army?
Gone.

Diplomacy
It exists.

And it's completely irrelevant.

You will go to war with someone by accident.

You will get confederated by Teclis because he stubbed his toe.

You will spend 50 turns improving relations with a faction, and just when you're about to ally...
Skarbrand teleports in again and eats their king.

The Bugs
They are legion.
They are eternal.

Your army pathfinds through a mountain and dies.
A minor faction declares war, kills five of your lords, then asks for peace.

Your AI ally blocks your siege.
Your reinforcements arrive on the wrong side of the map.

And when you finally beat the final Chaos realm and claim victory?

Crash to desktop.

Conclusion
Total War: Warhammer III is not a strategy game.
It’s a lifestyle.

It is:

Broken.

Beautiful.

Bloated.

Magnificent.

Chaotic.

And the most demonic dopamine factory you’ll ever install.

You will spend 400 hours perfecting your strategy, mastering faction mechanics, and crafting the perfect empire.

And then install 10 mods that break everything and start over.

I give it:

10/10 end-turn button anxiety
5/5 Blood for the Blood God™
And one Legendary Lord who wiped my save because he farted too hard on turn 47

Buy Total War: Warhammer III.
Buy all the DLC.
Then cry about it.
Then play more.

As always, more content to come.
Stay tuned.

Overall it is a good game. Carried on the previous legacy well.

-All aspects of it are overpriced. Wait for discounts all the time.
-We can not move our capitals or rename Legendary Lords. RP potentials are very limited.
-Settlement models used to change when a different faction captured them. It no longer does that. That is a let down (something we had previously but now gone).

-It would be much much better if the New World with Ulthuan was a larger seperate map travelled through nodes like the Americas in the Empire Total War. But I guess they wanted to fix it at this size for performance reasons. I would've preferred to have the large oceans and distant Ulthuan we had in WH2.
-I liked WH2 more.
-This is the first game we are ever introduced into Grand Cathay. Not much lore is revealed since the Emperor is missing but they are a fun faction to play as.
-Game seems to be still evolving in design. Some Legendary Lords start at very odd starting locations. But one of them (Balthazar Gelt) has a questline that helps him return home once it is done. Only he has it. Others like Teclis or Imrik do not have it. So I assume this is something they came up later, which suggests they are still trying to improve their design and RP potential.

Overall it is a good game. I liked WH2's map more that is all. Buy at discounts.

I was wanting to get into Warhammer and figured picking up the most recent Total War: Warhammer game would be a fun way to do it. It was on sale with all of its DLC. Awesome, let's do it! I get into the game and start up the tutorial. Being a grand strategy game, the tutorial takes way longer than 2 hours to complete (for me it was the 11 hours of playtime I've got with the game).

Finish the tutorial, get into the main game, and find that despite buying what I thought was the complete edition, half the game's playable factions are still locked behind a paywall. Apparently I'm the dumbass for not just knowing that in order to ACTUALLY have the full game you need to buy Total War: Warhammer 2 and all of it's DLC. It certainly doesn't say that on the store page, so I have no idea how I was supposed to just know - or even assume - this as someone completely new to the franchise.

So now I have a new hobby: submitting refund requests. Maybe some day it'll go through. I doubt it since the only response I get is the cookie-cutter "Derrrr it's been more than 2 hours!" response despite the fact that this game is straight-up misleading when it sells you a "complete" bundle and instead gives you a game with half the playable factions still locked behind a paywall.

Üçlemenin son halkası, Warhammer evreninin en karanlık ve en epik dönemlerinden birini sahneye taşıyor. Total War: WARHAMMER 3, sadece büyük savaşların değil; kadim tanrıların, efsanevi kahramanların ve sonsuz kaosun birleştiği bir destanın son perdesi.

Warhammer dünyası, tıpkı insan ruhu gibi karmaşık ve karanlık.
Burası, Khaine’in kanıyla sulanmış topraklardan, Kaos’un cehennem ateşiyle kavrulan Diyarlara kadar uzanan, birbiriyle sürekli savaşan güçlerin çatışma alanı.

Oyunda, İmparatorluk ile birlikte dört büyük kaos tanrısı — Khorne, Tzeentch, Nurgle ve Slaanesh — ve onların yıkıcı orduları sahnede. Khorne’un kan ihtirası, Tzeentch’in entrikaları, Nurgle’ın hastalıkları ve Slaanesh’in yıkıcı arzuları bu dünyayı perişan ediyor. Bu tanrılar sadece savaş alanında değil, oyuncunun stratejik kararlarında da hissettiriyor gücünü.

Bunun yanı sıra, Total War: WARHAMMER 3’te Kislev’in buzlu toprakları ve efsanevi Ulthuan’ın kutsal adaları gibi yeni mekanlar keşfediliyor. Kislev halkı, barbar doğu güçlerine karşı duran son kale iken, Ulthuan Elflerinin büyüsel mirasının merkezi. Bu diyarlar, hem stratejik hem de hikâyesel olarak derinlik katıyor oyuna.

Lore açısından oyunun kalbi, Khaine — eski elf tanrısı — etrafında dönüyor. Khaine’in ölümü ve yeniden doğuşu, elfler arasındaki güç mücadelelerini tetiklerken, tüm Diyarlarda yeni bir düzenin ya da kaosun doğuşuna zemin hazırlıyor. Bu mitolojik çatışma, oyunculara sadece ordu yönetimi değil, aynı zamanda kadim güçlerin, efsanelerin ve kaderin ağırlığını hissettiriyor.

Savaşlar büyük, görkemli ve yıkıcı. Ancak Total War: WARHAMMER 3, sadece fiziksel güçle değil, stratejik zekayla da kazanılır. Hangi tanrıyı destekleyeceğin, hangi ittifakları kuracağın ve düşmanlarına nasıl yaklaşacağın, bu destanın kaderini belirler.

Sonuçta, Warhammer evreninde sadece güç değil, aynı zamanda inanç ve irade önemlidir. Kıyametin gölgesinde yükselenler, sadece kılıçlarıyla değil, ruhlarıyla da savaşıyorlar.

“Diyarlarda yankılanan savaş naraları, kadim tanrıların sesleriyle birleşiyor.
Ve sen, bu kaosun ortasında, kendi efsaneni yazmaya hazırsın.”

[h1]Total War: Warhammer 3 – An Epic Introduction to Strategy[/h1]

[i]As my first experience with the Total War series, Warhammer 3 blew me away with its mix of grand strategy and intense battles.[/i]

[h2]What I Loved:[/h2]
[b]✔ Immersive world[/b] – The Warhammer fantasy setting is rich and detailed, full of unique factions, magic, and monsters.
[b]✔ Strategic depth[/b] – Managing your empire on the campaign map while commanding massive battles feels rewarding and complex.
[b]✔ Stunning battles[/b] – Watching thousands of units clash with spells, dragons, and giant monsters is epic and cinematic.
[b]✔ Accessibility[/b] – Despite being new to the genre, the game tutorials and design helped me learn without feeling overwhelmed.
[b]✔ Expansive content[/b] – Warhammer 3 offers even more factions and an engaging endgame with the Realm of Chaos, making it feel fresh and expansive.

[h2]What Was Challenging:[/h2]
[u]– Steep learning curve[/u] – There’s a lot to grasp, from diplomacy to army composition, but it gets easier with time.
[u]– Campaign pacing[/u] – Some turns felt slow, especially when managing a big empire.
[u]– AI quirks[/u] – Sometimes the enemy behavior is unpredictable or overly aggressive.

[h3]Final Thoughts:[/h3]
[i]Total War: Warhammer 3 is a fantastic gateway into strategy games, combining fantasy lore with deep gameplay.[/i]
[b]It’s complex but rewarding, and I’m excited to explore even more in this rich universe.[/b]

[i]If you’re new like me and love strategy and fantasy, this is a great place to start.[/i]
[i]4.5/5 stars – Epic battles and grand strategy done right.[/i]

ISSO NA PROMOÇÃO!

A Falsa Premissa do "Conteúdo Gratuito" e a Realidade da Venda Casada Velada
A Creative Assembly e a SEGA promovem o Total War: Warhammer 3 como um jogo completo, com sua própria campanha "Realm of Chaos". No entanto, a realidade do mercado e a preferência da vasta maioria dos jogadores é que o verdadeiro "carro-chefe" e motivo principal da compra do TW:WH3 é a campanha "Immortal Empires". Esta campanha, que une os mapas e as facções dos três jogos da trilogia, é percebida como a experiência definitiva da série.

A questão central é: para usufruir plenamente do "Immortal Empires" – ou seja, para jogar com as dezenas de facções e Lords que tornam esse modo tão vasto e rejogável – você é obrigado a possuir os jogos anteriores (Total War: Warhammer e Total War: Warhammer 2) e frequentemente seus respectivos DLCs. A empresa alega que o mapa em si é "gratuito" (não um DLC pago à parte), mas ignora que o conteúdo essencial para desfrutá-lo plenamente está bloqueado atrás de centenas de reais em compras adicionais.

Isso não é um "bônus". Isso é um requisito implícito e custoso para acessar a funcionalidade que, para a maioria dos consumidores, é o principal valor agregado do Total War: Warhammer 3.

Violações ao Código de Defesa do Consumidor (CDC) Brasileiro
A prática descrita acima pode ser questionada com base em diversos artigos do Código de Defesa do Consumidor, que visa proteger o consumidor de práticas comerciais desleais e abusivas:

Publicidade Enganosa (Art. 37 do CDC):
A Trava de Acesso Legado: Ao transformar os jogos I e II e as DLCs antigas em "chaves de desbloqueio" para o Immortal Empires, eles inventaram uma forma de manter produtos de 2016 e 2017 rodando com margem de lucro de jogo novo.

A empresa burla as leis internacionais para tirar dinheiro de você, ela obriga você a comprar a versão 1 e 2, para ter acesso ao jogo venda casada, mas o jurídico da empresa, lança, esses atrelamentos separados, como os vampiros, para justificar que você só compra as versões antigas para liberar mais barato, com isso eles burlam as leis, falando que é DLC e não venda casada, mas não se esqueça, o que eles estão fazendo, é você comprar os jogos antigos e pagar o preço atual por eles, NÃO COMPREM ESSE JOGO, BOICOTEM ESSA EMPRESA!

So.... After countless hours spent at this game. I can say it is at a much better place than it was back in 2022.

This game, is a fantasy strategists DREAM! I have been playing since Warhammer II and after they included the Immortal Empires and KEEP improving it year after year, this game could be probably played indefinitely. The amount of races and factions to choose, the ABSURD size of the map, the real time fantasy battles and ofcourse, the endgame scenarios.
And DON'T get me started about the mods, because the possibilites there on how to alter your experience are truly ENDLESS!

First, if you buy just the game and none of the DLC, i can say you will be missing out but you can certainly choose and pick. The games basic campaign Realms of Chaos and the tutorial are heavily story focused and are certainly quite good. The tutorial is just great for any newcomer to the series and the Realms of Chaos is a great launch point for anyone starting this game. It is esentially a race for whoever gets to the finish line first (after getting four metaphorical parts of a key, in four distinct and unique demon Realms). After you finish it once, its basically the same for the other lords here as well but that excluding the DLC lords.

I think the MAIN lure and what will get you to spent hours and hours on those "One last turn" moments, will be the Immortal Empires campaigns. They are esentially a sandbox mode with the whole world (or at least most of its) as your canvas to paint with your factions colors but still.. Your own sort of narrative and motivations you give yourself here can make every campaign even more enjoyable.

Let me put it this way, did you ever want to rule a human empire, uniting its separate states while fending off hordes of Chaos worshippers, demons, orcs and god knows what else while also tending to diplomacy with elves, dwarves and honorable French people (god, what a concept)? You can do so here with the power of the Empire.

Did you ever want to just rule an unstoppable horde of orcish green tide, pillaging, plundering and fighting whatever comes in your way while your armies just keep growing in size? Then the greenskins and their WAAAAAGH is here for you. (pst, they also have massive stone giants, humongous spiders with arrow towers on their backs and lots of trolls!)

Did you ever want to just mow down countless enemies who use primitive weapons like catapults, swords, bows and shields with the power of semi-modern technology? The Skaven have got your back-back with rotating minigun teams, sniper teams, litteral laser lightning canons, gas warfare with poison mortar teams and oh, how could i forget, A ****** NUKE!!! Yes, in this fantastical setting, the ratmen have the power of sort of modern technology and zero consideration for ethics or Geneva convention, cause that does not exist here. Oh and they also have huge rat abominations they send into battle alongside roided up ogre rat linebackers. What more could you want? <3 

Speaking of ogres, why not making the world your ogre swamp?... Wait... That would be more Nurgle thing... Ok, scrath that, why not pick up your chunky boys and do a road trip around the world?? Ogres love three things - meat, gold and fighting, so go ahead and help the boys out! Leading the ogres was as fascinating, as it was funny. The utmost joy of a whole horde of them charging into battle is just incredible. It is just simple fun with them and Ogre is very much my spirit animal. Plus they also ride brutal behemoth like Stonehorns, savage and bigger rhinos and they also, most recently, got yetis! Whats not to love? :)

Or how about a race of ancient lizardmen with dinosaurs? Lead your armies of cold lizards through jungles, while using huge T-Rex "like" dinosaurs, lizards riding Raptor "like" dinos and also flying Pteranodon "like" dinos. Unleash your Jurrasic Park against your enemies! They also have gargantuan lizards, charging Stegodons, walking hulking crocodiles and also ORBITAL SUN DEATH RAYS!

And thats STILL all just covering the surface of how much stuff you can command here. If anything that i described here have got your attention, please, try it for yourself! 

If you are still undecided, there are also giant forrest Ents, both high elves (with several flavours of dragons to choose from for your armies) and dark elves (with not only dragons but also hydras and medusas), Undead pirates with walking boat transformers and leviathan hermit crabs, classic undead Vampire lords and their own kingdom and ofcourse a ****ton of demons to choose from.

Be a protector of the world, be its savier, be its conquerer, its tyrant, but no matter what, have fun doing it! ;)

Total War: Warhammer III est un jeu de stratégie au tour par tour avec batailles en temps réel, développé par Creative Assembly. Il représente l’aboutissement mécanique et structurel de la trilogie Total War: Warhammer, et propose une expérience stratégique complète, dense et hautement rejouable.

Le système de campagne est efficace. Chaque faction bénéficie de mécaniques uniques, qui influencent de manière concrète l’économie, la diplomatie, l’expansion territoriale et la gestion des armées. Ces systèmes sont cohérents avec les identités ludiques et tactiques de chaque race, et offrent une variété de styles de jeu nettement différenciés. Le jeu intègre également des ressources secondaires, de la corruption, des événements dynamiques, et une gestion climatique, tous pertinents dans leur exécution.

L’IA stratégique a été améliorée par rapport aux précédents opus : les comportements diplomatiques sont plus lisibles, les alliances défensives et militaires fonctionnent mieux, et les réactions aux mouvements armés sont globalement cohérentes. La carte de campagne est vaste, bien structurée, et favorise des interactions constantes entre factions.

Le système de combat temps réel repose toujours sur le triptyque infanterie/cavalerie/projectiles, enrichi ici par les capacités spéciales, les effets d’aura, les unités volantes et les entités massives. Le positionnement, le contournement et la gestion du moral restent les clés de la réussite tactique. L’équilibrage des unités est solide dans la plupart des cas, avec une bonne distinction entre troupes de ligne, d’élite et de soutien.

Sur le plan technique, le moteur est stable sur des configurations modernes. Les temps de chargement sont raisonnables, les performances sont constantes même en fin de partie sur la carte Immortal Empires. L’interface est dense mais fonctionnelle, avec une ergonomie légèrement améliorée par rapport à Warhammer II. Les outils de lisibilité des informations en campagne et en bataille sont correctement hiérarchisés.

Le contenu post-lancement (DLC, Immortal Empires, patchs d’équilibrage) est conséquent, avec un suivi actif de la part du studio. La carte Immortal Empires constitue l’un des modes de jeu les plus complets jamais proposés dans un Total War, en intégrant l’ensemble des races et régions issues des trois épisodes.

I dabbled in Total Warhammer 2 before this, and while I had been excited for years to play the game, I just didn't click with it because of how obtuse learning to play it felt. So when I saw the rest of the series on sale, I really just bought it because I hoped one day I would get into them and everything would click, as I've wanted a good RTS since I last owned a PC. 

Booting up TW3, I expected much of the same, a great game that I just couldn't really understand, so when I got in and saw the "Prologue", I was quite intrigued, and while its not perfect, sometimes quests glitch forcing you to reload a previous turns save and just redo stuff, the tutorial absolutely opens up the game to newcomers like me and makes the rather incomprehensible mechanics far more enjoyable. I went from losing fights with superior armies, to learning to use the pause function (I am a noob, I very much don't care about making things more difficult than they already are) to perfectly micromanage my units to devastating effect. I've learned what the heroes are capable of, what to optimize for in early base building, how to think about my progress and plan for where I want to go. In short, the tutorial is everything it needs to be, and now my biggest problem is I play on a gaming laptop that, while perfectly capable of playing the game, gets a little toasty for my liking over the sort of play sessions I want to be sinking in. 

If you're interested in Total Warhammer, start with this one. You can buy the others and get all the content in the one game if you're so inclined, and the tutorial alone makes this the easiest one to get into that I've tried. It runs beautifully on my laptop (Asus ROG strix 18 2024) at all ultra settings, and best of all, its just fun. They really nailed the newcomer experience, and while parts of the tutorial are annoyingly handholdy, its a small price to pay for the variety of awesome factions you get to play with.

Spread disease as a bloated god-papa with no pants (Nurgle)

Seduce entire provinces into cults and chaos raves (Slaanesh)

Launch artillery made of skulls and hatred (Khorne)

Drop magic bombs shaped like frogs (Ogres)

Tunnel under empires as a backstabbing rat dictator (Skaven)

Eat entire maps as a dragon with a grudge (Cathay or Chaos, take your pick)

Or just say “screw it” and play as a talking book (Tzeentch)

Every faction is chaos in its own flavor.

Except the Elves. The Elves are salad. With opinions.

150 hours in and I’m still not tired. The AI is insane, diplomacy is a joke, but it’s MY joke.

Final verdict:
10/10 would raze Ulthuan again. Elves deserve less.

You see that greyed out star to the top right? It means I bought a Steam Key online at a discount instead of supporting the developer. This review outlines exactly why, so strap in for the most negative positive review I can possibly give. 

Things I Dislike: 
--- One of their team went on a mad one, blanket banning accounts in the forums for any criticism (constructive or not) some of those people not only being first adopters of their product in hope and hype, but also prominent modders in the community who improve their game for free with popular mods. The representative stating that, quote; "The right to discuss (their game) is a privilege—it is not an entitlement you earn by playing the game." Well that's news to me, so how about go f ucking f uck yourself you imbecile. 
--- Around the same time as the above, they released Total War Pharoah, a game no one asked for or gave a ♥♥♥♥ about because Rome Total War was released in 2004, Rome 2 was 2013, both had Egypt playable and everyone was and still is asking for Medieval 2. 
--- They split some of their DLC's into smaller DLC's, removing all the negative reviews that where racked up when the content first released. Why? Because ♥♥♥♥ all the opinions of people who actually review their content. If you haven't learned anything about CA so far, you should know you cant talk about their company in a way they dont like. And no, they wont outline how they want to receive feedback. They'd rather nuke it all for profit. 
--- THERE'S DLC IN MY DLC and the developers not only raised the price without raising the content, but defended this agregiously greedy ♥♥♥♥ against fans calling them out! This whole game, Warhammer 3 is a DLC to the two previous games. They literally plan to cut content and sell it to you afterwards at a premium. 
--- As I said, this is just DLC for WH2. SO all the issues of WH2 are still there, unfixed and unimproved upon, some amplified by the design of the story campaign. 
--- Some new additions are just completely unbalanced. I play on Normal and I looked online to see what the easiest campaigns are to complete on Legendary (for the achievement) and the one I picked at random is so insanely easy I was shocked when it ended, because I didn't even know I had won so fast. The Legendary achievement means nothing when you play a faction that can hire units, not only without waiting turns to recruit, but in enemy territory + at a discount + with teleporting armies + with a diplomatic game that lets you pick and choose enemies/allies. Again, I play on Normal, I should not be coasting through Legendary, turn 100+ with all my enemies on the ropes and all my allies as Vassals. I'm bored. 
-- I honestly dont like the main campaign "Realm of Chaos" map and factions. I feel like I see a lot of the same terrain and units compared to the time I put in WH2 and the ones that are different seem thrown in there as fodder. 
- Unlocking achievements for factions I'm not playing as. 
- Support is slowly winding down, with the skeleton crew still working on this game releasing (and delaying) further additions while the main team works on something (hopefully) we want. I've heard rumours of Star Wars Total War, 40K Total War and more historical titles, but rumours are all they are. 
- They didn't call the series Total Warhammer. 
- Issue with my specific card, 50 series, that things begin to flicker badly. It's between Nvidia or the devs to fix it and I dont think either of them will. 

Things I Like: 
+++ I liked Warhammer 2 because it's the best and most detailed Total War game to date, and this is more of that. 
+++ I got this cheaper than most people who own it (£10) and I didn't support this company. 
+++ Immortal Empires: Now the huge Warhammer 1+2 map is even bigger with 3. With an insane 330 other factions on the map (~25 playable), there are endless epic battles and turns to be had. So that means babies will go unborn, men will abstain from sex to play more turns, women's reproductive organs whither away into dust at every End Turn button press. This game officially contributes to the male loneliness crisis that effects all humanity and you have Creative Assembly and the nerds behind Warhammer to thank for that. 
+++ I'm not really into Warhammer, but I like demon stuff and there's plenty of flavours for demon stuff thanks to this DLC. There's this one you can play as where you can unlock body parts from all demon factions and mix and match to change the look of your monstrous Lord, their powers and stats. I love customisation, so one step towards creating your own leaders and adding them into a Total War game is great! 
++ In addition to the above, there are challenge battles to play, outside of the campaigns, where you can rack up points and unlock gear to start your campaign with as that demon lord! Cosmetically, there's maybe only 1 or 2 that are good. But stats/power wise, there are some good ones. 
++ The art is great and the music is grand. 
+ Workshop support: I wont give the developers credit for fan-made work, but I'm putting this here because fans of Total War games and fans of Warhammer are nerds, and I mean that in the best ways possible. Some of these mods are must-haves. 

And yes, I acknowledge they've apologised and adjusted prices accordingly, but I'm an adult so I can remember when someone's been an a$$hole and tried to get away with it. 

Remember: if people like me and you didn't stand up and call bullsh!t, they wouldn't be the only ones running these anti-customer strategies on us right now, it'd be everybody. I know I said I'm not really into Warhammer, but I can appreciate the passion behind the fans who just wanted a good game without any of the drama or content cutting.

With so much Negativity coming to light around TWW3 I must speak my piece and renew my opinion.

Yes, I do recommend this game. There is no way I could ever justify putting more than 500 hrs of my life into a game i couldn't turn around and say you shouldn't try. The Depth and immersion of the game as a whole is astounding, with each faction having completely separate feels be it army composition, technologies, legendary lords, building layouts, magic systems, and a whole swathe of mechanisms that may even change from legendary lord to legendary lord even within the same race. No other RTS Turn based hybrid game in history as far as I'm aware has the capability to allow you to play 24 different races with 100 different Legendary Lords. There are so many epic campaigns for you to be had with so many varying play styles. With all that beings said, what a feat! 

Now to address the issues. Am I a fanboi? Well... Yes. I'm sure you are too or will soon be. So here's the deal. There are issues with the game, A.I. is frustrating at times with armies not always following the best of tactics during battles, complete armies on the campaign map not doing the most optimal thing at times and even just sitting for turns and turns on end without attempting to gain any ground. Siege Battles are lacking hard with mapping problems, unit scaling, the lack of any real gravitas and meaning behind the battles, we could go on. Moreover, there are several factions that need updates and even complete re-works. 

Its a lot I know... But listen, I understand CA is all about the big bucks, they over-charge for DLC and they obviously push these harder than working to fix the issues the community has been telling them. Ultimately though, if it keeps the lights on for that coder and developer to keep working at this game for us, it's worth every penny. Games get dropped a year after launch sometimes, and here we are nearly 4 years on and getting patch after patch, content after content, even if it is slow in coming. And I'm not saying don't give them criticism, I'm just think it's worth noting and we should be greatful.

So in closing, Yes, buy the game, be aware it's not perfect, very occasionally will it ever be "not playable", but with how much content is here, i'm willing to overlook so long as the promise to keep working out those kinks is on the horizon, and I honestly think you should too.

A categorical step down from all other Total War games, the Warhammer franchise is a sort of 'arcade-ification' of the Total War series in the same way that Rainbow Six: Vegas and Ghost Recon 2 were action spin-offs of the authentic and ambitious tactical shooters that came before them.  

The Warhammer trilogy has flashy battle graphics, neat monster animations, and some fun flavor, but it not only misses the tone and pace of Warhammer Fantasy's "Old World" fantasy, it misses the mark on all strategic features that would make this game replayable and cognitively engaging.  Instead the replayability comes from repeated experimentation with differing factions as you explore their token specializations and unique sub-mechanics--none of which are fleshed out enough to be interesting in their own right, seemingly for the sake of accessibility and play speed.

Every strategic mechanism from administration and governance, to trade and diplomacy, to city composition and faction economics, has been severely dumbed-down from Warhammer's predecessors. Many mechanics are entirely absent--replaced by Paradox-style percent modifier stacks that serve not to enhance or broaden gameplay or strategy but to hand-wave otherwise interesting simulations they could have explored. 

Buy this if you want to play flashy monster battles and know you'll need to cheese the AI in battles and ambush stances as punishment for their anti-player bias and AI cheats. Skip it if you're looking for a grand strategy game.  Three Kingdoms and Pharaoh: Dynasties are the games you're looking for. They simulate courts and administration, espionage, trade and economics, population growth and manpower, and much more.
