When writing this review I have over 400 hours in this game, and I think it is safe to say that at its core the game is good and it has a ton of content and fun asymmetrical factions to play. I wish I could wholeheartedly recommend it, but the game also is dealing with some severe problems. 

The game has a lot of content but the majority of it is unfortunately locked behind (fragmented) DLC or ownership of the other two titles in the series (and their DLC), the pricing of some being pretty steep for what they offer. A more serious and unavoidable problem is the game's stability and buginess, which seems to be degrading with every patch and DLC released.  There's glaring issues like the 6.3 patch breaking the AI for two separate factions to smaller things like bugs that have been known yet unaddressed for years. The game is also a lot more prone to random crashes, freezes and other hiccups since 6.0, which have become a standard of the game experience for me. There is very little communication and acknowledgement of these issues from the developers and currently no clear outlook on when some of these issues are addressed, if ever. I'm worried that there is a real chance the game is going to be dropped at some point in a broken state, therefore cannot recommend it without a few warnings.

Warhammer 3, What a game!
I’ve never played a game this much in such a short time. It’s an amazing strategy game that keeps me coming back for more, I simply can’t stop playing. For me, Warhammer 3 is a solid 10/10 game. Sure, it has its ups and downs, and I’m still somewhat of a “new player,” but it’s an incredible experience that I’ll easily double my playtime in the coming year if I find the time.

But then there’s the company behind it… Creative Assembly.
Honestly, they’re terrible. They’ve become what EA Sports is to FIFA or The Sims 4, both could be 10/10 games, but the companies behind them keep dragging them down.
Recently, Warhammer 3 has become so buggy that parts of the campaign map are practically unplayable. Issues that should be easy fixes end up taking weeks, sometimes even months. There are factions that are currently unplayable, like Tomb Kings and Lizardmen, and others that have been broken since launch, like Norsca.

And don’t even get me started on the DLC policy. If you buy Warhammer 3 today, you’re basically getting a quarter of a full game. Sure, you can still have fun without all the DLCs, but you expect a complete experience and not a paid content disaster.

For me, Warhammer 3 is everything I wished the Civilization games had been: a deep, immersive, endlessly replayable strategy game that is just held back by a disastrous company.
If you’re planning to buy it, do yourself a favor and wait for a sale. Right now, you’re getting an incomplete, glitchy mess that is still 100+ hours of genuine fun.
Just don’t get too attached, because you never know when Creative Assembly will find a new way to screw it up again.

[h2]Jeder der Fantasy mag findet etwas[/h2]

TWWH3 ist wie schon gesagt ein sehr umfangreiches Spiel mit Zwergen, Bösen Zwergen, Elfen, Menschen, allerlei Dämonen und verschiedener Magie. Zahllosen unterschiedlichen EInheiten und einer riesigen Karte, der Immortal Empires Karte, auf der alle Fraktionen und Kommandanten sowie kleinere Fraktionen zu finden sind. 
Man kann mit jeder dieser Politik betreiben, Abkommen unterzeichnen und starke Allianzen bilden, sodass jeder der es wagt einem den Krieg zu erklären auf einmal 10 weitere Kriegserklärungen am Hals hat. [h2]Einzigartiges Spielerlebnis[/h2]

Wie schon zuvor gesagt ist der Mix aus Kampagnenmodus und RTS etwas, dass ich in einer solchen Ausführung nur aus Total War kenne und damit für jeden der sich für RTS und Fantasy interessiert einen Blick wert und mich selbst für einige hundert Stunden unterhalten hat. Die Art seine eigenen Armeen aufzustellen und damit selbst entscheidet ob man sich auf einen bestimmten Feind fokussieren möchte oder eine ausgeglichene Armee bauen möchte und damit sein Territorium vergrößert ist eine Power-Fantasy wie ich sie nur selten gesehen habe.

TTWH3 hat einen Triple A Titel Preis mit einer welche durch DLCS oder sogar andere spiele, TWWH1 und 2, gelocked sind. Zuvor musste man sogar die anderen Spiele kaufen, aber Credit where Credit is due: Creative Assembly hat mittlerweile eingesehen, dass die DLCS auch für Kunden welche nur ein einziges Spiel der reihe besitzen, ändert nur leider nichts daran, dass ein Großteil des Spiels gepaywalled ist und zusammengerechnet allein die DLCS etwa 320€ vollpreis kosten, dazu das Basegame bei 60€ sind wir bei ca. 380€.

Where do I even begin with Total War: Warhammer III? This game is the epitome of a toxic relationship. It shows you a beautiful world with incredible potential, promises you the moon, and then proceeds to completely ignore your needs, leaving you frustrated and wondering why you invested any time or money in the first place.

The core of the problem is Creative Assembly's baffling and consistent neglect of its community. They run public betas, gather mountains of detailed feedback from players who genuinely want the game to succeed, and then release the official patch with the exact same game-breaking bugs and balance issues that were reported weeks in advance. It's not just incompetence; it feels like outright disdain for the player base. Why should we spend our free time testing your product and providing free QA if you're just going to ignore it?

This cycle of overpromising and underdelivering has become the sad norm. Every DLC and major update is preceded by a slick marketing campaign, only for the release to be a buggy, unbalanced mess. It's a slap in the face to anyone who dedicates hundreds of hours to a campaign, only to have it ruined by issues that were not only foreseeable but were explicitly pointed out by the community.

And don't be fooled by the current Autumn Sale. That discount isn't a gesture of goodwill; it's a ploy to suck in new players. They're luring in a fresh wave of unsuspecting customers with a cheap price tag, knowing full well the game's long-term issues will lead to the same disappointment the veteran community feels. It's a cash grab, plain and simple.

Investing your time in Warhammer III feels like building a sandcastle while the tide is coming in. It's a fundamentally unsupported experience where the developers have proven, time and again, that their vision comes first, and player feedback is, at best, an afterthought. Save your time and your money. Don't make the same mistake so many of us have.

Giving a negative review to this game genuinely hurts — but it has to be done.
Seeing the potential this game could have reached, yet watching the developers fail to achieve it, has left the player base both sad and angry.

They **know** what to do.
They **can** do it.
The **players** have told them exactly what they want.
But instead of improving things, they somehow make it worse with every update.

Not listening to your community will be your downfall. There are many examples of this — too many to name here.

And just to be clear, I’m not writing this review solely because of the Lizardmen and Tomb Kings AI problems, nor because this was “the last straw.” The last straw was a long time ago, we just stopped counting. I kept giving this game a chance, again and again, thinking, “What can I do about it?”

Well, here I am.
I’m a fairly lazy person. I don’t usually write reviews or bother with this kind of thing. I just open Steam, play my games, and move on with life. So CA, think about what that means: your game and your company have reached a state where even a casual player with around 250 hours felt compelled to write a negative review.

And here’s the thing, I’m still going to play this game.
Because despite everything, this game is something truly special. It’s unique, with no real competitors, and that’s exactly why so many of us are upset. We see the potential. We know how amazing it could be. It’s your creation — your child — and it deserves care and love. Yet we, the players, find ourselves having to remind you to take care of it. That’s not how it should be.

I truly hope that one day I’ll be able to change this to a positive review. But for that to happen, a few things must change.

First of all, fixing your bugs and delivering a stable, playable experience isn’t enough. That’s the bare minimum. That’s your job. You were supposed to do that in the first place. You’ll need to go beyond that: actually update your game, add meaningful content, and do it without breaking everything each time.

And while we’re at it; if you’re adding new content that’s truly extra, ambitious, or resource-heavy to create, then sure, charge for it, but at a fair price. That’s completely reasonable.
What’s not reasonable is overcharging players for bare-minimum content that should have been included in the base game from the start. The “extra” content should be special — not essential fixes or features disguised as DLC.

Second, listen to your community. Stop acting like you’re above them. You’re not gods. You’re developers producing a product. We are the consumers, and customer respect matters.
Right now, it feels like some developers are sitting comfortably, doing the bare minimum, collecting paychecks, and acting like they’re untouchable. You’re not. Stop dismissing and disrespecting your community.


tl;dr : we want three simple, logical things: 
1. **Respect your community.** Treat your customers with the basic courtesy and appreciation they deserve. 
2. **Maintain your product properly**. If you’re going to charge more than the market average, then at least patch your bugs, update your game consistently, and deliver content that’s actually worth our time and money — which, again, is your job in the first place. 
3.**Fair pay for extra Content*. if you do add big, high-effort content, that’s fine — just price it fairly. Don’t charge premium prices for things that should’ve been part of the base game.

Normally don't post reviews, but I'll make an exception for a game that I've played so long.
Splitting my review in two parts. 

TL;DR
Overall review of the game. 4.5 out of 5 stars.
Current review of the game. 2.0 out of 5 stars. 

Part 1 - My overall view of the game.
Overall, the game is consistent and has been my go to for grand strategy games. The lore, the mechanics, and how no two campaigns are alike make this a game that I can rely on having fun playing. The sandbox mode for Immortal Empires makes for a really dynamic game play loop. I like the game enough to have all the DLCs and the first two versions of the game.

Vanilla game is at least a 4.5/5 stars for me. With such a rich modding community, the game is elevated and feels like I have multiple different versions of the game, including with significant QOL updates on things CA may have missed. 

Part 2 - My current review of the game. 
The current version of the game 6.3.1 has significant bugs that renders 11 major AI factions useless, thereby breaking the balance in at least 2 of the major continents or as much as the entire southern hemisphere of the map. If you play factions in the far north like Kislev and the Empire, then you may not notice significant changes; however, if you play any of the lizardmen in the south, Teclis of the high elves, or any of Tomb Kings, this will significantly impact your game. 

For two races, the lizardmen and Tomb Kings, the current AI for the playable factions will not: recruit units, build their settlements, or move out of the starting settlement - as if they are trapped on turn 1. If you play as these two races, then that can effectively lock you out of allies and the ability to confederate their legendary lords - both of which are pretty important aspects of playing a grand strategy game. Unfortunately this bug has existed for months, starting as noticeably as the 6.3.0 version and the hotfix released for the current version of the game has not addressed this at all. 

There has been little communication from their management team across many of the major channels regarding plans or timelines until the gaming community started voicing their concerns. Even then, the most recent communication has only stated that they might fix it when the DLC comes out - which is concerning as a consumer. Why would I be incentivized to purchase a product when the current version of the product has significant flaws in it? I feel that as a consumer, it's really disconcerting when the management team are unable to properly update or convey any future plans for when concerns about the game are being conveyed from the community - which is sad to see considering how well developed the game is. 

With the current state of the game, I would not recommend this to new users. Currently would score this at a 2 out of 5 stars - only rating it so highly because of how much I have historically I have enjoyed the game. 

I am open to changing this review to a more positive one when I see that Creative Assembly has properly addressed this issue.

I have been a big fan of the Warhammer genre for a very long time. Honestly, my hours on Steam don't depict how much I've actually played this game, as I owned it all on Epic before I bought it on Steam, which I only did to add modding support. 

Let me cut straight to the chase, Creative Assembly does not care about the player base. For literal years they have repeatedly told us "We're sorry that we never communicate anything to you, but we promise we're going to do better now", and then immediately stop communicating with the community. It is literally crazy to me that Games Workshop (the owners of the Warhammer IP) continue to allow CA to trash their IP over and over again and infuriate their fan base. Games Workshop loves Warhammer, the community loves Warhammer, Creative Assembly hates that community.

The best part about the Total War: Warhammer series that is that I get to live out table top fantasy. I get to play as the Emporer, Karl Franz, and babysit the Empire. I get to play as the Lizardmen and bring back their old reign. 

The worst part about Total War: Warhammer is that the game is never in a good place. CA is constantly breaking the game, and then refuses to admit that they've broken it, essentially just tell the entire playerbase that they're wrong, until the playerbase proves that they're right, and then CA promises to fix it. 6 months later, 8 months later, a year later? Who knows when. They STILL haven't addressed battle replays being completely broken for over a year now! All because they introduced "siege battle improvements" which weren't any good in the first place. But again, just ignore it instead of fix it. 

The other worst part about this game series is the ridiculous cost to keep playing it, for such mediocre content. I mean come on, who can possibly defend Shadows of Change? Omens of Destruction? PAYING FOR A DLC JUST FOR BLOOD EFFECTS?! I'm all for supporting a studio and paying for additional content, but seriously, the modding community has made some amazing "DLC" of their own, making entire new factions (both in lore and out of lore) that are better than 95% of what CA has put out. And we're lucky if we get even poor new content once or twice a year. 

There are some diamonds in the rough. Thrones of Decay was the chef's kiss for the Empire, Elspeth and the Nuln units were great. Chaos Dwarves were amazing (the cost of the DLC was not). 

But the last straw has to now be the completely broken AI. We've been screaming at CA about this for MONTHS. The AI just builds a bunch of armies and they just sit there, at a settlement, doing nothing. I have spent almost 800 hours playing this game (which blows my mind!). Clearly, at its core, that is an appealing gameplay loop. It is, like other Total War game, a fun mix of strategy/settlement management, and battlefield tactics.

I am also, it must be a said, a long-time fan of Warhammer Fantasy lore and this has certainly driven my interest in - and patience for - this game.

At the time of writing, this game is on sale for £12. At that price, this game is a buy: go for it, you will absolutely get £12's worth of fun out of it if you like other Total War games, or other strategy/wargames.

But is it worth £49.99? No, absolutely not.

Once you have a few campaigns under your belt, the loop starts to feel "samey". I will frequently start the game up in an evening, spend a few hours getting to turn 30 or 40 (or whatever), and then get board and not play it again for a few days (or even weeks). The challenge and variety isn't there - for me - to reward spending longer on individual campaigns.

But what has really hurt the game recently is the AI.

AI has always been bad on Total War games. CA (the developers) have never really bothered to address this - and they usually leave it to modders. But recently it's got even worse. Now enemy factions just don't recruit or do anything at all. What was already a relatively easy game becomes a walkover, as your opponents become passive. They are simply broken.

CA are on the ropes currently, and have assigned a skeleton crew to this game (apparently). Glaring issues with the game play - not little bugs - huge, immersion-breaking issues - aren't being fixed.

So - pick up this title if you can get it for £12, but otherwise save your money.

差评给游戏厂商，好评给社区，综合考虑，给出好评。
首先，全面战争：战锤3的原版，绝对算不上一款优秀的游戏，
漫长的过回合和加载时长，层出不穷的Bug，远程算力被卡，Ai四五个满编在家挂机，都会让玩家的体验直线下降。
【汉化问题】，这个版本更新了几个混沌地标，居然连中文汉化都没有，你一个正版玩家，遇到事件选择后，居然只见左右两个按钮，而没有文本，这种级别的错误，连一个残次品的Mod都比不了，居然是官方做出来的东西，实在是令人感到不满。
【DLC】再说本次的折磨之潮dlc，今年年初就说有戏，结果到了如今十月份，连预告试玩都没有出来，我很好奇CA的工作室究竟是否在维护战锤3，还是拿战锤玩家的钱，去搞其他失败的作品。一个dlc，做几个换皮兵种，模型一建，数据填一下，有时连新动作都不怎么做，就这个水平的东西，一年做一个还拖拖拉拉。
【创意工坊】我能玩上千个小时，一是由于锤三独特的生态位，确实没有竞争对手，二是由于丰富的创意工坊。这里点名，与龙同行，这个Mod才是我希望看到的DLC水准，可以说如果不是创意工坊中为爱发电的玩家们，这个游戏整体的可玩价值只有现在的1/4。
【初始体验】我回想起刚刚游玩战锤3，被官方的机制折磨，真的不是一段良好的体验。我当时最早玩的基斯里夫，被混沌打的左支右绌，那时候还没有小卖部和基斯里夫勇士，我又不会单体抱团，纯纯是一个电脑的沙包，每个回合都在亡命普拉格。有趣的是，CA给新人推荐的派系居然是“妙影”，全军弹药加成20%的”强大“派系能力，考虑到地缘也差，其实还不如某些大众脸震旦舒服，说到新人推荐派系，我建议是去地图【混沌魔域】里面，选择元伯，这个图过回合快，游玩效率高，元伯又不刷裂隙，不用四处救火，而且震旦前期经济好可以多满编推进，ps不建议买dlc给CA送钱，买本体就行了，dlc去网上找破解补丁，官方不做人，你给他送钱，把他送飘了，反而助长他的歪风邪气，看看他现在这个工作效率，简直不是个东西。
【战略缺陷】，CA不知道是为了游戏难度，还是希望节约算力，使得【城市发展】【军队维护】都受到了极大限制，其实你可以看到官方在尽一切可能拖慢你的游戏进程，浪费你的时间，不少其他游戏大地图都有传送机制，例如赛博朋克，黑魂3，超凡帝国这么大的图，不给几个传送阵，使得你可能上百回合的打后期，在外面推进的队伍还都是三本兵以下，使得游戏体验趋于【同质化】。
【扩张负收益】这个游戏有一个反直觉的点，扩张是亏本的，首先玩家十个城都不一定养得起两个满编，电脑一个城给你来个三五个轻轻松松，其次你扩张的版图越大，接敌面积就越广，防守压力就大，家里面再刷个流浪战帮，让你顾头不顾腚，而且你扩张还会加重周围人的敌意，【战略威胁】，也更加容易被宣战。所以很多秩序册其实比较建议守着早期的两三个行省（绿地）然后运营到高本兵，例如陆行船，高级部队成型，然后地图涂色。
【游戏体验】这个游戏本体体验其实是非常无趣的，游戏引导很差，不打MOD体验坐牢，也就是前期破局还有点趣味，后期基本上都是地图涂色，所以不少老玩家要么就是10回合天灾，要么就是15回合25城速推，还有玩PVP的，例如阿卡奇的CRK，玩到三四十个回合，游戏体验就会直线下降，大部分人一个存档连个中期胜利都玩不到都失去了兴趣，这恰恰反映出了这个游戏的设计失败。
【综上】好评给社区，差评给CA，本体可以打折买，dlc建议找破解，懒狗厂商不做人。

This is the first Steam review I have ever done. I have been playing Total War games since the first Shogun, yes I am really that old. Steam says I have 545 hours in this game, honestly I thought it was more. So how can I give my first ever Steam review a negative rating, if I have played thousands of hours of these games? Am I insane? Sadly not, if I was insane I would probably still enjoy this game as CA intended. 

You see almost all of those 500+ hours are spent heavily modded or using console commands to set up crazy scenarios to mess around with. When played un-modded, and as the developers made it, this would rate probably as the most broken user experiences ever created in a "strategy" game. CA have had years to build experience with this franchise, to refine their art around this famous brand, and what have they learned in all that time? Over all those development iterations, innumerable hotfixes and DLC's? Who knows, but as a software engineer/manager of over 30 years I can tell you what they HAVEN'T learned: the first thing about testing and release management. It seems to me, looking in from the outside, that what they have ACTUALLY got better at is covering up for the development failures, and pretending to everyone (including themselves) that its a REALLY REALLY good game, with just ONE OR TWO final bugs to squash.

This latest debacle where the only 100% honest and independent Total War content creator had to literally crash out in public to get CA to take their heads out of the money trough for 10 seconds and actually fix the fundamentally broken (for the 19th time in recent memory) campaign AI has tipped me over the edge. This is the first and probably last Steam review I will ever write, not in any hope that anybody at CA will care, but for my own sanity. Reading their apology for this mess just broke my brain, presumably SOMEONE out there fell for that garbled and transparent nonsense, but honestly it reads more like an apology to their own management team rather than to us, you know, the actual CUSTOMERS.

Back to the actual review.... can you enjoy Warhammer Total War III in it's un-modded state once you have played more than a few hours of an actual real campaign: watching the "AI" stumble drunkenly about the map randomly doing nothing for several turns and then suddenly the most stupid thing possible, and of course fought a few battles where at any point the enemy bundles up into a blob and seems like its fighting itself? I tried this for myself recently, accidentally of course since I forgot to re-enable mods after a release. My conclusion: maybe you could, but only if you have never played another strategy game.

Would I recommend that someone who has never played a Total War game start playing TWWH3 now? Of course not, NO NO NO, this game fundamentally sucks and only exists to sell DLC perpetually while the worlds worst publisher pretends to care. The best game in this franchise is Medieval 2, which was released 9 years ago. Says a lot really.

Oh boy, where to begin? I've been a Total War fan since Rome Total War and have enjoyed countless hours of my life with different Total War titles, they are each unique with their own upsides and downsides. I have also been a big fan of the Warhammer Fantasy universe since I was a kid and love the books and deep lore behind it, even if Games Workshop decided to temporarily delete the Fantasy Universe. I have to say, with all my hours in not just Warhammer 3, but the previous installments of Warhammer Total War as well, that while these games have both the Total War and Warhammer titles, It really bares no resemblance to Total War at all and gets the normal treatment of anything Warhammer in the fact that it now cost almost $380 for the game and all DLC, being as overpriced for new players as the tabletop game is.

I personally cannot say this game is in any sense of the word, a good Total War game! Stat stacking, single unit heroes, and cheese, are what will win your battles in this game, rather than quick tactical thinking or good terrain, as it forgoes Total War's older formula of emphasizing positioning and morale such as in shogun 2 and medieval 2. It instead goes for a more fast paced feel for battles and encourages 'Doomstacks' and auto resolving for newer players. The campaigns often turn into a horrid slog later on with almost no connection with your armies as half of the units for some factions are useless to take, such as many of the Empire's infantry unit roster, and is full of player traps for newer players which worsens the experience. This is on top of hardly explaining mechanics and the decision to make the game more difficult via giving the AI egregious cheats on the campaign map and battlefield instead of simply improving the brain dead AI, giving the illusion of difficulty. The Diplomacy is shallow, especially considering the leaps and bounds made for diplomatic actions in Three Kingdoms Total war, so shallow to the point that actively getting allies is actually a hindrance for the player as they will drag you into forever wars and seemingly never come to support you. The lack of customization options such as in Shogun 2 for units, generals, and symbols is crazy to me considering these were already features in previous games and the fact that customization of how you want your units to look is one of the main drives for people playing Warhammer. The streamlining of mechanics only serves to make the game more shallow, as basic mechanics such fire by rank for firearm units, shield walls, pike formations, and even reloading animations have been removed for no valid reason other than laziness on the developers part. The fact that siege battles are the worst they've ever been in any Total War to date is astonishing as I didn't think they could get worse from Empire Total War but they managed to find a way to half ass them even more in this game. I cannot speak to the competitive multiplayer scene as I haven't indulged in that area of the game as often. 

Warhammer 3 isn't all bad obviously, there are plenty of times you can get a certain enjoyment from the game, especially if you enjoy a power fantasy, however for older Total War fans such as myself, the battles feel to fast paced and stat based compared to the more tactical and morale based decisions you could make in older Total War titles. Creative Assembly should honestly be ashamed of the their lack of addressing the concerns or worries players have for this game, and instead would rather continually pump out an endless stream of DLC revenue rather than fix the broken and awful mechanics players have been complaining about since launch. My complaints and most players does not come from a place of hatred for the game but disappointment and annoyance that we have been saying these things for so long and yet Creative Assembly seems so unwilling to improve unless they are called out on mass. I would love for this game to get better and be the perfect mix of Total War and Warhammer as much as anyone as a fan of both series and until that happens this game will always feel like a massively missed opportunity to me for Total War and Warhammer.

Having played through all three iterations of Warhammer, I am disappointed to say that I cannot recommend Warhammer III (in its present state) to any new players.  

Outside of the outstanding AI issues surrounding major factions such as the tomb kings (a personal favorite) and lizard men, there have been a series of decisions by Creative Assembly executives that skewer fan trust and overall good will toward this IP. I have two general concerns.

Cost Concern:
Base games: $60 (You no longer have to own all three games to play on this map | a great decision in my estimation.)
DLC: $319.22 (Current Steam retail) 
Total cost to play the grand campaign ~$380 (retail, pre-tax)

Listen, I get it, this doesn't sound terribly different from the Paradox Model (I do love a good game of Stellaris/Space Themed Excel) however, CA languishes when it comes to maintaining their products. That said, I have had a great deal of enjoyment from the Warhammer series and, generally, don't regret the amount I have spent per unit of enjoyment (The blood DLC being an obvious outlier). However, I did not buy the most recent Omens of Destruction and do not plan to purchase further DLC due to, what I perceive, as a systemic hollowing of content for a quick cash influx. I vaguely recall paying less than $20 for the wood elf DLC (an entirely new faction) and now I am paying nearly $30 ($8.99/each) for three lords and a handful of units. I recognize that development isn't cheap and I agree that supporting development, sometimes through DLCs, is a reasonable way to keep the light on. That said, overall quality and depth is in decline. This brings up the second general concern. 

Technical Concerns
During the development of the second installment the code was forked to begin production on Warhammer 3. The fork occurred too early and, because of this, much of the effort spent by developers to correct bugs and errors in the second game did not make it into the initial publication of Warhammer 3. The result, spaghetti code and a reason for the seemingly cascading issues present in the third installment. In other words, they've been reinventing the wheel despite "having learned" from their mistakes in the second installment. I vaguely recall a period of over a year wherein CA development teams were actively working to enhancing the experience of Warhammer 2 (the potion of speed update came after such effort and the fork occurred prior to this update). Rather than pushing more DLC and additional content they focused on improving quality. This effort was not unnoticed and, like many in the community, I whole-heartedly threw my money at resulting DLC like The Warden and The Paunch and The Twisted and the Twilight. Enter my third and final point.

A General Plea
The Total War Warhammer Series has such value and impact. It deserves to be treated with the care and attention that many in the community (thank you modders) and developers have already given. I ask for a return to an instinct of workmanship. Focus on quality and consistency. Actually do thorough play-testing to identify game breaking (and player breaking) bugs, such as the current AI issues. Momentum is important. If I get the itch to play a Tomb Kings campaign (I'm a hard/hard difficultly kinda individual), and I find a map of main factions being steamrolled, I'm going to quickly grow bored and shift to a different game (enter Stellaris or Sins II). This momentum issue is compounded when one realizes how long some of these major bugs have languished in the "we will get to it" pile (to be clear, a decision sourced from corporate executives not the developers). Because of this, I cannot provide more resource to a company that struggles to realize the importance of quality, testing, and executive accountability (pushing shallow paid DLCs or foisting blame onto developers as examples). So, instead of sitting on my hands I shift to other games and, often, throw them money for a job well done. This isn't the only pseudo-rpg empire builder on the market. 

I love the Warhammer franchise, it was my entry into the Total War universe and remains one of my favorite games. It deserves to be maintained and repaired; however, until I see a return to an instinct of workmanship (an authentic care for the truly impressive product this game represents), I cannot advise someone spend the amount of money required to experience the full game. Regrettably, you wouldn't be able to in Warhammer 3's current state anyway.

Total War: WARHAMMER III is a major disappointment. There are several improvements from the last game in the franchise, for example multiplayer is a vastly better experience, but by and large this is a massive downgrade across the board. 

The game isn't nearly as challenging, even when the AI isn't bugged (it usually is) it's been lobotomized and you'll frequently encounter it doing absolutely nothing on both the campaign map and battlefield. Diplomacy changes are a great concept, but the implementation is a joke; if you play a faction capable of vassalization feel free to trade a single settlement to whoever strength rank 1 is and they'll happily become your vassal despite the fact they could crush you with ease. New or reworked factions are so overwhelmingly powerful that you have to neuter yourself if you want even a semblance of challenge on legendary (you can reliably win dwarven campaigns in sub-100 turns with 0 manual battles fought, only auto resolve). 

But the worst part of this game is by far the bugs. Almost every battle something buggy and frustrating happens; oh you want to actually command your units? Can't be done, one has split and ended up inside the walls so the others just stand there and take it. I've won battles because the AI just stood outside my walls and got pelted for 20+ minutes without moving and lost battles because my legendary lord (Morathi at the time) bugged out and flew into the sky ignoring all my move commands. Sieges in particular are just the worst, they're already frustrating and unfun so the fact they're especially bug prone is just painful. I’ve put in a lot of hours, mostly multiplayer campaigns with friends, and we have never had a flawless run. Desyncs, weird AI brain-farts, progress-ruining bugs—the kind of stuff that makes you close the game and wonder why you bothered booting it.

And then there’s the DLC mess. As much as I consider the core game very fun, the amount of money you’re expected to throw at it is just plain awful. You charge full price for a base game that comes with, what, a handful of factions—and then lock a small army of others behind DLCs and even previous titles? At some point you have to admit it’s immoral to sell a $60 game that effectively has five “groups of guys” unless you buy another 20 behind paywalls. Worse, you’ve split factions across multiple DLCs. Want a complete Lizardmen experience? Cool—buy like three different packs. What the actual hell is this design?

Meanwhile, core problems fester. CA isn’t prioritising basic AI fixes—especially for my favourite faction, the Lizardmen. Pathing, targeting, campaign logic—stuff that should be foundational is still wobbly.

And let’s talk about LegendOfTotalWar—because this matters. Love him or not, he’s been one of the most visible, knowledgeable, relentlessly active creators in the entire Total War ecosystem for over a decade. When someone at that level publicly throws in the towel (or even steps back) because they’re exhausted by the bugs, the fractured design direction, and the constant firefighting instead of foundational fixes… that’s not “just a YouTuber quitting,” that’s a canary in the coal mine for your game’s health and your relationship with the community. The guy has spent years stress-testing your systems, surfacing reproducible issues, and telling you—often early—what’s broken and why. Watching him walk away isn’t drama; it’s a verdict on trust and competence. If your most dedicated evangelists no longer believe their feedback leads to meaningful change, why should the rest of us keep buying DLCs and pretending things will get better?

So here’s where I’m at: this game can be brilliant, but it’s buried under negligence and nickel-and-diming. Shame on you for letting it get this far. [h2]Review[/h2]
Total War: Warhammer 3 is the third installment of its trilogy and brings some of the best the series can offer. 24 factions and nearly 100 lord choices on the mega map, the most recently updated effects for each of those factions, and smaller quality of life changes like changes to rosters, effects, abilities, and play style. It also has some of the most frustrating aspects of the game, with several qualities that have not been properly addressed since launching like unit path-finding, sieges, the most current of a long series of bugs that appear in a new patch. I'm aiming to compare this game a lot to its previous installment TW:WH2, in part to explain the differences by comparison, but also because I don't have much experience in other grand strategy games.

[h2]The Good[/h2]
[list]
[*]All factions, and the most updated version of each faction across all games, is found here. The examples that come to mind most are factions from WH1, where the Empire and Dwarfs got vastly expanded upon reworks. Other factions that were reworked from WH1, such as Beastmen, got those major updates in WH2, but Beastmen also have new units from DLC present in this game. There are some factions like Dark elves that got reworks to their economies, playstyles, and starting positions that make some prefer WH2, but I believe that the updates are still a net positive that I'm listing this in good.
[*]Certainly small effects are better. Toggle-able UI features for anything you want/don't want, in-game encyclopedias for unit rosters and spells. Helps keep you in the game. Also, small faction-specific changes. Its hard to explain this to someone without knowing some aspects of the game, but the effect I recognized immediately was playing High Elves, and using an effect that lets me fight siege battles with an ability to destroy walls. In WH3, this ability can target walls, towers, and gates directly. In WH2, I need to target a unit on the wall itself, which sometimes had no effect. It is just less finicky in WH3. I need to play other factions to recognize more of these patterns, but QoL made this effect less annoying in 3.
[*]Diplomacy has been improved. Going back to WH2 without the ability to trade settlements, or more-accurately quantify how close I was to making a deal certainly had me missing the current system. Its also not immediately a bad idea to make an alliance in WH3, where before it would mean getting dragged into wars. You can still be dragged into wars, but being able to borrow armies and recruit units outside your roster can be fun, and I had more fun with diplomacy in 3.
[/list]

[h2]Side-grades[/h2]
[list][*]AI cheats for higher difficulties are lower in this game. This in part helps more units (mainly melee) be useful in army composition, where previously they may have been ignored. I'm listing this as a side grade because there will be some who prefer the difficulty be higher and some who like that more of their roster is useful
[*]Its busier in WH3. Certain campaigns have super high-traffic areas because there's been so much introduced. I don't think it heavily shifts any of them into being negative, but it certainly feels different in a way that isn't really positive or negative
[/list]

[h2]The Bad[/h2]
[list]
[*]DLC. This is true for any installment of this series. Certain rosters in WH2 felt incomplete without the DLC it brought, but WH3 compounds that issue by having all three games DLC be available to play. I wouldn't say anything is "necessary," no DLC is a missing piece of a faction sold separately. But some factions in WH3 get pretty close to that feeling. I don't play a lot of Chaos but it would be lying to say that having the Champions of Chaos DLC didn't help the daemonic factions. Buying into the entire 24 roster is also a huge drawback. For many, the main decision of which game to play will be decided by its immediate roster, because you need to own the original game to play certain factions (for example, if you wanted to play Empire in WH2 or 3, you need to either buy WH1 or a faction for empire. And if you wanted any of the WH1 factions you need to buy WH1)
[*]The immensity of bugs. The notable bugs are fire-at-will, where units will use ammo when fire-at-will is not selected (this has been mostly addressed, but certain cavalry and chariots will fire at their targets when issued a charge order.) Path finding in certain maps may have units take a completely different route, most annoyingly when you want to path through a siege map and your unit decided to completely circle around a structure rather than go through a gate right in front of them. Flying units sometimes cannot land and do their attack animations and will be stuck. Large-sized entities have tons of trouble killing infantry-sized single entity models or small infantry groups. I don't recall many bugs when revisiting WH2, and its not to say they don't exist, but they are present and readily apparent in any WH3 campaign you play.
[*]Sieges. The Siege Rework was largely a failure in this game. It was suppose to turn sieges from being drab and unexciting into a more expanded-upon system. Aside from different maps, and a small defense building system, there is not much that excites people about sieges. They are still generally unfun to play through, and many bugs are derived from attempting to expand on sieges. It was a new feature that was supposed to be the biggest reason to play WH3, but has almost exclusive been a point against it
[/list]

[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]
I'm going to be honest and say my experience is limited. I'm not super in touch with metas but from what I understand the only real disruptions happen with DLC. I would say its overall better in WH3, it has more modes and units have been updated. I also watch several creators like Turin, Dahvplays, Human Boy Yes-Yes, any of the tournaments they or others do, and there seems to be a big community for it. That doesn't exist in WH2, at least not anymore. I've had fun, its good with friends. If you don't like randoms you have the big organizers and discords.

[h2]Concluding Thoughts[/h2]
As much as CA has made this game very well, there are many who feel the sentiment that it has taken two steps forward, one step back. I largely agree, and its hard to ignore recent events when its been a compounding issue over now [i]years[/i]. It definitely has some features that changed for the better, but also to many entrenched issues that are some of the worst. I would say that if CA gets their act together, this is a game to buy on sale. It has a tremendous amount of replay value and content to find, but it feels held back by its current issues that range in time from recent to from launch

What happened you may ask? Hyena's. Hyena's happened. The game developer went all in on that ill conceived 'game' and their publisher at the last moment saw what kind of disaster it would be and pulled the plug. But they had already sunk in tens of millions of dollars into this project and were understandably 'big mad'.

The publisher after that made sure the game developer did some quality control with the thrones of decay dlc and made the game developer to finally look back at Warhammer III (which most were probably reluctant to do, but many got sacked along the way) to get it to a decent state. This did work and that's where I stepped into Warhammer III (after leaving Warhammer II because I wanted to see if the game developer improved - and until thrones they did not).

But alas with all those sackings and basically the publisher putting the game developer on notice, management decided to focus on several new projects hoping to regain favour and dump this technical debt garbage to their sub studio in Bulgaria, who are currently overwhelmed and understaffed to save this forrest fire. It would take a youtuber to dramatically exclaim he quit and he would take his toys home, before the game developer felt any pressure to respond to the increasingly broken and abandoned game.

[h1]Warhammer 3: Style Over Substance[/h1]
A visually impressive game let down by shallow mechanics, repetitive gameplay, and poor design choices.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Simplistic and Repetitive Loop[/h2]
[i]Capture, build, repeat.[/i]
The core loop wears thin fast. You're either the Chaos Prince or "everyone else," but it all plays the same: walk around, take settlements, build, repeat. No real strategic depth. Playing tall is dull, ambushes are rare, and AI interactions feel lifeless. There'e no reward for razing settlements - What's the point!?

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Limited Choice, Paywalled Variety[/h2]
[b]Two campaign paths, little replay value.[/b]
Only the Daemon Prince offers a slightly different setup, but it's not enough. Most other factions are locked behind DLC. [i]This is not a full experience out of the box.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Poor Unit Management[/h2]
Caravans look like heroes, so it’s easy to waste skill points unless you micromanage. Combat feels off—units barely matter, and your main hero carries the whole campaign.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Punishing and Unclear Mechanics[/h2]
The game does a poor job of explaining key mechanics and punishes you whether you play fast or slow. Across multiple half-finished playthroughs, I noticed that enemy AI aggression scales with your progress—push too quickly, and you’ll trigger surprise wars and multi-front attacks, even early in the game. It feels like you're being punished for not staying on an invisible, predetermined curve.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Final Thoughts[/h2]
[b]Warhammer 3 looks great, but lacks depth.[/b]
It could’ve been a time sink—instead, it’s a grind. Locked content, unclear mechanics, and a boring loop make it hard to recommend.

[hr][/hr]
[b]Final Score: 4/10 – Not Recommended[/b]
I paid around £12 and still felt short-changed. I’ll keep the game and maybe pick up the all DLC if it drops below £20—but needing to spend over twice the base price just to unlock core features like blood effects feels ridiculous.

short:
A trilogy that started strong and peaked in the second installment ends in disaster. Total War: WARHAMMER III is a broken mess, and proof that quality, once lost, is hard to regain. Unless Creative Assembly makes a major course correction, I cannot in good conscience recommend this game – not at full price, not even on sale. It’s bloated, buggy, and broken. And at over 300€ for the full experience, the return on investment is a cruel joke.

Long:
A Frustrated Farewell to Total War: WARHAMMER III – A Once-Great Series in Steady Decline

As a long-time fan of the Total War: WARHAMMER series, this review is difficult to write. I’ve followed this franchise from the beginning, supported it with both time and money – over 300€ for the full experience including all DLCs – and watched it grow from something great into something sadly disappointing.

The first game was a solid foundation. It introduced a bold new direction for Total War and proved that a fantasy setting could work brilliantly with the formula. Then came WARHAMMER II, which many (me included) consider the peak of the trilogy. It delivered some of the best DLCs the Total War series has ever seen, with richly developed factions, engaging campaigns, and thoughtful mechanics that showed real care and passion from the developers.

Then came WARHAMMER III – and with it, a steep and painful decline in quality.

WARHAMMER III was supposed to be the grand finale, the game that brought everything together. Instead, it launched in a broken, half-finished state and has continued to suffer ever since. The decline in quality is not only noticeable – it’s undeniable.

Take the recent Skulltaker DLC campaign. It was hyped as a major content drop, but it released with game-breaking bugs that made it literally unplayable for many users. Basic mechanics failed to function, quests wouldn’t progress, and crashes were frequent. It was clear this DLC had not been tested at all, or if it was, it was pushed out regardless of its broken state. That’s not just careless – it’s insulting.

Sadly, this isn't an isolated event. Almost every new DLC or update in WARHAMMER III introduces more issues than it fixes. Each patch feels like it breaks as much as it adds. Bugs linger for months, and the community’s bug reports seem to fall on deaf ears. There is either no quality assurance process, or the studio simply no longer cares to use one.

What’s worse is that Creative Assembly appears more focused on pumping out new DLCs quickly than on fixing the core game. The strategy seems to be: release, profit, repeat – regardless of the content’s state. And we, the players, are expected to just keep paying while the game falls apart around us.

At this point, it feels like the developers don’t care about the players at all. Feedback is ignored, communication is minimal, and long-standing issues go unresolved for months. There is no sense of pride in their work anymore – just a factory-like churn of content that gets worse with every iteration.

To put it plainly: Total War: WARHAMMER III is where the wheels came off. It’s a tragic and frustrating end to a trilogy that started with such promise.

If I approach that enemy asking to trade or make a non-aggression pact, they'll tell me to go ♥♥♥♥ myself.

[h1] Total War: Warhammer III is, in its base, a good game, a great game even. [/h1]

However; Its quirks and some questionable design choices, especially on the corporate side, lead me to leave a negative review.

[h2] Preamble: [/h2]

As of my writing of this review, October 2025, there has been a string of ♥♥♥♥-ups perhaps caused by poor decisions of Creative Assembly (hereafter "CA") as an enterprise, perhaps also by the developement team.

To cut it short CA has proven time and time again that, especially in the wake of the upcoming release of the "Tides of Torment"-DLC, it as an enterprise producing video games is unable provide a satisfying quality of updates and or upkeep of its existing titles. Be it in the form of bug fixes or perhaps even taking the community seriously, especially in the form of prioritising "new content" in favour of maintaining and or fixing existing content (Such as the game breaking AI bugs for the Lizardmen and Tomb Kings that have caused recent drama).

[b] TLDR [/b] : As such I find it reasonable to inform any potential buyer of this game and or future CA titles, that they are buying a video game from a company that fails to guarantee the functioning of essential parts of the product bought.

[h2] Actual review [/h2]

As to make the following review "simpler" and easier to undestand, it will be presented in the popular "+ and -" bullet point format.
Of course, where needed, I will elaborate upon some points.

[h3] The positives [/h3]
In short ([i] insert clip of dwarves exclaiming "SHORT!??!" [/i])

+ The classic Total War game format (For better or for worse)
+ A nice turn based strategy game
+ Enjoyable field battles (Separated from the campaign map)
+ Cool unique champions providing a spin on the established formula
+ Unique faction mechanics
+ All the charm of the Warhammer Fantasy lore (implemented for better or worse) including but not limited to:
 I. Bootleg renaissance Holy Roman Empire
II. Russians on bears (+ Weird babushkas and orthodox extremist rasputin)
III. Lore accurate french people
IV. The chinese
V. Dragons (Some also just being chinese)
VI. Isolationism maxxing High Elves
VII. Racist Wood Elves
VIII. S+M Dark Elves
IX. D(a]emons (Small and large)
X. Rats including:
X.I. Religious rats
X.II. Chemical warfare rats
X.III. Tech rats
X.IV. Assasin rats
X. V. Human wave tactic rats
X. VI. Bio Engineering rats
XI. Orks
XII. Goblins
XIII. Skeletons
XIV. Vampires (Including vampire pirates)
XV. Lizards
XVI. Frogs

And many, many more

+ A Rich diversity of playstyles possible (Playing tall or wide, as a scourge upon the world, a cleanser of chaos. as a horde or a settled race etc.)
+ A miriad of units for each faction, with race specific unit rosters
+ A flourishing modding community providing quality and attention to detail CA fails to achieve (including community bug fixes)
+ Good performance (usually)
+ A very cool Sandbox of a game to play around with
+ Nice graphics (of course subject to your own preferences)
+ An engaged and dedicated community (As with all things associated with Warhammer)
+ Some (!) very fun and more or less well made DLC concent


[h3] The negatives [/h3]

- An oversimplified diplomacy system
- A miriad of bugs including but not limited to: (Of course many having been FIXED, so BIG PROPS to their very much existing capability to fix bugs):
I. Some factions being unable to recruits units they are supposed to be able to recruit
II. Bug fixes causing more bugs
III. The AI ceasing to function
IV. An "occupy settlement" bug that has been in the game since release
V. A bug that had cause a hero unit to become sonic the hedgehog
and many more (I'm not exactly an expert in these)

- An astonishing amount of player traps: The Karl Franz campaign (or the Empire as a whole) i.e. the campaign every beginner plays, being one large noob trap.
- Questionable unit design choices (Some Units are just so ass, they sabotage your gameplay experience, some so incredibly useless they aren't even worth it as a throw away unit)
- Some OP DLC factions (*cough* Jade Dragon *cough*)
- An incredibly boring late game (Once you snowball its just a grindfest of conquering the world)
- Very poorly thought out endgame crises (aka.: Haha Unit spam go brrrrr)
- No real "looming threat" except the arbitrary end game crises
- No actual binding of any playthrough to the lore (This however is a design choice, with the game being a Sandbox)
- Loads of content being hidden behind a paywall (including the immortal empires campaign) sometimes even requiring you to buy DLC for older titles (It's nice veterans of the series don't have to pay again, but they could have just included the darn content in the base game as well).
--> As of my writing the game including all possible DLC costs 423 CHF or about 529 USD. Of course for most buyers prices will be lower seing as game prices for swiss consumers on steam, contrary to the already higher buying power of the swiss frank, are higher than anywhere else, because ♥♥♥♥ us I guess. (Of course this opens a whole other can of worms, too large for this review).

- The already aformentionened questionable decision making of CA as a company, not necessarily of the developers themselves.
- The repeated need for community action to make CA fix their game
- The repeated inability for CA to learn from past mistakes
- The spaghetti code syndrome many games selling you a bajillion DLCs have

[h2] Conclusion [/h2]

Total War: Warhammer III as a game by itself is a game I would recommend you play. It's a very fun sandbox strategy game with epic field battles benefitting from a rich lore base.

The gameplay loop is fun, the battles are fun, the game is just fun.

It has its quirks, it has bugs, but it is still a great game even if the player thrash on it sometimes.

However, as stated before, it is up to you if you want to buy a, atleast for now functioning, game from a company that has shown time and time again, that it doesn't understand the wants and needs of its player-base in concern to Total War: Warhammer III,  that has shown it doesn't know what players want with other titles (see the many recent flopped iterations of the Total War saga) and is led by a management team that just doesn't get that the video game industry, or its consumers, just don't work like other industries do.

Despite the mostly negative reviews currently (Sept 2025), the game is one of the best fantasy army battle simulators out there. Where else do you get to battle kaiju sized crocodiles with zeppelins and helicopters piloted by dwarfs ?
Be a zombie-pirate and raid the coasts of kingdoms and empires or be conniving giant rats with nuclear missiles and deadly bio-weapons. Stand stalwart against the hordes of green skins as the proud Dawi. Brandish faith, steel and gunpowder to stave off threats as the men of the empire. or Be literal demons to cry havoc and let slip the hounds of war gainst all life.

This game has it all. Bottom line is this game is fun. Lot of people have played it and still play it. Join the fun and hey if you dont like it, papa Gaben has your back (under 2 hours or less).

So I have over 3000 hours in this game. All the dlcs from all 3 of the warhammer series and at points have really enjoyed the game. But…
I would say the points when I enjoyed the game the most was during warhammer 2 and what has led to this negative review.
First and foremost the state of the game right now is not worth your investment, and it seems to be getting worse.
The biggest issue at this point is compounding issues that are not being resolved and worse than that they are being made worse with the addition of new content. So let’s go over what I think are some of the main issues currently with the game. 
City battles. Moving your units in a city is a mess. Sometimes units, mostly monsters or characters will get trapped in walls and not be able to move. But that has been a long issue and has gotten worse. Now they are getting stuck on nothing. Making the somewhat frustrating task of moving your army through a city (even when not getting stuck) infuriating at times.
But that is not where it ends for battle issues. So let's talk about the battle maps. Many of these maps look like they were algorithmically created and green lit without any thought as to how they would play. Almost like no one there actually plays the game. It just is feeling more and more inconsiderate to the players. And to make this worse the getting stuck thing that happens in cities is now happening in battles. But don’t fret, sometimes the AI just chooses to do nothing with their units. The growing amount of issues with playability and ai functionality deserves an essay to fully cover. 
Next let’s touch on the Ai’s inability to play as certain factions. The beastmen, a faction that has been around for a while, just doesn’t know what they are doing. Dark elves don’t attack ports with their admirals. Chaos dwarves often make dumb and ineffective armies because they choose to make a capital city an outpost that can’t make high level units. A problem that could easily be resolved by just taking away the ability to make a capital anything but that. But again, I'm pretty sure no one at CA plays this game. 
Finally the biggest point to this review is that the game is just getting worse. New content brings new issues and exasperates old ones. Old issues are not being given consideration. 
And this has been the story of warhammer 3. 
So is it worth its high price tag to get all the content? Not any more.
Will I be getting the next Dlc? No, not if the game's state doesn’t seriously improve.
Moreover I was, and still kinda am, excited for the next total war title. But if this is how they treat an Ip and their players I will likely be waiting for reviews.
Stop making hollow apologies and bandaid fixes only to wreck it more with the next paid or hollow apology expansion to the game. If CA would only stop trying to take advantage of their players they would have to apologize less.
We the players want you to succeed, but this is only leading to disappointment. CA management needs to stop trying to turn this around and just make the game work, be fun and I will happily continually pay for each new game and Dlc.

This serves as a functional cop-out of any kind of AI Rework or Overhaul that this game desperately needs. It should be genuinely embarrassing for CA that modders who do it for the love of the game and for free are better at improving their AI than their paid development studio is.

I'll take a moment to quote Former Creative Assembly developer Julian McKinlay when he revealed in an interview that CA's management "instructed us not to improve [the AI] in certain ways, because they believed that players enjoyed being able to dominate the AI".

In many ways, it's quite clear that CA's management is the reason for most decisions around TW, not the developers. It explains why there are so many DLCs and yet still so many flaws. Profit efficiency is their priority. But profit margins don't strictly get us a better game. The sudden ability to address issues in the community as a result of the recent backlash and negativity around the broken AI is proof that they'll mobilize when their bottom line is threatened. The pressure can't let up if they only fix the Unit Recruitment issues. If that's where they stop, it will prove McKinlay was right; CA's TW management intentionally cripples the AI because they believe Total War players only want a power fantasy. They're wrong. They should fix the primary opponent that all TW players face in the campaign. They should overhaul the AI, and not just the Campaign AI. The Battle AI too. I'm sick of facing a brain-dead mob of enemies. I'm sick of having to give them cheats just so I can have a challenge. This is NOT acceptable from a HUNDRED-MILLION dollar company, and players should want and expect more from them if we're to fork over our money for the base game and the roughly TWENTY EIGHT DLCs on top of them.

TLDR: I can't recommend this game in its current state for anyone wanting a challenge in a strategy game. However, if you want to curbstomp brain-dead AI and face next to no challenge, or conversely, if you want to give the AI massive cheats just to have any semblance of challenge while constantly fighting from a disadvantageous position, then you may enjoy this game, but only if you enjoy Total War games.

I’ve been playing Total War since Medieval II, and I still love the core idea of these games — large-scale battles, strategy, and empire management. But each new release feels like another step backward in terms of stability, direction, and care for the community.

As someone studying game design, it’s painful to watch a studio with so much potential mismanaged like this. I don’t blame the developers — I’m sure many of them care deeply — but the leadership and project management are killing the soul of this series.

Every release ships with major bugs that take months (or years) to fix — if they’re ever fixed at all.

Every time a good patch arrives, it seems to break something else — like the recent AI recruitment bug, which makes the game borderline unplayable.

Feedback is constantly ignored, even from experienced voices like LegendofTotalWar, who was one of the few creators offering genuine, constructive criticism. Instead of listening, CA pushed away one of their best advocates.

And while the visuals and scale have grown, the depth and passion that made Medieval II special are gone — sieges, recruitment, and management used to be fun, not tedious.

At this point, I can’t recommend Warhammer III to new players until Creative Assembly changes how they manage projects and engage with their community. The devs deserve better leadership, and the fans deserve a game worthy of the Total War legacy.

The product works on the surface and seems good overall, but so many core design compromises were made just to cram the setting’s lore and fantasy into the Total War formula that it’s sometimes painful to look at. For example, the idea of undead factions like the Vampire Counts is completely castrated by the 20-unit (or 40-unit) army cap. Swarm units like skeletons and zombies — which should exist in massive hordes — quickly become obsolete as you replace them with stronger units due to limited slots. That design flaw makes factions like the Vampire Counts or Skaven feel lackluster. A more open system and setting-specific design would have been needed — but that should have happened ten years ago.

Now, with CA’s recent misstep of releasing a broken patch despite knowing it was broken, it’s just another drop onto an already hollow stone.

I’m adding my voice here as a long-time disgruntled fan frustrated by foundational laziness — their refusal to invest in proper groundwork for the Warhammer trilogy, their mistreatment of employees and customers, unjustified price hikes, and the fact that only massive public outrage ever forces them to act professionally. Because of that, I can’t in good conscience recommend supporting either the company or the game until things truly improve. Such a prospect sounds splendid on paper, yet in practice, we are faced with an unoptimized and fundamentally unfinished product, which the developers have sought to rectify through DLCs and patches. However, due to critical flaws embedded within the very core of the game, such efforts have proven futile. On the contrary, with each subsequent update, they merely add more content, which, in any case, is of dubious value: (we are presented with Bretonnia from the era of the first Warhammer, a Daemon Prince whom no one particularly likes, and a multitude of unplayable factions that are conceptually intriguing yet awfully underdeveloped) nevertheless, they choose to release a tenth update dedicated to the Skaven. Similarly, rather than learning to run, one orders a McDonalds meal to be delivered to one’s home every day, thus, one may gain weight, yet that does not signify an improvement in quality. The engine was revolutionary in its time, particularly compared to Warhammer II, yet it has since become excessively outdated and is unable to sustain this accumulation of new layers imposed every three months. Until I realized, too late, that CA does not seem to respect their own product enough to give it the most fundamental amount of care - to patch it and grow it adequately in order to earn my loyalty and my money.  Yet for years I have paid for DLC, often at full price, because I loved Warhammer Fantasy and I loved the beauty and passion CA once brought to this project.  No longer.  Since WH3 released, it has been a roller coaster of peaks (Thrones of Decay, Chaos Dwarves) and valleys (Shadows of Change, the launch /w Realms of Chaos), and now this seemingly creaks toward its terminal phase; not in glory, but in ignominy.

CA/Sega, if you've truly moved on to Warhammer 40K or whatever, do yourself a favor, if you can, and learn from the lessons of this debacle: nurture and cherish your products, and your fan base will give you our money and our support.  But as it stands, WH3 does not go out (yet) with a bang, but with a whimper.  I'm holding out hope for an End Times DLC or some sort of patching programme, but when my archers can't fire and two whole factions (Lizardmen and Tomb Kings) literally don't even work anymore, and I have to rely on mods to do for free what you charge for, you have forfeit my loyalty.

I'll preface this with: this is a great game and I love it. I both love warhammer fantasy (probably even more than 40k), and love Total War. I've gotten a lot of playtime from this game and the previous titles. It is particularly amazing with mods, it's just a totally different experience and I wish half of this games sales could go to the modders.

HOWEVER, there are some major issues with this game that I have to gripe over and will never stop griping over. While the scale of this game is massive with tons of units and factions and variety, and graphically looks amazing, in so many aspects it is a downgrade from previous total war titles. The campaign map probably suffers the worst from this, it seems arcadey in comparison to their other games. The trade system has almost zero depth, settlement building sucks, you can't have armies without generals, the supply lines system is awful and it's ironic that they kept it this way in the 3rd when they released 3k with a superior army supply system, no fort/castle building, no ship building or sea battles (which is funny since certain factions are literally themed around nautical warfare, like vampire coast, bordeleaux and the dark elves), public order doesn't really affect anything unless it's so bad that a rebellion happens (which still doesn't really do anything because the rebel armies will just sit there and let you immolate them), and most factions no longer have the option to make vassals despite being a prior feature in WH1 and 2. I will also point out that the map and factions feels very convoluted due to the game's obessession with "legendary lords." To be honest, they really need to throw away the idea of making every legendary lord their own faction. I know they expect every faction to confederate by turn 20 (which is another thing I hate since it takes away the personality of different factions within races), but man, you can only fit so many factions in their downsized wh fantasy map. It would also be nice to strip away legendary leaders immortality. Sure, maybe give them a certain amount of deaths before actually dying, and maybe keep a respawn mechanic for characters such as demons, but it makes factions feel so much more static. The emperor is Karl Franz on turn 1, and he is still emperor on turn 500. Also, the late game crisis' are actually so boring. WH1's End Times invasion felt intense now crisis' are basically "Oh no every skaven faction is resurrected and we've instantly spawned their full stack armies in everybody's backyard." Campaign AI also do not know how to, well, do anything. And this is before the current controversy. They have either been lobotomizes berserkers, like in the past where they suicide throw armies that have no chance of winning, and walk through 15 different factions just to attack the player, or they are like the current state: lobotomized pacifists. And it's funny since mods like Deepwar AI make them play so much better, and it's only a modification of the current AI rather than a groundup overhaul. 

The in battle gameplay is fun, and I would say the balancing is in a decent state now but also suffers. There's no weather or time of day options or modifiers, the co sync animations have mostly disappeared to the point where it's a shock to see one happen, and collisions are noticeably bad, leading to the fighting looking much less fluid. I've gone back to older titles and been impressed with how much more fluid the fighting looked on supposedly less technically advanced games. There is also a lack of attention to detail that those games had that helped the immersion when watching battle replays. In previous titles, handgunners had reload animations and artillery generally had decently detailed reload animations. Maybe not 1-for-1, but in comparison to this game where artillery reloads by... shuffling hands at it.. it felt much better. The battle AI 

The last thing, and this is most people's gripe, is the greedy dlc policy. Having to buy a dlc to see blood is atrocious. Buying a $60 game and only having access to 10% of the content is also atrocious. Modders have made full factions FOR FREE (and some of these are better than actual dlc factions, like Araby, Marienburg, the southern realms, the jade vampires, etc.). It's a page right out of paradox's book and that's the best summary of it. 

That being said, I still love playing this game because the modders have made some amazing and addictive content that they should be fully commended for. For that reason I still can recommend it, but my opinion on it is very bipolar so I will flip this review from positive to negative and vice versa depending on how CA's acting.

TLDR: This game IS good, and this series IS fun, ESPECIALLY with custom race mods to add in the factions that CA will not add in themselves, however expect some minor bugs here and there that are not too gamebreaking, + be prepared to sell an Arm or a Leg for WH1 + WH2 and its DLCs, on top of the DLCs for Warhammer 3 that came out in the past 4 years if you are just getting into this game as a new player. 

Lets divide this into 2 parts: the good, and the bad. 

THE GOOD: 
- Literally *every* faction is in this game. If it is not, its either: 
A: A mod that you can get off of the workshop and play.
B: Currently in development. 
This includes *entire custom races* or factions that never got a faction or rules for the tabletop like Khuresh, Ind, and soon (probably): Khosun. Glup ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fans from the tabletop rejoice! Your favorite nobody may in fact be already added if you just do a bit of browsing!

- When this game works (And we'll get back to this point later), it can be one of the most fun you can have in a Strategy game, and with some recent updates in the form of saving Lords you like and The Cabal unusual location: If you do certain actions, you can in fact influence your next campaign based on what you did previously. 

- The map size is the biggest in the Total War Warhammer side of things, assuming you play this for immortal empires like I and most players do. If you don't think its big enough, Immortal Empires Expanded exists, and it adds in Ind, Khuresh, The Eastern Steppes, more areas in the southern Wastes, etc. If for some reason, you want things to be in terms of Realistic Scale and size: The Old World Mod exists and provides the experience of a Realscale 1 to 1 Warhammer map with *most* factions within reason being on the map, with entire continents being their own much more brutal arenas with their own issues!

And on this note, time for the Bad. Namely the issues. 

THE BAD: 

1 - Pricing. If you are getting into this for the first time, you have to pay for a *lot* of DLC. And not just DLC: Previous **Games.** I got into this series back in Warhammer 2, right around the Hunter & the Beast, right before Shadow & the Blade dropped. Back then I got it + Warhammer 1 & all of the DLCS for both games for Christmas for roughly ~260 USD during the Holiday sale. A *Sale.* Since then there were 3 DLCS for Warhammer 2, and an Entire New game for roughly ~$60 USD with 5, soon to be 6 DLCs. This is an **expensive** game to get into to enjoy fully. Do not buy this unless there is a sale going on with at least 15-20% off on the different DLCs. 

EDIT: In the comments I've been told that there exists some companies and places that put this game, previous Warhammer total war's and their DLC's at even lower prices, but I admittedly know nothing about these sites, on account of me enjoying this game and others more casually to care that much. 

2 - The Bugs. (Previously there was a blurb here about how the lizardmen were broken, but it looks like they fixed it, at least from my campaigns.) Bugs are a major issue in this game on account of the game suffering from what I can understand - is severe Tech Debt. For the most part, these bugs are small and sometimes comical. From experience, there is a bug for me right now that enemy factions if shoved into a "Fortress" or "Gate" Settlement type, will spam recruit lords with 0 units. But this is a known bug that will *probably* be fixed, considering it has happened on occasion quite frequently. **You don't need to run the Community bugfix mod, but if you want to, then feel free, but I personally do not, and I run 30-40 different mods at once, and my experience with the game is okay.** 

3 - Powerscaling is also a major issue especially in Warhammer 3 in comparison to previous games, so do be aware that some factions might be more overpowered and broken than a faction that got added around ~5 years ago. 

if you really want this game, be ready to sacrifice an organ you don't need to get into this game when everything goes on sale. Moreover, seeing as how "The End Times" DLC is coming, this game is nearing the end of its life cycle, so do be aware that some factions may not have, or ever will recieve the same polish or fun mechanics as some of the newer factions or Races added to Warhammer 3. As of rewriting this on 12/10/25, the next faction set for a rework by the looks of things might be Vampire Counts, seeing as how Norsca got a major overhaul. This is on top of a possible Vampire Coast rework as well.
