As of 15/10/2025 I'm updating the review regarding Patch 6.3.2: The issues with Lizardmen and Tomb Kings seems to be solved as per reported by multiple players and tesers within the different online communities and subforums, so I'll specify some aspects of what I had written before:

##### Majority of this was written 9/10/2025, updates are in brackets preceded by the date ####

With more than 700h in this game, and an unaccountable amount through other games of the saga, I’ve decided to come and put a review on TWWH3 essentially because this game has become the epitome of what’s been wrong with TW since years ago.

I am not a game designer, I’m not a mechanics expert, but I am a software engineer and I can make my head around what issues may be behind the weird software bugs and the recurring errors that these games, and this delivery of the TWWH saga in particular, keep showing: A completely messed up game engine, and in addition, an obsolete AI engine.

For the game engine is blatantly obvious when you see errors that are worked on to be fixed, allegedly, for months, that yet come back to surface from different angles, but they are essentially the same (LoS, path finding, AI behaviour, units behaviour, animations, etc). Not only has this issue been recurring in TWWH saga, there have been errors replicated exactly from previous historical games, present here once again. Which shows that  the core code, or framework, which is at the base has been reused again and again, with little to no care for some coherence between versions. So we may be talking of a, possibly, +10 years old core of code being used as the foundation of a, wannabe, AAA strategy game in 2025. 

And then there’s the AI engine, this is all the assets, scripts, classes and libraries used to make the AI make decisions in battle and in campaign, which again not being a game developer in particular, it’s unknown to me if it’s the same core, then concretely implemented for battle and for campaign, or if it’s one unique decision engine that is further called depending on the context the game is displaying, nevertheless, is obvious for this aspect as well, that it has been the same for around 10 years or more, because I remember seeing “we gonna pump up the AI cheats to make it more competitive while ‘shaving’ the decision making tree” for the first time, within Rome2's first 6 months. TWWH3 is a far more complex game than it’s predecessors, much more rich in mechanics and strategy, and the AI simply does not play the game. That’s the reason behind lizardmen AI being broken currently [15/10/2025: not anymore since version 6.3.2], that’s the reason behind AI recruiting weird ass armies, and not using properly their mechanics, or abusing the one and only the may. Because the game is so complex, and the engine so bad implemented that it would take forever for 200 factions to do their things against a human player and be competitive. [15/10/2025: reviewing this I find saying “bad implemented” is stating my harsh opinion more than a fact, we may use the concepts “old” and “next to obsolescence”]

Now as a newcomer how does this affect you while playing TWWH3? Well you must know that when you enter this game you will immerse yourself in an ultra rich and highly mechanical, quite deep strategically, super diverse and decently entertaining BROKEN game. And there’s really no other way to put it, honestly, and sadly.

Because the game is currently that: broken.
[15/10/2025: Again broken might be a heated opinion, might as well say: “unbalanced”, “buggy” and “unstable” to be loyal to the truth]

With many AI's, not only Lizardmen or Tomb Kings, doing next to nothing for tens of turns. With their army recruiting being totally messed up , and killing the potential variety of units you could be facing. The diplomatic options being weirdly calculated, essentially are all out of context of the play-through going on at that moment [15/10/2025: all Chorfs factions’ recruitment is unbalanced currently, this is known by CA and only “partially fixed” with 6.3.2]. With the army and empire management competitiveness of AI strictly based on the difficulty you play on, which means: how much you wanna ♥♥♥♥ up immersion to favour cheats or they won’t stand a chance, and once you get used, you’ll see they don’t have a chance either.

It is immersion killing, strategy killing, gameplay killing, and is fun killing.

Any strategy games fan will easily discover that the campaign is a cake walk until you raise up difficulty and then it becomes a fancy version of a tower defence game, the only strategy is to place your army where and when it needs to be, there’s not a real exchange of punches through mechanics and tactics, is wak-a-mole of more of less buffed armies, and if this is obvious about AI relating towards players, is even more obvious when AI relate between them.

And there are many, many, aspects we could dive into: sieges, battle behaviours, campaign progression and end-game, but I won’t extend further, I wanted to place some points about the state of the saga and how this particular game expresses that state. Venting a bit in the meantime, to be fair, but to conclude:

Would I recommend this game? Currently never at full price because you would be buying a broken product.
[15/10/2025: once again let's say "unstable" instead of broken"]

Until it’s fixed, if ever happens, only if discounted, and I’d say heavily discounted, if you like fantasy strategy games and/or the Warhammer setting in particular, and want to do some roleplaying, cinematic battles, or play against friends in this setting.

Development needs to be prioritizing fixing issues rather than adding content. New mechanics for two factions don't matter if the campaign experience for every faction is broken.

In the state this game has been in for some time it is not worth the considerable investment to experience what it has to offer. For all the additional content and improvements, major issues that affect every faction have been created or gotten worse, and the company seems unwilling to invest the time and effort to fix it. There are three major areas that need to be fixed before I could recommend this game to anyone.

1. Campaign AI - It is worse than the prior game in every way. You see 5+ armies just standing there around a city not moving or attacking. The flagship races for an update had their AI broken. Large empires don't form to counterbalance your growth. The AI armies are regularly full of garbage units that are easy to overcome. The AI will send armies half way across the world to attack you instead of their neighbors. These issues have been known about for months or years, but even without a single DLC released this year they have not been fixed. Patches that claim to address these issues don't fix them or make them worse.

2. Sieges. They are now longer and worse. The "gate bug," where your units get stuck inside a city without the gate being captured or broken, happens way more than it used to and it is a huge problem. When CA talks about it, they just throw their hands in the air and say "IDK it's hard to fix." That is not an acceptable answer. Single entities have their animations break near gates and stop responding or fighting. Flying units get stuck on walls. The maps are also very poorly designed.  You can't form formations because the areas are too narrow. Units blob up so much magic becomes ridiculous and the only way not to make the fights a slog. Tower shots hit buildings because there is so much intervening terrain to block their line of fire.

3. Communication - CA stays silent when there are major problems with their game and don't talk until the community forces their hand. Then, they don't actually say what is going on. They called the game crashing on campaign start for AMD users an infrequent crash. They say they won't fix a major bug until months after it is introduced, to coincide with a DLC launch, but then when the community makes them talk about it they say that they have a fix so it "makes sense" to send that fix alone. They even have the gall to suggest that we somehow delayed the SINGLE DLC OF THE YEAR to punish us for having them fix their game.

Consider this review as a corollary to my WH2 review.

The multiplayer in this game is top-notch. There are diverse factions with diverse playstyles that can be played in many different modes. It's astonishing the amount of work that they put into multiplayer. 

That comes with some severe downsides. 
The game is much, much more expensive compared to WH2. The focus of all of the new DLC is on this game hence the game is more expensive.
The game requires a much stronger system compared to WH2.  I can barely eek out medium setting. In WH2, I run everything on Ultra. 
Single player campaigns are much easier compared to 2. I have abandoned at least 3 campaigns because they were simply too easy. They did not present much of any challenge. In comparison to 2, the difficulty is much easier and it really seems like they aimed the game for an entirely different set of players. 
There's no narration in the beginning of the immortal empires campaign. However, there are 3 campaign types compared to WH2 only having 2 campaign types. I consider this as a strict downgrade compared to 2 from an immersion and lore perspective, however. 
Units will not always listen to your commands when you are in battle. I personally found this to be unnecessarily frustrating compared to WH2 where unit movement is fluid and responsive. 
CA does not catch bugs and relies on the community to make a stink about it before it is fixed. I don't think it is behavior that should be encouraged. I believe it is in the best interest of both the players and CA to change their approach to this game. Catching bugs and addressing player issues should be a cornerstone of this game's development. 

If you take nothing else from this review, please understand that it has a fantastic multiplayer but it is run by a company that is not currently listening to it's player base. For this reason, I recommend that you purchase WH2 over WH3 at this time.

Total War: WARHAMMER III is an extraordinary game, that has been poorly managed since it's release. It is still filled with years old bugs, has an interesting but greatly neglected PvP scene and is hosted in a fairly outdated engine. The community has been ignored for such a long time, on so many matters and there is clearly a case of corporate greed happening for years.

Considering that in order to get a feature complete game, some people have purchased all 3 games of the series and all their DLC (on release) for nearly 500$ collectively (without any discounts and from the official Total War: Warhammer pages, on Steam), I cannot recommend it. Even if you take your time and find good sales for everything needed to have a feature complete game, right now, the price cannot drop bellow 180$. High price should be matched with high quality. All this game has is quantity right now. Sure, there's a lot of it to be honest, but it lacks depth. Every campaign ends too quickly and starts feeling very similar to the last one after a while. In my opinion, diminishing replay-ability.

Especially for newcomers, if you like what you see, check a few things first, how many DLC there are and what each of them provides. Find huge sales, bundles and pick only what you want to play. A great amount of campaigns (Legendary Lords and complete races for the Immortal Empires Campaign, a.k.a. the thing everyone is here for) are locked behind DLC or THE PURCHASE OF THE PREVIOUS BASE GAMES (Total War: WARHAMMER & Total War: WARHAMMER 2). Immortal Empires -> The Empire -> Emperor Karl Franz - Reikland cannot be picked, if you don't have the base game Total War: WARHAMMER, for example.

A game with massive potential (thanks to its setting) that will likely never be realized due to Creative Assembly's chronic incompetence, with out-of-touch middle management working a small team to the bone, while marketing runs the show.

They completely broke the AI for 3 races with the most recent patch, rendering them inert, and aren't communicating any intention of a fix.

If you're considering buying this tentatively-functional game or its upcoming DLC, remember that money is a reward, and rewards must be earned through good behavior.

It often feels like the developers are ignoring the community until a massive backlash or “♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥” forces them to respond. Meanwhile, smaller studios and similar strategy games release regular patches and actually listen to feedback and if its something mayor that takes longer to fix they point it out imidiatly.

There has been basically no meaningful new content for about a year, yet core issues — from AI stupidity and broken siege battles to unbalanced factions and performance problems — are still present. It’s especially sad that one of the most downloaded mods on Steam is a community bugfix mod that tries to fix what the developers won’t.

The game still has a huge amount of potential, but the lack of transparency, slow patch cycle, and focus on monetization over maintenance have really hurt it. Los Total War de Warhammer son de las peores cosas que he jugado en muchisimo tiempo con una diferencia abismal. No solo el juego está optimizado como si los trabajadores hubieran sentido completo desprecio ante la idea de hacer algo funcional, sino que además trataron a la IP como si le tuvieran odio. Y eso que esto es el tercer juego. Veamos, si sagas como El Señor de Los Anillos tienen tan solo 5 libros contandos oficiales de la historia fija que contar, siendo la triología, el Hobbit y el Silmarillion, contando con obras que, aunque complementan, no son indispensables (hijos de Hurin, La Caída de Gondolin, cuentos inconclusos), ha sido suficiente para que comunidades enteras modeen juegos y hagan mejores trabajos que desarrolladoras con cientos de empleados... Habla bastante por sí solo, pero ese no es el punto: Warhammer fantasy tiene más de cien novelas, cien libros contando la historia, profundizando en cada facción, y en teoría es un universo muy grande, ¿no? Hay como 20 razas, y todo eso, y sin embargo, la cantidad de unidades no solo resulta deprimente, sino lo realmente deprimente es que para poder jugar todo su jueguito feo tengo que pagar el costo completo de 4 Triples A, y aún me sobraría para comprar Silkgson, solo para poder jugar esta cosa y no morirme del asco teniendo que añadir mods o de lo contrario el juego es completamente injugable. Veamos, Brettonia, la única facción en DLC que es en teoría gratis pero aún así necesitas tener el primer juego para que se desbloquee completa?? Que broma es esa, pero veamos todavía más broma: yo no sé si Gameswhorkshop y sus escritores tienen una mentalidad deficiente, o es que en problema de este juego, ¿pero por qué Bretonnia, de las pocas facciones humanas, que en teoría debería ser medieval, no tiene unidades de picas, u honderos, o ballesteros, o literalmente la mayoría de ármas útiles de la antiguëdad? No me vale la excusa de que tienen bastante caballería, si literalmente la falange es una formación militar indispensable: las lanzas y picas son las armas más rentables de la historia de la humanidad, ¿y me estás contando que una facción con acceso a hechiceros no pueden idear una falange? Entiendo que el desarrollador diga que eso podría humillar y feo a los demonios, y estoy de acuerdo, Alejandro Magno se papea a Khorne y feo. Pero en serio, ¿facción "gratis" y tiene una cantidad de unidades que es deprimente? El Imperio tampoco se salva, que siendo la facción con más unidades disponibles, es deprimente ver que algo llamado "Imperio", en universo de magia y tal, posea unidades que harían llorar hasta sus enemigos, y no de miedo, sino de lástima. Yo no sé si esto sea problema del lore en sí, o de la desarrolladora por tener pereza de hacer unidades competentes, pero solo los mods son capaces de arreglar algo así. 
Por otra parte, la IA del juego está rota. No solo algunas facciones no funcionan, sino que otras actúan como si estuviera luchando contra la pesadilla de Annibal. 
las animaciones se fueron de total sábatico. ¿Alguien puede explicarme por qué, Rome 2 total war, salido en el año del pavo, con seguro una fracción del presupuesto de este juego, tenía animaciones a mansalva, más facciones jugables de facto, y mejor equilibrio? Es que es insultante. Aquí me metes que la caballería manda a volar a los enemigos no uno, ni dos, ni tres, sino ocho metros sobre el aire, y el muy flipado se pone de pie como si nada. ¿Qué sentido tiene ese? Sé que es un juego de fantasía, ¿pero es qué por qué no podrías hacer la carga simplemente más coherente? O los matas y ya, o que no arrasen tan fácil, o que no los manden a volar tantos metros. Por otra parte, la magia de este videojuego creo que es un hazmereír porque si creía que el de Warhammer 2 era malo, este me parece que está para que solo sirva como comodín: si en una batalla no lo empleas, puedes ganar fácilmente y como si no importase, en otras, si no la empleas con todo lo que tengas eres hombre muerto, muerto, muerto. Y eso podría dar juego a la estrategia, sí, de no ser porque los hechizos funcionan de una manera que me resulta deprimente. Tiene mucho potencial: me maraville al ver la Gran Catai y todo el tema de la energía y eso, para luego qué? Que unos demonios del caos con muchas ganas de expulsar popo por la boca me arrasen sin importar que mi facción, en teoría, tiene la potencia mágica para hacerles frente. 
Sé que es difícil hacer un videojuego de una saga de fantasía como Warhammer, donde la magia funciona como si estuvieras teniendo epilepsia, y que no es precisamente fácil hacer una adaptación de un universo que nadie ha vivido a diferencia de la historia donde podemos tener datos precisos de las facciones con cierto lujo de detalles. Pero en serio, en serio, ¿por qué los hastatis de Rome 2 parecen 10 veces más trabajados que la mejor y más útil unidad del Imperio en este juego? No es solo que me parece que los Suevos, literalmente bárbaros germanos que a duras penas y sabían como respirar, ¡tengan más y mejores unidades que toda Brettonia que sepa solo Khorne cómo no se han extinguido! Y ni hablar de Medieval 2 total war. Estoy seguro que si me pones un muro de picas españolas logro parar a 20 devoradores de almas de Khorne. ¿Cómo un juego de hace 25 años, con solo el 2% de gráficos que este juego, tenga más, mejor, y contado trabajo, costando a veces solo 4 dolares? Es que de verdad, ¡¡4 triples A!! ¡¡Yo soy el que está haciendo AAA viendo los precios!! Y yo que creía que Paradox era agresiva con su política de los DLCS, ¡pero al menos ellos me entregan algo que me de horas de entretenimiento, no esta cosa que ni bien tengo una facción me resulta que no saben hacer picas!!

This game's predecessor Total War: Warhammer II was one of my favourite gaming experiences and left me excited for this game. Despite a rough launch, this game iterated on that game in several ways and has added interesting factions and mechanics.

Unfortunately, it has also added a series of mis-steps that have led me to have furloughed this game for months now, despite regularly wanting to pick it up again.

The most key and invasive issue for me is the sheer amount of downtime as the game processes it's end of turn. TW:W2 originally felt similarly, and led me to purchase my first SSD to address the issue (successfully). It is disappointing to essentially feel wound back to before that improvement made the play experience tolerable.

The other major negative change from my perspective are the siege mechanics. I admit to being more of a simulationist and roleplayer than a strategic game player, so having invisible construction crews building  defences on the fly is an immersion break for me. It's an ambitious game plagued by issues that drag it down. Siege battles have been unfun since Total War Warhammer I, and at this point if I have to fight a siege I am probably just going to quit campaign. Khorne, Dwarves, and Skaven are great. Norsca and Daemons and Chaos suck. Indeed, the quality of legendary lords within factions can vary widely within a faction. Bug plague this game, the most annoying of which (for me) has been the long standing gate bug, where a gate in a seige battle will open, let like 10 units through, not close, and because it is open, become undamagable. AI is poor - setting aside recent issues with lizardmen and tomb kings, the AI is really only capable of rushing you all at once with the occasional unit flanking. Some factions (beastmen) don't seem to work well in campaign, and haven't sine immortal empires. Others (chaos dwarves) stack the most basic units even in later stages of the game where they should have access to their most powerful units. 

This game is such a big let down for me. Throughout the whole process we've been drip fed hope and promises of faction and siege reworks, dlc to expand, rework, and add to factions, and reworks to mechanics that didn't work great in Warhammer I and II (namely siege battles). These promises go un or under fulfilled, the community's frustration boils over, we get an AI generated corporate apology, some minor changes that give just enough hope to make us think CA has changed, only to go back to the same old lazy post launch support we've had 6 months later. I've enjoyed this game a great deal, and despite it's many issues probably still will in the future. However I can not in good conscience recommend this game. In its current state it is riddled with drastic, game-breaking bugs that have been left unfixed for weeks. That along with the sheer volume of DLC and the cost to obtain them speaks volumes to the greed of Creative Assembly/SEGA and their apparent disdain for the community. Long-term players are leaving in droves and the issues haven't even been properly addressed, much less fixed.

While the game is great from the perspective of someone new to the warhammer series. There was a whole lot to learn, but now that ive sat down and played a bunch of them here are my thoughts. 

For the ticket price of playing factions that interest me, along with the base game, and access to other factions on top of it.... it seemed like i was jumping through a lot of hoops to access content that should be just baseline a part of the game, like i was getting milked for old content. Furthermore, half the time these factions that were a part of my line of interest were so outdated or untouched for apparently years at this point that their gameplay loop just felt unrewarding or unrefined.

Furthermore when i looked into how communicative or up to date creative assembly has been in regards to keeping the player base informed on Warhammer, the game seems largely a side hustle, that they develop for at their leisure and dont really seem to care about the issues or opinions their player base brings to light with any semblance of quick resolution.

Things that are pretty baseline, games that we dont expect to get more content for (Elden Ring for example) gets CONSTANT bug and balance patches, updates to the player base and more. Riot games, while having its own issues, CONSTANTLY is fixing bugs and doesnt paywall functionality, but aesthetics instead and they are among the most communicative companies i have ever seen. There is a pattern here. Companies that do extremely well, communicate with their player base, put in the effort to fix their games and dont overextend their roster beyond their means. Every company that does the latter is backstabbing the faithful in their player base, usually at an agonizing pace for those who love a series, for the sake of cash grabs. And while I understand that three kingdoms is a better seller > warhammer... that theyve had good success with alien isolation and other titles. It feels like the fans that made this company successful over my lifetime have been forgotten.

In the current state of the game, I can recommend it to new players of total war or the warhammer series in general. To get your feet wet and fall in love with a goofy fantasy series with expensive asf little models. But for people who are long time fans, you'll get your fix, but then be left in the dust with little to no communication on what is being fixed or worked on. Left frustrated that the game you love is in a constant state of disrepair, on the cusp of being something truly great, never really quite getting there.

A Masterpiece Held Back by Monetization Greed

Core Game: A Beautifully Deep Experience
Let me be absolutely clear: the core game—Total War: Warhammer 3—is a phenomenal achievement. It is beautiful, deeply immersive, and offers a vast, unparalleled amount of gameplay. The variety between factions and the depth of mechanics are top-tier, cementing it as one of the best grand strategy titles available.

However, after hundreds of hours spent across all three titles in the series, I have to give this a negative review because the overwhelming feeling is that the studio's priorities are fundamentally centered on aggressive monetization, not the consumer experience. The true potential of this game is constantly being choked by exploitative business practices.

The Problem of "Immortal Empires" and DLC Access
I own all three core games (WH1, WH2, and WH3) and have been with this franchise from the beginning. It is utterly ridiculous that, even now, owning the flagship title does not grant "full" access to content from the first two games in the grand "Immortal Empires" campaign unless you also purchase their individual, often years-old, DLC.

The release strategy for the Immortal Empires map was particularly egregious. This map—the true promised endgame of the trilogy—was initially locked behind owning all three base games, a clear attempt to force triple-sales. It was only after immense, sustained community pressure and backlash that the studio finally relented and made it available to everyone. This entire sequence confirmed the community's worst fears: profit was prioritized over player goodwill and delivering the full experience.

Pricing and Obscurity
This is not a cheap game. While the base game may eventually see a decent sale, the DLC prices are astronomical and rarely budge, even for content that is approaching a decade old. This creates a massive, expensive barrier to entry for any new player wanting the "complete" experience.

Furthermore, the game is heavily reliant on external sources for basic competency:

Hidden Mechanics: Critical systems, like the intricacies of difficulty scaling, how diplomacy genuinely evolves, and the specific meaning of unit stats, are often obscured.

Required External Learning: To truly master and enjoy the game, you are practically required to spend hours on wikis, forums, or watching content creators who have done the community's job by digging out and explaining crucial, un-documented information.

Ultimately, the community and dedicated modders are the ones constantly pushing this game forward and fixing its systemic issues. I love the product the developers created, but I am profoundly disappointed in how the business is run. I sincerely hope the studio learns to trust its developers, let them create magic, and adopt consumer-friendly practices that reflect the quality of the game itself.

🐉 My 4000+ Hour Review of Total War: Warhammer III ⚔️
1. Why 4000+ Hours?

Because this game is an absolute masterpiece.
It’s easily my favorite game of all time — especially the campaigns, which are simply phenomenal.

If you’re playing offline (like I mostly do — 99% campaigns), I highly recommend going Legendary campaign difficulty with Very Hard battle difficulty for the best, most challenging experience.

After a long day of work, gym, and family, few things beat sitting down and commanding armies across the Old World. This game has become more than entertainment — it’s a hobby, a ritual, and my ultimate way to relax.

2. Balance ⚖️

The balance is solid overall. You won’t find many glaring exploits, though some factions are undeniably overpowered.
Usually, once you stabilize around turn 20, you’ll start snowballing fast. After turn 60, you’re basically unstoppable — at that point, your economy decides how many elite armies you can field.

3. Factions 👑

I enjoy most factions, but my personal rankings are clear:

🐊 Lizardmen — My absolute favorite.
I’ve spent over 2,100 hours commanding the ancient children of the Old Ones, and I still love every minute. Their armies, their magic, their dinosaurs — perfection.

💀 Tomb Kings — A close second.
I’ve logged around 700 hours with them, and I love their unique economy and immortal flavor.

I’m not a fan of horde factions or the Skaven.
Horde campaigns get boring after turn 40+, and Skaven suffer from terrible autoresolve and weak early- to mid-game units.

4. The Cons 🏰

Let’s be real — sieges need serious improvement.
Compare them to Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord sieges, and there’s no contest. Bannerlord’s siege battles feel alive, while Warhammer’s feel static and repetitive.

Also, to truly enjoy Warhammer III, you’ll want all the DLCs. It’s expensive, yes, but worth every cent in my opinion.

5. Mods 🧩

Mods make this already great game legendary. The modding community is fantastic, and I can’t recommend these enough:

Unlock All Skills – Self-explanatory; lets you unlock full potential (can get broken for Kislev and Nurgle heroes).

Double Skill Dump – Lords get 2 skill points per level (and so do AI lords). A level 50 Skarbrand becomes terrifying.

Expanded Lord Skill Trees – Works perfectly with the first two mods. Every faction benefits.

Expanded Research Tree – Keeps late-game turns (100+) interesting and rewarding.

Recruit Defeated Legendary Lords – Lets you add fallen legendary lords, from your own faction only,  to your pool, like a pseudo-confederation. Massive quality-of-life improvement.

6. Final Thoughts 💬

After 4000+ hours, Total War: Warhammer III still feels fresh and exciting. Every campaign tells a new story, every faction feels unique, and every victory feels earned.

Creative Assembly — you’re awesome. Please keep the DLCs coming (and faster)!

I’m not angry because of the bugs. I’m angry because the community — not the developers — are the ones truly keeping this game alive.
Modders have built entire new maps, added factions, units, and mechanics that genuinely expand and improve the experience. They’ve done what a massive, well-funded studio should have done years ago.

Meanwhile, the official product remains a cluttered, buggy mess. The AI is still brain-dead, pathfinding is broken, sieges are miserable, and every patch seems to fix one thing while breaking two others.

This is a company that’s taken hundreds of dollars from me through DLCs and expansions, yet somehow delivers less passion and less innovation each year. We could have had new campaigns, fresh scenarios, deeper faction reworks, and meaningful improvements to diplomacy and battle AI. Instead, we’re stuck replaying the same small, cramped map for the hundredth time.

What frustrates me most is not incompetence — it’s apathy. There’s no sense of creative drive anymore, no love for the world they built. Just endless monetization, unfinished updates, and corporate decision-making.

This game had so much potential, but that potential is being squandered.
I no longer feel like supporting this developer — not because I hate the game, but because I once loved it too much to watch it turn into this.

I'm not recommending this game to anyone and would even disincentivize everyone who ever asks me if it's worth it. It's not - in the current state.

I don't even play it with friends anymore... or solo because of all of the frustrating things about the game(which keep stacking). Each patch I get more and more exasperated with what I see. What's the point of releasing DLC's when the base game doesn't work properly(and they break it even more). For example, a recent patch is 6.3 and some of the things are:

20 new Unusual locations
Camera Blood Splatter

Some people probably don't agree but I don't want new fancy mechanics, nor to see blood splatter or whatever, I don't want new items or whatnot, just make the game playable - isn't that what the patch is for - to fix the game?? And why is it not playable - because of game-breaking bugs that are still yet to be fixed despite the game being more than 3 years old now? Who cares if you even see blood when you and your enemy fight - that's my least concern(it's not even a concern - it's just irrelevant to me) when I'm trying to play a game that requires even the slightest bit of attention.

A few examples, for some of my experience:

- I build mostly balanced armies with lots of archers and some front line. So why do my archers refuse to fire most of the time? Basic high elf archers should fire at least three volleys by the time a normal infantry unit reaches my line. Well, that's not the behavior I'm seeing -  15 or 20 entities fire and then they stop altogether. If more than half the entities decide to shoot from my whole unit - let me tell you, it would be a miracle. And sometimes they just stand there menacingly - 2-3 shots from lonely entities of a WHOLE UNIT. What's the point of hiring archers when they cannot do what they're supposed to do?

- Settlement battles - Mostly noticed this for high and dark elves battles - Why can archers hit me through the wall? They're shooting my units as they break down the gate through a SOLID WALL?! My units die when the enemy archers have absolutely no visibility on them trying to smash the gate. I cannot do this dark magic unlike the AI which displays skills to ignore basic mechanics and physics. 

- Why can the AI open the gate and keep my units stuck there until I break it down while they can shoot me through it - I mean the simple logic that their arrows go through should mean that my men can go through too, isn't it? But no, I have to actually smash the gate so I can enter.

- Again for settlement battles - When you tell your soldiers to enter the settlement, they enter through the wall if there is even ONE LADDER on the wall - hundreds of units will climb up that one ladder, REGARDLESS of whether you have captured or broken through the gate. Related to this - sometimes you position your unit or give them another command and instead of doing that, they try to fit half or all entities in one place - IN ONE PIXEL instead, looking absolutely ridiculous, with the rest of the unit displaying mind-boggling skills to not be able to find their place in the world... 

- Lizardmen issue - yeah, the community made that one heard. I've noticed it too in my most recent campaign, for example - Tehenuin is just roaming the lands aimlessly as if he's looking for a reason to exist - ignoring enemies, allies, even ignoring his own settlements. Sometimes he would return to his capital city like a lost kitty who finally found their way home.

Most of these bugs are game-breaking because, for example, in a battle you are actually able to win turns to a defeat because your archers wouldn't shoot or won't do as you tell them. Or because they shot your heroes and lords through the wall even though that's not how it's supposed to work. I mean, most battles are moderately hard and require you to micro a lot of units, which you cannot do effectively because your soldiers are acting like they have something against you.

Don't even get me started on the fact that your soldiers need you to repeat the same command over and over as if they're retarded and when cavalry or other enormous units cannot push out of the way even the most inebriated peasant that is shorter than a dwarf and get stuck on anything - another example: chariots getting stuck on their own fallen entity of the unit :)

Isn't mass supposed to be a thing? In warhammer 2, it wasn't a thing and my units didn't get stuck so much like they're in a certain type of video...

Yeah, that's a small portion of what I've noticed - If I've kept track of everything that is wrong with the game I'll probably be in a straitjacket by now just because of the amount of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ information.

CA and their subsidiaries give so much ♥♥♥♥ to creators that actually care about the game and give honest feedback - it's actually insane. I mean, you will most likely succeed in your ultimate goal to fill your pockets if you actually maintained the game and listened to the community. So you expect to do the minimal amount of work and when people are dissatisfied with your obvious lazy and greedy behavior, you suddenly scream to the heavens that you're being treated unfair or try to glaze it over? What kind of bipolar stuff is this?

I would assume the developers - the people who actually coded it are skilled enough so they could untangle the 'spaghetti' code little by little and it starts to look properly like a game, if given the chance. Speaking to you, management team - give them the chance. I'm sure you have more than enough funds to tackle it properly instead of glossing over it. Who knows - maybe it's such a mess that nothing could ever fix it but again - if something can be created, then it should be able to be unraveled as well, at least logically speaking.

I am writing a review with the primary intent of making plain my displeasure with the management at Creative Assembly, and how they have repeatedly failed to learn their lesson. They apologize for anti-consumer practices and try to make nice for awhile, only to do it again in a year or so. Enough.

I would have been more forgiving if they had quite simply been honest and said something to the effect of "Hey, sorry, we are just doing our fiduciary duty and leveraging the considerable advantages TW:W affords us as best we can. We over-leveraged and we'll back off and put in guardrails to make sure it will be way harder to create a situation where our developers are . . . [i]incentivized[/i] to do things that players are going to have good cause to take umbrage with e.g. de-prioritizing the remedy of widely known and reported bugs for months which are a significant, quantifiable detriment to the quality of our product." That might have mollified me somewhat, if only for the transparency. Now, I am afraid it is going to take rather more to win back my business. In fact, I am sufficiently incensed to actually put forth time to evangelize to other members of the community and articulate precisely why there is collective upset and for good reason.

Here is my bottom line: Total War: Warhammer, in all its incarnations, is a fantastic product [i]at its best.[/i] But, it is also an extremely attractive one from a business model perspective--it has one hell of a moat and no likely competition for its share of the market. It is populated by committed hobbyists and enthusiasts willing to spend large chunks of disposable income on DLC for a single game, year in and year out. Various pressures have caused CA to be less than concerned with quality assurance and good faith efforts at trying to ensure it remains anywhere near [i]at its best[/i] so long as the aforementioned advantage it holds guarantees that the money continues to flow regardless. 

I wish to remind CA: they are not Microsoft. We do not need them nearly as much as they need us, and CA's management is not "leaving money on the table" if they fail to ram lucrative, if unpopular, decisions down our throat. They are, at best, taking out a loan, with interest, borrowed against their own brand image and trust factor. Whoever pushed for conduct like this to happen should not be rewarded, they should be held responsible for the backlash.

I will reverse this review to positive, but only when real consequences are imposed upon the responsible party or parties within the company. Platitudes and token gestures will not be sufficient.

There have always been problems with the Total War games, it comes with the scale of the game. But things have changed. Corporate greed has taken hold and infested these great games. They used to be lovingly crafted, and actually patched after they shipped (and the old games had to actually work before they shipped, back when they were on physical copies). I have been playing since Rome: Total War, buying and supporting these games for decades. Seeing them slowly slide into an oblivion of bugs, errors, and slop has been extremely depressing.

It has gotten to the point where I just can't leave a positive review here. I have left negative reviews on DLC I thought was bad, but never a main game before. This may be an example of me putting yet another company on my boycott list like EA, Blizzard, Paradox, and so many more now.

The reason? I literally cannot play this game anymore. I don't mean that in some figurative sense, I mean that literally. I will start up the game and play for a bit, then a will click on the button to bring me to a settlement that needs to be upgraded. My screen will start to move, and then the game will crash. Alright, well I will just move manually to the places that need to be upgraded; then I get into a battle on the other side of my territory when the AI attacks me, or someone from half the world away starts diplomacy talks with me. Crash to desktop. I have posted on the Steam forums, on their own forums, I have contacted their support teams, nothing. I have installed mods that remove camera zoom, as well as a myriad of other suggestions from other players (zero response from anyone at CA). Nothing works.

Then I learn about the fact that several major and minor factions have had their AI completely and utterly broken for months with no fix. I have only been playing the main campaign version of this game at the moment, that does not have Lizardmen or Tombkings, so I didn't notice. So, if they are willing to let that MASSIVE issue affecting ALL players go on this long, will they be fixing my issue any time soon? Yeah right.

I cannot recommend that anyone reading this purchase the game. Maybe you won't have my issue, perhaps they will even fix their AI problems; but it will only be after having a massive community backlash come down on their heads. What does that say about their directives and goals as a company? They are not interested in making an affordable game that WORKS for the people who are PAYING them. I am sure that the game developers working there hate this state of affairs as much as we do. Pumping out more overpriced DLC while the main game suffers to pad the wallets of their corporate lords and make the numbers go up for the shareholders. It is a sad state of affairs.

Until these issues are resolved, I will not be buying another Total War game. If these bugs are never fixed, that is fine with me. There are plenty of other great games from awesome developers and companies on this platform for me to support.

Total War was one of the major reasons I decided to get back into PC gaming, I remember how hooked I was playing Rome I and Medieval II back in the day. Sadly, those were the days when CA peaked, I don't know what happened to CA, but the magic is gone. 
Gameplay is essentially the same copy/pasted formula since the days of Rome 1, but only... a lot worse? They added a whole bunch of complicated rulesets to the campaign designed to make the campaigns feel more dynamic based on the faction, which I admit is not all that bad sans all the glitches and cheating braindead AI, but where it really drops the ball are the battles, which is the real meat and potatoes of the series and its main selling point,- they've noticeably regressed since 20 years ago. Essentially it's the same rock/paper/scissors formula from 20 years ago, but with magic and monsters (which are basically re-dressed catapults and elephants from the days of Rome I), A LOT crappier (and less dynamic) AI, less options for your units- say goodbye to tactical formations like testudo formation for legionaries, wedge formation for cavalry, or phalanx formations for the Greeks, or Cantabrian circle for horse archers. You'd think they would add more of stuff like this and more that helps units and armies stand out from eachother (esp in such a rich setting like Warhammer) but NO. Units are just spreadsheets now more than ever, a bunch of messy squares and rectangles that feel both more rigid and more clumsy than in past TW iterations. It's mind boggling. Warhammer has SO much potential to give armies and units unique tactical advantages other than being a rock/paper/scissors spreadsheet but thats exactly what battles have become. Battles feel more glitch ridden than ever, whole units being held back from retreating thanks to 1 little soldier getting stuck on geometry which results in your whole unit getting massacred because they can't decide between moving or fighting (they can't do both), or watching the enemy army act completely suicidal in situations they can't win but they can't do anything else, like the entire enemy forces run up a hill into incoming fire. Often battles can be reduced to taking advantage of exploits and stupid AI behavior and exploiting pathfinding glitches. Every battle pretty much amounts to the same exact thing. Infantry hold the line, protecting your ranged units while your cavalry/special units flank. I've just described every battle. Monsters are magic elephants from Rome 1 and you have to keep them away from spears and that's about it. Half the time units are more busy tripping over themselves than fighting.
Siege battles are also a complete chore now, a unique exercise in UN-FUN, featuring the mindbogglingly bad AI path finding combined with glitches galore. Have fun getting your units unstuck all over the damn city and walls while your army gets massacred, I mean there's so many things wrong with the sieges alone that its more like a case of where do I begin, most people just auto resolve them because of how much of a punishment they feel like to play. 
This game is corporate greed personified, its incredible how much they sucked the soul out of this once great series. Modern TW feels like it's just parasitizing off the corpse of a once great series that showed true promise with plenty of innovation. Its almost like the original team is gone, because I can't imagine the brilliant people who made the original games could produce such slop.

I have fewer than 60 hours in this title - that'd be a lot for some games, but for a Total War game it's nothing. It should be a dream come true for me to have the entire Warhammer setting in a single Total War game. I should have hundreds or thousands of hours at this point, but I don't because I've been waiting for CA to get the game into an acceptable state. It's been an incredibly bumpy three and a half years and we are still not there.

They (allegedly, and very reluctantly at that) fixed the recent issues with Lizardmen and Tomb King AI with a hotfix today (and who knows what else they broke in the process), but this presents a problem because the community has a nasty habit of immediately forgiving CA the moment they make even the slightest move toward fixing anything. Then, when they break twenty other things for every bug they fix in the next update, everybody ignores it and showers them with cult-like worship because they totally fixed That One Thing, you guys! Nevermind that it took 8 months. The outrage has to build, sometimes for years, before the community holds CA accountable again. I've seen this happen with every single patch. Enough is enough.

The devs may or may not be incompetent, but the management certainly is, and this won't change until it's abundantly clear to them that we aren't a bunch of stupid walking wallets and they can't get away with lackadaisically frittering away this game's potential any longer. I'd be afraid of a Three Kingdoms situation if we all vote with our wallets, but let's be real, this is the only game that's still making them money at this point. They can't afford to kill it, and I for one see no reason to buy any of CA's future products if they'd even leave their golden goose to rot.

And speaking of a golden goose, rumor has it that they're probably planning on an unannounced 40k game taking Fantasy's place. That doesn't even make sense to me. What would the unit and stack sizes be? How are formations handled? What about cover? Flyers? Will I have to look at Primaris marines? Total War and 40k are antithetical and if you try to cram 40k into this decrepit engine it's going to creak at the very least, if it doesn't immediately crack or shatter. I would wager that Todd Howard himself would be left in slack-jawed awe of how much of a mess it would make. I would be thrilled to be wrong... but I won't be.

The game itself is fun. There are a variety of factions with unique play styles, unit compositions, magic and strategic goals. Especially DLC factions often have fun or at the very least very strong (sometimes sadly completely overpowered) mechanics, like collecting ingredients to create "food" to globally buff certain units.
A problem is that there are a LOT of DLCs at this point, which can be bought on sale. But a lot of factions (Karl Franz, Grimgor, Ungrim, to name a few) require Warhammer I or Warhammer II, which quickly becomes pretty pricey.
No other game I've played quite feels like this game, but sadly it is being ruined by the management of the developers. They only see their bottom line, and while I understand that a company wanting profit is nothing surprising or in and of itself morally reprehensible, but the *way* they persue the bag is horrible for this game. The recent outrage about 2 races being absolute braindead on the map (that being *11* major factions, plus a bunch of minor NPC only factions) is just the result of the latest of many scummy moves of the management, that being the decision to keep the bug in the game (they knew about it and made it worse with a "hotfix") and only roll out a fix with the upcoming DLC/influx of cash instead of prioritizing it. For years there have been TONS of bugs, for example with settlement battles: broken pathfinding and broken AI make for very tedious battles, ranged units just wanting to rush into melee instead of shooting at a target, or (groups of) large units being incapable of damaging single small units, instead just pushing them around for all eternity. Mind you, these are just a few.
They already attempted to repair their rapport with the players after their horrendous launch of the "Shadows of Change" (*cough* shortchange *cough*) and for a while it worked: the DLC after that, Thrones of Decay, was AMAZING, and it was followed by 2 major *free* mechanical additions for the Dwarfs. But once again, after the playerbase calmed down somewhat, the suits come crawling out of the woodworks, trying to milk it for all it's worth.
Again, I really really *really* like playing this game and the actual game devs are clearly very passionate about it.
But in a tale as old as time, it gets ruined by greedy higher-ups.

Lots of bugs and broken stuff that get only fixed when players pressure the company.

Game itself is also full of bad game design choices that leads to a repetitive, unintuitive, unfun gameplay experience that punishes the player for engaging with it.

Examples are:
-Inverted difficulty curve where all campaigns stop providing a challenge past the early turns.
-AI recruiting armies filled by one or two unit types that leads to extremely boring battles.
-A good chunk of all factions' rosters are made of irrelevant units you will never recruit and you are incentivized to just spam 2-3 good units or just doomstack. Once you do, all battles play out the same, quickly turning into repetitive timesinks.
-Tactics don't really matter. 
-Diplomacy as a game mechanic barely worked in previous two games. It is still a crapshoot in the third.
-Siege battles are a misery. As attackers, players have to deal with multiple towers with rapidfiring missile attacks that can decimate most units in the blink of an eye. As defenders, players will rarely get to fight a settlement battle that is winnable without cheese or AI-abuse as AI only attacks a settlement when there isn't an army nearby.
-No, you can't bolster a garrison with extra units, that mechanic was cut out of Total War ages ago. Yes, AI will ignore your armies and run straight at your undefended settlements.
-You can easily abuse the autoresolve system to win battles which takes far less effort than actually playing them. 
-Increasing game difficulty gives enemy units stat buffs, which you can turn off.
-If you are a warhammer fan, hope your favourite race is not Beastmen or Bretonia. 

Overall, Total War Warhammer is a game with lots of spectacle and very little substance. Even if all the bugs and broken stuff were to be fixed, the core gameplay will still be repetitive and boring due game design choices that no amount of modding or patches can fix. 

It is incredibly obvious CA doesn't care about providing a fun gameplay experience, but rather they want to exploit a passionate fanbase by selling DLC.

It is also the only modern Warhammer Fantasy Game where you get to command armies... Even if said armies is made up of 19 steam tanks or 19 dinosaurs or whatever.

I heavily suggest trying this game out yourself first before buying it. And if you decide to buy, wait for a sale.

Listened to feedback from community. Not everyone may agree with me leaving a positive review this early, but it's important to give some credit when they listen. I think it's a very good game that I find has a surprising level of depth. I almost exclusively play Kislev and even 250 hours in I'm still finding new ways to play the faction. My only real complaint (outside the obvious ones) is that some factions become almost impossible to play after so many updates. The main outrage was about lizardmen (who I think should have their DLCs consolidated) and Tomb Kings, who were literally broken but factions like Boris Ursus are basically impossible to play as intended because of changes that make their start unplayable.

 As it is right now, staying in the Chaos Wastes as Boris Ursus is literally impossible. The game is basically a disaster campaign from day one if you play as intended (On Legendary). With the addition of Arbaal and Tamurkhan, you will be dogpiled by AI Chaos factions, in my campaign ending with Archaon, Tamurkhan, Throgg, Throt, Arbaal, Tamurkhan, The Demon Prince and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Astroturf Nine-Iron collectively deciding that there was no such thing as overkill and sending 10 armies to take my final tier 3 minor settlement. Like, at this point I seriously doubt even LOTW can survive the current starting conditions there. The only way to live it is leave, abandon your starting settlement, and colonize Frozen Landing. There is no other way. Even then it's still a hellish start, but at the very least if you move quickly you can play a little Total Diplomacy and bribe Astrogolf to declare war on Arbaal and buy some time to possibly kill the rats before you get Deep-Throtted in the midgame. 

There needs to be substantial changes to the start and his faction to actually make it playable. From my experience, the best best changes would be:
A. Give him the option to leave and move to a more survivable location
B. Extend his attrition immunity to all armies
C. Give him initial ownership of the Tower of Torment and make it Level 2 with a starting fortification
    - Having a fortified location held by a second army makes the start alot easier to survive, + having an extra turn or 2 to consolidate holdings in the North to prepare for Archaon and the Demon Prince - and eventually Arbaal and Tamurkhan - will help ALOT with survivability.
D.  Give a recruitment time reduction for Tsar Guard and War Bears exclusive to Boris.
    - You basically never get enough time to actually recruit the units Boris does well with, mainly because he's the only Lord with an army that actually replenishes and doesn't slowly bleed away for existing outside a settlement. Maybe that'll be helped by allowing other armies to take over for him while he's recruiting, but it's probably not enough to handle the sheer quantity of high tier BS that Chaos factions can throw at you if you give them a moment to breathe. This'll allow you to actually use decent units in Boris's army on a turn that's before 60.
E. Either make Chaotic Wasteland suitable for Boris, or a way to negate the debuffs that can be available in the early-mid game. 
   - Even if you somehow manage to survive the early game, your economy will be crippled but the fact Chaotic wasteland is unsuitable climate and therefore difficult to develop. I was lying when I said the start was impossible, it is possible(but only because Boris doesn't require a settlement to survive). If you manage to defeat the menagerie of foes in the early game, be prepared to be completely rolled over in the mid-game because your only major settlement is in Chaotic wasteland and takes 8 turns to go up to tier 4 where you can actually unlock decent units - if it isn't taken and razed in the time if takes to build (which it will be). Before 6.1 there was an edit that allowed you to completely nullify the climate effects in exchange for losing devotion, but with the changes to devotion that came with that update they added an edict that gives +10 devotion and -10 corruption exchange for a -33% debuff to income. They also made it so that if you get 100 devotion you will no longer suffer climate debuffs. This problem is that this only offsets the -8 to devotion you get for playing legendary, you still have to undertake extensive efforts to actually get to 100 devotion. Even then all that needs to happen is the AI to raid your territory(WHICH THEY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WILL, EVEN IF NOT AT WAR WITH YOU), or God forbid take a settlement in which case enjoy taking 20 turns to rebuild it to the point where it can actually give you 100 devotion even with the -33% ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ income penalty.

So, I have between all three games about 2,100 hours. So I certainly feel qualified to make this review, and I hope that some people actually read this and actually take the time to understand it.

Total War: Warhammer 3, a fantastic game. Is it bugged? Yes, it's ABSOLUTELY massive, what do you expect? We're at like 100 Legendary Lords, calm down. CA is doing their best between budget cuts, and Sega getting the noose ready for them. I am sure GW is also applying pressure now due to the old world. They are much smaller than when Warhammer 3 started, and therefor you can't yell and scream at them for every single issue, when they are actively working on things.

Furthermore, they fixed the issue the community screamed about, and now we are complaining about old saves not working? On a new update? That reverts several coding lines? What did you expect, honestly I am a huge TW:W3 fan, but I am growing to dislike the wider community. This game is fantastic, does it have flaws? Yes, is it fun? YES.

To address the issue in regards to cost of entry, the series came out almost 10 years ago? 2016 for the first one. I am not saying that spending so much money on DLC's is great for everyone, but I have been on board since the release of the first game, and you can't honestly expect the developers to give all of their content for free. If it's not your thing, then I get that, and that's fair. But don't review bomb a nearly decade old game for being expensive, when there is almost a decades amount of content.

Overall, I personally rate this game a solid 10/10, I have invested 1,020 hours or so into the third game alone. I think that is more than justified, as I have spent so much time in these games. So, CA, keep up working on content, keep communicating, and don't let so many lack luster reviews fully ruin your efforts. At least some of us still support you.

I really would love to give a positive review, but I cannot. Although many lovely improvements have been made compared to TWW2, the game overly is corrupt, due to extreme issues with balancement. So the review does NOT include any personal opinions regarding pricing, being humbly based on (huge) game play errors. 

To mention at least one (smaller) improvements ahead, e.g.: 
- handling of campaign movement positions. In TWW2 is was extremely nasty to navigate in landscapes with attrition, because although the remaining movement barometer said >50% to change into camping mode, it often did not work (same for raiding, etc.). In TWW3 you just change into camping mode and use the remaining movement points staying in camping mode. 
- more equal starting positions, that allow, especially on higher difficulty modes to get started (because in TWW2 for some few races/legendary lords, it was almost impossible to get started in legendary mode)
-> there are surely many other such small improvements which I love and I am sure they have been described in detail elsewhere

However I would like to focus on the main point: The corrupt balancing. Please note, I only play in legendary mode as an experienced player, but I assume the comments are in general true also for other difficulty modes. 

- Main campaign: Besides being boring (which is more my subjective opinion of course), none of the other races besides the player race tried to free/capture a single soul -> how can this be possible; if thats an error, why hasnt this been discovered (most probably it has), but not been fixed before? 
- Balancing between races: Come on guys, races like Kislev, Dwarves get so many +faction wide reductions to recruitment/upkeek/building costs, you end up by having endless money, 1 billion + on the bank account, up to several 100k income each day, ridiculous (especially the dwarves, having access to underground buildings adding so many faction wide bonuses ...) -> compared to this, TWW2 was just perfectly balanced, even if there were always races like the dwarves that seemed a bit OP (especially also due to huge advantages in automatically resolved battles)
- Late game goal in the grand campaign "Special end game goal" (spoiler alarm): honestly, 4 stacks of a particular race that was chosen showing up at each starting position for that race, this is the end game challenge? Even for the first time, when you have your legendary lord around, he cleans them up in 1-2 moves - again, ridiculous
- and last but not least, stupid AI, especially in battles, most prominent when defending cities: just fight the battles yourself; in almost each city there is always a starting location where units can be displayed outside of range of any towers (never built any assaulting towers, you just dont need the stuff). the enemy units are dispersed over the whole city, while you cluster your army in only one particular spot cleaning most of the time only a small percentage of the enemy units, occupying the settlement with only a few if no losses at all. "No, why should we move to the position where the player is attacking, and help our dear fellows, its better to watch them die first, before its our turn" ... and many more examples, but this one makes almost each city fight a peace of cake
- many smaller issues that should just not occur in such a game / for this kind of large developer or should have been fixed a long time ago: e.g.,
-- recruitment of heroes always shows at first 2/4 (regardless of race or campaign), which is in general never the correct amount of heroes you have / can still recruit; changes only after you pick particular heroes  
-- Grombrimdal (legendary dwarf hero) has only 38 skill points on level 50 ... no comment 
-- additional pirate legendary lords are all displayed as having ranged weapons, while the have not (no ammunition)
-- many, many more of such small errors, that slipped through, but shouldnt 

Much more could be mentioned, but has most probably be done elsewhere. I think, for a fully fledged game, that was released a long time ago, this should have been resolved or actually, much better, not be a problem from the beginning. One really could get the feeling, that the developers favored quantity (potentially for selling purposes, DLC?) over quality. Yes, the game looks spectacular and many nice things have been implemented, but this cannot outwheigh those many basic errors. 

Hey, if you are a fan, buy and play, as I have surely enjoyed several hours, but sometimes I think more for craving for the general addictive elements the game has, rather than a perfect game.

Creative Assembly is treading water at the moment which is unfortunate. The Total War games are my favourite, and I have sunken hundreds of hours into this and many other titles from Creative Assembly. That being said the inornate amount of DLC you have to purchase just to have the base game experience for some factions is egregious, I have steadily built up my collection over the months through sales and still do not have access to everything. You can have fun without the DLC but it is frustrating constantly being reminded of things left locked by massive DLC banners on the campaign start menu. The game itself is not as smooth as former iterations of the series especially in the late game. While it is fun to have so many options there is a trade off in that the map does seem overpopulated not to mention some factions simply become behemoths by the late game that make the game less fun after about 100 turns.

Warhammer 3 offers the best UI, most detailed map, and beautiful visuals in the series though. At the same time I find the battles to be less visually smooth as compared to Warhammer 2 or 1, army movement and battle animations seem more filled with stuttering. Total War: Warhammer 3 stands out among strategy games for its characters, the depth it brings. It also has a beautiful board, which is what these games basically are, and what you will be looking at mostly. 

Unlike many titles where leaders feel generic and interchangeable, here each character is shaped by their history on the board (the tree guy had the crown I was looking for, the heck?). This adds a layer of immersion that’s often missing elsewhere.

I ended up making friends of enemies, where I felt it was easier to take a city – return it – for a peace agreement and trade deal. Mongolian style, but I was vampires who control the undead. 

Combat is engaging, especially when you choose to manually direct your armies. The game rewards creative tactics, whether you’re launching a surprise attack or reviving fallen troops for another round. 
Each session is immersive, and the battles feel consequential. 
However, I don’t appreciate how big the garrison armies are – I feel I cant manually fight these.

There’s a sense of unpredictability and challenge, especially when outnumbered or outmaneuvered. Playing defensively, setting traps, and negotiating truces become part of a larger strategy— (yes I see the dash, I don’t get paid to do this) not just necessities, but meaningful choices. The game never feels like it’s on rails, and each campaign offers new ways to test your skills.

Also you begin to see why other factions are important, are the dwarves from those mountains protecting me from the orc horde? (loses first battle against orcs) Maybe I should be helping them instead.

WH3 Campaign and more factions and add slight frustration from maps.

Let me preface this by saying that, bugs and issues aside, Warhammer 3 is fundamentally an enjoyable, good game.

Sadly, it's also subject to Creative Assembly's management side and frequent mistakes made regarding DLC and bug-fixing (Note, management. The developers, quite likely, have little to no influence/say in the matter). The whole debacle regarding Tides of Torment is just another in a cycle of their apology tour, making similar mistakes and then apologising once again to regain goodwill then doing the same thing later.

Until the management at Creative Assembly that's responsible for these mistakes answers for their constant abuse of people's patience and leniency, this negative review stands.

I've played a good deal of CIV and went into this expecting it to operate pretty much exactly the same way. I feel that CIV works really well for people who love to micro-manage and have the tolerance for a long, long game where there are several win conditions; in many ways, CIV is much more tedious. 
There was a bit of a learning curve, but it was absolutely worth it. I'm coming into this apparently missing the golden age of Warhammer, but I really have no actual complaints. From what I understand, the devs are a little lazy and let the community come together to mod the game into what it "should be" and there are just almost-universally accepted mods that you need - super easy and streamlined to download though (and I absolutely loathe mods). It's kind of amazing how much I love this game, even just scratching the surface. What's even more amazing is that with every defeat and hardship, I feel inclined to play more and hunker down to learn how things could have been better. Other than the learning curve, my only real complaint is that there is an awful lot of dlc that feels pretty crucial to being competitive against other actual players. I don't feel like I'm having trouble playing against AI whatsoever, though.
Playing as Skaven has been a blast and a half and I look forward to dumping many, many more hours into this game.

I had previously left a review in disgust/anger after yet another disaster siege battle (due to pathing, bugs, etc.), but the truth is, flaws included this is the best game(s) I've ever played and it really isn't particularly close. 

The overall combination of campaign or strategic gameplay where you build up provinces and armies while conquering or diplomatically acquiring more territory, with the best looking and incredibly diverse RTS tactical gameplay you can find anywhere, is awe-inspiring. You will find economic and infrastructure  systems, army and building buffs that you add to over time, and thousands of related details spread across a massive campaign map that contains hundreds of factions dancing to their own tune whether you are near them or not.

I have played thousands of hours and can still start up a campaign and find something new while having a good time playing a different way, which along with the playable faction diversity, gives this series the best replayability of any game out there. The most recent addition, Tides of Torment, seems well executed and perhaps worth the wait refreshing factions in need and adding at least one novel campaign game play (Aislinn).

There are negatives: bugs and oddities that annoying pop up in random places throughout, a siege system that despite numerous dev efforts never seems to be right, imbalance between races allowing some to consistently outperform others and/or render late games more repetitive. These really all make sense for a game of this magnitude though, and while infuriating at times, they are not enough to make me honestly recommend this game any less.

But lately, that joy has been replaced by disappointment and frustration, not because the developers have lost their touch, but because of the management team’s poor direction.

Updates feel disconnected from what the player base actually wants, communication has grown colder, and feedback is brushed aside or dismissed.

But the management’s leadership is steering it off a cliff. Their priorities have created a rift between the team and the players, and the result is a community that feels betrayed.

It’s sad, honestly. This game had something special — and it still could — if only the management would listen, respect their veterans, and stop making decisions that alienate their most loyal fans.

Oyunu ilk başta uzun süre tek başıma oynadım, daha sonra arkadaşlarımla oynamak için tekrar satın aldım. Arkadaşlarla oynamak gerçekten çok keyifli birlikte savaşlara katılmak ya da birbirinize karşı savaşmak ayrı bir zevk.

I was nervous about the Creative Assembly making a fictional game. I became obsessed with the original Rome Total War when I was in 4th grade, and the game instilled me with a love of history I'm not sure I'd have had otherwise. A fictional setting initially sounded far less appealing than the history-inspired series I'd come to love.

What I had not considered was just how much creativity and diversity such a setting could have if done properly. They did such an amazing job of that "properly" would not begin to describe it. The game is absolutely captivating and it is shocking how easily long hours can slip away playing it. There are just so many things to do, things to try, that it was easy for me to spend dozens of hours a week for months on end trying just some of them. The game is beyond compelling and aside from some minor AI improvements I can think of nothing the game lacks or appears weak in. 

If I'd known just how great the game is years ago I'd have bought a gaming PC years sooner - this is not something to miss.

A solid 10/10 for me; I wish their were others like it. I'd seriously pay 300$ for this game was it my only option to get it, and I'm pretty cheap by most metrics.

J'ai rigolé en voyant les notes des journalistes/sites gaming sur la page du magasin. Le jeu était mauvais à la sortie et est toujours plutôt moyen. Pas à la hauteur de ses ambitions, Total War Warhammer 3 souffre d'un code spaghetti et d'une équipe de devs squelettique pour mettre à jour ET faire des DLC.

Résultat le jeu est blindé de bugs plus où moins impactants, certains évitables (mais dont le joueur peut profiter : genre reset le mouvement d'une armée à seigneur seul, forcer une factions qui te déteste à rompre tout ses traités d'alliance...) d'autres non. Un bug récent assez sévère à provoqué une grosse review bomb et les dévs ont été forcé de se sortir les doigts en prioritéface au joli DLC mais y'a encore plein de boulot. Au dela des bugs, il y'a un problème d'équilibrage de divers éléments du jeu et une IA mal écrite qui fait beaucoup de choses qui n'ont aucun sens.

Après 3 ans de développement, on voit que la priorité est de faire le moins possible tout en réussisant à vendre des DLC à 25 euros (n'importe quel  bon jeu à 15-25 euros est un meilleur investissement qu'un DLC de TWW3). Le studio à fait une grosse bourde en perdant beaucoup d'argent avec un jeu pas sorti (Hyenas) et ils essaient de nous faire payer pour ça.

Tout n'est pas à jeter, si vous adorez l'univers, le jeu est fidèle à celui çi et plein de bonnes intentions. Le jeu est plutôt joli aussi. Le problème c'est que la priorité est allé à plein d'élément superficiels plutôt que d'avoir des bases solides qui se remarquent plus tu passes de temps sur le jeu.

Je doute que Total War Warhammer règle la moitié de ses problèmes avant que le jeu ne soit plus mis à jour. Si je me trompe je ferai un EDIT.

进入游戏，推荐图像设置，进入测试场景，动画播放到火球砸军队，卡死，重启电脑，键盘/鼠标/外接硬盘丢失，重启或者关机可能会无限转圈，必须断电才能重启……好家伙，跟上次一模一样，我什么都没玩到算我42分钟游戏时长了。

Total War: Warhammer III had the potential to be the definitive fantasy strategy game, but it’s buried under bad priorities and questionable monetization.

First off, it’s absurd that in a war game... literally a game about mass battles, demons, and carnage, you have to pay extra for blood and gore. The “Blood for the Blood God” DLC is a joke at this point. This isn’t a cosmetic pack or a fun expansion...it’s basic atmosphere that should be part of the core experience. Charging players for something so fundamental feels greedy and out of touch.

Then there’s the state of the game itself. After years of patches and “reworks,” Warhammer III still suffers from technical issues, performance drops, broken AI, and inconsistent balancing. Meanwhile, Creative Assembly’s attention seems to be laser-focused on churning out more paid DLC rather than ensuring the base game runs smoothly or that factions feel balanced and complete.

It’s disappointing because underneath the problems is a genuinely great strategy game. The world, factions, and battles could be incredible but it’s hard to enjoy them when the experience feels like an endless stream of monetized add-ons and half-finished systems.

If you’re new to the series, I’d wait. The game feels more like a storefront for DLC than a polished strategy title. The Total War name used to mean something, but Warhammer III makes it clear the developers are more interested in selling expansions than delivering a solid core experience.
