My last review from quite a while ago was kinda impulsive and biased due to CA being extremely unpopular at the time. And while that may be a reason in and of itself for being a negative review and possibly not getting the game, I felt that I didn't represent the game that well.

The good things are plentiful, with a ridiculous amount of content, Better and more unique mechanics than 2 for the most part I feel, though there is a lot of power creep that might derail a multiplayer campaign. Settlement trading used to be a required mod in 2, but is now a core mechanic in game, thank god, and melee units are now more viable, though I feel I have to quote that, as I played on a lower difficulty as a new total war player during 2, and can't reliably compare.

Do not take the fact that the positive section is really short comparatively to mean that it's outweighed by the negative. It really isn't, there are fewer negatives, but I hate those negatives with more passion.

The negatives are still fairly numerous. Threre were two other major reasons for my former bad review other than CA's shenanigans, and they were terrible sieges, and AI ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. 

I had to look up whether the siege rework came out yet, because it didn't come out during the last review, and my siege battle are still crap and unfun. I just mod them out when I'm not playing multiplayer games, I think it's actually worse than 2's sieges. There is a skaven siege that I did playing as Grombrindal, and that map is so massive that my slow dwarfs need to run for several minutes to get to spread out capture points, and it was so terrible that I decided to just hold 2 points and kill the skaven till I win. That was one of the longest battles I have ever done, and not fun enough to make up for it. Capture points need to be closer, the defender needs less leadership buffs, defense structures need a heavy rework, and that might be enough to not be terrible.

Now the AI. Not nearly as bad as I said, but it still needs improvment. The example I gave was playing as chaos dwarfs, specifically the one closest to Imrik. Grimgor ignores the local chaos dwarfs way closer to him, walks past, activates his waaagh, and attacks me in the first 15 turns or so and takes my capital while I'm killing Imrik. Not only should that never have happened, as he really should have attacked the other faction first, but he didn't even discover my faction, he just marched over, declared war in one turn, and ended my campaign with a army I could not possibly beat unless my main army was sitting in my capital doing nothing. Any army I had raised to defend the settlement I could have not possibly been able to afford that early on while I need the manpower to erase my nearby enemies. I'm not Legend of total war.

And hell, that brings me to another issue. Marching across neutral teritory is the most annoying thing in this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. It's too hard to get military access, and one trip across another factions province drops your relations by way too much. Either drop the relation penalty by half. or let you get access at +5 with said faction, I don't want to have my prospective ally declare war on me for helping them kill skaven because they refuse to give me military access.

My advice, get the game and play it. It's good, REALLY good. Might be the only game you play for a year kind of good. But please just mod the game and remove or alter Sieges and get a AI rework or something.

Before the qualities (or lack thereof) of this videogame can even be discussed, it is important to bring up the cost. I am writing this on the evening of the 25th of November, 2025; in a little over a week, on the 4th of December, the next DLC "Tides of Torment" will be released. To access everything in this game, you need to buy [b]3 STILL RETAIL PRICE games[/b] (that are 9, 7, and 3 years old respectively), for a total of $179.97. Once the base games are accounted for, if you scroll up the page a bit, you will see they have conveniently consolidated all 3 games DLC on this store page (minus Blood for the Blood God I and II which you don't [i]need[/i] unless you want to go back and play the previous 2 games with blood effects), for a total of $319.22. This puts the total cost of Total War: Warhammer III at [u]$499.19[/u], before any online sales taxes, and not accounting for the previous two blood packs.

When Tides of Torment releases on the 4th of December, Warhammer III will breach the $500 threshold, coming in at [u]$526.16[/u]. It should be common sense that [b]NO[/b] videogame that has ever been released, or ever will be released, is worth $500. There may be other grand strategy game players, simulator game players, and gacha game players that would argue that this is okay because some of their games can end up more expensive than this one. To them I would say, it is wrong when developers/publishers do it to you and your communities, and it is wrong when they do it to Total War players as well. Additionally, actual tabletop wargamers that play these Games Workshop produced miniature games (Warhammer Fantasy Battles, Warhammer the Old World, Warhammer Age of Sigmar, and Warhammer 40,000) will frequently claim that this game is a "value pack" considering the amount of factions contained within that $500, compared to the cost of a singular army of actual tabletop miniatures and materials to assemble/paint them. To them I would say, GW has led you around by the nose for [b]42 YEARS[/b] now, and your perspectives of both time and value are completely irreparably damaged.

[h1]Now with that out of the way, how is the game?[/h1]

[b]It's bad.[/b]

More specifically, it might very well be the greatest Warhammer: Fantasy Battles videogame ever released (low bar). However as a [b]Total War[/b] game, it is marinated in the bile of Total War: Rome II, and suffers many similar problems due to that. I will list off several things that come to mind, however there are more valid complaints than can be typed in a reasonable amount of time.

[h3]Terrible AI[/h3]
This is primarily a single player game (I will touch on multiplayer aspects later), most of your time will be spent engaging with AI opponents of two different flavors. The [b]Battle AI[/b] is absolutely feckless. On offense it forms a long single line and runs straight at you with no regard to the terrain, nor their opponents or their own army composition. This results in it forming giant blobs of its own units which are easily blasted into paste with ranged fire and spells. On defense it forms a long single line and sits there doing nothing until the player either weighs a flank (which causes the AI to pivot its whole force), or it takes enough damage from projectiles of any variety to cause it to flip into its offense mode detailed above. The [b]Campaign AI[/b] is absolutely craven. It spends its time sitting in walled settlements, sitting on units it recruited in the first 5 turns of the campaign because it can't disband them. It does this until it is in a state of war, where it decides to actively avoid enemy armies on the field, and go hit undefended, unwalled, minor settlements instead. It will only ever engage in a pitched battle if it perceives the autoresolve value to be in their favor before the armies actually make contact (the AI doesn't have fog of war and can see everything that isn't in ambush stance at all times, so it doesn't need any reconnaissance). The only time you will ever face it on the field is if you bait it with an ambush, or it has formed a big blob of armies and is moving them all together.

[h3]Cramped Campaign Map[/h3]
Despite being "the biggest Total War map ever", the Immortal Empires map (the only singleplayer mode anyone will play, I am not even going to discuss Realms of Chaos in this review) is so [b]condensed[/b] that it doesn't feel very big at all. Unless you are in a Jungle biome (which lowers armies movement by default), most settlements in the game are only 1 turn of movement away from each other. If you combine the AI's craven, avoidant behavior with the density of settlements, it results in [b]the[/b] problem that everyone complains about more than anything else.

[h3]Sieges[/h3]
The siege battle situation in this game is unacceptable. The frequency of these sieges are caused by the reasons I listed above. This wouldn't be as much of an issue if this battle type was actually fun; but the battle AI's passivity plus its terrible pathfinding, settlement layouts, stupid building and capture point mechanics, and bugs (primarily with the gatehouses and getting on and off wall segments) do everything in their power to make that not the case. The other problem is that the player is on offense 95% of these battles because the cowardly AI refuses to attack the player's hardpoints unless they have 4 stacks rolling together. I don't think that the solution to this problem is "remove sieges" as so many like to say, I think CA needs to take a hard look at Total War: Shogun II, and Total War: Medieval II, and use those two game's sieges as a baseline to build from.

[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]
Despite the singleplayer focus of the game, it [i]has[/i] multiplayer. On paper, a game like this should be a wonderful multiplayer experience, but once again there is a factor in play to prevent this from being the case. The main issue is the [b]complete lack of servers[/b]. All of the connections in this game are done peer to peer, and as a result whenever ping is involved, the game quickly turns into [i]Warhammer III the interactive slideshow[/i]. The way the game handles latency hasn't changed since [b]Total War: Rome from 2004[/b], it [i]sloooooows[/i] down, and depending on how bad the latency is, it will just stop.

[h3]Multiplayer Campaigns[/h3]
You can do multiplayer campaigns, which could be fun if you aren't playing with somebody from another country, or somebody who has poor quality internet. The more players you add to one of these campaigns (it goes up to 8) the worse it gets, as everybody is directly connecting to each other, rather than a server to sync the gamestate. In the previous titles, the maximum was 2 players in a multiplayer campaign, so the additional players is cool in theory. They also made it to where you can do your turns simultaneously, which is awesome until two players go to war with each other, and then it becomes a frantic clicking match as a [b]TURN BASED CAMPAIGN MAP[/b] goes realtime.

[h3]Competitive Multiplayer[/h3]
This community is split in 3 ways. The first split is between those who use the games built in matchmaking, and those who join insular Discord communities based around the tournament scene. The second split is between those Discord communities, between the newer Domination game mode, and the traditional land battle game mode (which is now doing Conquest mode instead). There is no siege battle focused community like there was in the heyday of Medieval II, this is because siege battles are terrible. The same latency problems are in play here, and on top of that now you're picking to play with either: automatch scumbags who spend their time abusing the lack of rules, or Discord eSports people who want to regulate you to death.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
If you don't have ANY of this games content, don't buy in. If you disregard that advice, buy in on sale. I am stuck in the sunk cost fallacy, be warned.

[b]Le Verdict[/b] : TWW3 est la conclusion spectaculaire et indispensable de la trilogie, mais son véritable potentiel est atteint grâce à la map Empires Immortels .

[b]L'Essentiel[/b] : Le jeu de base nous introduit aux nouvelles et fantastiques factions de Kislev 🐻 et de Grand Cathay 🐉, en plus des factions Démoniques du Chaos. Les batailles de siège ont été repensées (même si elles divisent), et l'échelle des conflits n'a jamais été aussi grande. C'est une immersion totale dans l'univers de Warhammer.

[b]La Vraie Raison de Jouer[/b] : C'est Empires Immortels. Ce mode, qui nécessite les trois jeux, fusionne les cartes des trois épisodes pour créer la carte de campagne la plus vaste et la plus dense de l'histoire du jeu de stratégie. C'est le bac à sable ultime où l'on peut jouer mon cher Noctilus (ou n'importe quel Seigneur Légendaire) contre tous les autres, sur un terrain de jeu gargantuesque. C'est l'expérience complète qui fait de TWW3 un chef-d'œuvre. 🤩

[b]Les Bémols [/b]:

- La Campagne du Royaume du Chaos (de base) est trop linéaire et répétitive pour les vétérans.

- Le jeu est exigeant en termes de performances, et des bugs sont encore présents malgré les patchs.

- La politique de DLC de Creative Assembly est un point de friction constant pour la communauté 💰.

[b]En Bref [/b]: Un incontournable absolu. Si vous possédez les deux premiers jeux, l'IE propulse TWW3 au sommet de la stratégie fantastique. Attendez-vous juste à ce que le contenu additionnel vous coûte cher sur le long terme.

[b]Note Finale [/b]: 9/10. Pour l'ampleur, la variété et la folie de l'Immortal Empires. ✨

Total War: Warhammer III rappresenta l’apice della trilogia sviluppata da Creative Assembly. Rispetto ai due capitoli precedenti, questo titolo risulta decisamente più completo e offre un’esperienza di gioco più ampia, migliorando sia la gestione strategica sia le tattiche militari. Il gioco presenta un’ampia varietà di fazioni, molto diverse tra loro, che spaziano da Kislev ai Demoni del Caos, ciascuna dotata di caratteristiche, identità e meccaniche proprie.

Sul piano della strategia a turni, la mappa della campagna si distingue per la sua vastità e per il notevole livello di dettaglio, con numerose regioni, risorse e minacce da gestire. Il mantenimento delle province risulta relativamente semplice da comprendere, e alcune città offrono strutture uniche in grado di fornire vantaggi significativi al giocatore e di influenzare profondamente le decisioni strategiche.

Per quanto riguarda le fazioni, Warhammer III offre una varietà notevole sia dal punto di vista estetico sia da quello del gameplay. Ogni fazione dispone di meccaniche uniche, spesso molto diverse tra loro, garantendo così un’esperienza nuova ad ogni campagna. Kislev combina elementi militari tradizionali con unità ibride e un sistema religioso che aumenta il morale delle truppe, mentre il Grande Catai introduce la particolare meccanica dell’Armonia, che richiede un costante equilibrio tra Yin e Yang per ottenere bonus strategici e militari.

Uno degli argomenti più discussi all’interno della community riguarda i DLC a pagamento: molti giocatori criticano il fatto di dover acquistare ulteriori fazioni o contenuti, percependo questi elementi come parte integrante del gioco base. Questo aspetto ha generato diverse polemiche e ha diviso l’opinione dei fan.

In conclusione, consiglio questo titolo non solo a chi ha apprezzato i precedenti Total War: Warhammer, ma anche a chi desidera provare uno strategico su larga scala, ricco di fazioni differenti e di possibilità tattiche. Total War: Warhammer 3 è molto completo e particolarmente appagante per gli amanti del genere.

《全面战争：战锤3》：宏大的终章，但并非完美的句点
作为奇幻策略游戏史上最雄心勃勃的系列收官之作，《全面战争：战锤3》无疑交出了一份分量十足的答卷。它继承了前作的所有精华，并将战场的规模与世界的疯狂推向了新的极致。然而，在无与伦比的辉煌之下，一些固有的顽疾与首发时的波折，也让这款巨作带上了一丝遗憾的色彩。

极致的阵营设计与超凡体验
如果说《战锤》全战系列的核心魅力在于其天马行空的阵营设计，那么《战锤3》在这方面达到了巅峰。基斯里夫的冰雪魔法与战争巨熊，震旦天朝的巍峨长城与空中楼阁，尤其是恐虐、奸奇、纳垢与色孽四大混沌恶魔阵营，它们不仅仅是兵种和数值的不同，而是从机制、玩法到美学风格的全方位颠覆。

机制迥异：扮演奸奇魔君，你可以通过“变化灵”肆意破坏敌方内政；作为纳垢军团，你则像一场缓慢蔓延的瘟疫，用建筑序列感染整个世界。这种高度不对称的体验，让每一场战役都充满新鲜感。

震旦与基斯里夫：作为系列首次深入展现的东方与斯拉夫风格势力，它们带来了独特的“阴阳调和”与“冰雪信仰”体系，既有传统全战的稳健，又融入了奇幻色彩，令人眼前一亮。

“超凡帝国”——终极的沙盒乐园
对于系列老玩家而言，《战锤3》的真正价值在“超凡帝国”模式中才完全展现。这是将前三作所有地图、所有种族、所有传奇领主融于一体的终极沙盒，其规模在策略游戏史上堪称前无古人。从露斯契亚的原始丛林到震旦天朝的繁华都市，你可以实现任何疯狂的跨时空对决。这不仅是CA对玩家承诺的兑现，更是一个能够持续游玩数千小时的、活着的战锤世界。

令人又爱又恨的战役设计
本作主线战役“混沌魔域”是一个大胆的尝试。它拥有出色的叙事和极具压迫感的氛围，但其“竞技场式”的规则也引发了巨大争议。玩家被迫在固定时间点进入混沌魔域争夺灵魂，这种设计虽然紧扣主题，却严重干扰了传统“种田”玩家的节奏，带来了强烈的被动与焦虑感。好在后续更新中，CA提供了关闭此机制的选项，并加强了“永恒之战”模式，给予了玩家更多自由。

技术与平衡的持久战
《战锤3》的发售之路并非一帆风顺。初期饱受诟病的性能优化、AI逻辑bug以及阵营间的不平衡，都曾一度影响游戏体验。CA通过一系列持之以恒的更新与修复，让游戏状态大幅改善，但时至今日，部分派系的强度、某些兵种的实用性问题依然是社区讨论的焦点。这仿佛是一场永无止境的军备竞赛，也是维持如此庞大游戏生态所必须面对的挑战。

瑕不掩瑜的史诗终曲
总而言之，《全面战争：战锤3》是一部优缺点都极其明显的杰作。它可能不是系列中最均衡、最稳定的一作，但它绝对是视野最宏大、内容最丰富、最具想象力的一作。它完美地承接了前两作的遗产，并将这个奇幻全战的梦想推向了现实。

最终评价：

对于战锤系列的粉丝，这是不容错过的、必须收藏的终极盛宴。对于策略游戏爱好者，它提供了一个无与伦比的、充满深度与变数的奇幻战场。尽管它存在一些技术瑕疵和值得商榷的设计选择，但当千军万马在混沌荒原上冲锋，当巨龙与恶魔在天空中缠斗时，你会发现，所有的等待与磨合都是值得的。《全面战争：战锤3》不仅为这个三部曲画上了一个宏大的句号，更为未来的模组与更新留下了无限可能。

So far, I'm happy with this game. I have thousands of hours invested in TW:WII and of course TW:WIII is mostly more of the same, except with an even bigger map and even more factions. So, I'm not as engaged as I was with TW:WII. But  still, I feel CA did a good job of introducing interesting, well fleshed out new factions, as well as doing some nice tweaks to some of the old factions. Here is what stood out for me.

My two favorites from TW:WII were the dwarves and the vampires and I was happy to see that there they've added a new dwarf lord and new dwarf and vampire units (although the dwarf content is behind a paid DLC). Vampires finally get a high end anti-large infantry unit (grave guard halberdiers) in the vanilla game, which is awesome. The faction also got a complete makeover. They have completely changed which building does what and tech tree is very different, as well as bloodline lord unlock perks. I'm not sure if it will make things easier or harder. Among other things, dwarfs get a cool new lord, grudge raker thunderers and a new kind of slayer, which is really nice. Some legacy units also got some nerfs/buffs.

One of the things I really like is how they have further dispersed the starting locations for the different lords in each faction. In TW:WII, you were pretty much always facing the same starting enemies regardless of which lord you chose. In TW:WIII, there is more variety, which adds to the replay value of each faction.

As for the news factions, there are several new evil demonic factions, which have similitudes as well as distinctive unit and perks. I'm not interested in chaos dwarfs that much (which are behind a DLC anyway), but I really like the Kislev and Cathay factions in the vanilla game. Very well fleshed out and fun.

Settlement battles have become more complex with defensive points you can invest to build various defensive buildings inside your settlement (during the battle). It is a little bit weird and takes time getting used to. Not sure if I like it, but I don't hate it.

Many people hate this game because they are angry at CA for screwing things up and having so much content behind a paywall. As annoying as it is, it is not so bad if you get the game and the DLC on sale. A game this huge and detailed must be pretty expensive to produce, so I won't hold it against them. More worrying are the game altering bugs, but so far I have not encountered anything that really broke the game for me. I am aware of the fact that some bugs were fixed before I started playing and that there is always a chance that a new update could break the game again.

Overall, I think that the game adds enough good new content to be worth considering.

I am a long time fan of Total War, first game I played was Rome 1. My father used to play Shogun 1 when I was a small kid and I used to watch him play. I bought the Warhammer trilogy in the month of July of 2025 and I love it (I love fantasy with elves and dwarfs and I love strategy games).

The game has a large variety, though I met some bugs at the beginning, like for example the Lizardmen were idle. After finishing the tutorial campaign of Kislev I finished he Chaos Rift campaign, then moved on to the Immortal Empires campaign. The map is huge. I started with Tyrion from the High Elves. Unfortunately the Lizardmen were idle and got defeated early by the southern Skaven faction called Clan Pestilens. Then of course this Skaven faction had to invade my lands. I was playing on Very Hard difficulty and this Skaven faction caused me a lot of headaches. If the Lizardmen would have been active, they could have been my allies and they could have protected me from the Skaven, probably. Doesn't matter, the game received an update (6.3.4) that fixed this bug, or at least I think it is fixed as there are no more Lizardmen around my territories.

Overall I enjoy playing this game, it is a mix between Total War and high fantasy (elves, orcs/orks, dwarfs), exactly what I love. This game also made me get interested in the Warhammer franchise and so I bought a few books about Warhammer Fantasy and Warhammer 40k. 

Currently I have 162 hours in the Immortal Empires with the Tyrion faction (on turn 220+). I explored like 80% of the american continent and probably 30% of the european continent (as I see it the whole Immortal Empire map is based on the real world). This game is huge, and I love it. A few bugs here and there will not stop me from enjoying this game.

One negative aspect that I can say is that the deployment lines are flickering from time to time, but I read online that it is due to my NVidia 5070 GPU, so I don't know if it is the game or my GPU. Hope this will be fixed. The flickering happens especially when I fight against Dark Elf Black Arks. All I do in this situation is restart the game after the battle and the flickering dissapears.

Other than that the gameplay is fun, pulling off hammer and anvil tactics is fun, the units look good, the factions are varied, units are varied, there are even tanks on the Empire factions, which I never though I would see in a Total War game. The whole trilogy is a bit expensive and I wish there would be a physical copy of all of the three games as I like collecting physical discs (grew up in the 90's with owning physical copies of NES and PC games), but overall I am happy with my purchase, the game is challenging (for me), I can spend time on thinking of the optimal strategy for my empire, it's a fun experience playing this game.

Считаю, что это лучшая часть не только среди "Warhammer: Total War", но всех Total War или одна из лучших.
Что касается сшитой карты "Империи Смертных", то ей не хватает такой важной детали как сюжетные условия победы, которые имеются в основной компании. В большой сборной карте требуется кого-то уничтожить на другом конце карты или захватить очень много территорий, что не так уж интересно, учитывая упрощенную цепочку строительства и экономику, свойственную фантастическим Total War.
В основной компании большая часть лордов носятся наперегонки за душами демонов. Примечательно, что можно добиться огромной экономической мощи, перебить всех вокруг и захватить много земель, но не успевать за соперниками в погоне за душами демонов, которые добываются в ходе выполнения заданий, появляющихся в период открытия так называемых разломов.
Те лорды, кому не нужны души демонов выполняют собственные задания, прямо не связанные с уничтожением какой-либо фракции и захватом территории.
В сюжетной компании по законам природы "сильные" быстро перемалывают "слабых" и из сотни фракций через несколько десятков ходов выживает где-то четвертая часть и это сводится +/- к противостоянию хаоса против нехаоса. Быстрое истребление большинства народов оскудняет компанию. Такое событие как воскрешение поверженной фракции из-за восстания в поселении мне не попадалось.
Больше всего понравилась Царица Кислева Катарина (остальные лорды рядом не стоят: безумный Распутин; Баба-Яга, потерявшая что-то в пустошах хаоса и окруженная демонами; Борис, воюющий непонятно где с гномами хаоса и орками вместо того, чтобы защищать границы страны от демонов и вампиров). Тут и стрелковая пехота, отлично сражающаяся в рукопашную, и кавалерия на любой вкус, гигантские медведи и змеи, отличающиеся красотой и силой.
Китай прикольный, но мало видов элитной пехоты по сравнению с теми же северянами + странно, что у народа, который поклоняется драконам, нет драконов, не считая лордов, которые умеют превращаться в чудищ в бою, но в ущерб своим магическим способностям. С караваями интересно придумали. Инь/Янь так себе реализовали, не сильно хотелось с этой механикой возится.
У Хаоса великолепная тяжелая пехота (избранные) и демоны разных размеров на любой вкус. Хорн показался самым колоритным с его огромными летающими монстрами. Больше нравилось биться с демонами, чем за них играть.
Гномы хаоса сильно перекаченные по сравнению со своими порядочными собратьями, которых быстро истребляют, если специально не заниматься их спасением.
Людоеды вызывают отвращение. Не демоны, но и нормальными их не назовёшь.
Остальные существенного влияния на карте не имеют. Иногда вырывается в лидеры имперская колдунья на драконе.

This review is right before the Tide of Torment DLC release.
I played a little of Warhammer 2 and I've been here since the release of Warhammer 3. There is a lot of hate directed at this game for multiple reasons. I understand the community's reasons to be upset. But seeing all these people with hundreds to thousands of hours of game time... The game has to be pretty good despite all those negative reasons, right? In my opinion, yes. I've not played any table top Warhammer, but I think they did a really great job at putting the setting into this type of game. The models, animations, map, voice acting, etc. They all look fantastic. Each faction's mechanics are unique (for the most part) and fun (for the most part). With 1400 hours, I'm still in the process of playing each legendary lord at least once. This is the type of game where time will slip by you without your notice. Hours will go by. 

There are downsides to getting into this series however. Most notably, the DLC's. If you want every single piece of content, you will need to purchase the first two base games in addition to all the DLC's from each game. Waiting for a sale is the best approach because it'll get... expensive. But playing just the base game is fine too because there's still a decent amount of content to start you off.

Regarding multiplayer, I've played both co-op and PvP. I'm a fan of both. Co-op is definitely fun with friends, helping each other out in the overworld and in battle, assigning individual units to your friends to micro in your stead is very fun (like using cavalry/chariots). PvP is an acquired taste. With friends, you gotta have willing PvP enthusiasts. Through matchmaking or mingling with the competitive community, it can hit or miss. I found it refreshing after having OP armies in the campaign. It can humble you. 

Overall, the game is fun and I'll continue to sink another 1400 hours I'm sure. I'm no fanboy of the devs, but I'm not a hater either. Creative Assembly has their flaws, but they've also addressed community gripes over the years and tweaked/fixed them... albeit a bit slow to the trigger. Give credit where credit is due. I do love the game and I have always had a very positive view on it, looking beyond what people tend to complain about. I own all the content, and with how many hours I've sunk into it, I feel like I used my money well. My only real gripe is not having any friends who want to PvP spar with me lol...

Recent drama aside, this game has remained the gold standard of what an RTS should look like. We know they've been working on a new engine, we know they keep pushing out fixes for bugs, we know that this game will continue to remain one of the most ambitious projects out there. There are a number of great features this game has. 

First, a massive combined three part map that can keep single campaigns going for hours. 

Second, real time turns that allow a large party of people taking their turns simultaneously. 

Third, huge variety of units, animations, stats, and play style to accomadate and enrich your experience. 

Fourth, beautiful maps and battles that can challenge players and strategists alike. 

The only thing I wish for is more more more. If you read the negative reviews that's what you'll see: a demand for more. More content, more fixes, more updates, more graphics, more changes, more games, more styles, more more more. The people have spoken, and we have an insatiable need for total war. 

We want a new engine, easier mod support, more community driven direction, and yes, more games. The masses are so in demand for Medieval 3, Empire 2, and Rome 3 that they went and built them some new overhauls of these games in right in the Steam Workshop (ie Rome 3 = Divide Et Impera, Empire 2 = Empire 2 Mod). It's only a matter of time before one day the devs stop publishing updates about even Warhammer 3 and then modders will go back and give me the total war I've been waiting for my whole life: Battle for Middle Earth. 

And while the recent reviews for now have won the day and kept this game at a mixed review status, I know that this game is a hallmark to any RTS player. It's so grand and all encompassing that everybody who is repeatedly drawn to RTS games will inevitably stumble upon even this title. I got my money's worth out of this game a long time ago. And I will continue to support this developer so long as they keep with the mantra: more, more, more.

My main frustration is the repeated and unexpected (and often unreproducable) crashes to desktop.  This could happen after a few minutes of play or after a few hours; the game would just freeze and drop to the desktop.  Getting back in was smooth, but it takes one out of the enjoyment or flow of the game.

Overall, even on Easy for both campaign and combat, it was a challenging game to play, frustrating even.  (Yes, I can hear the howls of the 'git good' crowd)

To be effective, armies generally seemed to need to be at or near full which would create a costly front end (an issue the AI didn't seem to deal with; I confederated with a few factions and went immediately into the red, as their economies didn't seem to be sufficient to support their armies).  Even when you haven't expanded out very much, because of the distances that armies travel (or more accurately, can't travel), you generally need 2 armies at any one time ... one to beat down enemies in your rear (and as everyone is always surrounded by enemies, you always have enemies at your back) the other to actually do anything.

This creates what I think of as a 'large but small' problem ... the maps are large, but your units can't move very far, so it feels like you're crawling about from turn to turn, not striding across the map.

Further to complicate it is that each army plays differently but there isn't a robust way of teaching HOW each army plays differently; online guides don't cut it, the learning should happen in game and shouldn't require a dozen hours or more per faction to get its playstyle (there are too many 'failure paths', choices that look good, or at least reasonable, but are ultiamtely self defeating and each faction has different ones of these, so it's difficult to transfer knowledge).  The tutorial levels are decent, if a bit scripted, but each faction really needs their own primer that isn't just a text bubble.

Combat locations feel generic ... they change, but they don't seem to reflect the particular area where you are; there was no sense of 'place' ... I seem to recall Total War used to better track where your armies were to match the battles, so a fight in an English plain woud feel different than a fight in an Italian plain.  With the emphasis on spells, normal units don't generally have interesting things they can do, like ranged units either firing at will, firing in tandem, rank firing, etc. and it isn't exactly clear how effective each spell is.

Overall I feel like the game captures the feel of Warhammer better than it plays as a Total War game.  I finished the Daemon Prince story campaign but it felt a bit too generic, with rank ups being +4% to X unit's attack speed or +6% to Y unit's armor, and about half the campaign I was at my Chaos Gods cap so I had unlocked all the equipment (of which many were just upgrades of previous versions, but there was no option to 'hide outdated equipment') so the choice as to who to dedicate each victory to became empty except for 'more XP / units back / gold'.

"Варвархаммер 3" — это долгожданное продолжение популярной стратегии в жанре фэнтези, разработанное компанией Creative Assembly. Игра сочетает в себе масштабные сражения, глубокую тактику и богатую сюжетную линию, основанную на вселенной Warhammer.

Графика и дизайн
Игра впечатляет детализированной графикой, живописными локациями и эффектными анимациями. Модели персонажей и монстров выполнены с высокой точностью, что создает ощущение погружения в мрачный и жестокий мир.

Геймплей
"Варвархаммер 3" предлагает масштабные битвы с участием сотен единиц, требующие стратегического мышления и правильного распределения ресурсов. В игре присутствует разнообразие фракций, каждая со своими уникальными юнитами и тактиками.

Сюжет
Сюжетная линия насыщена интригами, предательствами и эпическими сражениями. Игрокам предстоит вести свою фракцию через сложные политические и военные испытания, чтобы сохранить власть и победить врагов.

Особенности

Расширенные возможности кастомизации армий
Новые механики магии и ритуалов
Улучшенная система искусственного интеллекта
Кооперативные и мультиплеерные режимы
Итог
"Варвархаммер 3" — это достойное продолжение серии, которое порадует как поклонников классики, так и новых игроков. Игра сочетает в себе стратегическую глубину и визуальное великолепие, создавая незабываемый опыт в мире Warhammer.

Dopo centinaia di ore passate a muovere pedine sul Risiko storico, l'universo di Warhammer è stata una boccata d'aria fresca che, ammetto, ha fatto storcere il naso a molti fedelissimi della serie storica. Ma per chi ha accettato il fantasy, il risultato è stato un'epopea senza precedenti.

Total War: WARHAMMER III non è solo la chiusura di una trilogia, è il punto d'incontro definitivo tra la strategia tipica di Total War e l'eccentricità profonda del dark fantasy. E se all'inizio la campagna del Reame del Caos era, diciamo, particolare, con l'arrivo della campagna Immortal Empires (che unisce le mappe dei tre giochi), questo è diventato, senza esagerare, il più grande e folle Total War mai creato. Un sandbox colossale dove tutto può accadere.

Il pregio più grande di questo titolo è come la lore è stata implementata, trasformando ogni fazione in un'esperienza unica. Non si tratta più solo di "fanteria pesante vs fanteria leggera":

Kislev: Combatte non solo con la fede, ma con Orsi Polari corazzati e la Magia del Gelo, gestendo un'economia che è un delicato equilibrismo tra la volontà dello Zar e il rifornimento costante di truppe e, ovviamente, di Orsi.

Nani del Caos: Il loro obiettivo non è conquistare territori, ma accumulare schiavi e risorse. Trasformano i prigionieri in manodopera o in proiettili per le loro macchine infernali forgiate nella fucina infernale, gestendo il lavoro sporco con una burocrazia che fa impallidire l'Impero.

Tzeentch: Giocano a Monopoli con la diplomazia e la Magia del Cambiamento, manipolando le fazioni a distanza. Possono ribaltare intere guerre con una semplice mossa strategica o un incantesimo ben piazzato sulla mappa.

Ogni Lord Leggendario cambia drasticamente le regole. Giocare con N'Kari è una festa della seduzione strategica e del duello, mentre Grombrindal ti fa viaggiare attraverso il mondo con un esercito fantasma per vendicare ogni torto subito. L'esperienza di gioco è così stratificata che 600 ore sono veramente poche per assaggiare la varietà totale.

Dal punto di vista estetico, le battaglie sono una meraviglia sanguinosa e caotica. Gli scontri tra i Grandi Demoni sono epici, i dettagli delle armature sono curatissimi e l'atmosfera su una mappa del Reame del Caos è palpabile. Il gioco ti fa sentire davvero nel Mondo che Fu, un luogo decadente, brutale e pieno di magia di ogni sorta.

E quando pensi di aver visto tutto, arriva la Comunità di Modding, il workshop di Steam. La libreria infinita di modifiche a disposizione è la vera assicurazione sulla longevità. Mod che aggiungono nuovi Lord, nuovi alberi delle abilità o rework completi delle meccaniche. I mod rendono questo gioco un parco giochi personale illimitato, permettendoti di correggere, espandere o semplicemente stravolgere il gioco a tuo piacimento. Se Creative Assembly ha messo l'ossatura, la comunità ci ha messo il cuore e i muscoli.

Total War: WARHAMMER III è l'apice della serie fantasy. Sì, preparatevi a qualche frustrazione tipica di Total War (come le dichiarazioni di guerra multiple e coordinate dei nemici contro di voi), ma l'ampiezza della mappa, la diversità delle fazioni e la cura nella trasposizione della lore lo rendono assolutamente indispensabile per i fan di questo genere.

È un mostro di rigiocabilità che ti terrà incollato molto più a lungo di quanto tu voglia ammettere.

Ora scusatemi, devo tornare a far proliferare una pestilenza di Nurgle.

This is one of those games where I wish steam reviews weren't just a simple Yes or No recommendation.

At its core, TW:Warhammer III is a good game that stands out from games in other Total War series due to its variety and uniqueness of factions, units, and playstyles. Even if you're not into the Warhammer franchise, you can enjoy this game if you're into strategy, big battles, and fantasy. The sound is good, the visuals are good, the voice acting is great. The battles can be very entertaining.

I like the game, I really do. However, I just can't RECOMMEND buying the game for people new to the series.

Let's get this out of the way first. The DLC situation with this game is particularly egregious. Even if you paid full price for this game, you only get a fraction of the factions unlocked. And even those unlocked factions in the base game aren't fully unlocked, portions of it, legendary lords (which determine your starting point and playstyle) and even some upper tier units, are locked behind DLC. The DLCs combined for Warhammer III can cost you way more than twice as much as the base game. But let's say you like the game, you decide to buy all the DLCs for the WH3... and yet, you still don't have everything unlocked. Why? Because not only do you need to buy all the DLCS for WH3, [u]you need to buy Warhammer 1 AND Warhammer 2 AND all their respective DLCs in order unlock everything[/u]. In addition, they don't support cross platform, so if you have WH2 on epic and WH3 on steam, guess what? You gotta rebuy WH2 on steam just to unlock the stuff for WH3.

But let's say you're mister/missus money bags and you don't mind spending a couple hundred dollars to unlock things in the game. There are many minor (not game crashing) bugs and bad design choices that aren't terrible on their own but are horrible when they all come together. Not all factions are equal, and understandably so, as it's difficult to perfectly balance a game around all these factions and legendary lords that can completely change how you play a faction, but those are not the bad design choices I'm talking about. For example, in the previous games, minor settlements can gain walls if you built the correct building and upgraded it. Certain factions were unable to do this but gained other advantages to make up for their lack of walls. In WH3, they've completely done away with gaining walls in minor settlements for every faction without making up for it. As another design choice, they've nerfed the garrisons defending your settlements. By design, the AI, to compensate for not playing as smart as a human, gets more resources and have less upkeep, which allows them to field more armies than you (and the higher the difficulty, the more resources and less upkeep). This results in the AI generally being in more places and able to just steamroll your minor settlements, regardless of your defensive buildings, if you don't have an army babysitting it (and most factions can't support having an army babysitting every settlement). In the previous games, the walls forced them to siege your minor settlements buying you time to get an army over to save the settlement, but in WH3, it's like playing Whack a Mole with all their armies running around going for your undefended bits, which quickly gets very tedious. It wouldn't even be so bad if your major walled settlements were choke points or something, but no, the AI just waltzes on by. Just a bunch of bad design choices coming together to make a horrible (and very common) situation.

There's also all these weird (but not game crashing) bugs that just ruin things sometimes. The more commonly noticeable one is when the AI gathers several armies around a town and... just sits there doing nothing (for possibly the entire game). And this is a VERY common occurrence. The other more commonly noticeable (well, if you play with a faction with ranged units) is that sometimes your ranged units just stop firing at will. They'll shoot if you manually tell them to attack a target but that defeats the purpose of firing at will. They could have clear line of sight to the target, no obstacles, on a flat plain, with ammo, in range, and they just won't fire at will. This makes things particularly unpleasant if you're playing a range heavy faction and downright cost you some battles if you're in a big battle and you don't notice your ranged units doing absolutely nothing because you were busy micromanaging another part of the battle. Even melee units will have brain farts at times where you order them to engage/chase an enemy unit and they just walk in and stare while the enemy is busy whacking away at them or just follow (and not attack) the enemy that's running away even though your unit is faster and should be cutting them down while running.

I could go on but this review is long enough as it is. I like the game but I just can't quite recommend it buying it especially if you're new to the series. I understand companies need to make money, but it just doesn't feel like the value is worth how much they're charging. Some people can argue that just the base game alone is worth it but you definitely feel the difference when you play a base game faction and find out some of your unit roster is locked behind DLC. And if you're expecting people to spend hundreds of dollars, at least try to keep it as bug free as possible.

This game is dope. There's a learning curve for sure if you're just starting. Once you get over that hump, oh boy. Get ready to lose a couple weeks of your life every time you start a campaign. Every faction has unique mechanics, units to play around with, and a different set of objectives for you to win. While yes, ultimately it boils down to make big army, big money, and control the map, every faction has it's own unique way of doing so. Find a faction or two you like and drop 100 hours just playing them. In terms of bang for your buck this is the game. 

Couple things to address. First the DLC. The DLC does not lock you out of actual gameplay mechanics or parts of the map. Every unpurchased lord or race is available to play against so you see them on the map when you play them. The base game has plenty of races. How this game works is if you buy 3, you have access to the immortal empires, which is the huge campaign with every single race involved, however you are limited to play as only the factions in immortal empires. If you buy 1 and/or 2 you have access to the factions in those games. Then you can buy the DLC for factions and Lords for factions you find are interesting. It looks like a lot, but genuinely just buy the DLC for the faction you think looks the coolest. You don't have to buy it all at once, so don't let that complete package price daunt you. 

Secondly, there's a lot of drama with the company and youtubers. Creative Assembly is a greedy video game company, simple as that, and there's a popular total war youtuber who basically quit because of them. They also tend to do things like have bugs that come out while they ship DLC that doesn't work. Welcome to gaming in 2025 unfortunately. 

Barring those two things, this game is an absolute gem and if you are remotely interested in warhammer or strategy games I highly recommend giving this game a shot.

I’ve had a ton of fun with Total War: Warhammer 3, which is exactly why it hurts to say I can’t fully recommend it. The foundation of the series is built on layer after layer of old code, WH3 sits on WH2, which sat on WH1, and it shows. The game’s systems feel tangled, and meaningful improvements often require CA to fight their own engine. This slows updates, limits innovation, and lets long-standing issues linger.

But the deal-breaker for me is the siege design. It’s simply bad. Traditional siege tactics don’t work, defending walls is a trap, and the optimal play is usually to hide deep in the settlement and cheese the enemy through attrition. Making it worse, around 80% of battles end up being sieges anyway, because AI lords almost always run and hide into their settlements the moment you have the strength advantage. You’re forced into the worst part of the game again and again.

On top of that, the community has long agreed that the campaign has become bloated with too many systems that don’t meaningfully interact, and the battle AI still struggles with basic pathing, flanking, and decision-making (especially in siege battles). There’s also a widespread feeling in the community that CA has prioritized monetization over maintaining or improving core gameplay, with frequent DLC and slow responses to major issues making players feel ignored and undervalued. $400 total for all games and DLC, call me crazy. These issues pile up and drag down what could be a masterpiece.

There’s greatness here, but until these core problems are addressed, it’s hard to give a wholehearted recommendation.

Las grandes "calamidades" que azotan al mundo son interesantes al principio, pero luego se quedan como una amenaza local que puedes expulsar más con fuerza bruta que estrategia, pero seguí jugando, especialmente por Kislev, los enanos y en ocasiones los altos elfos, caos, el Imperio, etc. Lamentablemente aquí es donde comienza el problema, las amenazas y el caos ya no son lo que eran, ahora solo son un momento mínimamente épico que queda bien como algún cuadro, incluso ya no están las cinemáticas cuando el "Consejero" o "Asesor" era devorado por su cuervo y este se convertía en Sarthorael, volviendo al punto, ya no suponen amenazas reales o bien, ya no son mecánicas que cambien el rumbo en el juego, adicionalmente, cuando juegas con el Caos, especialmente con Archaon es sumamente flojo, ya no esta la mecánica de horda que me gustaba en Warhammer II y lo sustituyeron por poder avasallar a los aliados, que el 90% no son ningún aporte, este es uno de los problemas de la lista que suma y sigue, pero creo que no es necesario continuar. Es ist gleichzeitig Meisterwerk und Wahnsinn, und genau das macht es so witzig wie faszinierend.

⚔️ Die Fakten – mit einem Augenzwinkern
Epischer Abschluss: Warhammer 3 ist der letzte Teil der Trilogie und gilt als bestes Total War seit 14 Jahren.

Immortal Empires: Mit dem großen Update wurde die gigantische Kampagne integriert – jetzt kannst du alle Fraktionen und Karten ohne die Vorgänger spielen.

Story-getrieben: Die Hauptkampagne ist noch stärker auf Handlung und Rivalitäten ausgelegt als Warhammer 2.

Neue Armeen: Dämonenfraktionen wie Khorne, Nurgle, Slaanesh und Tzeentch bringen völlig neue Spielweisen – von „alles kaputthauen“ bis „alles verrotten lassen“.

Kritikpunkte: KI wird teils als „braindead“ beschrieben, und Day-1-DLCs wie die Oger-Armee sorgten für Stirnrunzeln.

😂 Die witzige Seite

Die Kampagne fühlt sich manchmal an wie ein Fantasy-Bürokratie-Simulator: Du kämpfst gegen Chaosgötter, aber verlierst, weil du vergessen hast, die Steuern einzutreiben.

KI-Generäle sind so planlos, dass man denkt, sie hätten ihre Taktik aus einem Würfelspiel übernommen.

Multiplayer-Schlachten sind weniger „epische Fantasy-Kriege“ und mehr „wer spammt zuerst die Drachen“.

Total War Warhammer III es la culminación de una saga temática que, hasta la fecha, ha sido el proyecto más ambicioso de la franquicia Total War.

Siempre que analizo este juego (y toda la saga en conjunto) hay que comentar que gracias a que tuvieron que abordar la integración de magia, fantasía y señores épicos dentro de un total war se expandió enormemente lo que se podía hacer tanto en un mapa de campaña como en batalla. La riqueza de batalla actuando cómo estratega es sublime con gran variedad de estrategias nunca vistas antes. Pasando de aspectos como la magia, monstruos o unidades voladoras, una importante integración es la aparición de unidades únicas (héroes) que pueden tener monturas, objetos y habilidades únicas. Esto que fácilmente ha podido ser adaptado a otros juegos históricos fue una novedad de esta saga.

Centrándonos más en TW WH 3, la culminación del mapa de todo el universo de WH es, sin duda, un proyecto colosal y en continua expansión y mejora. La expansión de las campañas multijugador de hasta 2 jugadores a un máximo de 8 jugadores es también un punto increíble que facilita jugar cuando tienes un grupo de amigos interesados en jugar y que, hasta ahora, ningún otro TW lo permitía. 

También es destacable el proceso de actualización y mejora del juego. Con cierta asiduidad se actualizan contenidos, se pulen errores y van añadiendo alguna cosa para añadir más diversidad y hacer más equilibradas las facciones. 

Me parece un juego referente del género de estrategia, por todas las novedades estratégicas, la absoluta libertad y diversidad para coger una facción y mecánica que se adapte a tus gustos (muchas veces realmente divertidas o sorprendentes) y que, desde luego, tiene mucho que decir todavía. Considero que es un juego al que le quedan cientos de horas por jugar, y nuevos contenidos que pueden enriquecer todavía más este juego referente.

The short abridged review (given this is not exactly a new style of game) if your a fan of the TW series you'll most likely enjoy this installment (more so if you are a Warhammer fan as well) and as always better yet if you can catch it on a sale (at the time of writing this review 75% off).

The Pros & Cons:
The game has most of the modern updates and UI/mechanics of the Troy TW and plays quite similar in the overall gameplay loop just with Warhammer theme and characters.

The game was a huge disappointment.

Difficulty and AI

The biggest issue is the shockingly low difficulty. The AI is simply incompetent: it often makes irrational moves, fails at positioning and prioritization, and doesn’t punish mistakes in any meaningful way. On the highest difficulty settings, the game mostly relies on flat statistical and economic buffs for AI factions (more income, stronger armies, etc.) rather than improving decision-making, strategic variety, or tactical behavior.
A good example of how trivial the challenge feels is that I managed to complete 100% of Steam achievements in roughly 125 hours, which strongly suggests the game lacks long-term strategic depth and meaningful resistance.

Immersion and campaign design

In terms of immersion, the game feels weaker than Total War: WARHAMMER II. In the grand campaign, multiple factions appear to be placed in absurd or forced locations, the geography feels altered in a way that hurts believability, and many character goals and story beats seem exaggerated or artificial rather than organically grounded in the setting.
The campaign also lacks more developed faction narratives: there are few meaningful long-term faction goals, and there’s a noticeable absence of strong story presentation (for example, cutscenes or event chains that show the situation evolving as you progress).
Instead, the game leans on “busywork” systems, such as shallow item quests - including quests for equipment that the lord visibly already has on their model - which makes the content feel repetitive and low-effort. Many race and lord mechanics also feel underwhelming and fail to meaningfully change how you approach strategy or campaign planning.
Diplomacy
Diplomacy also needs a complete rework. Too often it feels like a system designed mainly to annoy the player rather than create interesting mid- and late-game political gameplay. Compared to modern strategy titles with deeper negotiation systems, Warhammer III’s diplomacy feels limited and unreliable.
Honestly: please benchmark it against other contemporary strategy games.

Mods/DLC dependency

In my opinion, the game is barely enjoyable without mods and DLC. The base experience feels incomplete and requires community fixes and additional content to reach a satisfying state.

What deserves praise

The one clearly positive element is the tutorial campaign as the Kislev prologue prince: it’s reasonably engaging and does a good job of building immersion and introducing mechanics.

Everything the other 2 did well has been perfected in this one and as a 40k fan for over 20 years this series has given me a love for Fantasy Warhammer at least as much as 40k. Is it perfect. Do not be dissuaded by the negative reviews. There is literally no other game that compares. If you like Total War strategy and Tolkienesque D&D-like fantasy, you should remove all doubt and just dive right in. Whatever the shortcomings of Creative Assembly, they've made the world and all its characters come to life in a remarkable way, with great animations and outstanding voice casting. 

What I highly recommend you do, however, is to play it with Venris's SFO: Grimhammer III and Hecleas' AI mod. They will greatly improve the length and challenge of your campaigns, combined with whatever QoL mods to suit your fancy. There are literally hundreds of mods that pick up the ball where CA dropped it or that add additional content.

I warn you though, that, if you get into it, you may have to pull out your purse more often than you expected, not because the game has micro-transactions, but because there are over a 100 unique Legendary Lords / factions to play with (and more to come), many whom will need to be unlocked by purchasing their respective game (Warhammer I or II) or DLC they came with. But even without them, you'll have many options to get you going for hundreds of hours. You will have access to 10 or 12 factions if you only buy Warhammer 3. 

People can complain about the price tag, and since Warhammer III, it's not without reason. Warhammer 1 & 2 offered DLCs which added 2 new factions for 7,49€; Warhammer 3's DLCs generally offered 3 new factions for 25€, now 23€, a steep incline. Although you can choose to pay only for one faction at a third of the price. 

But even if I have spent approximately 440 bucks in total on all the games + DLCs since 2016 (you should be able to get all for less than half of that during sales), it's given me over 5,000 hours of game time. Happy 25 anniversary, Total War! And what a 25 years it was. Just try out any TW game from the 2000's to instantly see how much has been lost. There's a reason why Medieval 2 and Empire are still some of the most popular TW games to this day. The amount of cut content and removed features is staggering, which only makes sense when you consider their monetization strategy: the classic endless DLC mill, which is slowly but surely getting less and less attractive with each release.

"But how's the game?" I hear you ask. I don't know! I don't think the game behaved as intended at any point. It's simply not finished. I could sum it up as an endless barrage of "This seemed to work fine before but now it's worse needlessly". Archers randomly decide not to shoot on "Fire at will" stance even with clear line of sight and no friendly units in the way. Major factions just randomly die to minor factions now, seemingly for no reason and without a fight, letting them absolutely snowball. Allies just decide to take a nap during battles, letting you handle the overwhelming forces while they sit back and watch the show. Routing enemies will run right through your units and casually barrage through your backline while "fleeing". And on top of that you have crashes, crashes and more crashes (mostly during lengthy sieges, go figure).

"Well surely there's a bunch of mods in the workshop that fix these things". Yeah. Maybe. Assuming there's any modders left by this point. CA has been going to war against them for some reason, and against the community at large, downright threatening them in very bizarre ways. Stranger still, considering how CA has the ignoble habit of ignoring long-standing bugs and leaving it up to the community to fix if they care so much.

The AI in particular is just hopeless at this point. Making decisions at random, often undoing what it just did or going back to where it just came from. Just yesterday I watched Cathay, the strongest faction on the map in my game, park NINE fully stacked armies in a corner and proceed to do -nothing- with them for the entirety of the game. Siege maps are especially egregious about this, because the AI has so much trouble navigating them that even your own unit's pathfinding will struggle with it. The only reason AI factions can put up a fight at all is because they very blatantly cheat in everything they need, and are exempt from systems and restrictions that would apply to the player. The worst part is that this has been a present issue for so long that it's been almost normalized to the point where it's expected, so the company makes little effort to improve it.

Here's to another 25 years of corporate neglect! Maybe by then you'll actually finish developing the game, after chopping it into little pieces that you sell to us one by one of course.

With the release of the new DLC Lords I thought I'd sound the regular Creative Assembly alarm. Let's start off with the classic quote ([i]say the line Bart[/i]) [b]"The right to discuss is a privilege—it is not an entitlement you earn by playing the game"[/b] from a now 2 year old steam community thread; that is a direct quote from CA PR, we the players who have given them a platform since, oh gee, the year 2000, don't deserve to complain about an obvious decline in quality over the years or want the games we love(d) to be better. 

CA does not value you as a player or customer, they just want your money as is evident by the DLC at the time of writing (12/4/2025) costing a total of $204.77 and that is with all but 4 pieces at least 25% off. That is on top of buying Total Warhammers 1, 2, and 3, if you bought them at release that's $180 added to that DLC. Is Total Warhammer really worth $384.77? Of course you don't have to buy the DLC (although we have been threatened before that if the DLC doesn't sell well then they'll stop working on the game. And honestly as you can see Total War games are like 70% DLC nowadays so you are getting a pretty empty experience without it), but CA wants your money, CA is asking you to shell out several hundred dollars for a game, keep your mouth shut and smile when you encounter bugs. **EDIT** I was unaware of an as of writing new update that gives players who own TW:WH1&2 the third game for free. If that applies to you then my review isn't super helpful to you since this will be free and I would also like to point out what a half-hearted gesture this update is. If you liked the series and bought the games when they came out- congratulations you paid full price for a game that became free. Second, I really can't imagine this free update applies to many players in the first place, if you own the first two games chances are you bought the third one, and if I'm wrong about that then that indicates a big playerbase falloff after the second game and you could imagine why that may be while reading my review.

In terms of the game itself TW:W3 is my least favorite of the fantasy iterations so far. The single player campaign is several times less fun than the previous 2 games' campaign modes and imo the new Chaos factions are the weakest part of the game for me. I would rather have that Mortal Empires Chaos jank than how they are fully implemented and center stage this time around. Honestly, I'd rather be playing TW:W2 with the new Lords they've added to the old factions, I think every new faction they added in 3 fell flat on its face.

I don't recommend this or any contemporary Total War game, try the old ones, they're going to be a lot cheaper and they were released as complete experiences.* Give Shogun 2 a shot, its debatably objectively the best TW game. Medieval 2 is also very good but isn't as digestible as Shogun I'd say. So yea, keep up the bad work CA, keep burning fans, we don't forget. 

*Yes I know the old games would get one (1) singular expansion pack released but please scroll down to the DLC section of Total Warhammer and don't be pedantic

 Manche Fraktionen haben es insbesondere am Anfang nicht einfach und es gibt welche, wo ich bis heute das Balancing in Frage stelle, vorallem wenn es um Autoschlachten geht, dennoch ist dies erstmal "okay"

Total War: WARHAMMER TRILOGY セットで、１・２・３を同時に手に入れましょう。
多くの基本勢力をプレイできるようになり、遊び方の幅が広がりますます。セールが破格にお得です。
なおインストールは「３」だけで良いらしい。

剣と魔法のWARHAMMERのダークファンタジー世界が、バトルに開けくれるこのゲームに最適です。
景観を盛り込んだ世界MAPは、細かく観察すると雰囲気があって面白いです。

昔「２」だけ購入して、遊べる種族の少なさや、ゲーム進行と描画の虚無さに２０時間も遊べませんでしたが、
改めてセールで見つけて１２３セットを購入したところ（支払いは１と３の分だけで済みました）、
いろいろ洗練されていて面白いです。
有志による日本語化MODも素晴らしい。
慣れるまでプレイ時間３０時間は練習です（笑）。

部隊UNITを、正面の向きや戦術を考えて戦場MAPに配置してから戦う、戦術・戦略SLG。
MAPでは昔ながらのターン制（待ち時間が少し長い）
戦場ではリアルタイム（たった２０部隊でも広い戦場で指揮するのは大変です）
１ボタン戦闘完了では圧勝の予想表示でも、自分で操作すると大損失とか、、、下手くそかという楽しさ。
種族毎に特徴が異なる、歩兵、騎兵、射撃兵、大型モンスター、飛行兵、単身リーダー各等を組み合わせた部隊編成の工夫が楽しめます。
種族別・リーダー別に、歴史背景を元にした進行ガイドが序盤にセットされていますが、実質ストーリーは有りません。
好きな方向へ、ひたすら戦闘と征服に明け暮れることが出来ます。
パラドゲーのような開戦事由縛りもありませんし、
種族別に戦略パート（内政ぽい部分）の仕様やユニットが異なるので、それぞれ違う遊び方が出来ます。

DLCは遊びたい勢力があれば追加購入すればOKです（結局３のセットと２の幾つかを購入しました）。
追加で選択出来るリーダーや、種族に追加のユニットを入手出来ます。

購入注意点は。
今の時代、動画配信者のプレイの様子を見ない人は居ないと思うけれど、
steamストアの動画や画像は、あくまで宣伝用のイメージムービーとイメージ画像に過ぎないことを留意する点です。
「２」の時に虚無りました（苦笑）。

近頃PvPやcoop仕様が主流なSLG界の中、ソロでじっくり時間をかけて楽しめます。

Easily one of my favorite games of all time, and a gateway drug into all things Warhammer. If you're even remotely interested, and you got a PC that can run it, I'd highly recommend picking it up on sale.

The biggest issue that makes it hard for me to recommend, however, is the large DLC debt that's accrued over the 10  year lifespan. It's the biggest weakness, and strength, of the series, which combines all three games into one massive, global campaign map that has nearly unmatched variety. While there are still tremendous issues with certain mechanics that you'll see other reviews mention, and a laundry list of bugs, that is something that they continue to tackle with frequent updates.

Does it make the wait for these overhauls worth it if it's being accomplished piecemeal? I don't know. But if the negative reviews make you hesitate, I'd say you should first look at their time played.

With the new update that unlocks the main campaign for owners of any of the titles (I, II, or III), I'd recommend looking at which factions each unlocks and buy the one you're most interested in. Despite every faction having DLC that unlocks more units, every single one is playable without them and still gives hundreds of hours worth of content. Trust me, there's nothing else out there quite like this game, and if you like large-scale RTS and fantasy, this game's really going to hook you.

This game gets A LOT of unjust hate from its community, mainly because of some "foot in mouth" comments made by CA. but This is my review of the GAME.

I’ve spent a good amount of time with this game and honestly, it’s one of those games that swings between frustrating and absolutely brilliant, but when it hits, it really hits.

The first thing that grabbed me was the scale. The battles feel massive, chaotic, and cinematic in a way that very few strategy games pull off. Watching lines of troops clash while spells explode across the battlefield is just… satisfying. It captures that Warhammer fantasy vibe perfectly.

The faction variety is also a huge plus. Every kingdom, daemon faction, or race feels different, not just cosmetically, but mechanically. Switching factions genuinely changes the experience. It kept the game fresh for me even after multiple campaigns.

I also appreciated the improvements in the tutorial and UI. Compared to earlier Total War titles, Warhammer III feels more welcoming, even if you’re not a veteran of the series. ( I promise you'll understand the game quickly) 

And yeah, the game has a ton of DLC, but honestly, you don’t need any of it to enjoy the base game. The base game already comes with plenty of factions and content to keep you busy for a long time that more than justify it's price. The DLCs are more like optional extras, fun if you really want a specific race or lord, but definitely not required to get your money’s worth.

Plus, the DLCs go on sale all the time. ( at the time of writing this everything is 50% of, i've seen up to 66% off)  If you ever decide you want more content later, you can just wait for a discount and grab whatever interests you. There’s no pressure to buy everything at full price, and you can still have a great experience with just the base game.

Now that being said, many people can make many criticisms but I really only have 2. 

1. AI, for your first several playthroughs is fine and you won't probably notice, but it a bit wonky and mid-late game it doesn't offer the challenge it could. theres updates made to it every patch. but after a while you'll want to grab a AI MOD ( I wouldn't start the game with the mods, just because they can be a bit more aggressive than a new player would be used to) 

2. End game events could be so much more.

"It's super fun, with a huge modding scene, which is super cool despite its early launch problems.  Also  on December 4th, 2025, they allowed Total War: Warhammer 1 and 2 players to play with owners of this game. Sounds cool, right? It kind of is.

However, what the devs did not say out loud, and what is just being discovered as of this review, is that you are no longer allowed to roll back to any update before 7.0. Luckly it seems they are not removeing the ablity to rollback completely. However it is still a bad situation currently. 

"What does this mean?"
Nothing if you play the vanilla game.

But almost nobody does that. For people who use mods,  particularly huge mods that overhaul the campaign, the units, or anything big like that, you are sh*t out of luck. 

Unless the mods get updated, you aren't using them; your save files (that you have put 200 turns+ into and a ton of fun and time investment)  Will no longer function.  This is bad if you had some really fun mods from a pre 7.0 update and the mod author has left the scene or something. Which is a lot of cool mods. 


"This has always been the case."
Yes It has. However you could downgrade freely before so it was not such a big issue. 

"But mods get updated fast, right?"
Nope, absolutely not! They do not. The mods that are broken by this  consumer-unfriendly choice are the ones that take months to even years to update, Thankfuly they do not seem to be removeing the ablity to roll back completely. 


"It COULD get worse"
We are not fully shure yet. But now that things have calmed down a bit it seems as though they are not removeing rollback completley. But that is not a gurentee. And there is still the issue of pre 7.0 mods no longer working and no longer haveing any way TO work.  

"I don't care about mods."
Fair enough; however, these practices are super anti-consumer. The more these things receive no pushback, the closer we get to mods being removed from all AAA games; the push to do this is huge. Companies get way more cash off of live services, microtransactions, and DLC than they do from games that embrace modding. I don't like that they are takeing options away, perticularly considering this game is NOT CHEEP. this is a very very expensive game. Perticularly if you have the other 2 or bought diffrent armys. Anything that takes my ablity to do as I like with the thing I bought is not a good thing. I do not like everything being a live service. 

Conclusion
This is a fun game, However The removeal of rollback has some bad implications for modding. And I don't much like this modren push to remove modding from games of this kind, or make it harder. This is not a cheep game, this is a very expensive 100 doller title if its not on sale where I am. And thats without dlc. So anything that messes with modding annoys me. 

I would sugjust for a bit, that you Go play Total War: Warhammer 2. It does not receive updates now, as it's 15 years old, but the mods are, as a result, complete and compatible in their best form now and forever!"

Recipe for Potato Dumplings (Varenyky)
Ingredients:
For the dough:
Wheat flour – 500 g
Water – 200 ml
Egg – 1
Salt – 1 tsp
For the filling:
Potatoes – 1 kg
Onions – 2
Lard or butter – 50 g
Salt – to taste
Ground black pepper – to taste
Preparation steps:
Making the dough:
Sifting the flour: Sift the flour into a large bowl.
Making the dough: Add salt and the egg to the flour. Gradually pour in the water, constantly stirring. Knead the dough until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Resting the dough: Wrap the dough in plastic wrap or cover it with a towel and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Preparing the filling:
Boiling the potatoes: Peel the potatoes, cut them into large pieces, and boil until tender in salted water.
Preparing the onions: While the potatoes are boiling, finely chop the onions. Sauté the onions in lard or butter until golden brown.
Making the potato puree: Drain the potatoes and mash them. Add the sautéed onions, salt, and pepper to taste, and mix well.
Forming the dumplings:
Rolling out the dough: Roll out the dough into a thin sheet about 2-3 mm thick. Use a glass or cutter to cut out circles approximately 7-8 cm in diameter.
Forming the dumplings: Place a spoonful of potato filling on each circle of dough. Fold the dough in half and pinch the edges tightly to seal the dumplings.
Cooking the dumplings:
Boiling water: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add salt.
Cooking the dumplings: Gently drop the dumplings into the boiling water, stirring carefully to prevent sticking. Cook until done (approximately 5-7 minutes after they float to the surface).
Serving:
Removing the dumplings: Remove the dumplings with a slotted spoon and place them on a plate.
Serving: Serve the dumplings hot, optionally drizzling with melted butter, sour cream, or sautéed onions.
Enjoy your meal!

If you want a proper strategy game, get something else. 

The strategy in this strategy game is juvenile. There is a large breadth and variety of fantastical elements, but the depth of the gameplay is shallow. 

The "great replayability" touted by this game's fans does not come from being a complex game with a variety of interconnected systems to learn. It's replayable because you can spend one campaign playing as Dwarf #1, and the next campaign playing as Dwarf #2, or as Elf #1. Maybe Dwarf #1 makes your axe guys stronger, but Dwarf #2 makes your arrow guys stronger. You can get a few hours of fun out of that, and then repeat it 200 times.

This is a great game if you just want to bash some action figures together. 

Be warned: because there is so little depth, you will always want a new action figure to play with. Be prepared to spend plenty of $ to expand your collection. This addictive spiral is evident by the fanbases rage at any stoppage in the content pipeline. When there's no new figures to play with, one is faced with the fact that the game they've spent $300 and 1,000 hours on is not very good.

Every aspect and feature has been developed to the highest level, including diplomacy, empire-building, battles, customisation options, and quests/events. Another nice thing is that the campaign map is absolutely enormous, with hundred of settlements and forts. Also, the game supports modding, and even includes a customisation tool you can enable in the options. Even though the game has suffered from several bugs in the past, my experience with it has been nothing but positive so far. Compared to the first Warhammer: Total War, this game is better in every single way, and is in my opinion the best one in the franchise yet.

Et bien la réponse est là dans ce TW: Warhammer 3 : se concentrer sur le contenu. I can't recommend a game in this state. I can't recommend a game that semirandomly stops working. The only "workaound" is spamming inputs in the hope your units will start responding again. 

It doesn't help that there are control loss & order deferment mechanics built into the game. Makes determining what's going on real difficult when the description of an unintentional bug is near identical to a feature. 

Not a big fan of the devs saying they've fixed these highly inconsistent & multifaceted bugs a dozen+ times & one-sidedly put down those bug reports as solved. 2,000+ hours across the entire trilogy, and still my all-time favorite game franchise.

Is it flawless? Absolutely not. There are bugs, balance issues, questionable design decisions, and plenty of things Creative Assembly could have handled better. Some of CA's business decisions have also clearly prioritized profit over what I think is best for the game and its community.

Do I still recommend it? 100%. Without hesitation.
The sheer scale, faction variety, replayability, and sandbox freedom are unmatched. Immortal Empires is an absurd achievement and gives you an entire Warhammer world to play in.

What keeps me coming back isn't simply conquering the map—it's creating my own stories. I've played campaigns as Alith Anar, Malekith, Valkia, Skarbrand, Daemons of Chaos, Snikch, and many others, deliberately building armies, choosing wars, and making decisions around lore, character, and immersion rather than pure optimization.

The modding community takes that experience even further. You can essentially tailor the game to whatever kind of Total War experience you want.

After thousands of hours, I can still start a new campaign and think, "Okay... what story are we telling this time?"

If you like Warhammer Fantasy, fantasy in general, Total War, strategy games, or sandbox games where you can create your own stories: BUY IT.

It's not perfect. But it's one of the most ambitious, replayable, and endlessly entertaining strategy games ever made. 10/10 — absolutely recommended.

I get the hate on this game but I think the Warhammer series are the best installation of the Total War franchise. Most of the hate I see comes from the really good players who have figured out how to beat the AI easily but the game is still endlessly replayable, factions are all unique, and while the DLCs tend to be overpriced and suck; the game overall is very fun and keeps you coming back.

Do not be dissuaded by the negative reviews. There is literally no other game that compares to this AMAZING game. If you like Total War strategy and Tolkienesque D&D-like fantasy, Dwarves, rats, demons, and more, you should remove all doubt and just dive right in. 

I warn you though, that, if you get into it, you may have to pull out your wallet more often than you expected, not because the game has micro-transactions, but because there are over a 100 unique Legendary Lords / factions to play with (and more to come), many whom will need to be unlocked by purchasing their respective game (Warhammer I or II) or DLC 50+ they came with. But even without them, you'll have many options to get you going for hundreds of hours. You will have access to 10 or 12 factions if you only buy Warhammer 3.

People can complain about the price tag, and since Warhammer III, it's not without reason. Warhammer 1 & 2 offered DLCs which added 2 new factions for $7.49; Warhammer 3's DLCs generally offered 3 new factions for $18, now $15, a steep incline. Although you can choose to pay only for one faction at a third of the price. The games and DLC's tend to go on sale multiple times throughout the year making it a worth while buy for Warhammer lovers. 

But even if I have spent approximately 440 bucks in total on all the games + DLCs since 2016 (you should be able to get all for less than half of that during sales), it's given me over 1,000 hours of game time. Even at full price. 

Ever seen a T-Rex fight a Black Dragon? A giant War Mammoth vs a Treeman? An army of undead against a dwarven shield wall? Ever marched through Chaos-infested wastelands filled with devils and demons with a bunch of spearmen and bear riders? Well what are you waiting for?

В целом игру рекомендую. Если в душе вы стратег и обожаете средневековый фентези, то игра определённо для вас. Эта игра буквально Герои меча и магии, но более комплексная и созависимая.
Что хотелось бы отметить:
1. Очень высокая реиграбельность. Вариантов развития в пределах одной компании и одного лорда очень много, а лордов игре на данный момент ровно 100 шт.
2. Динамика механик. Есть общий скелет в виде глобальной карты и карты боя, но у каждой фракции и почти у каждого лорда есть уникальные механики и именно они определяют как вы будете взаимодействовать с этим скелетом. 
3. Масштабность. На огромной глобальной карте пересекаются множество фентези сил. Крысолюди, динолюди, вампиры, пираты, скелеты, хаос, огры, орки, дворфы, эльфы и т.д. В общем сегодня вы пират грабящий порты, завтра диктатор людской империи пытающий восстановить силы порядка. Но вы не только играете в симулятор городов, но и непосредственно участвуете в масштабных баталиях управляя большой армией со своими уникальными юнитами и особенностями.
4. Дорого. Чтобы полноценно получить весь игровой экспириенс вам нужно купить 3 игры + куча длс. Да, тем кто играет с релиза первой части крайне удобно, ведь её наличие всё ещё актуально, но для многих, кто только хочет присоединиться это вызывает только отторжение и выстраивает огромный пейвол. Я бы порекомендовал брать ТОЛЬКО по скидке 3ю часть > потыкаться, посмотреть, зайдёт игра или нет > выбрать наиболее подходящую по вайбу фракцию > докупить на скидках все длс/другие части к ней. 
5. Повер крип. Разработчики понемногу убивают игру, выпуская длс в которых новые лорды на доли сильнее предыдущих.
