Bewertung: Total War – Warhammer 3 / Eine Hassliebe

Total War: Warhammer 3 ist ein gewaltiges Strategiespiel mit enormem Potenzial, beeindruckender Atmosphäre und einer faszinierenden Mischung aus mittelalterlich-europäischer, asiatischer und teilweise sogar amerikanisch-mythologischer Fantasie. Die Welt wirkt lebendig, die Fraktionen sind kreativ gestaltet und machen spielerisch meist großen Spaß. Doch je länger man spielt, desto deutlicher zeigen sich Probleme, die den Spielspaß bremsen.

„K.I.“ oder doch einfach nur NPC-Verhalten?
Eines der größten Missverständnisse rund ums Spiel ist die Bezeichnung „KI“. Was wir hier haben, ist keine lernfähige künstliche Intelligenz, sondern eine klassische NPC-Verhaltenslogik, die nach starren Algorithmen arbeitet. Sie ist komplexer als ein Schachprogramm, aber weit davon entfernt, sich klug, vorausschauend oder „menschlich“ zu verhalten.
Diese Logik sorgt dafür, dass Warhammer 3 sich häufig nicht wie ein strategisches Spiel anfühlt, sondern einfach wie ein ständiger Kriegssimulator ohne Pause. Egal ob du gewinnst oder Ruhe suchst: Neue Feinde tauchen sofort auf, ohne nachvollziehbaren Grund, außer „der Spieler muss beschäftigt bleiben“. Strategisches Nachdenken wird dadurch weniger belohnt als permanentes Kämpfen.

Dauerkrieg statt Strategie
Wer defensiv spielen möchte, wer diplomatisch vorgehen will oder wer ein Handels-Imperium aufbauen will, wird dafür selten belohnt. Denn:
Passives Spiel führt zu Feinden, die plötzlich Krieg erklären.
Handel ist oberflächlich, ohne Tiefe oder besondere Bedeutung.
Das System wirkt mehr wie „Füllmaterial“ als wie ein echtes strategisches Element.
Dabei hätten Mechaniken wie Diplomatie, Handel oder Bündnisse eigentlich enormes Potenzial, gerade in einem so tiefen Universum.

Vasallen, Konföderationen & Diplomatie gutes Konzept, schlechte Umsetzung
Einige Völker sind darauf ausgelegt, mit Vasallen, Abkommen oder Konföderationen zu arbeiten. Theoretisch klingt das fantastisch. Praktisch jedoch:
Vasallen unterstützen kaum.
Sie agieren extrem passiv.
Selbst im Krieg tun sie fast nichts außer hin und wieder einen kleinen Trupp zu schicken.
Man schützt seine Verbündeten mehr, als dass sie einem helfen.
Statt also durch Diplomatie ein Reich aufzubauen, kümmert man sich nur darum, dass die KI nicht sofort ausradiert wird und verliert dadurch selbst Zeit und Ressourcen.

Die DLC-Preise sind ein kontroverses Thema. Kleinere Inhalte teuer zu verkaufen ist fragwürdig. Um Kritik zu vermeiden, werden Nutzerbewertungen oftmals erst am Veröffentlichungstag zugelassen, sodass unliebsame Kommentare im Vorfeld ausgehebelt werden. Das wirkt so, als wolle man zunächst möglichst viele Käufer gewinnen, bevor negative Rückmeldungen sichtbar werden. Natürlich müssen Firmen wirtschaftlich arbeiten und Mitarbeiter bezahlt werden, doch für Spieler wirkt diese Vorgehensweise schwer zu rechtfertigen und wenig transparent.

Fazit:

Total War: Warhammer 3 hat eine beeindruckende Spielwelt, grandiose Fraktionen und die Grundlage für eines der besten Strategiespiele der letzten Jahre. Aber seine veraltete NPC-Logik, das Chaos aus endlosem Krieg und die schlecht genutzten diplomatischen Mechaniken verhindern, dass es sein volles Potenzial ausschöpft.

Total War: Warhammer III has some clever, creative faction mechanics, but they’re trapped inside a world that feels like a kid dumped every toy into one box and called it a universe. The setting is a random pile of historical knock-offs, demons, monsters, and grimdark clichés with no cohesion or self-control. The writing is endless but hollow more noise than narrative and the factions are shallow caricatures pretending to be cultures. Balance is an afterthought, diplomacy barely exists, and the whole thing is obsessed with nonstop war. Compared to the rich, grounded storytelling of Lord of the Rings or Game of Thrones, Warhammer’s world feels 100× less coherent and far more ridiculous. It’s mechanically inventive, but artistically childish and creatively empty.

Total War: Warhammer III — це вражаюче завершення грандіозної трилогії, яке демонструє, наскільки масштабною та різноманітною може бути стратегія у фентезійному сетинґу. Гра майже з перших хвилин вражає своїм великим і продуманим світом, де кожна фракція не лише має унікальний стиль гри, а й відчувається частиною живої, насиченої лору всесвіту Warhammer Fantasy.

Однією з провідних сильних сторін проєкту є висока варіативність: різні раси пропонують зовсім інші підходи до битв і глобальної стратегії, тож кожна нова кампанія відчувається свіжо та по-іншому. Із доповненням Immortal Empires гра взагалі перетворюється на один із найбільших стратегічних майданчиків у жанрі — з майже безмежною кількістю сценаріїв для нових проходжень.

Графічно Warhammer III також робить крок уперед: деталізація юнітів, масштаб епічних битв та опрацювання ландшафтів створюють справжній ефект занурення. Візуальні ефекти та дизайн демонів, армій та оточення викликають щиру естетичну насолоду.

У підсумку, Total War: Warhammer III — це не просто продовження серії, а амбітний, красивий і напрочуд варіативний стратегічний епос, який вартий уваги як фанатів Warhammer, так і любителів глобальних стратегій.

I wanted to like this game so bad, but I just can't. It feels actually more broken and downgraded compared to years ago. I have to downvote solely because the campaign AI in this game is broken and poorly implemented. It got worse from TWWH1 to now instead of getting fixed. Also bugs that existed 5 years ago still exist in the game despite constant DLCs being added.

AI does not seem to have any greater plan and acts very illogical and contrary to its stated personality in the diplomacy screen. I observed what my vassal did, you can preview the plans for each army, nd I did not understand the rationale behind army movements at all, it just felt random. The AI can be very passive most of the time, but then also can get very active for several turns out of nowhere. It sometimes will try to regain lost provinces and other times do everything to lose them. But most irratingly, strong factions may just park 6 stacks at a random town for dozens of turns. Also instead of defending, enemies often just run away and let you destroy their entire economy without a fight, especially if you approach with more than 1 army stack. What is the strategy behind this? Losing even harder? In any case the AI felt more active and reactive in TWWH2.


In TWWH3 I also started ignoring my town defenses and just roam around trying to cause fights every turn. The money you get from a fight also largely outweights whatever you could earn with your economy so why build up a capital city for 40 turns that will be razed in 1 turn? Why also invest in your towns at all? They designed them, except for highly upgraded capitals, to be entirely undefendable with thease meagre garissons that route immediately against any decent army, and  areeasly harassed and weakend by enemy heroes and scavenging armies. 

If you build up defenses, your enemy can siege you in their turn, pausing progress, and once you can react by sending out your garrison to shoo them away you unpause this but lost a turn. In fact, in this way the AI enemy can exploit you to never build up any defenses although they never had a proper siege up at all (you always lifted the siege asap, but u dont get the progress back). Similar design flaws exist in this game. Mainly the fact that you can run from one town to another in one turn means there is no point trying to defend each town at all. You can never help out in time. It is gone, razed, occupied, before you would be able to send any relief force or aid.


During sieges the enemy spawns deep within, not outside, of tower range and the towers shoot seemingly at random timings, with huge gaps, they just seem worthless and sometimes also ignore their own ranges shooting either further than displayed or not at all. The enemy does not wait for siege weapons to arrive, moving them into tower or melee range when it eventually does arrive and half their army is already crushed by the defenses. Not very tactical. Medieval 2 had this figured out better already (although there, the 2nd layer of wall defenses made the AI behave wrong when it came to siege equipment). In Medieval 2 you also wouldnt just overrun a town usually in one turn unless you had the proper siege equipment and even then you would mostly first build some ladders and battering rams. In the meantime you would be able to often send a relief force against the siege.

Do I like the idea of this game? A lot. It is an amazing concept and the huge battles and variety of factions units heroes and equipment is huge fun, the huge campaign map is fun too. But do I like the execution? Simple battles are fun. Sieges have a huge room for improvement. Campaign AI and design is quite a mess though.

This is not a bad game. It could be an amazing game but like it is now it is just a okay game. I get more annoyed with the campaign than I have fun with it due to the design and AI issues. I hope it will be fixed in patches but since the core design has not changed (town defenses being generally a joke and not worth it and  AI getting worse at some and better in other areas each patch) since WH1 I kind of dont believe it will happen. Whoever has the ability to fix it either has no power to decide or change things at CA for the game or has left that company a long time ago.

With all that said, I still think it is one of the best games of its kind (huge fantasy battles), it is just the campaign that is botched. I m still buying any DLCs for factions I am interested in playing, despite everything i said, it is just frustrating a potential 10/10 game is a 6/10 due to weak campaign AI and poor design choices.

NOTE: I just played a different campaign and the faults in the AI were less visible. The more chaotic the game gets the less it is noticable. The Empire regions are very chaotic and there it didnt come out as much with so many small nations but the AI still doesnt act all too smart here either. I think the bigger a faction gets, the more armies it has, the dumber it acts.

[b]TWWH3[/b] was not worth the cost of "free". All the same old mistakes from [b]WH1[/b] and [b]WH2[/b] are back, but now with a grotesquely bloated world, ridiculously "rebalanced" factions & placements, and the good old Creative Assembly trick of making new DLC overpowered, then nerfing it in each subsequent patch, so by the time you get around to a new campaign, you've lost what made the DLC worth any price.

Like many, I got the "free" copy of [b]WH3[/b] in December 2025. It only included the base world map, and I could only play with content I had already purchased with [b]WH1[/b] and [b]WH2[/b]. Okay, fair. You get what you pay for. I purchased the Upgrade Pass for $15 (at 75% off) to unlock the base [b]WH3[/b] factions (like Chaos Demons, Kislev, etc.). Other DLC was tempting, but I wanted to see how this new, massive world played before I put another penny into it.
I'm so glad I waited.
The new world is way too massive even for a computer strategy game. You can achieve a Normal Ultimate Victory before you conquer 1/4 of the map. (In this case, [i]what is the point of the two other continents??[/i]) The 296 factions that mean I spend more time waiting for turns to tick over than I do managing my armies & cities on my own turn (even with the sped-up turn management). In the expanded regions, it might take you multiple turns to get from one settlement to the next even in Forced March stance. This is particularly stupid for factions like Chaos, who need constant raiding & sacking to survive.
The placement of Legendary Lords has been scrambled and bears little resemblance to the same placements from [b]WH2[/b]. Sure, the Empire is where the Empire always is, but Lords like Queek Headtaker, Malus Darkblade, and the new Chaos Legendary Lords are scattered all over the world. (Bel'akor even ends up in the equivalent of Antarctica for some inane reason.) They have - I assume on purpose - placed overly powerful Legendary Lords next to underpowered Legendary Lords for the sole purpose of feeding specific factions. For example, the new Chaos Daemons Legendary Lord (a customizable Daemon Prince) is placed one minor faction away from Malus Darkblade, a Lord who can refill his entire healthbar once per live battle. He also starts dealing attrition damage to your army/garrison [i]immediately[/i] upon sieging a settlement (and of course, my armies don't). All you get for being a four-story-tall Daemon Prince is being more of a target. I had to restart my Chaos Daemon campaign [i][u]six times[/u][/i], and only once did I succeed in even [i]holding back[/i] Malus Darkblade and Hag Graef.
Maybe the newest DLC for [b]WH3[/b] is worth it - my friend bought Sayl the Deceiver, and rants about how good and useful his mechanics are. I expect that to quickly dissolve away to bare-bones effectiveness that ends up not having a real impact on strategic play or battles, after the next few patches. Certainly, the poster-abomination Daemon Prince has no advantage against even regular Heroes - against Normal Dark Elves, Kislev, Dwarfs, and Nurglite Daemons, he fell every time in one-on-one combat. He couldn't even succeed with the Daemon Prince + 2 units of Forsaken against 1 Kislev Lord.

Save your money and your patience: Do not spend any money on [b]TWWH3[/b].

Большего разнообразия механик, фракций и геймплея вы не сможете нигде найти. Гигантский продуманный лор, с множеством интересных героев, событий, в которые при каждом запуске новой компании так приятно погружаться. Возможность реализовать любую тактику ведения битвы: хоть снести врагов быстрым натиском, хоть задрочить соперника отрядами дальнего боя или закидать магией неприятелей, хоть отыграть битву против фулл армии врагов, имея небольшое количество отрядов с лордом и одержать верх - все так сказать зависит лишь от вашей фантазии и скилла.
А видели насколько детально проработана игра? Сколько тонкостей можно увидеть рассматривая внешний вид отрядов или само поле сражения, либо же летая по карте компании замечать маленьких волков, летающих бычков и многих других обитателей континентов, поражаясь живостью земель, по которым ходят твои армии.
Каждая фракция имеет собственные уникальные особенности, позволяя получать удовольствие от различного геймплея, даруя игроку большую реиграбельность.

WH3:TW is a game built on WH2:TW, which was build on WH:TW. However, as time has gone on, QA standards have slipped, power creep has grown, individual armies and abilities become stronger, and the executive mismanagement shown their cracks more clearly (eg: siege rework, which did nothing to help the problems with sieges).

Settlements at this point are nothing more than moneymaking points for the enemy to snatch away from you, as recruitment is now done more and more by mechanics (eg: LM Blessed Spawning requires no time, recruitment cost, or recruitment buildings). Lords and lord abilities become stronger, reducing battle tactics into a question of who stacked enough +melee defense on their doomunit.

In essence, while WH1 was a strategy game, and WH2 was a strategy game, WH3 is an arcade beat'em'up where you romp around with your doomstack killing everything.

Now, this isn't neccessarily a bad thing, and the game genuinely is quite fun. But I *have* to give this a negative review due to my moral concern over the company's direction. This article, by a former developer at the company, ( https://medium.com/@julianmckinlay/total-war-rome-ii-and-creative-assembly-my-statement-ten-years-on-d964f65b0a8f ) is the basis for a lot of my concerns.

WH3 is a good game. But it could have been an outstandingly great game. But weird executive oversight: a classic case of mismanagement: means devs have to put their time into meaningless features like four types of new defensive towers, instead of actually fixing the core problems with the game (eg: generally weak AI, sieges are tedious, smaller armies run amok, replenishment makes casualties meaningless as long as you win, provinces have never been a liked mechanic due to several flaws, hero actions are BS, and so on).

This is clearly shown with the latest 3 DLC, Tides of Torment, in which all the features are half-baked, don't work in the context of an empire-building strategy game, and quite broken (we've had TWO hotfixes since launch with more on the horizon).

Again, a great game that genuinely is value for money due to the sheer amount of content in it thanks to the series' ten-year history, but it's inconsistent with my morals to be able to give this a positive review. Fire all the higher-ups (joke's on me, they're the last people who will take a pay cut over the developers) and I'd change my tune.

The more I play this game, the more impressed I get by it.  If you dive in, there's a LOT to learn.  I was getting my ass handed to me even on Easy difficulty.  Check out videos and guides from creators like ElvenPlotArmor and Malleus Gaming to learn how to suck less.  Join the discord.  Don't get discouraged.  As you start to wrap your head around the campaign and the battles (this game is kind of an epic Real-time Tactics game inside a light-ish 4x game), systems open up and you begin to realize what's possible.

A couple of points if you're considering a purchase but on the fence, especially because of the scale/price of the whole collection:

* As of this month, you can play the full modern version of the game, which is the "Immortal Empires" campaign mode, inside Total War: Warhammer 3 as long as you own ANY of the games.

* That matters because you can pick which race you most want to play to start out and you can buy just the game they came with.  e.g. TWW1 for Dwarves or TWW2 for High Elves.  And then you install and run TWW3 for free, boot up Immortal Empires, and you'll have access to whatever you bought.  You don't have to buy TWW3 at all unless you are ready to try out e.g. Cathay or Kislev or whatever.

* You'll see discussion of content broken down by "race" and also by "faction" or "legendary lords".  Every single Legendary Lord (each of which represents a unique faction, so those two are equivalent) is a very distinct campaign.  Like, VERY distinct.  Factions within a race have a lot in common, but but each faction/lord is a very different game experience, especially for the first few dozen turns.  That might not sound like a lot, but a few dozen turns as a new player takes many hours, and you'll have to try many times to actually survive past that point.

* No matter what you've purchased, the *entire Immortal Empires game exists*.  In other words, not owning Dwarves doesn't take them off the map.  It just means you can't play as a Dwarven faction.  You can, and likely will!, have to fight them on the field.  And if you think "damn, those look cool, I want to try that!", then you can buy TWW1.  But until you feel that way, there's no need to buy them.  You get the same game experience regardless.  (There's a tiny footnote here about "confederation", but it's something you can 99% ignore until you get a lot further into playing the game.)

* The game feels really feature complete at this point.  It's not a 10-year-old game, it's a game that's been improved and refined for over a decade.  It's really really really good.  Absolutely worth waiting for a sale, because especially TWW1 tends to go on sale for a pretty deep discount, and at this point you can have absolutely the full modern TWW3 experience for whatever that sale price is.  (A week ago you could get TWW1 for $15 on steam, for example.)  It's frankly worth it at full price, if you're in a hurry.  But for $15 it's just an absurd amount of content.  And then if you like it, there's a world of other stuff you can add over time.  But you only need whatever faction you're playing today, so you can pace yourself.

El juego está bien; aunque si lo pienso de forma clara no ha cambiado tanto desde el primer juego, es el mismo con facciones nuevas y mecánicas nuevas para las facciones, pero sigue teniendo problemas muy importantes de balance y de prácticas antijugador que no tienen sentido.

Desde que salió el juego han ido sacando DLC que son bastante mierdecilla, todo lords legendarios (Algunos metidos con calzador y con perks que no tienen sentido), un par de facciones nuevas, y han ignorado zonas del mapa como Ind o Khuresh, siendo lo peor que lo tienen en el mapa pero lo dejan vacío, con niebla para que no puedas ir. Hace cosa de 1 año o más pusieron un par de ciudades en la frontera como diciendo, mira lo que llega, para luego pasar de nosotros.

Con problemas de balance me refiero a que siempre que sacan un nuevo lord le ponen cosas que están rotas, que revientan a todos y no lo parchean hasta después de un par de meses, para que así la gente se compre el DLC. Luego cosas de unidades que no tienen sentido, no tiene sentido que una rata, por muy bueno que sea, se pueda pelear una unidad de martilladores y de dracohierros a la vez y ganar, si fueran basura goblin o zombies de los vampiros que no tiene moral, puede que sí, pero enanos que están con armadura a tope y que la moral no les cae, no es lógico. 

Con lo de practicas antijugador me refiero al mapa de “Imperios inmortales”, donde tienes los “end games” que se activan a partir de un determinado punto, y que la lógica que tiene el juego para declarar la guerra en esto no es ni medio normal. 
Explico caso, Soy un Enano (Malakai Makaisson) y estoy al norte del imperio, pegado a los desiertos del caos, peleando por ahí, llega el turno 60 y empiezan dos de los “end games”, esta vez sale la pirámide negra y la gran cacería. La Pirámide, la cual esta situada en los desiertos del sur (Si pensamos en un mapa humano, yo estoy peleando en Noruega y la pirámide negra es el Congo en África) y la facción decide que me tiene que declarar la guerra a mi, cuando tiene al lado a bretonianos, otros enanos, orcos, demonios…. Y yo estoy fácilmente a 15 turnos corriendo desde su ubicación, y ni me conocen. Y el otro end game que sale es el de la cacería salvaje, que es mas de lo mismo, elfos silvanos se despiertan por todos los lados y deciden declararme la guerra, los que se despiertan en medio del imperio se la declaran al imperio y a mi, los que lo hacen al lado de los elfos oscuros (En Naggaroth; Mapa humano es EEUU), a los elfos oscuros y a mi…. Básicamente todo el juego me declara la guerra a mi como jugador, aunque este en el quinto pino. Esto no sería un problema tan grande si, aunque te declaran la guerra si decidiesen atacar a todo lo de alrededor y luego seguir expandiéndose hasta llegar a ti, pero no lo que hacen es marchar por todo el territorio enemigo hasta llegar a ti, ignorando ciudades enemigas, ejércitos….
Gráficamente a evolucionado desde el primero, pero no son saltos tan grandes como para decir es una evolución bestial.

Gracias a dios que existen los MODS, que solucionan muchos de estos problemas; por ejemplo tenemos uno que expande los “imperios inmortales” por toda la zona de Ind o Khuresh, lo que hace que existan cosas ahí, el problema es que son facciones existentes y no las que por lore tendrían que estar ahí; también tenemos MODS para quitar el antiplayer, hacer que que las facciones que por lore son enemigas se declaren la guerra de forma lógica… mejoras graficas y de lore… gracias a toda esta gente que hace esto tenemos un juego mucho mas completo del que nos ofrecen y solucionan cosas importantes.

Si eres un jugador que viene de los Total War clásicos, no te recomiendo esto, ya que un factor clave en el juego es la magia, que no tiene ningún sentido, y si vas con la mentalidad de tropas enfrentándose, con cañones, caballería, arqueros e infantería, te van a dar para el pelo cuando de repente veas a ratas, enanos o cosas así salir del suelo o que te caiga un rayo y te aniquile media tropa…. Quédate en el 3 Kingdoms y espera al nuevo Medieval.

I have to start with this... After playing a game for hundreds, even thousands of hours, it is absurd to leave a review that picks on all the things you found annoying after spending a full year playing the game. I can easily sit here and tell you the MANY things I don't like about this game at this point. I wish they would fix them all. Except I played for a mere 300 hours across several different campaigns, all with same friend in pretty frictionless coop. So I'd say that means I REALLY enjoyed it. Steam reviews crack me up, but Total War seems to attract a lot of these fans for some reason. Therefore this games real score ought to be much higher than what it shows, but whatever...

And while CA has certainly made these bigger games much pricier with DLC content everywhere you turn, while also having had some pretty big stumbles at times, it has made most new Total War entries objectively better than the last despite it basically being its own competition in this niche. I'd say that's showing good intent at the very least. 

These games are not for everyone, but if you like Total War, you buy Total War, you wait patiently for Total War to fix things while happily painting the map over and over. Sometimes they listen, sometimes they don't. But I wouldn't give up this novel strategy franchise's successful existence over, for example, a complaint the AI isn't challenging to beat after you have put 200 hours into the game. 

Yes of course buy this release now if you like TW games. If you love RTS or 4X strategy but have somehow never played TW series yet because presumably you have been living under a rock, just buy this. It's unique fun. If you are someone that doesn't know strategy but the battles look cool, buy an older one on sale to grasp their style first. It's big strategy. Some complex strategy game jank will occasionally show itself in AI being brain dead and odd little glitches at times, but it's been remarkably bug free for me over last two years in particular.

At the end of the day I've put nearly 600 hours into this franchise for a reason. Total Warhammer is perfect if you're a Warhammer fan, an RTS fan, a Fantasy fan or all of the above/anything in-between.

Ups and downs have been had over the years but when it comes down to it there are few games for me I can argue spending so much on and fully getting my money's worth.

I have full faith in CA to complete this project with the End Times DLC and move on to bigger and better things.

The Total War series, in general, has great battle engines that keep improving, laboured with terrible 4X campaigns that haven't got better since the 90s, and WH3 is the worst of the lot...

Paused, the map is Tolkienesque, but in action this Old World is so cramped and haphazard it's more Wrestlemania, where the best strategic decision is often to leave an enemy alone because they'll be killed by someone else for free, and player campaigns are usually one epic clash followed by joyless slaughter of small garrisons the rest of your saturday night (the Rome classic) or (WH's innovation) a pile of sticking plasters and hacks to force interesting strategic choices and thematic battles every few turns, between joyless garrison slaughter.

A lot of the 4X part is just broken, not delivering on the promises of the genre. Some factions have correct builds which are only apparent after hours of trial and error, or fortunes decided by NPC conflict beyond your borders, which you simply must have foreseen. One faction gives up entirely and just teleports you around the map to whenever exciting stuff is happening, in between 'be here on this turn or lose' events (which, as we all know, are really just 'save scum the last three turns' events).
This takes different forms for each faction, but ultimately I think it comes from the bizarro Noah's Ark deathmatch map, where every action is necessarily berserk, zero-sum, kill-or-be-killed, be clairvoyant or lose, take half their stuff in one turn or be behind forever cheesy metagaming.

There are some thematic mechanics and even gestures at storytelling which, for what it's worth, have you RPing pretty well.
The Dwarves and Lizardmen have esoteric aims where you conflict with other good guys, before having to put your differences aside to face Chaos.
Dwarves, Orks and Skaven can use the Underway for all-or-nothing gambits through the mountains, while Beastmen wage occult guerilla war through the forests.
Undead factions have a curious mix of speed and frailty, able to raise units anywhere, but relying heavily on magic and characters to fight attrition.
Orks have an almost natural rhythm of building up Waaaghs and tearing into the civilised world, before losing steam and retreating into the hills.
Skaven find a new food source and their population explodes, only to fall to infighting when it runs out, while their economy is a literal rat's nest, which was funny the first time.

Of course, all this only works when it's you doing it. The AI will happily YOLO its Beastmen, make an Orcish Rome of half of the map, or lose Karaz-a-Karak on turn 20, so you have to squint, hard.

And there are just as many weird choices.
Dwarves are really an arcadey time attack mode, where optimal play means single-minded expansion if you want to get the best prize to help the next bout of single-minded expansion. 
Karl Franz has an Empire to manage with a ton of different levers to pull, but Sigmar help you if you do anything except spend the correct currency on the correct buffs and play the correct first turns with the correct army in the correct place at the correct time, otherwise you're screwed 50 turns later by factions you aren't even aware of.
Wood Elves follow a script, and you either know how the script works or you're always behind.
Other factions impose so many layers of extraneous, gamey stuff - currencies, bars, courts, reputation - that it's like trying to solve a maths puzzle through the glovebox of a 4X, while juggling battles, and I'm often tempted to flip the battle AI down to easy and autoresolve everything to keep up the flow of the puzzle-solving.

I think Total War's problem is that mechanical solvability, zero-sum mathiness and the innately conservative play of 4X conflicts with what's fun to do in the battle engine. You build boring buildings and bargain armies for abstract profit later on, nihilistically politick Syracuse/Byzantium/Marienburg until you have them surrounded and invade in three turns, exploit the battle AI because your economic house-of-cards demands it, enemies like idiot dominoes, one front at a time, one complete victory buys you the next, one loss is ruin, anything else puts you behind schedule.

░░ ██ ██ ██ ██ Fabuła / klimat / imersja ██ ██ ██ ██ ░░
Świat gry to potężny wycinek uniwersum Warhammer Fantasy, zrealizowany z ogromnym rozmachem. Produkcja jest świetnie osadzona w lore, zachęcając do zgłębiania historii na własną rękę w zewnętrznych źródłach. Klimat wylewa się z ekranu – opisy budynków, drzewka technologiczne czy same jednostki sprawiają, że w to uniwersum po prostu się wierzy i łatwo się w nie wciągnąć.

░░ ░░ ██ ██ ██ Wyzwanie / poziom trudności ██ ██ ██ ░░ ░░
Gra tłumaczy podstawy, ale nie podaje wszystkiego na tacy – wielu zależności trzeba nauczyć się samemu w praniu. Poziom trudności jest nierówny i zależy głównie od tego, jak bardzo komputer oszukuje. Na niskich poziomach AI jest po prostu tępe; na wysokich dalej jest tępe, ale nadrabia to absurdalnymi buffami do ekonomii i wojska, przez co może nas przegonić statystykami, a nie taktyką. W samych bitwach komputer bywa nieobliczalny – raz podejmie błyskotliwą decyzję, by chwilę później dać się wymanewrować w najprostszy sposób. Wyzwaniem jest tu głównie ogromna różnorodność jednostek, których trzeba się nauczyć kontrować. Jednak gdy nabierze się doświadczenia z czasem, gra staje się zdecydowanie prosta bo przestaje nas przytłaczać swoim rozmachem i skomplikowaniem.

░░ ██ ██ ██ ██ Muzyka / udźwiękowienie ██ ██ ██ ██ ░░
Soundtrack jest poprawny – ma swoje momenty i przyjemnie przygrywa w tle, ale to udźwiękowienie robi tu największą robotę. Odgłosy wystrzałów, ryki potworów, okrzyki dowódców czy szczęk oręża mają odpowiedni ciężar i moc. To buduje niesamowitą satysfakcję z rozgrywki. Nawet tak proste dźwięki, jak ukończenie budowy czy powiadomienie o wygranej bitwie, są zrobione tak, że działają na korzyść odbioru całości.

░░ ░░ ░█ ██ ██ Gameplay ██ ██ █░ ░░ ░░
Jako fan serii akceptuję jej wady, ale nie mogę ich ignorować. Gram wyłącznie w immoratl empires (mapa z tej części mnie nie interesuje). Każda rasa ma inny archetyp rozgrywki (jedni stawiają na ekonomię, inni na plądrowanie), ale gra słabo to komunikuje, co na początku może wprowadzać chaos. Nowości w bitwach o osady są dla mnie marginalne, a system wieżyczek na murach został mocno osłabiony. Największą bolączką jest jednak system automatycznego rozstrzygania bitew – jest niekonsekwentny (wygrywasz przegrane starcia i odwrotnie) i irytujący przez zmianę czytelnego paska szans na suchy opis tekstowy wyniku.

░░ ██ ██ ██ ██ Regrywalność ██ ██ ██ ██ ░░
Obrzydliwie duża. Masa frakcji, lordów i mechanik sprawia, że każda kampania wygląda inaczej. Early i mid-game są świetne – czuć rozwój i realne zagrożenie. Niestety, late game (końcówka gry) zamienia się w nużące malowanie mapy i zarządzanie ekonomią. AI w późnych etapach potrafi spamować dużą liczbą armii o fatalnym składzie, przez co wielkie bitwy zamieniają się w powtarzalną rzeź bez większej taktycznej głębi.

The 3rd game in the trilogy is by far the worst despite having all the factions and some of my favourites at that. I held off on buying it for years despite being a Warhammer fan. There are so many bugs, it's as if there is no Q&A and the devs don't even play the games.

The game is also completely unbalanced and broken. The RPG skill trees render your LEGENDARY Lord a complete wimp unless you use mods to increase the skill point gain. Malekith who is one of the most powerful magic users in the world doesn't even know basic spells as a start. Even without increasing skill points. The skill tree renders lords and some heroes completely immortal on the battlefield unless you use another Legendary Lord against them. There is sometimes no point to armies at all. Let alone siege battles which they have somehow achieved the unimaginable feat of making much worse in Warhammer 3. They have balanced the game around multiplayer with no consideration for what character skills trees are in the campaign. 99.9% of people buy total war games for the sandbox campaign, yet CA in their infinite wisdom are catering the entire game to the 0.01% of players that want to pvp.

As a former tabletop player myself stemming back over 2 decades at this point. When building armies, you had limits on the amount of units you could take. With the focus being on "core" units with "special" and "rare" units having caps on them that increased depending on the size of the army. You'd think then that there would be some form of soft cap system in place to ensure that there aren't massive stacks of dragons steamrolling the map. But there isn't. Whilst WH3 did introduce soft cap mechanics for some factions such as chaos dwarves as well as Tomb Kings having soft caps from WH2. Most factions still roam around with so called doom stacks of elite units. It lacks immersion and demonstrates that virtually no one at CA, or at least those that make the decisions actually have any knowledge of what they were creating.

There is also a severe case of unit bloat with shielded and unshielded variants of units as well as other similar variants. Whilst the TT did indeed have some unit equipment choices, there more often than not weren't any corresponding model choices, nor did it make much sense for a unit of shades to have great weapons as an example. It especially doesn't translate well into the game and feels like a lot of bloat. But where there needs to be units, they have none. There are no Night Goblin Spearmen despite Night Goblin spearmen being a staple of Night Goblin armies and actually have real life models for them. This has been an issue since WH1. You'd think that by introducing a night goblin faction, you would actually be able to field a full and diverse army of night goblins.

At this point, I don't think any real Total War, let alone Warhammer fans work at CA. You'd be insane to want to, seeing them breaking with lore and factual history such as with the Rome 2 Womanz update. Already shoe horned in female Dreadlords in an already female heavy faction with Dark Elves despite there being no record or lore for there being female Dreadlords in existence.

The only reason why I am playing the game is because I'm creating mods to make this game somewhat playable since the end of development is at least in sight, and CA can't break the game much further than it already is. From overhauling the skill system to "fixing" female Dreadlords eventually I'll get this game up to a playable state for myself.

Also to note, merely having the launcher open counts as time played. I've only played a few dozen hours of this game and I've had the launcher open for the rest as I was modding/afk or doing other things. So the player numbers for this game may very well be highly inflated.

Pros
-Massive campaign scale and variety
-Deep, engaging strategy and faction mechanics
-Excellent visuals, audio, and atmosphere
-High replayability
-Strong modding support and active community
-Lore-rich and immersive Warhammer setting

Cons
-Inconsistent faction balance
-DLC pricing and quality can vary
-Some factions need more polish
-Can be overwhelming for new players

Full disclosure I am a long-time fan of the Total War series, going all the way back to the first Rome: Total War. After many years, I started to feel burned out on the historical settings. Then Total War: WARHAMMER released, completely reigniting my love for the series. It also introduced me to the Old World of Warhammer and eventually Warhammer 40K (I did my best to avoid the plastic crack).

Total War: WARHAMMER III is easily one of the best strategy games you can get at the time of writing this review. The scale, mechanics, visuals, audio design, optimization, active modding community, and replayability all come together to create an outstanding experience.

Is the game without issues? No. Admittedly, the developers can be greedy, but let’s be honest, that’s pretty much industry standard at this point. Balance between factions isn’t always perfect either. However, I actually think this works in the game’s favour most of the time, as it feels more lore accurate and creates unique challenges depending on who you play. Some factions definitely need more work than others, but overall it remains a fun and engaging experience. I recognize that balance issues will matter more to some players than others.

As for DLC, I’m generally not a fan of paying extra, but I make an exception here. It’s still cheaper than buying miniatures, and while DLC quality can vary significantly, doing your due diligence usually pays off.

Overall, I really enjoy this game because of its setting, variety of playstyles, challenge, immersion, visuals, and sheer scale. It delivers everything the Total War series is known for wrapped in an absolutely massive Warhammer package.

I'ma be real, I got this game for $10 knowing full well that it's a genre I'm not familiar with.. I got this as a sort of tutorial to get ready for Total Warhammer 40k, but after putting a few hours in, I just don't think this is for me.

It's not a bad game, just very different than what I'm used to. It's like an army simulator more so than an RTS, but still requires a lot of micromanagement?

So I started the tutorial, and while it does a good enough job introducing someone like me to the various mechanics, it also does a bad job explaining how to actually play the game. 
I hopped into a match against bots and kept losing over and over, looking online to see what unit counters the other, and while this game is incredibly complex, I also found it lacked variety once you have the right units for the job.

At the very most basic strategy, you get the enemy line to get "stuck" in battle with your infantry so you can manually flank with cavalry, telling them to charge in to break up enemy formation, but then spam click to get them out of there.
Spears / axes counter cavalry to protect your own flanks, terrain plays a big part in how a unit performs, there's clearly a lot to this game.. but the fights themselves felt pretty simple once I got a decent enough roster.

Keep in mind, I'm speaking entirely as someone who played against bots using the same faction so I could learn their counter. The complexity is learning this for every faction, because there are some units the game straight up doesn't explain what they're classified as.

While I'm personally putting a thumbs down, this game isn't bad at all, it's just not for me, and I'm glad I played this for $10 so I could learn that, because I might skip the Total Warhammer 40k game if it's similar to this one.

I appreciate this game immensely, which is why I don't want to see it get stuck with sieges in their current state. Siege battles are typically more time consuming than land battles, and players are often forced to manually resolve when attacking walled settlements to avoid losing units in a pyrrhic victory. Considering we have been putting up with this for a decade, it's felt like a complete slap in the face from CA.

I would not recommend spending money on this game until these issues are addressed. I think purchasing Lords of the End Times would send the wrong message to CA. Great grand strategy game where you can battle lots of creatures as most factions within the Warhammer Fantasy universe, being faithfully implemented with different mechanics in this (almost) full in-universe map.

I want to recommend this game, really I do, but they dropped the ball SO MUCH that I cannot:

The loading times are, quite honesty, absurd.  I have a high-end PC, and I alt-tab out to watch a couple of youtube videos while waiting for, really, anything to happen.  End turn?  Take a nap.  Load a save, go out and get your shopping done.

The difficulty is FAR FAR FAR too high.  I don't know if the developers know this, but some of us have jobs, and want to come home to a relaxing power fantasy game to wind down at the end of the day.  Even on the easiest difficulties, the game is impossibly hard if you don't dedicate your life to it.  There are entire Youtube channel dedicated to helping people defeat battles, and even then, those tend to exploit undocumented mechanics in order the "cheeze" the battle.  I wanted massive battles with strategic army placement that rewards good tactics; not running a couple of units around the map that are "high value", while hiding most of my real army to try to peel one or two units back at a time.  I wanted to play a Total War game, not a MOBA.

Then we get to HOW the difficulty sliders actually work.  The battle difficulty apparently has nothing to do with the difficulty of the battles AT ALL, and rather, the auto-resolve only.  So, apparently, the developers decided that, if you don't dedicate your life to the game, you don't get to participate in the ONE THING people play the game for, but are rather encouraged (required) to auto-resolve all the battles.

Overall, the concept is great, but the execution is about as bad as it could possibly get.  If you have time to dedicate your life to the game, then yeah, it's a great game.  If you have a job and want a fun game to play to unwind at the end of the day....look elsewhere, as this game is anything but.

I would like to review Warhammer 3. The battlefield feels very realistic. The shooting ranges, firearms, obstacles, and line of sight for infantry units are all very well designed. For example, if you place Dwarfs on the front line, human ranged units standing behind them can still shoot enemies because the Dwarfs do not block their line of sight. This kind of detail is done very well.

However, the downside is that the late game becomes quite boring. You have to manage many armies, and most battles end up relying heavily on autoresolve. The campaign itself is not very exciting, especially in the later stages, because it does not feel like you are playing through a story. Unlike the Vortex Campaign, there are no cinematic scenes that tell the story after completing objectives, showing what happens next like in an RPG.

I wish the developers would create story-driven campaigns based on legends for individual lords. Each campaign could have multiple possible endings depending on the player’s choices. [b]Total War: WARHAMMER III[/b] is the glorious continuation of my sacred duty: roleplaying as a grumpy Dwarf with trust issues and an aggressively maintained filing system for betrayal.

The game is brilliant. The battles are huge, the campaigns are wild, and the world is so packed with nonsense that it feels like the Old World is being run by a committee of goblins. I’m having a great time, especially as the Dwarfs, because nothing says “fun” like winning through sheer stubbornness, iron discipline, and a complete refusal to experience joy.

But the [u]real[/u] WARHAMMER III experience is multiplayer with friends.

My friend decided to play [b]Chaos Dwarfs[/b], and I have never raised my thick eyebrows so hard in my life. Imagine showing up to game night and your mate arrives wearing your face like a hat, running a factory powered by cruelty, and going “[i]Relax, it’s just business.[/i]”
Aye? [b]Just business?[/b] That’s how grudges are born, lad.

Did he “peacefully” expand his industrial empire by turning half the map into a smoke-belching nightmare? [b]Grudge recorded.[/b]
Did he “borrow” resources while I was busy protecting the realm like a responsible beard-owner? [b]Grudge recorded.[/b]
Did he look me dead in the eyes and say “We’re still dwarfs though” while fielding artillery that screams in lowercase evil? [b]GRUDGE. RECORDED.[/b]

The game itself? [b]Fantastic.[/b]
The scale? [b]Insane.[/b]
The diplomacy? [i]Suspicious.[/i]
The AI? Still occasionally acts like it’s been hit in the head with a hammer ([i]lore-accurate, honestly[/i]).
The multiplayer? [u]A friendship stress-test with siege weapons.[/u]

[b]10/10.[/b] Would defend the Karaz Ankor and [strike]forgive my friends[/strike] judge my friends again.

And to my Chaos Dwarf “ally”: enjoy your smoke, your profit, and your lies.

This is an attempt to write an evergreen review for Total Warhammer 3.

Sometimes new patches and DLC come with game breaking bugs that take too long to fix. Sometimes, the new stuff that comes in a DLC isn't really worth the money. Sieges are often pretty unfun. If you liked Total Warhammer 2, know that corruption is now trivial and several areas no longer feel like themselves after having so many factions shoved into them (ie Lustria doesn't feel like a lizardman jungle after adding at least 3 nonlizard LLs). If you liked Medieval 2 Total War, know that replenishment is king and that the idea of having to move up reinforcements from the heart of your empire to the front isn't really a thing.

That said, the game is an incredible achievement and a load of fun. It has at least 22 playable races, each more different from any other race than any 2 races were in any historical Total War game. It has over 100 playable factions, each with a unique leader and starting position. The IE campaign spans the size of the planet. It is imo the best Total War game and easily the best Warhammer Fantasy game. Its total development has been over a decade. I have over 500 hours sunk into it and I don't plan on stopping anytime soon.

Maybe the best part is the free stuff you get. Buy any of the Total Warhammer trilogy and you have access to the planetwide Immortal Empires campaign map. There's over a dozen completely free lords in addition to the 8 each game starts with. Buy what DLC interests you from any of the 3 games. Or don't buy any. Most of it goes on sale for a few bucks every summer and winter and even the base game factions and free factions get updates to bring them up to par with the DLC sides.

[h1]買った記憶がないのに勝手にライブラリに入ってる。ナンデ？[/h1]
過去作を持っている人は、2025年12月からこのゲームのコンテンツ「Immortal Empires」を無料で遊べるようになった。
TW:WH3を買っていないのにライブラリに入っているのはそのため。
「Immortal Empires」はTW:WHシリーズの看板コンテンツ。詳細は後述。

[b]今からTW:WH1や2を買った人でも、同じようにTW:WH3のコンテンツ「Immortal Empires」を無料で遊べる。[/b]Totalwarシリーズを開発した会社が25周年を記念して、そういう方針にしたらしい。[b]AI君が言ってた。[/b]

「AI君が言ってた」という文言だけで一気にうさん臭く感じた貴方はとても正しい。
筆者と違ってまともな日本語ソースがあるのでURLを記載する。気になる人はそちらを参照してほしい。

https://doope.jp/2025/11161850.html
「初代「Total War: WARHAMMER」と2作目の所有者を対象とする大型キャンペーン「Immortal Empires」の提供がアナウンス、解禁は12月4日」
　
　
[h1]じゃあ、これを買わずに1作目や2作目を買った方が得じゃない？[/h1]
という訳でもない。
[b]TW:WH3から登場した新勢力で遊ぶには3本体を買う必要がある[/b]ので、それらの勢力で遊びたいなら3本体も買うことになる。
DLCではなくTW:WH3本体。それとストーリー重視のTW:WH3専用キャンペーン「混沌の領域」も3本体が無いと遊べない。

クソアホAI君に質問すると「1や2を既に持っている人はTotal War: WARHAMMER III UPGRADE PACKを買えばいいよ」と促してくるが、これは3専用のDLCも含めたバンドル。
[b]本体単品の方が安いなら本体だけを買えばいい。[/b]それかTotal War: WARHAMMER TRILOGY。
TRILOGYは3部作セットのバンドルだが、1,2を既に持っている人はちゃんと値引きされる。3本体を単品で買うよりちょっぴり安い。

ちなみに2025年のウィンターセールではTW:WH3本体が1,750円に対して、UPGRADE PACKはセールなしの定価7,000円。
UPGRADE PACKの日本語レビュー欄でコレについてメーカーに問い合わせた上で言及している賢者がいた。
やはりいつの時代も信じるべきは炭素生命。AI君に疑問を抱いた貴方はやっぱり正しい。
　
　
[h1]Immortal Empiresって何だよ[/h1]
冒頭で述べたように、TW:WHシリーズの看板コンテンツ。約290勢力が参戦する超クソデカマップで遊ぶキャンペーン。
これといったストーリーは無く、プレイの度に趨勢は変わる。闇ときどき光が勝つ、ぐらいのバランス。

2作目経験者の方であれば、「あの頃より更に規模が増えるのか…自分のターンになるまで時間がかかりそう」と懸念されるかもしれない。
しかし安心してほしい。2作目よりずっと早くて快適になっている。
　
　
[h1]どれ買ったらいいのか分かんないよ[/h1]
まず遊びたい種族を選ぼう。種族によって遊び方が全然違うので、もう最初は顔で選んで良いと思う。
3本体だけを買っても1や2で登場した勢力で遊べない（NPC勢力として全員登場はする）ため、どれか1つ試しに買って気に入ったらバンドルのTotal War: WARHAMMER TRILOGYを買うのが良いんじゃないかなと思う。
TW:WH1やTW：WH2のDLCを買うことで遊べるようになるマイナー勢力もいる。

・ドワーフやアンデッド、人間で遊びたい：1作目を買い、TW:WH3をインストールする。
・エルフや恐竜、科学力世界一のネズミで遊びたい：2作目を買い、TW:WH3をインストールする。
・東欧や東洋の人間、混沌勢力とか闇堕ちドワーフで遊びたい：TW：WH3を買う。

・本体ではなく、1や2のDLCに遊びたい勢力がいる：そのDLCを買うだけで良いらしい。

[b]※「1や2本体を買わなくてもDLC買うだけでTW:WH3のImmortal Empiresを遊べるよ」とAI君が言ってますが、この点だけは確証ないです。無料のDLC（FLC）をインストールしてWH:WH3を遊ぶ、も出来ないそうです。対象は有料のコンテンツのみ。[/b]
　	
　
執拗に「TW:WH3をインストールする」と強調しているのは、3作目が一番洗練されていて快適に遊べるため。1作目と2作目の反省点が改善されているので、今から遊ぶならTW:WH3が一番お勧め。
　
　
[h1]TW:WH1のドワーフで遊びたいけど、TW:WH3で遊ぶ場合でもTW:WH1本体をインストールする必要ある？[/h1]
インストールしなくていい。TW:WH3を起動した際に、ユーザーが所持している過去作や各DLCを確認してプレイアブル勢力としてアンロックされる。
3で遊ぶ場合はTW:WH3だけインストールすれば良い。1や2の本体、あるいは気になるDLCがあれば、それらを購入する。
　
　
[h1]日本語ある？[/h1]
公式では対応していないが、日本語化MODはある。
ワークショップで「JAPANESE Language MOD」で検索してね。翻訳の質はスゴイ高い。

ゲームを起動すると最初にランチャーが出てくるので、画面左側の「MOD MANAGER」をクリック。ここでMODをオンにしないとゲーム内で反映されないので注意。
日本語化MODと「Better Camera」MODは最初から入れておくべきってぐらい必須。

Game is a Total Waste of Time

Total War: Warhammer III  Wastes Your Time

I wanted to love this game. I put real time into it 100+ turns, multiple games, careful play, turtling as a defensive faction, building up holds the game explicitly encourages you to build.

Then the game erased 20–30 turns of progress instantly via an invisible agent action that:

ignores walls

ignores garrisons

ignores preparation

has no meaningful counterplay

is decided by pure RNG

Fully upgraded settlements can be de-leveled and have buildings destroyed with a single dice roll, with zero battle and zero warning.

That’s not difficulty. That’s not strategy. That’s time disrespect.

The deeper problem is systemic:

Territory is a liability, not a reward

Garrisons are mostly pointless without mods

Borders can’t be secured

Defensive play is actively punished

The “correct” way to play is exploiting AI blind spots and cheese tactics

If you play honestly, building cities, fortifying borders, progressing slowly, the game punishes you for it. The only way to “win” is to stop playing the fantasy the game sells and start gaming its flaws.

I don’t mind losing battles.
I don’t mind overwhelming odds.
I do mind a strategy game deleting hours of progress through invisible mechanics and RNG.

This game doesn’t respect your time.
That’s the real failure.

Not recommended unless you’re happy modding out half the systems or playing exploit-heavy.

Şirketin uçuk fiyatlandırmaları herkesin malumu olduğu için oyunun kendisi hakkında yorum yapmak isterim.

Favori oyunlarımdan biri ''TW Warhamer 2'' ye yaklaşık bin saat harcadığımdan ve serinin devamı olduğu için bu oyuna da aynı heyecanla büyük umutlarla başladım ancak sadece 300 küsur saat dayanabildim. Yani yanlış anlaşılmasın bu 300 saat oyunu sevdiğimden değil sadece önceki oyuna benzerliğinden ve yeni factionları deneme süresinden kaynaklanıyor.

Oyunu 'Legendary' yani en zor olan zorluk seviyesinin bir altında 'Very hard' ile oynadığımı ve düşman yapay zekasının yeteneğini belirleyen en önemli etkenin bu olduğunun belirterek:

Eski oyuna kıyasla neredeyse 2 katı ırk, bu ırkların içinde de daha çok çeşit(faction) seçip oynayabildiğinizden eğlenceli ve ilgi çekici duruyor. Ancak hangi ırkın hangi factionu ile başlasam oyun 30-40 turdan sonra geri dönüşü olmayan bir tekrara düşürüyor. Kendi gelirlerimi düzeltip 2-3 tane kendi factionumun üst seviye birliklerinden oluşan ordular kurduktan sonra hiçbir düşman gelip senin ordularınla karşılaşmak istemiyor. Düşmanın yerleşkelerine saldırmak için ordunu ilerletiyorsun, düşman yapay zekası ister kendisinin en önemli en gelirli yerleşkesi, ister bir tur önce fethettiği düşük seviye yerleşkesi olsun hepsinden ordusunu kaçırıyor. Sen de önceden ayarlanmış bu yetersiz garnizonla savaşıp yerleşkeyi ele geçiriyorsun. Bazı oyunlarımda düşmanın son şehri olsa bile, burayı kaybederse teknik olarak oyunu kaybedeceğini bilse bile yaklaşan ordumu görünce kendi ordusunu o şehirden kaçırdığını hatırlıyorum. Yukarıda bahsettiğim konu bu. 30-40. turdan sonra oyunda yapacağın savaş türünün %90'ı düşman yerleşkenin dandik garnizonuyla kuşatma/meydan savaşı oluyor. Bu savaşları da bir süre sonra artık otomatik yaptırıyorsun çünkü bütün garnizonlar hemen hemen aynı ve orduna asla tek başlarına karşı koyamıyorlar yani savaşın da heyecanı kalmıyor angaryaya dönüyor.

Oyunun 80-100. turlarında 10-20 yerleşkesi olan yani durumu kötü olmayan düşman factionlar oyunun bu evrelerinde bile sana karşı koyabilecek bir ordu kuramıyorlar. İmkanı ve parası yetse bile yapay zeka sırf 2 tur hızlı ordu basayım diye tek turda yetiştirilebilen dandik üniteler çıkarıyor. Bazen de bu bahsettiğim durumu iyi olan factionlara baktığımda hiçbir yerleşkelerinde bu kadar tur geçmesine rağmen bir üst seviye ünite yetiştirme binası basmamış olduğunu görüyorum ki yine dandik ünitelere mecbur kalıyorlar.

Hal böyle olunca savaş yapay zekasını övebileceğimi veya yerebileceğimi bile sanmıyorum ki amacı savaşmak olan bi oyunun savaşlarındaki sıkıcılık savaş içerisindeki yapay zekadan değil, sefer yapay zekasının tasarımındaki beceriksizlikten/umursamazlıktan kaynaklanıyor. 

Anlayacağınız düşman senden kaçıyor çünkü TOTAL WAR adlı oyunun yapay zekası düzgün ordu kuramıyor. Oyunun başı haricinde yapacağınız neredeyse tek savaş türü default garnizonu otomatik savaşla alt etmek oluyor.
Yani TOTAL WAR WARHAMMER 3 adlı oyunda savaşların bir tadı bir eğlencesi olmuyor.

I have 600+ hours in Warhammer 2 and 600+ hours in Warhammer 3, and I own all the DLC.

The game is fun. If you enjoy strategy games and the Warhammer universe, there is a lot to like here. Big battles, lots of factions, and tons of content.

But there are also serious issues.

Creative Assembly feels very focused on monetization. To get the full experience, you end up paying a lot for DLC, which is especially painful if you’re from a third-world country like me.

Some mechanics feel lazy or badly designed, like siege ladders. Sieges are often too easy. Many times I don’t even use my full army and can win with just a lord and a few heroes, which kills immersion.

The AI cheats, and it’s obvious. Balance is still questionable. If you think you can just build a normal balanced army, think again — ranged spam is still extremely strong. Some units look great on paper, but their animations are so bad that they never perform as well as their stats suggest.

Faction balance is also uneven. Some factions are so weak or annoying that I never want to play them again, while others are so strong that if you want easy wins, you’re pushed toward those.

What frustrates me most is that CA often feels disconnected from the community. Core problems stay for a long time while new paid content keeps coming.

I still enjoy the game and have spent hundreds of hours on it, but it’s also frustrating, unpolished in places, and sometimes feels more focused on profit than player experience. Just know what you’re getting into — especially if multiplayer matters to you right now.

A lot of people dismiss Total War: Warhammer III as a “DLC money grab,” but that criticism really does not hold up once you actually look at what the game offers.

First of all, Warhammer III by itself is already a complete and finished game. It has a full campaign, solid faction variety, and a clear gameplay loop that stands on its own. The idea that the base game feels “incomplete” simply is not true. On top of that, Creative Assembly has continued to actively support the game, especially since Immortal Empires was fully integrated. Yes, there were some rough and buggy updates in the past, but since then they have made stability, balance, and polish a top priority, and it shows.

One of the biggest misunderstandings comes from how DLC works in this series. Immortal Empires is an enormous sandbox mode where factions from all three Total War: Warhammer games coexist on one massive map. That is not “cut content.” It is the opposite: it is older games being preserved, upgraded, and modernized inside a newer engine. If you already own Warhammer I and II, all of that content is available to you in Warhammer III at no extra cost. Units and mechanics are reworked to fit modern standards—for example, collision damage now actually works properly instead of being mostly visual, as it was in Warhammer II.

If you want everything, yes, you would need to own all three games, which is a huge amount of content. But the key point is that you do not need all of it. I have around 360 hours in the game and I have not even touched half of the available races and factions; probably closer to 30 percent. This alone shows that the base experience is far from lacking.

Creative Assembly has also made the DLC model more flexible over time. Lord packs are now split into smaller, individual purchases, so players can buy only the faction or lord they care about instead of paying for a large bundle they may never fully use. With upcoming updates like version 8.0, you will not even need to own Warhammer III to play certain DLC factions. You can simply buy the race or lord you want and enjoy it in a sandbox-style experience, similar to a digital tabletop wargame.

Another point that often gets ignored is the amount of free content. Major updates frequently add free Legendary Lords, reworks, and mechanical overhauls. These are not locked behind paywalls. Older and neglected factions get revitalized at no extra cost. A good example is the Norsca rework—one of the most forgotten races from the first game, released almost eight years ago, which now plays far better thanks to a free overhaul. The same applies to reworks like Slaanesh: the core improvements are free, and you only pay if you want new lords with different playstyles.

For a mostly single-player-focused strategy game, this level of long-term support is genuinely impressive. Your money is not going toward content that was removed from the base game, but toward ongoing development that improves the experience for everyone.

So if you are hesitant because you hear people yelling about “DLC fiesta,” do not be. Total War: Warhammer III is a finished product with a huge amount of content right out of the box. Immortal Empires is an optional sandbox mode that brings together all three games, and of course you need to own older games to play their factions. That does not mean the game is being sold in pieces.

Try it for yourself. Look at the player numbers, wait for a sale if needed, and judge it based on actual playtime rather than online outrage. The DLC is optional, extra content—functionally closer to classic expansion packs, just smaller and cheaper.

Total War: Warhammer III is, at its core, a fantastic game. Unfortunately, it continues to suffer from instability and questionable development priorities.

Dear Creative Assembly:
If money has become more important than quality, then please just move on and develop Total War: Warhammer IV, or whar ever. What you should stop doing is reworking the current game every few weeks. In 2,700 hours of playtime, I have only ONE completed a single campaign without having to restart because a patch broke it. That is simply unacceptable.

By now, I play almost exclusively with mods—and even then, only for about two hours per campaign, just to test whether the latest update breaks something in single-player. If it does, that save is abandoned immediately, and the game is never touched in multiplayer co-op. A Total War title that players avoid playing properly out of fear of bugs has fundamentally failed.

The unfinished and unreliable mod management system makes both single-player and multiplayer a disaster to play. If fixing it does not generate direct profit, it is clearly ignored, pushing the game further into a downward spiral. Modding is officially “supported,” but in practice the system is broken.

The new faction-based purchase model is also deeply unappealing. Paying the price of an entire race pack just to unlock a single new faction is terrible value. Hard pass.

Conclusion:
An excellent game concept is being undermined by constant patching, poor stability, and aggressive monetization. Creative Assembly needs to make a clear choice: properly maintain a stable, finished game—or move on to the next installment. A stable, complete product should not be optional; it must be the standard.

[h1] A misbegotten hot mess of monetized DLC aimed at Warhammer collectors & multiplayer [/h1]
I write this as a fan of the single-player Total War series.  I played - and repeatedly beat - each game in the series starting from the original Shogun all the way through to Total War Warhammer II.

TWW3 is not a strategic challenge in the mould of the rest of the series.  Graphically, it's beautiful.  If watching animated demon ladies with pincer hands (that presumably explain their inability to sew practical garments) is your thing, buy this game.

If getting said demon ladies to spank one of your mate's armies of leather-clad Bear guys to death with their satanic handbags is your thing, you're in for a treat.

If you want to play Total War, buy something else.

[h3] Quantity not Quality [/h3]
If you've played Total War, you'll know the drill: 120-200 territories, full of strategic nuance, occupied by 30-50 competing powers.

That's fun, but one of the recurring criticisms of Total War over its first two decades was the amount of time players had to spend watching the computer determine the actions of all the NPC factions.  At no point during Medieval II or Rome II did any player say "this game could really do with more animation of factions I don't control interacting with each other".

TWW3 starts with [b] 270+ live factions on turn 1 occupying 550+ territories [/b] ... for now.  Those numbers will no doubt soon be out of date, [i] because the business model benefits from a constant conveyor belt of shiny new content [/i] .  Buy some popcorn, get the ironing out, maybe open up Netflix on another screen: you're going to need something to do while the AI trawls through its ever-expanding roster of sprites and you, "the player", do nothing.

[h3] Competent AI sacrificed on the altar of content monetization [/h3]
With 270+ competing entities on a vast map, you might be wondering how on earth the developers balanced the complexity of that.

They didn't.

The AI in Total War titles has always been somewhat arbitrary (I'm sure we've all had a pope or 5 who only threatened excommunication when we went on the offensive, but never when the NPC factions attacked us).  Fine.  It's a game, there will be rails.

In TWW3, that not only reaches silly proportions - it also sometimes fails.

To keep the player “challenged,” NPC factions engage in behaviour that makes zero sense outside the code. Undead pirates leave the ocean, march hundreds of miles inland past weaker targets, purely so they can get in your way. You want to conquer that Himalayan mountain? You can’t. There's a horde of rum-soaked Caribbean corpses sat on it who've just inexplicably declared war on you.

That level of silliness would be amusing if it were a late game phenomenon.  Thing is... in TWW3 it kicks in from around turn 10 onwards.  Yep.  In order to keep the game challenging, the NPC factions genuinely do bizarre things to you from almost the very beginning.  I've had a full 20 unit stack of late-game Imperial units including 5 tanks turn up in the mountains of Naggaroth on turn 9, allegedly as a marauding "horde", and waltz past 4 other NPC factions just so that they can declare war on me.

You might be wondering why, but that becomes evident on the occasions when the heavy-handed anti-player bias doesn't slow you down.  Fitting all those territories into one play experience means that the distances are somewhat compressed.  If you start to snowball, goodness me do you snowball quickly.  The game flips from absurdly unenjoyable due to arbitrary difficulty into absurdly unenjoyable due to being far too easy in about 20 turns.

[h3] Summary: Total Glitz, not Total War [/h3]
This isn't a fine-tuned strategy game.  It makes eff-all sense as a play experience.  It's very impressive to look at, and if you like collecting Warhammer-themed stuff and playing with it with friends, then this is probably worthwhile.

But it's not Total War.  Not even close.

Sega and Creative Assembly  lost touch with reality a long time ago.
What is happening now with the Total War series and other projects under Sega’s wing is a tragedy for the industry. Creative Assembly (CA) is no longer the studio that gave us Rome or Shogun.
Why I hate them:
•	Greedy DLC Policy: Selling scraps of content for $25–30 that used to come as free patches is an insult. Sega has turned beloved franchises into cash cows, squeezing every last cent out of fans with minimal investment in development.
•	Technical Degradation: Games are released in an "early access" state but at full AAA prices. Bugs that have migrated from engine to engine for years remain unpatched, yet the in-game store works perfectly. "Optimization" is a word that CA seems to have forgotten entirely.
Bottom line: Buying products from Sega and CA today means supporting stagnation and greed. Until sales drop to zero, they won't start working properly. Give us back the old Total War or sell the license to someone who actually loves strategy games, not just quarterly reports.

I wish these companies nothing but the worst.

Total War: WARHAMMER III is a grand-strategy game where you run an empire on a turn-based map and then fight the decisive moments in real-time battles. The appeal is the scale and the spectacle: massive armies, absurd monsters, world-ending magic, and campaigns that spiral into personal rivalries and grudges you didn’t plan to have.

On the strategy layer, you’re constantly juggling money, growth, recruitment, diplomacy, and keeping provinces stable while threats pop up on multiple fronts. It’s the kind of game where one “quick turn” becomes an hour because you’re optimizing buildings, plotting an invasion route, and trying to keep three different neighbors from deciding you look weak.

Battles are where the series still feels unmatched. Front lines collapse, flanks matter, ranged units punish mistakes, and a single well-timed spell can swing a fight from “lost” to “wipe them out.” Even when it looks like pure chaos, good positioning and target priority reliably win, especially on higher difficulties.

Faction variety is the game’s secret weapon. Different races don’t just have different unit lists—they often play by different rules, with unique economies, corruption systems, special resources, and campaign mechanics that change your entire approach. Switching factions can feel like learning a new game, which is why it stays interesting for so long.

The hero and lord layer adds another dimension: characters level up, unlock skills, and can be built into specialized roles that shape your army’s identity. Army composition matters a lot, and the best campaigns come from leaning into a faction’s strengths rather than trying to play everyone the same way.

For long-term play, the big draw is the gigantic trilogy-spanning sandbox campaign (Immortal Empires), which ties together an enormous map and a huge roster, with access depending on what you own across the trilogy. Between that, frequent balance changes, additional content packs, and a strong modding scene, the game is structured as a platform you can keep coming back to.

It’s an easy recommendation if you want deep campaigns and cinematic battles in a fantasy setting, and you’re happy learning layered systems. If you dislike complex management, don’t want to engage with an ever-expanding DLC ecosystem, or prefer tighter, shorter strategy experiences, it can feel overwhelming—because its core strength is also its biggest commitment.

Total War: Warhammer 1-3 is one of those games that quietly eats hours of your life and leaves you wondering where the real world went.

Im about 30 hours in, playing campaign only, mostly sandbox and a good chunk of that has been spent in co-op campaigns with a friend. That said, this game does not hold hands. Expanding a full army and empire feels like spinning plates while riding a unicycle. There are a lot of moving parts. Economy, diplomacy, unit synergies, tech trees and while that depth is impressive, it also makes completionist achievements feel basically impossible. Which is devastating because my brain wants them lol.

What Warhammer does best is immersion. once you're in, you're in. Hours pass without noticing. the combination of lore, scale and longterm planning pulls you in and doesn't let go.

I haven't even touched the story campaigns yet. just the sandbox and it already feels massive. immortal empires alone is a game you could live in.

If you've never played warhammer before - yes, it's a lot of lore but if you give it the time it deserves, you'll be glad you did.

Warhammer III is one of those games that really clicks once you stop trying to play every faction the same way. Every race has its own mindset, and the game actually rewards you for leaning into that — whether that’s Skaven being sneaky and expendable, Chaos Dwarfs turning war into an industry, or just deleting armies with artillery from good positioning.

What I love most is how much strategy actually matters. Terrain, formation, economy, and timing all make a real difference. When I lose, it’s usually because I messed up — not because the game felt cheap. And when it works, watching a plan come together is incredibly satisfying.

It’s not a super casual game, but if you like strategy, variety, and figuring things out as you go, Warhammer III is absolutely worth playing.

Another big con is the ai, it’s crazy! The beginning few rounds the AI is on steroids and can absolutely crush you with huge unfair advantages. If you manage to overcome that initial wall, it’s very easy to crush them in return. It’s also very common to see factions with several strong armies just sitting in a corner doing nothing. After about 60 turns it gets very boring and you can see all the problems, which takes away from the experience. 

Overall, I would only recommend this game on discounts. Never at full price.

Este juego se ha convertido en la antiestrategia:
El capitán de nivel 2 se mete entre tus 4 batallones de lanceros todos ellos bien apretados, les saluda cordialmente y pasa a través de ellos para atacar a los arqueros que estaban, aparentemente, bien custodiados. Y claro, como no huyen bien, pues se quedan a charlar un rato del tiempo con el capitán. Y los que están alrededor, les encanta quedarse ahí a cotillear a ver si hablan del marido de la vecina.
Y, por supuesto, el capitán de nivel 2 es más duro que la piedra y se permite el lujo de ser todo lo temerario que quiera, mientras que, si tú haces lo mismo con tu héroe de nivel 40, le lanzan dos virotazos y ya le entra ansiedad.
O cuando ese batallón enemigo decide, en un arrebato de locura temeraria, ignorar el campo vacío y aparentemente libre de peligro que tiene detrás de sí para huir hacia adelante, donde está todo tu ejército, para, después de huir un rato, acordarse de que dejó el fuego de la cocina encendido y regresar atrás y tocarle la moral a todas las unidades que tenías tranquilamente en la retaguardia.
O que la IA pueda convocarte batallones mágicamente al lado de tus tropas a distancia y te jode toda la estrategia que has planificado porque "magia".
O que la IA pueda usar sus hechizos desde el otro lado del mapa (cuando tú tienes que acercarte a la cocina para poder usar los tuyos), mientras vas perdiendo tus tropas y el general enemigo solo se dedica a huir e ir diezmándote las tropas.
O que la artillería enemiga pueda acertar repetidamente a tu héroe, que es un blanco solitario en movimiento y además va montado en una montura voladora... Muy chistoso.
Todo muy absurdo y patético y ocurre hace ya tiempo. Total War se ha convertido en esto, pero eh, que es Warhammer y da igual pues ahí se queda…

En mi caso, más de un 50% de las batallas de campaña que he entablado, han comenzado con la ventaja en el terreno de la IA. Ellos están en el terreno elevado y a ti pues te toca hacer de Anakin Skywalker, porque está subestimando tu poder. Parece que tus generales deciden de antemano totalmente borrachos dónde tener una batalla y dónde es buen lugar para desplegar tus tropas.

Lo de que cuando te atacan asentamientos solo puedes salir a presentar batalla y no te permite defenderte dentro de la población porque un día decidieron así ahorrarse tiempo en diseños… eso es de traca.

La diplomacia sí es cierto que han puesto más opciones (y les ha costado, ¿eh?), pero tampoco nos vengamos muy arriba, que sigue teniendo la misma esencia de los anteriores.
Y es que, en general, te quedas un poco como con la sensación de los FIFAs, que te sacan cada poco uno con plantillas nuevas, pero sin apenas cambios significativos que mejoren jugabilidad y demás. Hacer caja, vamos.

Y... ¿Qué decir de su política de monetización de DLCs? Ya de eso ni hablo, porque todo el mundo ya sabe lo que hay.

En fin, y ahora, después de haber probado un tiempo el juego vanilla, me voy a descargar 700 mods para intentar arreglar un juego roto, porque al final acaba siendo lo mejor de todo: la comunidad de modders que, en muchos casos, arreglan un juego que la empresa sacó de aquella manera. Claro, eso si Creative Sssembly no les declara la guerra…

I recently bought two games. Then I noticed I have warhammer III. I was confused at first. I bought I+II a while ago in a pack for very cheap. I wasn't happy with the game (see II review). Now I am. All my gripes are gone. There isnt much new game here I believe, but it looks better, runs better (?!??), and is for free. For. free. I played for 200 hours now. For free. I played many races already and am about to start installing mods.

There are 3 phases for the immortal empire game (the only one aside the tutorial story, available for free). This is the sandbox version.

1) You dont know whats what, many things are a bit confusing, partly due to the UI and the lag. Gameplay is exciting but exhausting.

2) You get better, a lot more things become fun, like battles. From "what happens when I do that? woops lost a unit elsewhere" to "I want to do this, I know this will happen, I can prevent this in the mean time, although it's not optimal, but...." you feel like a general. This is the best phase, and battles are the core. Total War style, this what this game does best (and most). But also the campaign map, civ-style, is better now, since you know what to expect, and no sudden megastacks surprising you at your doorstep.

3) You understand that what you hoped for, diversity for the races, different stories, different feelings, is only very meagerly so. Typical gaming balance problem. Instead of shifting things from player to Ai, they balanced everything into oblivion I guess. I guess because of multiplayer. Orcs fight basically just like elves or humans. There are only minor differences of a poweful elven mage, and my beloved Wurrzag. You nuke enemy units, buff or debuff.
Once you understand whats what, it's clear that the differences vanish. That's a big no no for a campaign and lore that suggests a chaos of different races and factions. In the end it's all samey, even chaos creatures and undead. Compare to humans, and dwarves. Read  it again. Same?!
Anyways it's not yet so bad I want to stop playing. Some mods probably will help (a lot, I hope)

I will certainly buy a lord or so (dieing to play wood elf units, and theyre so far elduded me to ally), just for my conscience to pay the company back some bucks.

If you haven't got it, I suggest buying low price I+II, because then you get III for free. Every content you buy is in III, just more modern. It's perfect.

Just if you want the story part (I read it's not that good), buy III righout.

Happy 2026, all you good guys and gals!


P.S. Forgot the most important trick I encountered so far: From A youtube video of Zhevkovic (or so): Set Battle difficulty to how difficulty you want it it to be (as a newbie). I started with the recommended 'hard' which is pretty tough. BUT set the AI stats to MINIMUM. So all the enemy units are bonkers bad. They will still knock your ass around, I promise. The point of this: AI is good, but weak. But most importantly, your 'feeling' for AUTO RESOLVE, is correct. It says easy victory? Then auto resolve. It says something else, you can improve the result by playing yourself. This way you actually get better as a general. Later, when you win even AR:losses easily by hand, you can gradually increase the stats for AI units by hand, mid campaign. I haven't^^ It's tough enough. And winning is more fun.

You don't have to buy the previous game anymore to access the big Immortal Empires campaign, so just buy this one and try it out. I think it's finally at that stage where it can rival Total War Warhammer II, The III's Realm of Chaos campaign is ass compared to II's Vortex campaign, but Immortal Empires campaign is fun now and most of the factions have been brought up to speed compared to previous games. If you've played Warhammer II and were holding back because of the atrocious release state of this game, you can finally move on to Warhammer III after years of patches and DLCs. It still has higher minimum spec requirement compared to II's, but it's not as resource demanding as back when released. The loading times and end turn speed is comparable to Warhammer II despite the enlarged map of Immortal Empires.

With that said, the DLCs and patches for this game have gotten even slower than Warhammer II's pace. So if you got a favorite race or unit that's not in the game yet, you'll have to wait even longer. Some of the problem from II's are still here. Lizardmen are still boring to play, and the rats are still OP, but now you can play also as proper Chaos faction to bring about the end times.
